2. It was presided over by J.L. Simonsen.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
6.x: Statement 1 is correct: the first session was held in 1914 at the Asiatic Society, Kolkata. Statement 2 is wrong: Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee presided; J.L. Simonsen and P.S. MacMahon only took the initiative to found the association. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' each misjudge one statement.
6.tq: Founders (Simonsen, MacMahon) are not the first president (Ashutosh Mukherjee).

6.s: The Indian Science Congress Association was founded in 1914 on the initiative of:
o: Homi J. Bhabha and S.N. Bose
Anil K. Gupta and Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee
6.x: The association was founded in 1914 on the initiative of British chemists J.L. Simonsen and P.S. MacMahon.
6.tq: Use the founder-versus-president trap in an institutional history question.

6.s:
Arrange the following Indian Science Congress events in chronological order:
A. First session at the Asiatic Society, Kolkata
B. 88th session in New Delhi
C. 108th session at RTM Nagpur University

Select the correct answer:
6.x: The first session was held in 1914, the 88th session in 2001, and the 108th session in January 2023. Therefore, the order is A, B, C.
6.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intermediate session.

6.s: The theme of the 88th Indian Science Congress, held in New Delhi in 2001, was:
o: Science and Technology for Sustainable Development with Women Empowerment
Science and Technology for Rural Development
Frontiers of Science and Technology in Health
6.x: The 88th session (2001, New Delhi) had the theme 'Food, Nutrition and Environmental Security' (asked in UPSC 2001). 'S&T for Sustainable Development with Women Empowerment' was the theme of the 108th session (Jan 2023, Nagpur). The other two options are not ISC themes given in the notes.
6.tq: 88th ISC 2001 = Food, Nutrition, Environmental Security; 108th 2023 = Women Empowerment.

6.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Academy)
 a. NASI
 b. IASc
 c. INSA
List-II (Headquarters)
 i. New Delhi
 ii. Bengaluru
 iii. Prayagraj

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
6.x: NASI is headquartered at Prayagraj, IASc at Bengaluru and INSA at New Delhi.
6.tq: Start from the sure headquarters pair and eliminate codes with a repeated mismatch.

6.s:
Arrange the following Indian science academies in chronological order of their founding:
A. INSA
B. NASI
C. IASc

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
6.x: NASI was founded in 1930, IASc in 1934 and INSA in 1935. Therefore, the order is B, C, A.
6.tq: Use the first and last founding years to establish the sequence before checking the middle item.

6.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
6.x: NASI was founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences. C. V. Raman founded IASc in 1934, while INSA was founded in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India.
6.tq: Check both the founder and founding year in each pair to catch swapped identities.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian National Science Academy (INSA):
1. It was founded in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India.
2. Its headquarters is in New Delhi.
3. It was renamed INSA in 1970.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All three statements are correct. INSA originated as the National Institute of Sciences of India in 1935, is headquartered at New Delhi and adopted the name INSA in 1970.
6.tq: Verify the institutional origin, location and later renaming as separate factual elements.

6.s: Vigyan Prasar is an autonomous organisation under which of the following?
o: Department of Science and Technology, Ministry of Science and Technology
Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Human Resource Development
6.x: Vigyan Prasar is an autonomous organisation of the Department of Science and Technology under the Ministry of Science and Technology. It was set up in 1989 at New Delhi.
6.tq: Use the parent-department trap by distinguishing DST from the Ministry of Education.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding DD Science and India Science:
1. DD Science is a one-hour daily science slot on DD National.
2. India Science is an Internet-based science channel run by Vigyan Prasar.
3. Both platforms were launched on 15 January 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: DD Science is a one-hour daily science slot on DD National, while India Science is an Internet-based science channel run by Vigyan Prasar. Both were launched on 15 January 2019.
6.tq: Test a platform table by combining nature, operator and launch date.

6.s: Vigyan Dhara is best described as:
o: A DST umbrella scheme merging three schemes relating to capacity building, research and innovation
An autonomous body for grassroots innovations under NITI Aayog
A radio network operated by IGNOU
A single television channel for school education
6.x: Vigyan Dhara is a DST umbrella scheme merging schemes concerning S&T institutional and human capacity building, research and development, and innovation, technology development and deployment.
6.tq: Identify the umbrella-scheme concept rather than a communication channel or institution.

6.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India Science — One-hour daily slot on DD National
DD Science — Internet-based OTT science channel
DD Science and India Science — Two science communication platforms launched together in 2019
Vigyan Dhara — FM radio counterpart of Gyan Darshan
6.x: DD Science is the one-hour daily slot on DD National and India Science is the Internet-based channel run by Vigyan Prasar. They were launched together in 2019; Gyan Vani, not Vigyan Dhara, is the FM counterpart of Gyan Darshan.
6.tq: Find the correctly matched platform by separating television, Internet and radio services.

6.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: SWAYAM Prabha — Group of free DTH educational channels
Gyan Darshan — Higher-education channel of UGC-CEC
Vyas — FM radio counterpart of Gyan Darshan
Gyan Vani — Group of free DTH educational channels
6.x: SWAYAM Prabha is a group of free DTH educational channels of the Ministry of Education. Vyas is the UGC-CEC higher-education channel, while Gyan Vani is the FM counterpart of Gyan Darshan.
6.tq: Separate similar educational media platforms by their operator and mode of delivery.

6.s: Gyan Darshan was launched on:
6.x: Gyan Darshan was launched on 26 January 2000 as an educational television channel involving MHRD, IGNOU and Prasar Bharati.
6.tq: Distinguish the launch year from nearby anniversary dates.

6.s: Gyan Vani is the:
o: DTH channel group of the Ministry of Education
FM radio counterpart of Gyan Darshan
Internet-based science channel of Vigyan Prasar
6.x: Gyan Vani is the FM radio counterpart of Gyan Darshan and is associated with IGNOU.
6.tq: Discriminate between similarly named Gyan Darshan and Gyan Vani services.

6.s: The National Council for Science & Technology Communication (NCSTC) functions under which organisation?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
6.x: NCSTC is organised under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).
6.tq: Identify the correct administrative authority from closely related science institutions.

6.s: ‘Science on Wheels’ mobile laboratories, including those operating in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, are associated with which body?
o: National Council for Science & Technology Communication
6.x: The ‘Science on Wheels’ mobile laboratories are an NCSTC initiative; the programme also includes Alluri Sitharama Raju district in Andhra Pradesh.
6.tq: Use the location clue to identify the associated outreach body.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Council of Science Museums (NCSM):
1. It is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Culture.
2. It was formed on 4 April 1978.
3. Its headquarters is located in Kolkata.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All three statements are correct. NCSM is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Culture, formed on 4 April 1978, with headquarters at Kolkata.
6.tq: Check each institutional detail separately before selecting the combined code.

6.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Council of Science Museums?
o: It administers 49 innovation hubs and is headquartered at New Delhi.
It operates only mobile laboratories under the Department of Science and Technology.
It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Education established in 2015.
It administers a network of 26 science cities, centres and museums and is described as the world’s largest network of science centres under one administrative umbrella.
6.x: NCSM has 26 science cities, centres and museums and is regarded as the world’s largest network of science centres under one administrative umbrella.
6.tq: Distinguish the scale and administrative character of NCSM from those of other outreach programmes.

6.s: The National Council of Science Museums is the nodal agency for which scheme of the Ministry of Culture?
o: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science
6.x: NCSM is the nodal agency for the Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS).
6.tq: Identify the nodal agency by matching the body with the exact scheme name.

6.s: Which of the following correctly describes Science Express?
o: It was a mobile laboratory of NCSM first launched in 1978.
It was a school programme of the Ministry of Education launched in 2015.
It was a science exhibition on wheels organised by CSIR in 2003–04.
It was an exhibition train of DST with the Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre, Ahmedabad, first flagged off in 2007.
6.x: Science Express was organised by DST with the Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre, Ahmedabad, and was first flagged off in 2007.
6.tq: Use the organiser-partner-year combination to reject swapped institutional descriptions.

6.s: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched in 2015 under which ministry and with what broad purpose?
o: Ministry of Earth Sciences, to teach climate science through exhibitions
Ministry of Culture, to establish science museums in every district
Department of Science and Technology, to operate mobile science buses
Ministry of Education, to promote practical and inquiry-based learning of science and mathematics in schools
6.x: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of HRD, now the Ministry of Education, to encourage practical and inquiry-based science and mathematics learning in schools.
6.tq: Combine the launch year, ministry and purpose instead of relying on the programme name alone.

6.s: Which institution trains teachers under the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan?
o: Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre
National Council of Science Museums, Kolkata
6.x: IISER Tirupati trains teachers under the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan.
6.tq: Identify the institution linked to implementation rather than the ministry that launched the programme.

6.s: 'Vigyan Rail', a science exhibition on wheels run in 2003-04, was organised by:
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
6.x: Vigyan Rail was organised by the Department of Science and Technology (DST). CSIR is the classic trap (UPSC 2005). NCSM (Ministry of Culture) runs science centres and mobile exhibition buses, and the Ministry of HRD ran the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, not the science trains.
6.tq: Science trains (Vigyan Rail, Science Express) = DST, not CSIR.

6.s: The Raman Effect commemorated by National Science Day was discovered by C.V. Raman in:
6.x: National Science Day commemorates C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928.
6.tq: Use the year attached to the commemorated scientific discovery.

6.s: National Mathematics Day was declared in 2012 to commemorate the birth anniversary of:
6.x: National Mathematics Day commemorates Srinivasa Ramanujan's birth anniversary. It was declared in 2012, his 125th birth year.
6.tq: Distinguish the scientist associated with Mathematics Day from those associated with physics and technology.

6.s: Which one of the following pairs of day and date is correctly matched?
6.x: National Science Day is observed on 28 February, marking C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect (1928). National Mathematics Day is on 22 December, Srinivasa Ramanujan's birth anniversary. The first two options swap these two dates, and 11 May is not Mathematics Day.
6.tq: 28 Feb = Raman (Science Day); 22 Dec = Ramanujan (Maths Day).

6.s: The India International Science Festival (IISF) is best described by which of the following statements?
o: An annual festival begun in 2015 in New Delhi, organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and the Ministry of Earth Sciences with Vijnana Bharati
An annual exhibition organised by NCSM under the Ministry of Culture since 1978
A school science congress organised by the Ministry of Education since 2015
A biennial festival begun in 2007 by DST alone
6.x: IISF began in 2015 in New Delhi and is organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and the Ministry of Earth Sciences with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA).
6.tq: Match the festival with its start year, place and complete group of organisers.

6.s: ICMR-SHINE, a science and health outreach initiative, is intended primarily for which group?
6.x: ICMR-SHINE, expanded as Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers, is an outreach initiative for students of Classes 9–12.
6.tq: Use the target-group distinction to separate school outreach initiatives.

6.s: Which organisations are associated with ICMR-SHINE?
o: ICMR and the Department of Health Research
NCSM and the Ministry of Education
DST and the Ministry of Culture
VIBHA and the Ministry of Earth Sciences
6.x: ICMR-SHINE is an outreach initiative of ICMR and the Department of Health Research.
6.tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership rather than the ministry associated with IISF.

6.s: ICMR-SHINE, in its second edition, is linked with which initiative?
6.x: The second edition of ICMR-SHINE for Classes 9–12 is linked with the initiative called “One Day as a Scientist”.
6.tq: Recognise the exact programme linkage rather than selecting a familiar health-sector mission.

6.s: The National Innovation Foundation-India was set up in March 2000 with the support of:
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
6.x: NIF-India was set up in March 2000 with the support of the Department of Science and Technology and functions as an autonomous body of DST.
6.tq: Use the parent-department trap to identify the institutional sponsor.

6.s: Which of the following best describes the mandate of the National Innovation Foundation?
o: To scout, support and spread grassroots technological innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge
To regulate all patent applications in India
To operate national educational television channels
To conduct advanced research exclusively with foreign institutions
6.x: NIF's mandate is to scout, support and spread grassroots technological innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge. It is not mandated to conduct advanced research exclusively with foreign institutions.
6.tq: Reject the wrong-activity trap by identifying the institution's actual mandate.

6.s: The National Innovation Foundation grew out of the:
6.x: NIF grew out of the Honey Bee Network, associated with Prof. Anil K. Gupta, SRISTI and IIM Ahmedabad.
6.tq: Link the institution to its origin network and reject unrelated science platforms.

6.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the National Innovation Foundation?
o: Festival of Innovation at Rashtrapati Bhavan
National Biennial Grassroots Innovation and Traditional Knowledge Awards
VIGYANOTSAV quiz for National Science Day
6.x: The National Innovation Foundation conducts or is associated with the grassroots innovation awards, IGNITE and the Festival of Innovation at Rashtrapati Bhavan. VIGYANOTSAV is associated with National Science Day outreach by NCSTC.
6.tq: Find the one programme belonging to a neighbouring institution rather than NIF.

6.s: Under STIP 2020, grassroots innovators are to be supported particularly through:
o: IPR and patent filing assistance through higher education institutes
Replacement of traditional knowledge with advanced research
6.x: STIP 2020 envisages helping grassroots innovators with intellectual property rights and patent filing through higher education institutes.
6.tq: Identify the practical policy support mechanism rather than an unrelated institutional role.

6.s: The first Indian Science Congress (ISC) was held in which year and at which place?
6.x: The first Indian Science Congress was held in Kolkata in 1914.
6.tq: Use the first-event year and place as a paired recall fact.

6.s: Which organisation won two PRSI National Awards in 2025?
o: National Council for Science & Technology Communication
6.x: The National Council of Science Museums won two PRSI National Awards in 2025.
6.tq: Match the award achievement with the correct science outreach organisation.

6.s: The second edition of ICMR-SHINE, linked to the Prime Minister’s ‘One Day as a Scientist’ call, concluded in which month and year?
6.x: The second edition of ICMR-SHINE concluded in August 2026 and was linked to the Prime Minister’s ‘One Day as a Scientist’ call.
6.tq: Link the edition number with the exact month and year instead of the associated campaign alone.

6.s: On National Science Day 2026, the events at VIT-AP were addressed by whom?
o: S. Kiran Kumar, former ISRO chief
6.x: A. S. Kiran Kumar, former chief of ISRO, addressed the National Science Day 2026 events at VIT-AP.
6.tq: Use the office-holder and event-location combination to identify the correct personality.

6.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with NASI?
o: Founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences and regarded as the oldest Indian science academy
Founded in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India at New Delhi
Renamed in 1970 after being founded by C. V. Raman
Founded in 1934 by C. V. Raman at Bengaluru
6.x: NASI was founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences and is regarded as the oldest science academy in India.
6.tq: Combine origin, founder and relative status to distinguish similar academies.

6.s: The first session of the Indian Science Congress Association was held in 1914 at:
6.x: The first session of the Indian Science Congress was held in 1914 at the Asiatic Society in Kolkata and was presided over by Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee.
6.tq: Separate the first-session venue from later session venues and innovation events.

7.s: INSPIRE was launched in 2008 by which organisation as a flagship programme?
7.x: INSPIRE, or Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research, is a flagship programme of the Department of Science and Technology launched in 2008.
7.tq: Direct year-and-agency recall.

7.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its full form and target group?
o: SEATS — Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science — school students
SHE — Support for Her Education — doctoral researchers
AORC — Assured Opportunity for Research Careers — only school students
MANAK — Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge — university teachers
7.x: SEATS means Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science and targets school students. SHE is Scholarship for Higher Education, AORC concerns doctoral and post-doctoral careers, and MANAK concerns school students in Classes VI–X.
7.tq: Full-form trap using familiar-looking but incorrect expansions.

7.s: MANAK under INSPIRE is intended for students who are:
o: In Classes VI–X and generally aged 10–15 years
In Classes I–V and aged 6–10 years
7.x: MANAK targets students of Classes VI–X in the age group of approximately 10–15 years.
7.tq: Direct age-and-class range discrimination.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about INSPIRE components:
1. SHE stands for Scholarship for Higher Education.
2. SHE supports top-ranked students in undergraduate and postgraduate natural and basic sciences.
3. AORC includes the INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty programmes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct. SHE is the higher-education scholarship component, while AORC covers research-career opportunities through INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty.
7.tq: Component-scope statement testing with a look-alike expansion trap.

7.s: The INSPIRE component 'MANAK', aimed at school students of Classes VI-X, stands for:
o: Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge
Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge
Mission for Advancing National Aptitude and Knowledge
Model Awards for Nurturing Aspiring Kids
7.x: MANAK = Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge, for Classes VI-X (age 10-15). The other expansions are made up; 'Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge' is a common wrong guess.
7.tq: MANAK = Million MINDS (school ideas), not awards.

7.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Ramanujan Fellowship?
o: It supports school students with innovative ideas
It supports senior scientists through an excellence grant only
It supports institutions adopting gender-equity charters
It supports Indian scientists abroad who return to India
7.x: The Ramanujan Fellowship, administered by SERB and now under ANRF, is intended to attract Indian scientists working abroad back to India.
7.tq: Brain-gain scheme identification by target group.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship — Indian life-science and biotechnology scientists abroad — DBT
VAJRA — Overseas scientists, including NRIs and OCIs — SERB/ANRF
J.C. Bose Fellowship — Active senior scientists recognised for excellence — SERB/ANRF
PMRF — Women scientists returning after a career break — Department of Biotechnology
7.x: PMRF is for PhD scholars in IITs, IISc, IISERs and other top institutions and is administered by the Ministry of Education. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
7.tq: Find the wrongly assigned target group and awarding body.

7.s:
Which of the following schemes are identified with the objective of converting brain drain into brain gain?
1. VAJRA
2. Ramanujan Fellowship
3. INSPIRE
4. FIST
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
7.x: VAJRA, the Ramanujan Fellowship and INSPIRE are identified as brain-gain schemes. FIST is a DST infrastructure-upgradation programme, not a brain-gain fellowship.
7.tq: Eliminate the infrastructure programme from a target-group list.

7.s: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship was begun in connection with:
o: The centenary of the Indian Science Congress
7.x: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship began in 1997 to mark 50 years of India’s Independence and supports young scientists with a proven record.
7.tq: Date-event association using a commemorative milestone.

7.s: Which one of the following is NOT a scheme or initiative associated with the Department of Science and Technology in the material listed?
7.x: The Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is a DBT (Department of Biotechnology) scheme for Indian life-science and biotech scientists abroad who return, so it is the odd one out. INSPIRE, Vigyan Jyoti and the Nano Mission are DST schemes.
7.tq: Separate departmental flagship schemes from fellowships administered in the research-grant system.

7.s: Which one of the following schemes is intended for meritorious girl students studying in Classes 9 to 12 and is implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti?
7.x: Vigyan Jyoti targets meritorious girl students in Classes 9 to 12 and is implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti.
7.tq: Identify the scheme from its precise target group and implementing organisation.

7.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (Scheme)
A. CURIE
B. WiSLP
C. SEED
D. GATI

List-II (Focus)
1. Early- and mid-career women scientists with the British Council
2. Gender equity through structural reforms in institutions
3. State-of-the-art research facilities for 22 Women PG Colleges
4. STI Hubs for SC/ST communities

Codes:
7.x: CURIE relates to research facilities for 22 Women PG Colleges; WiSLP works with early- and mid-career women scientists and the British Council; SEED has established STI Hubs for SC/ST communities; GATI promotes institutional gender equity.
7.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched scheme purposes.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding WISE-KIRAN:
1. It is associated with the Department of Science and Technology.
2. It particularly supports women scientists who have experienced a career break.
3. Its programmes include WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF and WIDUSHI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct. WISE-KIRAN is a DST initiative for women scientists, especially those with career breaks, and includes WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF and WIDUSHI.
7.tq: Statement combination using the common body, target group and component relationship.

7.s: WIDUSHI, associated with WISE-KIRAN, is intended primarily for which of the following groups?
o: Women scientists seeking their first extramural biotechnology grant
Senior women scientists conducting interdisciplinary research in science and technology
7.x: WIDUSHI is meant for senior women scientists engaged in interdisciplinary research in science and technology.
7.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination between WIDUSHI, BioCARe, GATI and Vigyan Jyoti.

7.s: GATI is best described as a programme that:
o: Offers fellowships to doctoral students in natural sciences
Promotes gender-equity charters in institutions and is modelled on the UK's Athena SWAN
Provides short-term research visits for overseas scientists
Provides grants to women scientists in biotechnology after a career break
7.x: GATI stands for Gender Advancement for Transforming Institutions. It promotes institutional gender equity through a charter modelled on the UK's Athena SWAN.
7.tq: Purpose-based identification of an institutional gender-equity programme.

7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SERB-POWER — Women researchers in academic and R&D institutions
GATI — Women scientists returning to India from abroad
Vigyan Jyoti — Senior interdisciplinary women scientists
7.x: SERB-POWER (now under ANRF) gives research grants and fellowships to women researchers in academic and R&D institutions. The others are mismatched: BioCARe (DBT) supports women biotech scientists after a career break, GATI is the institutional gender-equity charter, and Vigyan Jyoti is for girl students of Classes 9-12.
7.tq: Find the sure scheme-target pair and reject swapped beneficiaries.

7.s: BioCARe is a DBT initiative that primarily supports:
o: Senior scientists recognised for excellence in research
School students aged 10–15 with innovative ideas
Women scientists, mainly unemployed or career-break scientists, in biotechnology
7.x: BioCARe is a DBT programme for women scientists in biotechnology, particularly unemployed women or those returning after a career break. It provides the first extramural grant.
7.tq: Direct body-and-target matching with nearby scheme distractors.

7.s: Which one of the following programmes was launched through collaboration between CSIR and Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan in 2017?
7.x: JIGYASA was started through CSIR–Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan collaboration in 2017.
7.tq: Identify the programme from its partner bodies and launch year.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Smart India Hackathon:
1. It is associated with the Innovation Cell of the Ministry of Education.
2. AICTE has been a partner from 2017.
3. It enables students to solve problems posed by ministries and industry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct. The Smart India Hackathon is partnered by the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell and AICTE and addresses problems posed by ministries and industry.
7.tq: Test all partner and objective statements before selecting the comprehensive combination.

7.s: VIPNET is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Establishing a network of science clubs across India
7.x: VIPNET, associated with Vigyan Prasar, aims to build a network of science clubs across India.
7.tq: Use the organisation–objective association to distinguish closely related programmes.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM):
1. It was launched in 2015.
2. It is jointly run by DST and MeitY.
3. It is implemented by C-DAC and IIT Bombay.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NSM began in 2015 under DST and MeitY. Statement 3 is wrong: it is implemented by C-DAC and IISc Bengaluru, not IIT Bombay. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options include the false statement 3.
7.tq: NSM implementers = C-DAC + IISc Bengaluru.

7.s: Which one of the following was the first National Supercomputing Mission system?
7.x: PARAM Shivay was the first NSM system, established in 2019.
7.tq: Use the first-in-series clue to identify the earliest PARAM system.

7.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (PARAM system)
A. PARAM Shivay
B. PARAM Brahma
C. PARAM Pravega
D. PARAM Ganga
List-II (Host institute)
1. IISER Pune
2. IIT Roorkee
3. IIT (BHU) Varanasi
4. IISc Bengaluru
7.x: PARAM Shivay is hosted by IIT (BHU) Varanasi, PARAM Brahma by IISER Pune, PARAM Pravega by IISc Bengaluru and PARAM Ganga by IIT Roorkee.
7.tq: Start with the sure host institute and match the remaining pairs without repeating a host.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
7.x: PARAM Brahma is hosted by IISER Pune, not IISc Bengaluru. PARAM Pravega is associated with IISc Bengaluru.
7.tq: Find the swapped host institute in the PARAM-system list.

7.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional structure of NM-ICPS?
o: 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads established as statutory bodies
25 Technology Innovation Hubs established as Section-8 companies in host institutes
25 science clubs established exclusively in Kendriya Vidyalayas
7.x: NM-ICPS provides for 25 Technology Innovation Hubs, constituted as Section-8 companies in host institutes.
7.tq: Use the composition and legal form to identify the correct institutional arrangement.

7.s: Which of the following is NOT a technology vertical mentioned in connection with the NM-ICPS hubs?
7.x: The listed NM-ICPS technology verticals include AI/ML, robotics, cyber security and quantum technologies. Agricultural marketing is not listed among them.
7.tq: Find the option outside the stated set of technology verticals.

7.s: The NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hub associated with IISER Tirupati focuses on
7.x: The IISER Tirupati TIH, IITTNiF, is associated with Positioning and Precision Technologies.
7.tq: Match the host institution with its specific technology vertical.

7.s: The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) was approved by the Union Cabinet in which year and with what outlay?
7.x: NM-ICPS was approved by the Cabinet in 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore (for nine years in current notes; older notes say five), and set up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs. Rs 6,003.65 crore (2023) is the National Quantum Mission, Rs 10,371.92 crore (2024) is the IndiaAI Mission, and 2015 is the year NSM began.
7.tq: ICPS = 2018 + 3,660 crore + 25 TIHs.

7.s: NIDHI, launched in 2016, is an initiative of which department?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
7.x: NIDHI, or National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, was launched in 2016 by the Department of Science and Technology.
7.tq: Direct scheme-and-department recall.

7.s: Which of the following is NOT a component associated with NIDHI?
7.x: NIDHI includes PRAYAS, Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Seed Support System, Technology Business Incubators, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is a separate startup-support programme associated with NCGTC.
7.tq: Find the programme component belonging to another startup scheme.

7.s:
The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme is administered by DPIIT and provides funding for:
1. Proof of concept
2. Prototyping
3. Market entry
4. Regional access to high-end analytical instruments
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme supports proof of concept, prototyping and market entry. Regional access to high-end analytical instruments is the purpose of SAIF, not SISFS.
7.tq: Separate startup financing purposes from DST facility purposes.

7.s: Which organisation is associated with the Fund of Funds for Startups involving ₹10,000 crore?
7.x: The Fund of Funds for Startups, involving ₹10,000 crore, is associated with SIDBI. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is associated with NCGTC.
7.tq: Agency-and-amount discrimination between two startup finance mechanisms.

7.s: TIDE 2.0 is correctly described as:
o: Training Initiative for Digital Enterprises, implemented by DBT for biotechnology scientists
Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs, implemented by MeitY to support ICT and technology start-ups through incubators
Technology Innovation and Development of Education, implemented by DPIIT for school students
Technology Infrastructure Development for Education, implemented by DST for universities
7.x: TIDE 2.0 stands for Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs. It is a MeitY programme launched in 2019 to support ICT and technology start-ups through incubators.
7.tq: Full-form, ministry and target-sector discrimination.

7.s:
Arrange the following initiatives in chronological order of their launch or beginning:
A. TIDE 2.0
B. NIDHI
C. INSPIRE
D. Swarnajayanti Fellowship
7.x: The correct order is Swarnajayanti Fellowship (1997), INSPIRE (2008), NIDHI (2016), and TIDE 2.0 (2019).
7.tq: Use the first and last dates, then place the two middle initiatives.

7.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the components of the Atal Innovation Mission and their focus?
o: Atal Tinkering Labs—start-ups; Atal Incubation Centres—school laboratories; Mentor India—rural infrastructure
Atal Incubation Centres—school students; Atal Community Innovation Centres—large industries; Atal Tinkering Labs—district rankings
Atal Tinkering Labs—schools; Atal Incubation Centres—start-ups; Atal Community Innovation Centres—rural and underserved areas
Atal Community Innovation Centres—urban start-ups; Atal Incubation Centres—basic infrastructure; Mentor India—school examinations
7.x: ATLs operate in schools, AICs support start-ups, and ACICs focus on rural and underserved areas. Mentor India is also a component of AIM.
7.tq: Start from the sure pair linking incubation centres with start-ups.

7.s: Atal Tinkering Labs primarily cater to students of which classes and promote which combination of activities?
o: Undergraduate students, with exclusive training in agricultural marketing
Grades 9–12, with exclusive training in financial accounting
Grades 6–12, with exposure to IoT, 3D printing and robotics
Grades 1–5, with training only in conventional handicrafts
7.x: ATLs are established in schools for students in grades 6–12 and provide exposure to technologies such as IoT, 3D printing and robotics.
7.tq: Match the institution with its target group and operational technologies.

7.s: Atal Innovation Mission is a flagship initiative of
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
7.x: Atal Innovation Mission is a flagship initiative of NITI Aayog.
7.tq: Identify the parent institution rather than a collaborating ministry.

7.s: Atal Innovation Mission was set up in 2016, although it was announced in which Union Budget year?
7.x: AIM was announced in the 2015 Budget and set up in 2016.
7.tq: Separate announcement year from establishment year.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Atal New India Challenges — school grades 6–12 only
7.x: ARISE stands for Atal Research and Innovation for Small Enterprises and is associated with MSMEs. AICs support start-ups, ACICs focus on under-served areas, and Atal New India Challenges address national challenges.
7.tq: Use the component’s target sector to reject neighbouring AIM components.

7.s:
Consider the following components or targets of AIM 2.0:
1. LIPI, involving 30 vernacular innovation centres in 22 scheduled languages
2. 2,500 new Atal Tinkering Labs
3. 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads
4. Deeptech Reactor
Which of the above are associated with AIM 2.0?
7.x: LIPI, 2,500 new ATLs, 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads and the Deeptech Reactor are all associated with AIM 2.0.
7.tq: Prefer the comprehensive option when every listed component belongs to the same initiative.

7.s: Which State was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0?
7.x: Tripura was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0.
7.tq: Use the first-in-series fact to distinguish the state from other innovation leaders.

7.s: Atal Innovation Mission 2.0, approved in 2024, has an outlay of:
7.x: AIM 2.0 has Rs 2,750 crore and runs till March 2028. Rs 500 crore to Rs 3,200 crore is the 2026-27 Budget rise for Atal Tinkering Labs, and Rs 10,000 crore is the SIDBI Fund of Funds for Startups.
7.tq: AIM 2.0 = 2,750 crore, till 2028; 3,200 crore = ATL budget.

7.s: The allocation for Atal Tinkering Labs in the Union Budget 2026–27 rose from:
7.x: The allocation for ATLs increased from ₹500 crore to ₹3,200 crore in the Union Budget 2026–27.
7.tq: Read the paired before-and-after figures together rather than treating them as separate amounts.

7.s: How many Atal Tinkering Labs are reported to be functioning in Andhra Pradesh?
7.x: Andhra Pradesh has 590 Atal Tinkering Labs.
7.tq: Distinguish the Andhra Pradesh figure from the national programme totals.

7.s: Generative-AI assistants are being added to approximately how many Atal Tinkering Labs?
7.x: Generative-AI assistants are being added to 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs.
7.tq: Identify the rounded programme scale associated with the technology upgrade.

7.s: The India-France ATL Bridge was launched at which location during Bharat Innovates 2026?
7.x: The India-France ATL Bridge was launched at Nice during Bharat Innovates 2026.
7.tq: Discriminate between the launch city and other innovation-related locations.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RDI Scheme:
1. It was approved by the Cabinet on 1 July 2025.
2. It provides ₹1 lakh crore over six years.
3. ₹20,000 crore is earmarked for 2025–26.
4. It is steered by the Governing Board of ANRF, with DST as the nodal department.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All four statements correctly describe the RDI Scheme’s approval, funding, first-year allocation and institutional steering arrangement.
7.tq: Combine date, financial allocation and institutional responsibility in one policy question.

7.s: The 8th Youth Co:Lab challenge 2026 is associated with which partnership?
7.x: The 8th Youth Co:Lab challenge 2026 is a UNDP–Atal Innovation Mission initiative.
7.tq: Identify the two partner organisations rather than the mission’s parent body alone.

7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
7.x: Amaravati Quantum Valley is an Andhra Pradesh initiative. IITTNiF is associated with IISER Tirupati, PARAM Shivay with IIT (BHU) Varanasi, and the India-France ATL Bridge was launched at Nice.
7.tq: Use location-based elimination across closely related innovation initiatives.

8.s: Which of the following institutions jointly steers the National Supercomputing Mission?
8.x: The mission is jointly steered by the Department of Science and Technology and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
8.tq: Identify the correct pair of nodal agencies rather than the implementing institutions.

8.s: The supercomputers established under the National Supercomputing Mission are linked through the National Supercomputing Grid over the:
8.x: The systems are linked on the National Supercomputing Grid over the National Knowledge Network.
8.tq: Test the exact network name and reject nearby connectivity terms.

8.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the indigenous technology stack of the National Supercomputing Mission?
o: Rudra server board, Trinetra interconnect and AlmaLinux software
AUM processor, Vajra interconnect and Ubuntu software only
PARAM board, Shakti interconnect and Windows software
Rudra board, Garuda interconnect and proprietary software exclusively
8.x: The indigenous stack comprises the Rudra server board, Trinetra interconnect and open-source AlmaLinux software.
8.tq: Match the technical components as a complete stack and beware of the ‘exclusively’ trap.

8.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (System)
 a. PARAM Shivay
 b. PARAM Porul
 c. PARAM Pravega
 d. PARAM Ananta

List-II (Host)
 i. IISc Bengaluru
 ii. IIT Gandhinagar
 iii. IIT (BHU)
 iv. NIT Tiruchirappalli

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
8.x: PARAM Shivay is at IIT (BHU), PARAM Porul at NIT Tiruchirappalli, PARAM Pravega at IISc Bengaluru and PARAM Ananta at IIT Gandhinagar.
8.tq: Start from the sure machine–host pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong pair.

8.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
8.x: PARAM Kamrupa is hosted at IIT Guwahati. PARAM Shakti is at IIT Madras, PARAM Rudra systems are at Pune, Delhi and Kolkata, and AIRAWAT is at C-DAC, Pune.
8.tq: Find the correctly matched pair among closely related supercomputing hosts.

8.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Rudra server from the AUM programme?
o: AUM is the interconnect used in all PARAM systems, whereas Rudra is a software platform.
Rudra is a server board used for the mission, whereas AUM is a separate C-DAC HPC chip programme.
Rudra is an HPC chip programme, whereas AUM is the mission’s open-source operating system.
Both Rudra and AUM are names of the same processor.
8.x: The Rudra machines are built on the Rudra server, while AUM is a separate C-DAC high-performance computing chip programme.
8.tq: Discriminate between look-alike technical names by identifying their different functions.

8.s: AIRAWAT, the artificial-intelligence supercomputer associated with the National Supercomputing Mission, is located at:
8.x: AIRAWAT is located at C-DAC, Pune.
8.tq: Test the host institution of a named machine rather than its ranking.

8.s: India’s supercomputing programme began in the:
8.x: India’s supercomputing programme began in the late 1980s.
8.tq: Distinguish the programme’s beginning from the launch of a particular machine.

8.s: Vijay Bhatkar is associated with which description?
o: Architect of the Deep Ocean Mission
Founder of India’s quantum communication mission
Chairperson of the ANRF Governing Board
8.x: Vijay Bhatkar is recognised as the father of Indian supercomputing.
8.tq: Match the personality with the precise title used in the field.

8.s:
Match the Indian supercomputer with its developer or site:

List-I
 a. Flosolver
 b. Anupam
 c. Pratyush
 d. Mihir

List-II
 i. NCMRWF, Noida
 ii. NAL Bengaluru
 iii. BARC
 iv. IITM Pune

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

8.tq: Start with a sure site association and verify that no List-II item is reused.

8.s: Which of the following is regarded as the first National Supercomputing Mission machine assembled in India?
8.x: PARAM Shivay is identified as the first National Supercomputing Mission machine assembled in India.
8.tq: Separate the 'first Indian supercomputer' fact from the distinct 'first NSM machine assembled in India' fact.

8.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Quantum Mission?
o: A MeitY mission with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore for 2024–29
A DBT mission with an outlay of ₹4,077 crore for five years
A MoES mission with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore for 2021–26
A DST mission with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023–24 to 2030–31
8.x: The mission is under DST, has an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore and covers eight years from 2023–24 to 2030–31.
8.tq: Compare mission ministry, outlay and period together to avoid cross-matching with other missions.

8.s: The National Quantum Mission aims to develop intermediate-scale quantum computers containing approximately:
8.x: The target is intermediate-scale computers with 50 to 1000 physical qubits within eight years.
8.tq: Use the exact numerical range and distinguish physical qubits from logical qubits.

8.s:
Which of the following are targets or technological areas of the National Quantum Mission?
1. Satellite QKD over 2000 km within India
2. Inter-city QKD over 2000 km
3. Quantum links with other countries
4. Development of magnetometers and atomic clocks
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
8.x: All four listed areas form part of the National Quantum Mission’s targets and technological objectives.
8.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying every listed application.

8.s:
Match the thematic hub of the National Quantum Mission with its host:

List-I (Thematic hub)
 a. Quantum Computing
 b. Quantum Communication
 c. Quantum Sensing and Metrology
 d. Quantum Materials and Devices

List-II (Host)
 i. IIT Delhi
 ii. IIT Bombay
 iii. IISc Bengaluru
 iv. IIT Madras

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

8.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a start-up supported under the National Quantum Mission?
o: QNu Labs — 500 km QKD network and QShield
8.x: QNu Labs is associated with a 500 km QKD network and QShield. QpiAI is associated with a 64-qubit QPU, PQuest with a Quantum Diamond Microscope, and Prenishq with a diode laser.
8.tq: Use the one-correct-pair method for start-up and technology associations.

8.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bio-E3 Policy (2024):
1. Bio-E3 stands for Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Energy.
2. Its core objective is to build a bio-manufacturing ecosystem.
3. DBT's next plans include biomanufacturing hubs, biofoundries and 'Moolankur' hubs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the third E is Employment (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment), not Energy. Statement 2 is correct: the core aim is a bio-manufacturing ecosystem. Statement 3 is correct: DBT plans biomanufacturing hubs, biofoundries and Moolankur hubs. So '2 and 3 only'; the other options include statement 1.
8.tq: E3 = Economy, Environment, Employment - no Energy.

8.s: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over which amount in 2024?
8.x: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over US$165 billion in 2024.
8.tq: Recall the exact scale figure and distinguish it from public-sector mission outlays.

8.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a thematic sector of the Bio-E3 Policy?
8.x: Inter-city quantum key distribution is a National Quantum Mission objective, not a Bio-E3 thematic sector. The other three are listed Bio-E3 sectors.
8.tq: Find the sector borrowed from a neighbouring science mission.

8.s: Biopharma SHAKTI, announced in Budget 2026–27, involves an outlay of:
8.x: Biopharma SHAKTI has an outlay of ₹10,000 crore over five years and concerns biologics and biosimilars.
8.tq: Separate the policy’s budgetary initiative from the outlays of other national missions.

8.s: Who is the ex officio President of the Governing Board of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation?
o: The Union Minister of Science and Technology
8.x: The Prime Minister is the ex officio President of the ANRF Governing Board.
8.tq: Identify the office-holder by constitutional or statutory position, not by ministerial association.

8.s: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation subsumed which institution?
8.x: ANRF subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board, or SERB.
8.tq: Discriminate between a predecessor research body and mission advisory or implementing bodies.

8.s: The ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund is associated with the ANRF through a:
8.x: ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund through a two-tier Special Purpose Fund.
8.tq: Combine the fund amount with its institutional mechanism.

8.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as an ANRF scheme?
8.x: PAIR, MAHA-EV and the JC Bose Grant are listed ANRF schemes. Matsya 6000 Fellowship is not listed as an ANRF scheme.
8.tq: Identify the unrelated programme by comparing scheme names across missions.

8.s: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), which subsumed SERB, derives its legal basis from:
o: The Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008
8.x: ANRF was set up under the ANRF Act, 2023 and subsumed SERB. SERB itself was created by a 2008 Act, which is why that option is a trap. The 2019 ordinance and the 2025 Act are made up; 2025 is the year of the RDI Scheme, not of a statute.
8.tq: ANRF = Act of 2023; PM heads its Governing Board.

8.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the two Quantum Test and Reference Facilities in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 1S at SRM University-AP and 1Q at Medha Towers, Gannavaram
1S at IIT Hyderabad and 1Q at Amaravati Secretariat
1Q at SRM University-AP and 1S at Medha Towers, Gannavaram
8.x: The 1S test bed is at SRM University-AP and the 1Q facility is at Medha Towers in Gannavaram.
8.tq: Separate similar facility codes by matching each code with its precise location.

8.s: India's first Quantum Test and Reference Facilities in Andhra Pradesh were launched on:
8.x: The facilities were launched on 14 April 2026, observed as World Quantum Day.
8.tq: Distinguish the exact launch year and date from nearby policy years.

8.s:
Which of the following combinations was associated with the seven MoUs signed in February 2026?
1. UNICC Centre of Excellence
2. IBM training one lakh youth
3. A NIELIT Quantum AI deemed university
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
8.x: The seven MoUs included a UNICC Centre of Excellence, IBM's training initiative for one lakh youth and a NIELIT Quantum AI deemed university.
8.tq: Recognise a complete set of related MoU outcomes rather than selecting a partial combination.

8.s: The Quantum Valley project is associated with which national mission?
8.x: The Quantum Valley project has 50 acres under the National Quantum Mission.
8.tq: Match the specialised technology project with the correct national mission.

8.s: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at which of the following places?
8.x: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at Uddandarayunipalem.
8.tq: Use the location-based direct-recall method and distinguish the foundation site from associated facilities.

8.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly identifies the institutions whose components were used in India's first Quantum Reference Facility test beds?
o: TIFR, ISRO, DRDO and IIT Madras
ISRO, CSIR, BARC and IIT Delhi
IISc, CSIR, BARC and IIT Bombay
TIFR, IISc, DRDO and IIT Bombay
8.x: The test beds incorporated components from TIFR, IISc, DRDO and IIT Bombay.
8.tq: Discriminate among closely related scientific institutions by checking the complete institutional combination.

8.s:
Consider the following statements about incentives and human-resource development in the Amaravati Quantum Valley:
1. Technology firms in the Valley are eligible for 100% exemption from stamp duty and registration fees.
2. Andhra Pradesh plans to train 4.5 million people in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies.
3. The exemption applies only to registration fees and not to stamp duty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: The policy provides 100% exemption from both stamp duty and registration fees, and the plan includes training 4.5 million people in AI and quantum technologies. Statement 3 incorrectly excludes stamp duty.
8.tq: Split the paired financial terms and identify the statement that reverses the scope of the exemption.

8.s: The NIELIT Quantum and AI campus at Amaravati is being established by which Ministry, with classes scheduled to begin from September 2026 at which institution?
o: Ministry of Science and Technology; SRM University-AP
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology; Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur
Ministry of Education; Andhra University, Visakhapatnam
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; IIT Tirupati
8.x: The campus is associated with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, and classes are scheduled from September 2026 at Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur.
8.tq: Use the 'which ministry and which institution?' two-part discrimination method.

8.s: Which State became the first in India to have a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to be among the top five global quantum hubs by 2030?
8.x: Andhra Pradesh is the first State with a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to make the Amaravati Quantum Valley one of the top five global quantum hubs by 2030. The notes record no such policy for Karnataka, Telangana or Tamil Nadu.
8.tq: First quantum policy = AP (Amaravati Quantum Valley).

8.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a mission with its ministry and outlay?
8.x: The IndiaAI Mission is under MeitY with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore. Semicon India is under MeitY with ₹76,000 crore, NQM is under DST with ₹6,003.65 crore, and NM-ICPS is under DST.
8.tq: Match all three dimensions—mission, ministry and outlay—before selecting the pair.

8.s: The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) was approved in 2018 under DST with how many Technology Innovation Hubs?
8.x: NM-ICPS was approved in 2018 under DST and provides for 25 Technology Innovation Hubs.
8.tq: Link the mission’s approval year and ministry with its distinctive hub count.

8.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the National Geospatial Mission?
o: DST through Survey of India — Budget 2025–26 — runs till 2031
8.x: The National Geospatial Mission is associated with DST through the Survey of India, appears in Budget 2025–26 and runs till 2031.
8.tq: Match the implementing authority, budget year and duration as a three-part combination.

8.s: India-Germany cooperation in quantum and deep technology is being pursued through which combination of institutions?
8.x: India-Germany quantum and deep-tech cooperation is being pursued through the Indo-German Science and Technology Centre (IGSTC) and the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF).
8.tq: Identify the correct institutional partners instead of substituting nearby research or technology bodies.

8.s: India's first supercomputer, developed by C-DAC in 1991, was:
8.x: PARAM 8000 (1991) was built by C-DAC under Vijay Bhatkar and was India's first supercomputer. PARAM Shivay (2019) was the first NSM machine, Anupam is a BARC machine, and AIRAWAT is the later AI supercomputer at C-DAC Pune.
8.tq: First supercomputer = PARAM 8000; first NSM system = PARAM Shivay.

9.s: J.C. Bose invented which instrument to measure plant growth?
9.x: J.C. Bose invented the crescograph to measure plant growth.
9.tq: Identify the instrument from its specific biological application.

9.s: J.C. Bose was a pioneer in microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and used which of the following components?
9.x: J.C. Bose pioneered microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and worked with a coherer and a galena semiconductor detector.
9.tq: Match the scientist’s research area with the characteristic apparatus associated with it.

9.s: Which one of the following is a book written by J.C. Bose?
o: The Mathematical Theory of Black Holes
9.x: The Nervous Mechanism of Plants was written by J.C. Bose. His other listed works include Response in the Living and Non-Living and the Bengali science-fiction work Niruddesher Kahini.
9.tq: Distinguish the scientist’s own book from works associated with other disciplines or authors.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about J.C. Bose:
1. He showed that plants respond to stimuli like animals.
2. He founded the Bose Institute, Kolkata, in 1917.
3. He formulated the theory of thermal ionisation of elements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bose showed that plants respond to stimuli, the 'plants have life' idea. Statement 2 is correct: he founded the Bose Institute in Kolkata in 1917. Statement 3 is wrong: thermal ionisation (the Saha equation) is Meghnad Saha's work. So the answer is '1 and 2 only'.
9.tq: J.C. Bose = plants have life + crescograph + Bose Institute 1917.

9.s: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked at Cambridge with which mathematician?
9.x: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked with the British mathematician G.H. Hardy at Cambridge.
9.tq: Identify the collaborator from a set of scientists connected with different fields.

9.s: Which of the following subjects is NOT associated with Ramanujan’s mathematical work?
9.x: Thermal ionisation of elements is associated with Meghnad Saha. Ramanujan worked on number theory, partitions, infinite series, continued fractions and mock theta functions.
9.tq: Find the odd field among several genuine areas of the scientist’s work.

9.s: The number 1729 is popularly known as the:
9.x: The number 1729 is known as the Hardy-Ramanujan number.
9.tq: Recognise a famous numerical association rather than a date or institutional fact.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about Srinivasa Ramanujan:
1. His birthday, 22 December, is observed as National Mathematics Day.
2. 2012 was observed as National Mathematical Year to mark his 150th birth anniversary.
3. The biopic 'The Man Who Knew Infinity' is based on his life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: he was born on 22 December 1887, and that date is National Mathematics Day. Statement 2 is wrong: 2012 marked his 125th birth anniversary, not his 150th. Statement 3 is correct: 'The Man Who Knew Infinity' is the biopic on him (UPSC 2016). So the answer is '1 and 3 only'.
9.tq: Born 1887, so 2012 = 125th anniversary; 22 Dec = Maths Day.

9.s: The Raman Effect was discovered by C.V. Raman on 28 February 1928 at which institution?
o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata
9.x: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in Kolkata.
9.tq: Link the exact date of a discovery with its location and institution.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about C.V. Raman:
1. He founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934.
2. He founded the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru in 1948.
3. He was the first Indian director of the Indian Institute of Science.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Raman founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948, and became the first Indian director of the Indian Institute of Science.
9.tq: Check a chronological institutional career through multiple statements.

9.s: Which of the following musical instruments did C.V. Raman study in relation to their harmonic nature?
9.x: C.V. Raman was the first to study the harmonic nature of the tabla and mridangam.
9.tq: Distinguish a less commonly remembered contribution from the scientist’s better-known optical work.

9.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Indian scientific institutions in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Raman Research Institute
B. Establishment of the Indian Academy of Sciences
C. Establishment of the Bose Institute
D. Establishment of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research
9.x: The Bose Institute was founded in 1917, the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934, TIFR in 1945 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948.
9.tq: Arrange institutions by their foundation years, using the earliest and latest events first.

9.s: National Science Day is observed in India on 28 February to commemorate:
o: The birth anniversary of Homi J. Bhabha
The founding of the Indian Institute of Science
The discovery of the Raman Effect by C.V. Raman
The launch of India's first satellite, Aryabhata
9.x: C.V. Raman announced the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 at IACS, Kolkata, and that date is now National Science Day. The day is not linked to Bhabha's birth, the founding of IISc or the launch of Aryabhata (1975).
9.tq: 28 Feb = Raman Effect (1928) = National Science Day.

9.s: The Saha equation was formulated by Meghnad Saha from his theory of:
9.x: Meghnad Saha formulated the Saha, or ionisation, equation from his theory of thermal ionisation of elements.
9.tq: Link an equation to the theory from which it was derived.

9.s: The Saha equation is a basic tool for reading stellar spectra because it helps determine the:
o: Distance and magnetic field of oceans
Temperature and ionisation state of stars
Age and chemical composition of plants
Mass and rotation of planets only
9.x: The Saha equation helps interpret stellar spectra by indicating the temperature and ionisation state of stars.
9.tq: Apply the scientific equation to the observational problem it is used to solve.

9.s: Which statement best describes Meghnad Saha’s contribution to river planning in India?
o: He prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.
He designed the first irrigation project on the Krishna River.
He founded the first river-water tribunal in India.
He established the Central Water Commission.
9.x: Meghnad Saha was regarded as the chief architect of river planning in India and prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.
9.tq: Match a national development project with the scientist associated with its original plan.

9.s:
Meghnad Saha founded which of the following institutions?
1. Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, Kolkata
2. National Academy of Sciences, India, in 1930
3. Bose Institute, Kolkata
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Meghnad Saha founded the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics at Kolkata and the National Academy of Sciences, India, in 1930. The Bose Institute was founded by J.C. Bose.
9.tq: Separate institutions founded by two scientists working in related scientific fields.

9.s: S. N. Bose sent his paper entitled “Planck’s Law and the Hypothesis of Light Quanta” to which scientist?
9.x: S. N. Bose sent the paper to Albert Einstein, who translated it into German and arranged its publication.
9.tq: Identify the collaborator directly associated with the named paper.

9.s: Bose–Einstein statistics is associated with the work of which scientist?
9.x: Bose–Einstein statistics emerged from S. N. Bose’s work on the statistical treatment of light quanta.
9.tq: Use the scientist’s name embedded in the technical term while distinguishing J. C. Bose from S. N. Bose.

9.s: The term “bosons” was named after S. N. Bose by which scientist?
9.x: Paul Dirac named the class of particles called bosons after S. N. Bose.
9.tq: Apply the who-named-what pattern without confusing the collaborator Einstein with the namer Dirac.

9.s: Rabindranath Tagore dedicated his only science book, *Visva-Parichay*, to:
9.x: Rabindranath Tagore dedicated *Visva-Parichay*, published in 1937, to S. N. Bose.
9.tq: Link the literary work, its year and its dedicatee rather than its scientific subject.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bose–Einstein Condensate:
1. It is described as the fifth state of matter.
2. It has been observed in space through NASA experiments on the International Space Station.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
9.x: Both statements are correct. Bose–Einstein Condensate is described as the fifth state of matter, and NASA experiments on the ISS observed it in space.
9.tq: Combine the definition and application statements, checking whether both parts belong to the same concept.

9.s: Homi Bhabha is popularly known as the:
9.x: Homi Bhabha is known as the Father of India's nuclear programme.
9.tq: Recall the distinctive title associated with a national scientific programme.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Atomic Energy Commission — First chairman, Homi Bhabha, 1948
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre — Founded by Homi Bhabha in 1945
9.x: The Atomic Energy Establishment at Trombay was founded in 1954 and was renamed BARC after Homi Bhabha's death in 1966. It was not founded as BARC in 1945.
9.tq: Find the institution-year statement that reverses the original name and later renaming.

9.s: Who was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission of India?
9.x: Homi Bhabha was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission in 1948.
9.tq: Identify the correct authority-holder in an institutional leadership question.

9.s: Homi Bhabha’s three-stage nuclear power programme was conceived as a:
9.x: Homi Bhabha conceived India's three-stage nuclear power programme as a thorium-based programme.
9.tq: Connect a national programme with its underlying resource base.

9.s:
Which of the following contributions is associated with Homi Bhabha?
1. Bhabha scattering involving electrons and positrons
2. Cascade theory of cosmic-ray showers
3. Development of the Saha ionisation equation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Bhabha scattering and the cascade theory of cosmic-ray showers are associated with Homi Bhabha. The Saha ionisation equation was formulated by Meghnad Saha.
9.tq: Use a nearby-scientist substitution as the false statement in a specialised-work question.

9.s: Homi Bhabha died in which incident and in which year?
o: A laboratory accident in Trombay in 1954
An air crash over the Alps in 1948
A mountaineering accident in Geneva in 1955
An air crash on Mont Blanc in 1966
9.x: Homi Bhabha died in an Air India crash on Mont Blanc in 1966.
9.tq: Test the distinctive event-location-year combination rather than the scientist’s general field.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about early Indian women scientists:
1. Anandibai Joshi was the first Indian woman to earn a degree in Western medicine (MD, 1886).
2. Kamala Sohonie was the first woman admitted to the Indian Institute of Science.
3. Kamala Sohonie was the first woman to obtain a D.Sc. from an Indian university.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: Anandibai Joshi took an MD from the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania in 1886. Statement 2 is correct: Kamala Sohonie was the first woman admitted to IISc. Statement 3 is wrong: the first woman D.Sc. from an Indian university was Asima Chatterjee (Calcutta, 1944); Sohonie's first was a science PhD (Cambridge, 1939). So '1 and 2 only'.
9.tq: Sohonie = first PhD (Cambridge 1939); Asima Chatterjee = first D.Sc. (Calcutta 1944).

9.s:
With reference to Janaki Ammal, consider the following statements:
1. She pioneered plant breeding and worked on sugarcane hybrids at Coimbatore.
2. She co-authored the book Chromosome Atlas of Cultivated Plants.
3. She was awarded the Padma Shri in 1977.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Janaki Ammal was a botanist and cytogeneticist associated with plant breeding, sugarcane hybrids, the cited book and the Padma Shri of 1977.
9.tq: Combine several precise biographical facts and test whether all statements belong to the same scientist.

9.s:
With reference to Asima Chatterjee, consider the following statements:
1. She was the first woman to obtain a D.Sc. from an Indian university.
2. She developed Ayush-56 as an anti-malarial drug.
3. She was the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statement 1 is correct: she got a D.Sc. from Calcutta University in 1944, the first woman to do so. Statement 2 is wrong: Ayush-56 is an anti-epileptic drug; her anti-malarial work was separate. Statement 3 is correct: she was the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress (1975). So '1 and 3 only'.
9.tq: Ayush-56 = anti-epileptic, not anti-malarial.

9.s: Anna Mani is popularly known as the ‘Weather Woman of India’ primarily because of her work in which field?
o: Meteorological instruments, solar radiation and wind energy
Cosmic rays, mesons and particle detectors
9.x: Anna Mani contributed to making India self-reliant in meteorological instruments and worked on solar radiation and wind energy. She also served as Deputy Director-General of the India Meteorological Department.
9.tq: Infer the field from the descriptive title and the associated applications.

9.s: Which of the following statements regarding Bibha Chowdhuri is correct?
o: She pioneered plant breeding at Coimbatore.
She founded the Bose Institute at Kolkata.
She formulated the equation of thermal ionisation.
She worked on cosmic rays and mesons with D.M. Bose.
9.x: Bibha Chowdhuri worked on cosmic rays and mesons with D.M. Bose and completed her Ph.D. under P.M.S. Blackett. The star HD 86081 was named ‘Bibha’ by the IAU in 2019.
9.tq: Eliminate options by matching each scientist with the specialised field stated in the question.

9.s: Who was the first Indian woman to obtain a PhD in a science discipline (Cambridge, 1939)?
9.x: Kamala Sohonie, a biochemist, earned her PhD from Cambridge in 1939 and was also the first woman admitted to IISc. Asima Chatterjee was the first woman to get a D.Sc. from an Indian university (Calcutta, 1944). Janaki Ammal was a pioneer of plant breeding, and Anna Mani is known as the 'Weather Woman of India'.
9.tq: Sohonie = first science PhD; Chatterjee = first D.Sc.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: S.N. Bose — Quantum statistics and bosons
Birbal Sahni — Engineering and Diwan of Mysore
9.x: S.N. Bose is associated with quantum statistics and bosons. Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in chemistry, Birbal Sahni in palaeobotany, and Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar with CSIR.
9.tq: Match scientists with their areas while rejecting swapped specialised fields.

9.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?
o: C.V. Raman — Light scattering and acoustics
Ramanujan — Nuclear physics and cosmic rays
9.x: C.V. Raman worked on light scattering, optics and acoustics. J.C. Bose worked on plant physiology and radio or microwave physics, S.N. Bose on quantum statistics, and Ramanujan on number theory.
9.tq: Use area-based elimination to separate scientists whose names and fields are easily confused.

9.s: M. Visvesvaraya served as the Diwan of Mysore during which period?
9.x: M. Visvesvaraya, associated with engineering, served as the Diwan of Mysore from 1912 to 1919.
9.tq: Identify the correct range from closely spaced chronological options.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the honours received by C. V. Raman?
o: Nobel Prize in 1930, Bharat Ratna in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
Nobel Prize in 1954, Bharat Ratna in 1929 and knighthood in 1930
Nobel Prize in 1929, Bharat Ratna in 1930 and knighthood in 1954
FRS in 1930, Padma Bhushan in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
9.x: C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in 1930, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954 and was knighted in 1929.
9.tq: Use the exact year-and-honour combination to avoid swapped-date traps.

9.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. J. C. Bose — Knighthood in 1917 and FRS in 1920
2. Srinivasa Ramanujan — FRS in 1918
3. Meghnad Saha — FRS in 1927
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
9.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. J. C. Bose was knighted in 1917 and became an FRS in 1920; Ramanujan and Meghnad Saha became FRS in 1918 and 1927 respectively.
9.tq: Check each person against the associated honour and year before selecting the combined code.

9.s:
With reference to Homi Bhabha and S. N. Bose, consider the following statements:
1. Homi Bhabha became an FRS in 1941.
2. Homi Bhabha received the Padma Bhushan in 1954.
3. S. N. Bose received the Padma Vibhushan in 1954.
4. S. N. Bose became an FRS in 1958.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All four statements are correct. Bhabha received the FRS in 1941 and Padma Bhushan in 1954, while S. N. Bose received Padma Vibhushan in 1954 and FRS in 1958.
9.tq: Treat a multi-person honour list as separate statements and verify every year.

9.s: The Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Kolkata, was founded in 1876 by:
9.x: IACS was founded in Kolkata in 1876 by Mahendra Lal Sircar.
9.tq: Match the institution with its founder and founding year.

9.s: Which one of the following best describes the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science?
o: A university founded by Tagore for literary and scientific studies
A nuclear research centre established by Homi Bhabha and funded exclusively by the Union Government
The oldest institute for basic research, funded by the Department of Science and Technology and the Government of West Bengal
The oldest Indian space agency, funded exclusively by NASA
9.x: IACS is described as the oldest institute for basic research and is funded by the Department of Science and Technology and the Government of West Bengal.
9.tq: Separate the institution’s function and funding bodies from nearby scientific institutions and organisations.

9.s: Which of the following groups of scientists is associated with work at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science?
o: V. Raman, Homi Bhabha, Tagore and Mahendra Lal Sircar only
Homi Bhabha, Albert Einstein, Paul Dirac and Ramanujan
J. C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S. N. Bose and C. V. Raman
Ramanujan, Einstein, Saha and NASA scientists only
9.x: J. C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S. N. Bose and C. V. Raman all worked at IACS.
9.tq: Identify the complete institutional association instead of selecting a partly overlapping group.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the 'Matilda effect' debate in Indian science:
1. It refers to women scientists being left out of public memory.
2. Janaki Ammal and Anna Mani are cited as examples.
3. IACS, Kolkata, revives such scientists through its India@75 series.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Matilda effect is the leaving out of women scientists such as Janaki Ammal and Anna Mani from public memory. Statement 3 is wrong: the India@75 series that revives them is from the National Book Trust (NBT) India, not IACS. So '1 and 2 only'.
9.tq: India@75 revival series = NBT, not IACS.

10.s: Which of the following statements about Vikram Sarabhai is correct?
o: He became Chairman of ISRO only after the launch of Aryabhata in 1975.
He headed INCOSPAR in 1962 and was the first Chairman of ISRO until his death in 1971.
He founded ISRO in 1947 and chaired it until 1980.
10.x: Sarabhai headed INCOSPAR from 1962; it became ISRO in 1969, and he served as ISRO’s first Chairman until his death in 1971.
10.tq: Distinguish the predecessor organisation, its conversion into ISRO and the correct tenure dates.

10.s: Which institution was founded by Vikram Sarabhai in Ahmedabad in 1947?
10.x: Vikram Sarabhai founded the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad in 1947. The Community Science Centre was established in 1965, while TERLS was set up near Thiruvananthapuram.
10.tq: Use the founding year and location to distinguish among institutions associated with Sarabhai.

10.s: The Satellite Instructional Television Experiment associated with Vikram Sarabhai provided television education to approximately:
10.x: SITE was conducted during 1975–76 and provided television education to approximately 2,400 villages.
10.tq: Combine the programme’s acronym, period and scale to avoid number and date swaps.

10.s: The facility formerly known as the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station is now known as:
10.x: The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station was renamed the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre at Thiruvananthapuram.
10.tq: Identify the renamed facility by linking its original and present names.

10.s: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal was constituted in 1990 for:
o: Scientists working exclusively in marine biology
10.x: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal, constituted in 1990 by COSPAR and ISRO, recognises space scientists from developing countries.
10.tq: Read the eligibility phrase precisely and avoid the trap of restricting the medal to one country or one unrelated discipline.

10.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is associated with which of the following scientific discoveries?
o: Development of the first artificial satellite
Atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
Structure of the DNA double helix
10.x: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is known for determining the atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit, which provided insight into protein synthesis.
10.tq: Use the scientist–discovery association and distinguish ribosomal research from unrelated landmark discoveries.

10.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009 jointly with:
o: Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg
Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath
10.x: The 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath for studies of the ribosome.
10.tq: Test the exact co-laureates rather than confusing them with laureates in medicine or agriculture.

10.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is correct?
o: He served as President of the Royal Society from 2015 to 2020.
He served as President of the Royal Society from 2003 to 2010.
He was knighted in 2003 immediately after becoming an FRS.
He received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2014.
10.x: Ramakrishnan was President of the Royal Society during 2015–2020. He became an FRS in 2003, was knighted in 2012 and received the Nobel Prize in 2009.
10.tq: Separate closely spaced years and distinguish the Royal Society presidency from other honours.

10.s: Har Gobind Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize with:
o: Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath
Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg
10.x: Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg.
10.tq: Discriminate between two Nobel-related groups by matching the correct co-laureates to the correct scientist.

10.s: Which of the following best describes the work for which Har Gobind Khorana received the Nobel Prize?
o: Interpreting the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis
Determining the atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
Discovering the structure of the neutron
10.x: Khorana was recognised for interpreting the genetic code and explaining its role in protein synthesis.
10.tq: Distinguish closely related molecular-biology contributions by identifying the precise wording of the achievement.

10.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, winner of the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, was born at:
10.x: Ramakrishnan was born at Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu (asked in APPSC-GS 2012). Erode is Ramanujan's birthplace and Bhimavaram is Yellapragada SubbaRow's. Raipur appears in the notes for neither.
10.tq: Ramakrishnan = Chidambaram; Ramanujan = Erode.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about M.S. Swaminathan:
1. He was associated with the development of high-yielding dwarf varieties of wheat and rice.
2. He chaired the National Commission on Farmers.
3. He founded the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation in Chennai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
