10.x: All three statements are correct. Swaminathan was associated with high-yielding dwarf crops, chaired the National Commission on Farmers and founded MSSRF in Chennai.
10.tq: Combine agricultural contribution, commission and institution facts in a coded statement question.

10.s: M.S. Swaminathan received the first World Food Prize in:
10.x: M.S. Swaminathan received the first World Food Prize in 1987.
10.tq: Distinguish the award year from the years of his other honours and institutional activities.

10.s: M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024:
o: during his lifetime for literary contributions
during his lifetime for work in space science
posthumously for his contribution to agriculture
posthumously for work in nuclear physics
10.x: M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 for his contribution to agriculture.
10.tq: Read the qualification carefully and distinguish posthumous recognition from a lifetime award.

10.s: M.S. Swaminathan was described by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) as the:
10.x: UNEP called M.S. Swaminathan the 'Father of Economic Ecology' (UPPSC 2007). He is the architect of India's Green Revolution. The Blue Revolution is fisheries and the White Revolution is milk (linked to Verghese Kurien), and 'Father of Green Chemistry' is not his title.
10.tq: Swaminathan: UNEP = Father of Economic Ecology; first World Food Prize 1987.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes A.P.J. Abdul Kalam’s role in India’s space programme?
o: Founder of the Physical Research Laboratory at Ahmedabad
Project director of SLV-3, which placed Rohini in orbit in 1980
Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission during Aryabhata’s launch
Director of SITE for the transmission of programmes to 2,400 villages
10.x: Abdul Kalam was the project director of SLV-3, which placed the Rohini satellite in orbit in 1980.
10.tq: Match the scientist with the precise project role and reject roles belonging to Sarabhai or other programmes.

10.s: Which of the following missile programmes was led by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
10.x: Kalam led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme, associated with missiles such as Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Trishul and Nag.
10.tq: Identify the correct programme from a group of nearby scientific and developmental initiatives.

10.s: Which of the following is the correct set of books associated with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
o: Wings of Fire, Ignited Minds and India 2020
Agriculture Cannot Wait, India 2020 and The History of Indian Agriculture
Wings of Fire, An Equal Music and India 2020
Ignited Minds, The Discovery of India and Wings of Fire
10.x: Wings of Fire, Ignited Minds and India 2020 are associated with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
10.tq: Use a complete-set question and eliminate books associated with agriculture, fiction or other authors.

10.s:
Arrange the following events associated with India’s space and nuclear programmes in chronological order:
A. Pokhran-II
B. Launch of Rohini by SLV-3
C. Renaming of Wheeler Island as Abdul Kalam Island
D. Abdul Kalam’s term as President of India begins
10.x: The correct order is SLV-3 placing Rohini in orbit in 1980, Pokhran-II in 1998, the beginning of Kalam’s presidency in 2002 and the renaming in 2015.
10.tq: Place the anchor years first: 1980, 1998, 2002 and 2015.

10.s: In 2006, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam became the first President of India to fly in a fighter aircraft. Which aircraft was it?
10.x: In 2006, Kalam, India's 11th President (2002-2007), flew in a Sukhoi-30 MKI and became the first President to fly a fighter (RPSC 2007). The MiG-21, Mirage 2000 and Tejas are other IAF fighters, but none of them is linked to this first.
10.tq: Kalam: 11th President, Sukhoi-30 MKI 2006, Missile Man.

10.s: C.N.R. Rao is primarily associated with:
10.x: C.N.R. Rao is one of the foremost scientists in solid-state and materials chemistry, including structural chemistry.
10.tq: Use the scientist–field association and distinguish chemistry from biological and engineering disciplines.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about C.N.R. Rao:
1. He received the Bharat Ratna in 2014.
2. He headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.
3. He received the Energy Frontiers Award.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: All three statements are correct. C.N.R. Rao received the Bharat Ratna in 2014, headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister and received the Energy Frontiers Award.
10.tq: Combine award, advisory and scientific-recognition facts in a complete coded statement set.

10.s: Who led Pokhran-I in 1974?
10.x: Raja Ramanna led Pokhran-I in 1974 and was associated with BARC.
10.tq: Match the nuclear test with the scientist who led it, avoiding confusion with Pokhran-II.

10.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anil Kakodkar — Atomic Energy Commission; Advanced Heavy Water Reactor
Tessy Thomas — ISRO; Aryabhata satellite team
U.R. Rao — DRDO; Agni-IV project director
Raja Ramanna — ISRO; drafting committee of NEP 2020
10.x: Anil Kakodkar was associated with the Atomic Energy Commission and the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor. Tessy Thomas was associated with DRDO, U.R. Rao with ISRO and Raja Ramanna with BARC.
10.tq: Use organisation–contribution matching and identify the swapped institutions in the distractors.

10.s: K. Kasturirangan is associated with which of the following roles?
o: Chairman of ISRO and chair of the drafting committee of NEP 2020
Chairman of BARC and leader of Pokhran-I
Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission and developer of the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor
Director of DRDO and project director of Agni-IV
10.x: K. Kasturirangan served as ISRO Chairman from 1994 to 2003 and chaired the drafting committee of NEP 2020.
10.tq: Combine the institutional position and later policy role to distinguish Kasturirangan from other modern scientists.

10.s: Tessy Thomas is popularly known as the “Missile Woman” because she was associated with:
o: The Agni-IV project as its project director
The Rohini satellite as its project director
10.x: Tessy Thomas of DRDO was the project director of Agni-IV and is popularly known as the “Missile Woman.”
10.tq: Match the popular title with the precise project and organisation.

10.s: Satish Dhawan is associated with which of the following developments?
o: The drafting of NEP 2020 and ISRO chairmanship from 1994 to 2003
The leadership of Pokhran-I and BARC
The launch of Aryabhata and renaming of SHAR as Satish Dhawan Space Centre
10.x: Satish Dhawan was associated with the launch of Aryabhata, and SHAR was renamed the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
10.tq: Use the organisation and contribution together to separate Dhawan from other space and defence scientists.

10.s: Yellapragada SubbaRow, associated with important contributions to biochemistry and medicine, was born at which place?
10.x: Yellapragada SubbaRow was born at Bhimavaram. Guntur district is associated with Yelavarthy Nayudamma.
10.tq: Use the birthplace distinction between the two scientists from Andhra Pradesh.

10.s: The Fiske–SubbaRow method is associated with the study of the role of which substances in muscle?
10.x: Yellapragada SubbaRow contributed to understanding the role of ATP and phosphocreatine in muscle through the Fiske–SubbaRow method.
10.tq: Match the named method with its specific scientific contribution rather than with another contribution of the same scientist.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about Yellapragada SubbaRow:
1. He contributed to the synthesis of folic acid.
2. He was associated with the development of the anti-cancer drug methotrexate.
3. He was associated with the first tetracycline, aureomycin.
4. He was associated with the anti-filarial drug Hetrazan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: All four statements are correct. SubbaRow contributed to folic acid synthesis and was associated with methotrexate, aureomycin and Hetrazan.
10.tq: When all listed contributions belong to one scientist, verify each item before selecting the comprehensive combination.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about Yelavarthy Nayudamma:
1. He served as Director of the Central Leather Research Institute, Chennai.
2. He belonged to Guntur district.
3. He died in the Kanishka bombing of Air India Flight 182.
4. The Kanishka bombing in which he died occurred in 1986.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Nayudamma died in the Kanishka bombing in 1985, not 1986.
10.tq: Check the date carefully in a statement containing a correct event but a changed year.

10.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scientist)
 a. Birbal Sahni
 b. P. Maheshwari
 c. K.C. Mehta
 d. G.N. Ramachandran

List-II (Area of work)
 i. Plant embryology
 ii. Protein structure
 iii. Palaeobotany
 iv. Plant pathology—cereal rusts

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
10.x: Birbal Sahni is associated with palaeobotany, P. Maheshwari with plant embryology, K.C. Mehta with cereal rusts and G.N. Ramachandran with protein structure.
10.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing an incorrect scientist–discipline association.

10.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: C.N.R. Rao — Solid-state and structural chemistry
10.x: Jagdish Bhagwati is associated with economics, particularly trade, not palaeobotany. Palaeobotany is associated with Birbal Sahni.
10.tq: Find the swapped area of work among otherwise familiar scientist–discipline pairs.

10.s: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar is associated with which of the following?
o: Plant embryology and establishment of MSSRF
Solid-state chemistry and chairmanship of ISRO
10.x: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar was associated with chemistry and was the founder-director of CSIR.
10.tq: Link the scientist with both the discipline and the institutional role rather than with a single isolated fact.

10.s: Yellapragada SubbaRow and Yelavarthy Nayudamma have which geographical association in common?
o: Both were associated with coastal Andhra.
Both were born in Tamil Nadu.
Both worked as directors of ISRO.
Both received the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal.
10.x: SubbaRow and Nayudamma are both identified as scientists from coastal Andhra. The other options combine unrelated associations.
10.tq: Find the common regional link while rejecting swapped institutional and award associations.

10.s: Who became the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian to win the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026?
10.x: Annapurni Subramaniam won the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026, becoming the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian recipient.
10.tq: Use the award-recipient distinction to separate a current scientist from the prominent scientists associated with the award’s namesake.

10.s: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal won by Annapurni Subramaniam in 2026 was associated with which event and location?
o: The 47th COSPAR Assembly at New Delhi
The 46th Indian Science Congress at Bengaluru
10.x: The award was presented at the 46th COSPAR Assembly held at Florence in 2026.
10.tq: Separate the correct edition and venue from options containing near-miss numbers and locations.

10.s: A Parliament debate on the future of ISRO held on 25 August 2026 invoked the contributions of which group of scientists and space leaders?
o: Sarabhai, Dhawan, Brahm Prakash, U.R. Rao and Kalam
Sarabhai, Swaminathan, Khorana, Ramakrishnan and Nayudamma
Dhawan, Brahm Prakash, SubbaRow, Swaminathan and Khorana
SubbaRow, Nayudamma, Swaminathan, Khorana and Rao
10.x: The debate invoked Vikram Sarabhai, Satish Dhawan, Brahm Prakash, U.R. Rao and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
10.tq: Recognise the complete set of names linked to a specific institutional and policy discussion.

10.s: Which one of the following statements about Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is correct?
o: He was the first Indian Head of State to pilot a spacecraft.
He was the first Indian Head of State to command a submarine.
He was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter aircraft.
He was the first Indian Head of State to serve as DRDO Chairman.
10.x: Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter aircraft.
10.tq: Reject exaggerated or substituted claims by identifying the precise achievement.

10.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)?
10.x: Vikram Sarabhai was the first Chairman of ISRO. Satish Dhawan, Brahm Prakash and U.R. Rao are other prominent figures associated with India’s space programme.
10.tq: Apply the first-in-office cue while distinguishing among closely associated space-science leaders.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nobel Prize:
1. It was instituted by the will of Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite.
2. The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1895.
3. The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Stockholm.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is correct: the prize comes from Alfred Nobel's will. Statement 2 is wrong: the first prizes were awarded in 1901 (1895 is the year of the will). Statement 3 is wrong: the Peace Prize is given by the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo, not Stockholm. Hence '1 only'; every other option includes a false statement.
11.tq: Will - 1901 - Peace Prize in Oslo (Norway), the rest in Sweden.

11.s: Which of the following represents the original five Nobel Prize categories?
o: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace
Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Agriculture and Economics
Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, Economics and Peace
Physics, Mathematics, Economics, Literature and Peace
11.x: The original five categories were Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace. Economics was added later.
11.tq: Identify the original list and eliminate the later-added category.

11.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Economics prize associated with the Nobel Prize:
1. It was added in 1968.
2. It was first awarded in 1969.
3. Its official name refers to the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel.
4. It was one of the original five prizes specified in Alfred Nobel's will.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Economics was not one of the original five prizes in Nobel's will.
11.tq: Use the original-versus-later-added category trap.

11.s: The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences is awarded by the
o: Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences
11.x: The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences is awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
11.tq: Identify the correct awarding body rather than the body associated with the Peace Prize.

11.s: Which statement about Nobel laureate status is correct?
o: It can be revoked by the Nobel Committee after the award ceremony.
It automatically passes to the laureate's institution after death.
It may be transferred permanently to another person along with the medal.
It cannot be transferred, shared or revoked; only the physical medal can change hands.
11.x: Nobel laureate status cannot be transferred, shared or revoked. Only the physical medal can change hands.
11.tq: Apply the distinction between an honour and the physical award object.

11.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Har Gobind Khorana — Structure and function of the ribosome
S. Chandrasekhar — Experimental approach to alleviating global poverty
Venkatraman Ramakrishnan — Structure and function of the ribosome
Abhijit Banerjee — Interpreting the genetic code
11.x: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for studies of the structure and function of the ribosome.
11.tq: Match the scientist with the precise contribution; reject swapped achievements.

11.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Har Gobind Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1968.
2. His Nobel-recognised work concerned interpretation of the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis.
3. He was a United States citizen when he received the Nobel Prize.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All three statements are correct. Khorana received the 1968 Medicine Nobel for work on the genetic code and was a US citizen at the time of the award.
11.tq: Verify the year, field and citizenship together rather than relying on nationality alone.

11.s: Abhijit Banerjee shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for
o: the mathematical theory of black holes
an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty
the discovery of the Raman Effect
research on the structure of the ribosome
11.x: Abhijit Banerjee, along with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer, received the 2019 Economics Nobel for an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty.
11.tq: Direct recall of the award-winning contribution.

11.s: Who among the following received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913?
11.x: Rabindranath Tagore received the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature and was the first Indian and Asian Nobel laureate.
11.tq: Link the award year to the laureate; distinguish literature from science awards.

11.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes C.V. Raman from S. Chandrasekhar?
o: Raman won in 1930 for the Raman Effect, whereas Chandrasekhar won in 1983 for stellar structure and evolution.
Raman won in 1983 for stellar evolution, whereas Chandrasekhar won in 1930 for light scattering.
Both won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on ribosomes.
Both were the first Indian scientist Nobel laureates.
11.x: Raman received the 1930 Physics Nobel for light scattering, while Chandrasekhar received the 1983 Physics Nobel for stellar structure and evolution.
11.tq: Separate two frequently confused Indian Physics laureates by year and contribution.

11.s: Who was the first Asian recipient of a Nobel Prize in a science discipline?
11.x: C. V. Raman became the first Asian recipient of a Nobel Prize in a science discipline when he received the Physics Nobel in 1930.
11.tq: Use the first-in-region distinction, not merely the general Nobel-recipient fact.

11.s: The Chandrasekhar limit refers to the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf, approximately equal to
11.x: The Chandrasekhar limit is approximately 1.4 solar masses, the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf.
11.tq: Handle decimal-place and magnitude traps in astrophysical values.

11.s: When a white dwarf exceeds the Chandrasekhar limit, it may collapse into a
11.x: Beyond the Chandrasekhar limit, a white dwarf can collapse into a neutron star or a black hole.
11.tq: Apply the threshold concept to the consequence of exceeding the limit.

11.s: Which one of the following statements about S. Chandrasekhar is correct?
o: He was the uncle of C.V. Raman and remained an Indian citizen throughout his career.
He was the nephew of C.V. Raman, became a US citizen in 1953 and guided more than 50 PhD students.
He discovered the genetic code and founded the Centre for Ecological Sciences.
He received the Turing Award as the first Asian recipient.
11.x: S. Chandrasekhar was C.V. Raman's nephew, became a US citizen in 1953 and guided more than 50 PhD students.
11.tq: Combine biographical facts while rejecting swapped achievements.

11.s: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, launched in 1999, was named after
11.x: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, launched in 1999, was named in honour of astrophysicist S. Chandrasekhar.
11.tq: Identify the person commemorated by a named scientific observatory.

11.s:
Consider the following statements about the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize:
1. It is awarded by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR).
2. It was first awarded in 1968.
3. It is named after the founder-director of CSIR.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Statement 1 is correct: CSIR awards the prize. Statement 2 is wrong: CSIR has awarded it since 1958, not 1968. Statement 3 is correct: S.S. Bhatnagar was the founder-director of CSIR. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 include the wrong year.
11.tq: CSIR + 1958 + founder-director; 1968 is the Khorana Nobel / Economics-prize year trap.

11.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the disciplines covered by the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize?
11.x: The seven disciplines include biology, chemistry, earth/atmosphere/ocean/planetary sciences, engineering, mathematics, medicine and physics. Political science is not included.
11.tq: Find the outsider in a named disciplinary list.

11.s: Madhav Gadgil is associated with which of the following?
o: The genetic code and protein synthesis
The first Turing Award in computing
People's Biodiversity Register and the Gadgil Commission on the Western Ghats
The discovery of the Raman Effect and the Chandra Observatory
11.x: Ecologist Madhav Gadgil was associated with People's Biodiversity Registers and chaired the 2010 Gadgil Commission on the Western Ghats.
11.tq: Associate a prominent awardee with his principal environmental contributions.

11.s:
Which of the following is the correct correspondence between the categories of the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar and their purposes?

1. Vigyan Ratna — Lifetime achievement
2. Vigyan Shri — Distinguished contributions
3. Vigyan Yuva-SSB — Young scientists up to 45 years
4. Vigyan Team — Team of three or more researchers

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
11.x: All four statements correctly describe the four categories of the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar.
11.tq: Check each category against its specific eligibility or recognition purpose.

11.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar:

1. It is India's highest science and technology recognition.
2. It replaced several earlier science awards administered by ministries.
3. It absorbed the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize as the Vigyan Yuva-SSB category.
4. It covers 13 domains, including physics, chemistry, medicine, engineering, agricultural science and computer science.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All four statements are correct. The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar replaced multiple ministry awards, incorporated the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize as Vigyan Yuva-SSB, and spans 13 domains.
11.tq: Test the institutional scope, replacement function and numerical coverage together.

11.s: Who was the first recipient of the Vigyan Ratna in 2024?
11.x: G. Padmanabhan was the first recipient of the Vigyan Ratna in 2024.
11.tq: Distinguish the first Vigyan Ratna recipient from the 2024 Vigyan Shri recipient and Kalinga Prize winners.

11.s: Annapurni Subramaniam received which Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar category in 2024 for her contribution to space science?
11.x: Annapurni Subramaniam received the Vigyan Shri in 2024 for space science.
11.tq: Separate the named individual award from the other three RVP categories.

11.s: Who received the Abel Prize in Mathematics in 2007?
11.x: S.R. Srinivasa Varadhan received the Abel Prize in Mathematics in 2007.
11.tq: Direct award-winner recall from mathematics distinctions.

11.s: Which of the following pairs of Fields Medal recipients and years is correctly matched?
11.x: Manjul Bhargava received the Fields Medal in 2014 and Akshay Venkatesh received it in 2018.
11.tq: Match two similar mathematical honours with their correct years.

11.s: The International Prize in Statistics, often described as the 'Nobel of statistics', was awarded in 2023 to
11.x: C.R. Rao received the 2023 International Prize in Statistics, regarded as the Nobel equivalent in statistics.
11.tq: Distinguish the statistics prize from mathematics and computing awards.

11.s: Raj Reddy is associated with which distinction?
o: The 1994 Turing Award and recognition as the first Asian recipient
11.x: Raj Reddy received the Turing Award in 1994 and was the first Asian recipient of that award.
11.tq: Associate the computing award with its recipient and distinguishing record.

11.s: Jainendra K. Jain received the 2026 Wolf Prize in Physics for work associated with the
o: composite fermion model for the fractional quantum Hall effect
11.x: Jainendra K. Jain was recognised for the composite fermion model for the fractional quantum Hall effect and was the first Indian-origin recipient of the Wolf Prize in Physics.
11.tq: Identify the precise theory linked to a recent physics award.

11.s: The Kalinga Prize is associated with which of the following?
o: Lifetime achievement in Indian science administration
Young scientists working in agricultural science
11.x: The Kalinga Prize is a UNESCO prize for the popularisation of science.
11.tq: Match the award with its exact objective rather than with a neighbouring science-award purpose.

11.s: The Kalinga Prize was instituted in 1952 with a donation from:
o: The Indian Council of Medical Research established by G. Padmanabhan
The Government of India’s Department of Space
The Kalinga Foundation Trust established by Biju Patnaik
11.x: The Kalinga Prize was instituted in 1952 with a donation from Biju Patnaik through the Kalinga Foundation Trust.
11.tq: Use the founder-and-institution pair to avoid confusing the prize with Indian government science awards.

11.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Indian winner of Kalinga Prize)  List-II (Year)
a. Jagjit Singh                         i. 1996
b. Narender K. Sehgal                   ii. 1963
c. Jayant V. Narlikar                   iii. 2009
d. Yash Pal                              iv. 1991

Codes:
11.x: Jagjit Singh received it in 1963, Narender K. Sehgal in 1991, Jayant V. Narlikar in 1996 and Yash Pal in 2009.
11.tq: Start with the sure year-person pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong match.

11.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal — Political science
Birbal Sahni Medal — Botany or palaeobotany
11.x: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal is associated with space research by scientists from developing countries, not political science.
11.tq: Find the incorrectly matched award and field.

11.s: The J.C. Bose Fellowship or Grant is associated with
11.x: The J.C. Bose Fellowship or Grant supports science and engineering research and is associated with ANRF.
11.tq: Direct award-to-field association.

11.s: Which of the following fields is included among the areas of the Infosys Prize?
11.x: The Infosys Prize covers engineering and computer science, humanities and social sciences, life sciences, mathematical sciences and physical sciences.
11.tq: Recall one precise category from a multi-field award list.

11.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not considered titles under Article 18 of the Constitution.
2. The Padma Awards in 2025 comprised 7 Padma Vibhushan, 19 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri awards.
3. The total number of Padma Awards in 2025 was 139.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
11.x: All three statements are correct. The 2025 Padma Awards totalled 139, comprising 7 Padma Vibhushan, 19 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri awards; these awards are not titles under Article 18.
11.tq: Verify both the constitutional distinction and the component-wise numerical total.

11.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:

A. First Nobel Prize awarded
B. C. V. Raman became the first Indian scientist laureate
C. First Indian-origin recipient of the Wolf Prize in Physics

Select the correct sequence.
11.x: The first Nobel Prize was awarded in 1901, C. V. Raman became the first Indian scientist laureate in 1930, and the first Indian-origin Wolf Prize in Physics recipient was recorded in 2026.
11.tq: Place the dated milestones first and last before resolving the complete sequence.

11.s: Jainendra K. Jain was associated with which recognition in 2026?
11.x: Jainendra K. Jain received the Wolf Prize in Physics in 2026.
11.tq: Separate current international recognitions by matching each scientist with the exact award.

11.s: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in
11.x: Although Alfred Nobel's will established the prizes, the first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901.
11.tq: Separate the founding decision from the first award year.

11.s: C.V. Raman received the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on
11.x: C.V. Raman was awarded the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering and explaining the Raman Effect, involving the scattering of light.
11.tq: Direct field-of-contribution recall.

12.s:
Arrange the following computer generations in chronological order of their core technologies:
A. Integrated circuits
B. Vacuum tubes
C. Microprocessors
D. Transistors
12.x: The correct sequence is vacuum tubes, transistors, integrated circuits and microprocessors, corresponding broadly to the first through fourth generations.
12.tq: Fix the first and last technologies, then place the intermediate generations.

12.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the fifth generation of computers?
o: Artificial intelligence, ULSI and parallel processing
12.x: The fifth generation is associated with artificial intelligence, ultra-large-scale integration and parallel processing.
12.tq: Use the distinctive technology cluster to identify the generation.

12.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Charles Babbage — Analytical Engine
b. Ada Lovelace — First programmer
c. Douglas Engelbart — Computer mouse
d. Larry Tesler — Cut, copy and paste
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
12.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Babbage is associated with the Analytical Engine, Lovelace with the first program, Engelbart with the mouse, and Tesler with cut, copy and paste.
12.tq: Match each inventor with the specific contribution, avoiding famous-name substitution.

12.s: Who is associated with the creation of the World Wide Web in 1989?
12.x: Tim Berners-Lee is associated with the World Wide Web, developed in 1989.
12.tq: Identify the person linked to the named invention and its date.

12.s: The stored-program architecture is associated with
12.x: John von Neumann gave the stored-program architecture, in which programs and data are kept in the same memory. Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, Ada Lovelace was the first programmer and Larry Tesler devised cut/copy/paste.
12.tq: Discriminate between closely related pioneers by their specific contribution.

12.s: In the context of computing history, “technology preservation” refers to a
o: method of storing data in RAM
12.x: “Technology preservation” is associated with a computer museum, where earlier technologies are retained and displayed.
12.tq: Recognise the exact term-to-meaning association instead of interpreting it literally.

12.s: Which one of the following was India's first indigenous computer?
12.x: TIFRAC was the first indigenous computer built in India. ENIAC (1946, Eckert and Mauchly) was the world's first general-purpose electronic computer, and UNIVAC was another first-generation American computer. PARAM 8000 (1991) was India's first supercomputer, not its first computer.
12.tq: First Indian computer = TIFRAC; first Indian supercomputer = PARAM 8000.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about types of computers:
1. Analog computers work on continuous quantities, as in a speedometer or thermometer.
2. Hybrid computers, such as hospital ICU monitors, combine analog and digital features.
3. Digital computers process continuous quantities rather than discrete data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: analog = continuous quantities (speedometer, thermometer). Statement 2 is correct: hybrid computers such as ICU monitors and ECG combine both. Statement 3 is wrong: digital computers process discrete (binary) data, as in PCs. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the other options include the false statement 3.
12.tq: Analog = continuous, digital = discrete/binary, hybrid = both (ICU, ECG).

12.s:
Which of the following are included among personal or microcomputer devices?
1. Desktop
2. Laptop
3. Tablet
4. Smartwatch
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: Desktops, laptops, tablets and smartwatches are all included among personal or microcomputer devices. Smartphones, fitness trackers and AR glasses also fall within this broad group.
12.tq: Recognise the inclusive device category rather than restricting personal computers to desktops.

12.s: Mini and mainframe computers are primarily characterised as
12.x: Mini and mainframe computers are multi-user machines used in organisations.
12.tq: Match the computer class with its scale and user pattern.

12.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a supercomputer?
o: A computer with the highest processing power, commonly expressed in FLOPS
A computer with the lowest processing speed, measured only in bytes
A computer that represents information only through qubits
A computer used exclusively as a word processor
12.x: Supercomputers provide the highest processing power and their speed is commonly expressed in FLOPS.
12.tq: Use the defining performance feature to distinguish supercomputers from other types.

12.s: FLOPS is used to express
12.x: FLOPS means floating-point operations per second and is used particularly to indicate supercomputer performance.
12.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with the correct performance measure.

12.s: The Arithmetic and Logic Unit of a CPU primarily performs
12.x: The ALU performs arithmetic calculations and logical operations.
12.tq: Match each CPU component with its specific responsibility.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about CPU components:
1. The control unit fetches and decodes instructions.
2. Registers are very fast storage locations inside the CPU.
3. The power supply unit directs the execution of program instructions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: The control unit fetches, decodes and directs operations, while registers provide very fast internal storage. The PSU supplies power and does not direct instruction execution.
12.tq: Reject the statement assigning a CPU control function to a power-supply component.

12.s: Which one of the following was the first commercial microprocessor?
12.x: The Intel 4004, introduced in 1971, was the first commercial microprocessor.
12.tq: Link the historical milestone with the specific processor model.

12.s: Which one of the following devices can function as both an input and an output device?
12.x: A touch screen displays output and also receives input through touch.
12.tq: Apply the input-output classification to a dual-function device.

12.s: A barcode is best described as
o: a printed image converted into editable text
a two-dimensional matrix of square modules
machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths
a magnetic character sequence used on cheques
12.x: A conventional barcode consists of machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths.
12.tq: Distinguish barcode, QR code, OCR and MICR by physical form and function.

12.s: Which one of the following is a non-impact printer?
12.x: Laser printers are non-impact printers; dot-matrix, daisy-wheel and line printers are impact printers.
12.tq: Separate printer classes by whether the print mechanism strikes the paper.

12.s: Printer quality and speed are commonly expressed, respectively, in
12.x: Print quality is measured in dots per inch (dpi), while speed may be expressed in pages per minute (ppm).
12.tq: Match measurement units with the correct printer performance parameter.

12.s: The communication from a computer mouse to the computer is an example of which transmission mode?
12.x: A mouse only sends signals to the computer, so the communication is one-way, or simplex (APPSC 2019). Half duplex is two-way but one direction at a time, as in a walkie-talkie. Full duplex is two-way at once, as in a telephone. Multiplexing combines several signals on one channel; it is not a direction mode.
12.tq: Mouse/keyboard = simplex (one-way).

12.s: A nibble in computer terminology consists of
12.x: A nibble is a group of four bits.
12.tq: Recall the fixed-size relationship between binary storage units.

12.s: Which one of the following statements about RAM is correct?
o: It is slower than magnetic tape.
It is temporary working memory and is volatile.
It is erased only by ultraviolet light.
12.x: RAM temporarily stores data and instructions currently in use and loses its contents when power is removed.
12.tq: Distinguish volatile working memory from non-volatile storage.

12.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SRAM is used in cache memory.
2. DRAM is commonly used as main memory.
3. Both SRAM and DRAM are types of ROM.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: SRAM is associated with cache and DRAM with main memory. Statement 3 is false because both are forms of RAM.
12.tq: Identify the single wrong classification in a set of related memory statements.

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: EEPROM — erasable only by ultraviolet light
12.x: EPROM is erased using ultraviolet light. EEPROM is electrically erasable, while ROM is non-volatile.
12.tq: Use the exact technical distinction among closely related memory terms.

12.s:
Arrange the following in descending order of access speed:
A. RAM
B. Registers
C. Magnetic tape
D. Cache
12.x: The speed order is registers, cache, RAM and magnetic tape.
12.tq: Arrange items by performance hierarchy, beginning with the fastest.

12.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of a solid-state drive?
o: It uses flash memory and has no moving parts.
It uses a blue-violet laser to read data.
12.x: An SSD uses flash memory, has no moving parts and is generally faster than an HDD.
12.tq: Separate storage devices by their underlying technology.

12.s: Which storage medium is primarily associated with sequential access and archival backup?
12.x: Magnetic tape is a sequential-access medium commonly used for backup and archival purposes.
12.tq: Match a storage medium with its characteristic use.

12.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the approximate single-layer capacity?
1. CD — 700 MB
2. DVD — 4.7 GB
3. Blu-ray — 25 GB
12.x: A single-layer CD stores about 700 MB, a single-layer DVD about 4.7 GB and a single-layer Blu-ray disc about 25 GB.
12.tq: Check all numerical pairings before selecting the coded option.

12.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Operating system — system software
2. Disk cleanup — utility software
3. Word processor — application software
4. Device driver — application software
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
12.x: Operating systems, disk-cleanup tools and word processors are correctly classified. A device driver is system software, so pair 4 is false.
12.tq: Spot the wrongly classified software category.

12.s: Which one of the following is NOT an example of application software?
12.x: A compiler is a language translator and therefore system software; the other three are application programs.
12.tq: Find the exception by separating system tools from end-user applications.

12.s: Which statement best describes open-source software?
o: It is limited to operating systems produced by one company.
Its source code is permanently hidden from users.
It can never be commercially distributed.
Its source code is free to view, modify and share, subject to its licence.
12.x: Open-source software makes source code available for viewing, modification and sharing under the applicable licence.
12.tq: Reject absolute claims and identify the precise definition.

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
12.x: Richard Stallman initiated the GNU project in 1983. Linus Torvalds developed the Linux kernel in 1991.
12.tq: Use the person-project-year trap to distinguish related open-source milestones.

12.s:
Which of the following is NOT a normal responsibility of an operating system?
1. Managing hardware
2. Handling processes and memory
3. Managing files and device drivers
4. Manufacturing the motherboard
12.x: An operating system manages hardware resources, processes, memory, files and drivers. Manufacturing a motherboard is not an operating-system function.
12.tq: Find the unrelated function among genuine operating-system responsibilities.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about types of operating systems:
1. In a batch operating system, jobs are grouped and run without user interaction.
2. In a time-sharing (multi-user) operating system such as UNIX, many users share CPU time.
3. Real-time operating systems have no fixed response deadlines, so they are unsuitable for missile guidance or air-traffic control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: batch OS groups jobs and runs them without user interaction. Statement 2 is correct: time-sharing OS (e.g. UNIX) lets many users share CPU time. Statement 3 is wrong: real-time OS work to fixed response deadlines and are used precisely for missile guidance, air-traffic control and medical devices. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' and '1 and 3 only' drop statement 2 or add the false 3, and '1, 2 and 3' includes the false statement.
12.tq: Real-time = fixed deadlines (missiles, ATC, medical devices); time-sharing = UNIX.

12.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding mobile operating systems?
o: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google.
Android and iOS are command-line-only systems.
BharOS was developed by a private foreign corporation.
12.x: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google, while iOS is associated with Apple. BharOS was developed at IIT Madras.
12.tq: Use the developer-platform-location distinction to reject swapped associations.

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CLI — icons and windows controlled mainly by a mouse
12.x: MS-DOS is associated with a command-line interface. GUIs use icons, windows and mouse interaction, as in Windows and macOS.
12.tq: Distinguish CLI and GUI by their visible interaction method.

12.s: Which programming-language generation uses mnemonics and requires an assembler for conversion?
12.x: Second-generation assembly language uses mnemonics and is converted into machine language by an assembler.
12.tq: Match the language generation with its characteristic translator.

12.s: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Assembly language is a fourth-generation database language.
SQL is a first-generation machine language.
FORTRAN was the first high-level language and appeared in 1957.
12.x: FORTRAN is identified as the first high-level language and dates from 1957. SQL is a fourth-generation language used for database queries.
12.tq: Combine the language-generation fact with its historical date.

12.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes a compiler from an interpreter?
o: A compiler translates only comments, whereas an interpreter translates only variables.
An interpreter is used exclusively for assembly language.
A compiler translates the whole program at once, whereas an interpreter translates and runs it line by line.
Both always translate only one line at a time.
12.x: A compiler processes the complete program before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes line by line, making debugging easier.
12.tq: Compare paired translators by the unit and timing of translation.

12.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a flowchart symbol with its function?
12.x: An oval represents start or end; a diamond represents decision, a parallelogram input/output and a rectangle a process.
12.tq: Use the symbol-function pair and reject swapped flowchart meanings.

12.s: The pictorial representation of an algorithm is called a:
12.x: A flowchart is the pictorial form of an algorithm, which is a finite step-by-step procedure (APPSC 2019). Pseudocode is an English-like text outline, a compiler is a language translator, and source code is the written program.
12.tq: Algorithm in pictures = flowchart; in English-like text = pseudocode.

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its number-system base?
12.x: Binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal have bases 2, 8, 10 and 16 respectively.
12.tq: Check the base rather than the familiar name of the number system.

12.s: The hexadecimal number (FF)₁₆ is equal to
12.x: F represents 15, so FF equals 15 × 16 + 15 = 255.
12.tq: Convert hexadecimal by applying place value and digit value.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about logic gates:
1. NAND and NOR are universal gates.
2. An XOR gate gives output 1 when its inputs are the same.
3. AND, OR and NOT are the basic logic gates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: NAND and NOR are the universal gates. Statement 2 is wrong: XOR gives 1 when the inputs differ, not when they are the same. Statement 3 is correct: AND, OR and NOT are the basic gates. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and the other two options include the false statement 2.
12.tq: XOR = 'exclusive' = 1 only when inputs differ; universal = NAND, NOR.

12.s:
Consider the following Boolean identities:
1. A + A = A
2. A · A′ = 0
3. (A + B)′ = A′ · B′
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three are valid Boolean identities; the third is De Morgan's law.
12.tq: Verify each algebraic identity independently before selecting the combined code.

12.s: Word length of a computer refers to the
o: number of bits handled by the CPU at one time
physical length of a memory module
number of characters stored in a file name
number of instructions executed in one minute
12.x: Word length is the number of bits that the CPU can handle at once, such as 32-bit or 64-bit processing.
12.tq: Separate a processing-width term from storage and speed terms.

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Clock speed — floating-point operations per second
12.x: Bandwidth measures data-transfer rate in bits per second. Clock speed is measured in hertz, MIPS denotes million instructions per second, and word length is measured in bits.
12.tq: Match each performance term with its precise unit or meaning.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about computer performance terms:
1. MIPS stands for million instructions per second.
2. Clock speed is measured in bits per second.
3. FLOPS (floating-point operations per second) is used to express supercomputer speed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: MIPS = million instructions per second. Statement 2 is wrong: clock speed is measured in hertz (GHz); bits per second is the unit of bandwidth. Statement 3 is correct: FLOPS expresses supercomputer speed. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 include the false unit.
12.tq: Clock = hertz, bandwidth = bps, supercomputer = FLOPS.

12.s: Which benchmark measures floating-point performance while solving large dense linear systems and forms the basis of world supercomputer rankings?
12.x: The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.
12.tq: Identify the benchmark from its distinctive workload and ranking application.

12.s: According to the ISC 2026 ranking referred to here, the world’s fastest supercomputer is
o: El Capitan of the United States
12.x: China’s LineShine topped the ISC 2026 supercomputer list, replacing the United States’ El Capitan.
12.tq: Track the current ranking and the country-replacement relationship carefully.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about Param Shakti at IIT Madras:
1. It was launched by MeitY.
2. It has a capacity of 3.1 petaflops.
3. It uses C-DAC RUDRA servers.
4. It operates with open-source AlmaLinux.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: Param Shakti at IIT Madras was launched by MeitY, has 3.1 petaflops capacity, uses C-DAC RUDRA servers and runs open-source AlmaLinux.
12.tq: Verify all institutional, numerical and technical attributes before choosing the complete code.

12.s: Param Shakti at IIT Madras was funded under the
12.x: Param Shakti was funded under the National Supercomputing Mission.
12.tq: Identify the correct government mission associated with the named installation.

12.s:
Which of the following are associated with quantum computing?
1. Superposition
2. Entanglement
3. Cryptography
4. Optimisation
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: Quantum computing uses superposition and entanglement and has applications in cryptography and optimisation. All four statements are correct.
12.tq: Combine the underlying principles with the listed application areas.

12.s: Q-Day refers to the point at which quantum computers may be capable of
o: breaking RSA-2048 public-key encryption using Shor’s algorithm
converting every file into PDF format
increasing the clock speed of classical processors
12.x: Q-Day denotes the anticipated point when quantum computers can break RSA-2048 public-key encryption through Shor’s algorithm, proposed in 1994.
12.tq: Link the specialised term to its specific security consequence and algorithm.

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its file type?
12.x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format. MP3 is audio, PDF is a document format and MOV is a video format.
12.tq: Start from the sure file-type pair and eliminate the swapped categories.

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
12.x: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics, not Portable Network Graphics Interface. AVI, MOV and GIF are correctly matched.
12.tq: Find the altered word in an otherwise familiar acronym expansion.

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ASCII:
1. ASCII is a 7-bit character-encoding scheme.
2. ASCII represents 128 characters.
3. Unicode extends the character-representation capability of ASCII.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: ASCII is a 7-bit code representing 128 characters, while Unicode extends the range of character representation. All three statements are correct.
12.tq: Check each numerical and relationship statement before selecting the combined code.

12.s: JPEG is primarily associated with which of the following?
12.x: JPEG, or Joint Photographic Experts Group, is an image format commonly associated with lossy compression.
12.tq: Distinguish the file format’s information type from unrelated compression categories.

12.s: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) is best understood as an umbrella term covering devices and applications used to
o: replace all forms of human communication
access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information
12.x: ICT covers devices and applications used to access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information, including mobiles, networks, software, the internet and satellites.
12.tq: Choose the comprehensive definition rather than an exclusive or extreme description.

12.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate associated with ICT?
12.x: Privacy risks, the digital divide, job insecurity and over-reliance on technology are identified concerns. Guaranteed elimination of technological dependence is not such a criticism.
12.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated group of ICT concerns.

12.s:
ICT aims to facilitate communication among which of the following?
1. Human and human
2. Human and machine
3. Machine and machine
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication. Therefore, all three forms are included.
12.tq: Read the communication relationships separately before selecting the combined option.

13.s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
13.x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
13.tq: Link the historical network with its sponsoring organisation and legacy.

13.s: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) was founded in which year?
13.x: Tim Berners-Lee founded the W3C in 1994. The other years correspond to ERNET, the invention of the WWW and the emergence of Satyam Infoway as a private ISP.
13.tq: Discriminate between closely related milestones by their years.

13.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the Indian Internet milestones in chronological order?
o: Public internet by VSNL, ERNET, Satyam Infoway
Satyam Infoway, ERNET, public internet by VSNL
ERNET, public internet by VSNL, Satyam Infoway
ERNET, Satyam Infoway, public internet by VSNL
13.x: ERNET began in 1986, public internet was launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995, and Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
13.tq: Use the first, middle and last dates to establish the sequence.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network types:
1. A PAN links an individual's personal devices, typically through Bluetooth.
2. A MAN generally covers a city.
3. A firm linking its LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi is using a MAN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: PAN = personal area, e.g. Bluetooth. Statement 2 is correct: MAN covers a city. Statement 3 is wrong: linking LANs in different cities needs a WAN, which spans large areas (the internet is a global WAN) - this was the APPSC 2019 answer. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: Across cities = WAN; within one city = MAN.

13.s: A Virtual Private Network primarily provides:
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
13.x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
13.tq: Identify the function rather than the physical form of the network.

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding network topologies:
1. In a bus topology, all nodes share one backbone cable.
2. In a star topology, failure of one node normally isolates the entire network.
3. In a ring topology, each node is linked to two neighbouring nodes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. In a star topology, failure of one node is generally isolated; failure of the central hub can stop the network.
13.tq: Find the incorrect resilience statement before selecting the code.

13.s: Which topology is characterised by every node being connected to every other node?
13.x: In a mesh topology, every node is linked to every other node, making it highly resilient but costly.
13.tq: Use the complete-connectivity clue.

13.s: A tree topology is best described as:
o: A single circular connection of nodes
A topology in which every node has a direct link to every other node
A network using only one backbone cable
13.x: A tree topology combines star networks in a hierarchy. Failure of a parent can affect the branch below it.
13.tq: Match the structural description with the topology name.

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Device)
a. Hub
b. Switch
c. Router
d. Modem

List-II (Primary role)
i. Routes packets using IP
 ii. Converts digital and analogue signals
 iii. Broadcasts data to all ports
 iv. Forwards frames using MAC addresses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: A hub broadcasts to all ports, a switch forwards frames by MAC address, a router routes using IP, and a modem converts between digital and analogue signals.
13.tq: Start from the sure device-function pairs and complete the code.

13.s: A gateway differs from a router chiefly because a gateway:
o: Operates only as a physical cable
Broadcasts every frame to all ports
13.x: A gateway joins networks that use different protocols and may operate across all or upper OSI layers.
13.tq: Discriminate between two nearby networking devices by their interoperability function.

13.s: Which of the following represents the correct top-to-bottom order of the OSI model?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Network, Transport, Data Link, Physical
Presentation, Application, Session, Transport, Data Link, Network, Physical
13.x: From the top layer downward, the OSI model is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical.
13.tq: Use the first and last layers, then verify the middle sequence.

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
13.x: A modem is associated with the Physical layer because it modulates and demodulates signals; it is not a Transport-layer device.
13.tq: Find the device placed at the wrong OSI layer.

13.s:
Match the following OSI layers with their associated functions or protocols:
List-I (Layer)
a. Presentation
b. Session
c. Transport
d. Data Link

List-II (Function or protocol)
i. TCP and UDP
ii. Encryption, compression and formats
 iii. Opens and closes sessions
 iv. MAC addressing and frame forwarding

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: The Presentation layer handles encryption, compression and formats; the Session layer opens and closes sessions; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP; and the Data Link layer handles MAC-based frame operations.
13.tq: Start with the distinctive TCP/UDP and MAC pairs.

13.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the OSI layer?
1. HTTP — Application layer
2. IP — Network layer
3. MAC — Data Link layer
4. Cables — Physical layer
Select the correct answer.
13.x: HTTP is an Application-layer protocol, IP belongs to the Network layer, MAC is associated with the Data Link layer, and cables operate at the Physical layer.
13.tq: Use protocol and device layer matching to validate each statement.

13.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with its transmission mode?
1. Radio or television broadcast — Simplex
2. Walkie-talkie — Half duplex
3. Telephone conversation — Full duplex
Select the correct answer.
13.x: Simplex permits one-way transmission, half duplex permits two-way transmission one at a time, and full duplex permits simultaneous two-way transmission.
13.tq: Compare the direction and simultaneity of communication.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about Internet connection media:
1. DSL uses telephone copper lines.
2. Cable Internet uses coaxial television cable.
3. Fibre Internet transmits data as light pulses through optical fibre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: DSL uses telephone copper lines, cable Internet uses coaxial TV cable, and fibre Internet uses optical fibre carrying light pulses.
13.tq: Match each technology with its physical transmission medium.

13.s: Satellite Internet generally consists of which three segments?
13.x: Satellite Internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments and does not require a terrestrial wire connection.
13.tq: Recall the three-part system architecture.

13.s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
13.x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.
13.tq: Match the protocol with its immediate communication function rather than with a neighbouring networking function.

13.s: DNS performs which of the following functions?
o: Assigns MAC addresses to network cards
Converts human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses
13.x: DNS acts as the Internet’s directory by translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
13.tq: Identify the service needed when a user knows a name but the network requires an IP address.

13.s: Which protocol is primarily used for reliable delivery of data in the TCP/IP suite?
13.x: Within TCP/IP, TCP ensures reliable delivery, while IP addresses and routes packets.
13.tq: Separate the transport reliability function of TCP from the addressing and routing function of IP.

13.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: POP3 — downloading mail to one device, usually deleting it from the server
IMAP — permanently deleting mail from the server after downloading it to one device
13.x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices. POP3 generally downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server.
13.tq: Distinguish the confusable mail protocols by their treatment of messages on the server.

13.s: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network?
13.x: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically. DNS translates names into IP addresses, while HTTP and TCP perform different communication functions.
13.tq: Identify the protocol by its automatic address-assignment function.

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Protocol element)
A. Syntax
B. Semantics
C. Timing

List-II (Meaning)
1. Meaning of each field
2. Format of data
3. When and how fast to send

option_a
13.x: Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics specifies the meaning of each field, and timing specifies when and how fast data is sent.
13.tq: Start from the sure pair ‘syntax–format’ and complete the protocol-element mapping.

13.s:
Assertion (A): HTTPS provides greater security for browser-server communication than HTTP.
Reason (R): HTTPS encrypts the traffic between the browser and the server through TLS.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
13.x: Both statements are true, and TLS-based encryption directly explains why HTTPS provides greater security than HTTP.
13.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the security difference between HTTP and HTTPS.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network addresses:
1. An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and written in dotted decimal, e.g. 192.168.1.1.
2. An IPv6 address is 128 bits long and written as eight groups of hexadecimal separated by colons.
3. A MAC address is a 64-bit logical address assigned by DNS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: IPv4 = 32 bits, dotted decimal. Statement 2 is correct: IPv6 = 128 bits, eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Statement 3 is wrong: a MAC address is a 48-bit (6-byte, 12 hex digits) physical address burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer; DNS only turns names into IP addresses. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options either miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: 32 / 128 / 48: IPv4 / IPv6 / MAC; MAC is physical, burnt into the card.

13.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents IPv4 address classes by their first-octet ranges?
1. Class A — 1 to 126
2. Class B — 128 to 191
3. Class C — 192 to 223
4. Class D — 240 to 255
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Classes A, B and C have ranges 1–126, 128–191 and 192–223 respectively. Class D is 224–239 for multicast; 240–255 is Class E for experimental use.
13.tq: Check each numerical range against the class boundary, especially the swapped D and E ranges.

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
13.x: The 127.x.x.x range is used for loopback. Class D multicast is 224–239, Class E experimental is 240–255, and 192–223 is Class C.
13.tq: Find the correctly matched exception among deliberately interchanged class ranges.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about wireless standards:
1. Bluetooth follows IEEE 802.15.1 and is a personal area network (PAN) technology.
2. Wi-Fi follows IEEE 802.11 and uses the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, with 6 GHz in Wi-Fi 6E.
3. Wi-Fi Direct needs an existing LAN to link two devices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bluetooth = IEEE 802.15.1, a PAN technology. Statement 2 is correct: Wi-Fi = IEEE 802.11 on 2.4 and 5 GHz (6 GHz in Wi-Fi 6E). Statement 3 is wrong: Wi-Fi Direct links devices with no LAN. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the other options include the false statement 3.
13.tq: 802.15.1 = Bluetooth (PAN), 802.11 = Wi-Fi (WLAN); 'Direct' means no LAN needed.

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bluetooth and Wi-Fi:
1. Bluetooth generally has a short range of about 10 metres for a class 2 device.
2. Wi-Fi generally provides coverage over a longer range, such as a whole building.
3. Bluetooth operates only in the 5 GHz band.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Bluetooth class 2 devices have a short range of approximately 10 metres, while Wi-Fi generally covers a larger area. Bluetooth operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, not only in 5 GHz.
13.tq: Use range and frequency comparisons to reject the absolute frequency claim.

13.s: The 2019 APPSC key identified which version as the latest version of Bluetooth?
13.x: The 2019 APPSC key treated Bluetooth 5.1 as the latest version. This is a time-specific reference and should not be confused with later versions.
13.tq: Recognise the dated examination reference rather than applying an unspecified current-version claim.

13.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the function of HTML tags in a webpage?
o: They define and mark up the structure of text and other content
They assign numerical IP addresses to webpages
13.x: HTML tags mark up and structure the text and other content of webpages. Encryption and indexing are performed by other technologies or services.
13.tq: Distinguish the structural role of HTML from the functions of encryption, addressing and search.

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding web technologies:
1. A web server stores webpages and sends them when requested.
2. A web browser requests webpages and displays them on the screen.
3. A search engine indexes webpages so that they can be found.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: All three statements are correct. The server stores and serves pages, the browser displays them, and the search engine indexes them for discovery.
13.tq: Separate the closely related functions of the server, browser and search engine.

13.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of the principal parts of a URL?
o: Protocol, domain name, path to the file
Protocol, path to the file, domain name
13.x: A URL contains the protocol, such as https://, followed by the domain name and the path to the file.
13.tq: Test the internal order of URL components instead of merely recalling its expansion.

13.s: The principal role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is to:
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
13.x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
13.tq: Identify the responsible body by its standard-setting function.

13.s:
With reference to Web 3.0, consider the following statements:
1. It represents the third generation of the web.
2. It changes how the web is used, how sites are managed and how services are delivered.
3. OCEN is linked with Web 3.0 and aims to democratise lending.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Web 3.0 is the third generation of the web and involves changes in usage, site management and service delivery. OCEN seeks to democratise lending and improve credit terms for small borrowers.
13.tq: Combine the definition, scope and associated initiative without confusing Web 3.0 with a single application.

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its description?
o: Surface web — not indexed by search engines
Deep web — entirely associated with illegal markets
Dark web — hidden subset of the deep web requiring tools such as Tor or I2P
Surface web — accessible only through anonymous networks
13.x: The dark web is a small hidden subset of the deep web and is associated with anonymous access through tools such as Tor or I2P. The surface web is indexed, while the deep web is not necessarily malicious.
13.tq: Use the defining access and indexing features to separate surface, deep and dark web.

13.s:
Arrange the following layers of the web in descending order of their approximate share:
A. Dark web
B. Surface web
C. Deep web
Select the correct sequence.
13.x: The deep web accounts for approximately 90–95%, the surface web about 4–5%, and the dark web is a small hidden subset.
13.tq: Order categories by relative size, beginning with the largest share.

13.s: ICANN, established in 1998 as a United States non-profit organisation, is primarily associated with:
o: Coordinating the global domain name system and IP address allocation
13.x: ICANN coordinates the global Domain Name System and IP address allocation. It was established in 1998 as a US non-profit organisation.
13.tq: Use the organisation-function and year combination.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about NIXI:
1. It was established in 2003.
2. It is a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY.
3. It runs the .in registry and IRINN.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: NIXI was established in 2003, functions as a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY, and runs Internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.
13.tq: Check each institutional detail before choosing the combined code.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about the multilingual internet:
1. Internationalised Domain Names (IDNs) are domain names in local scripts, such as .Bharat in Devanagari.
2. Universal Acceptance means every app and e-mail system accepts all such domain names and e-mail IDs.
3. BhashaNet was launched by ICANN in 2022 to promote Universal Acceptance for Indian languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: IDNs use local scripts, e.g. .Bharat in Devanagari. Statement 2 is correct: that is what Universal Acceptance means. Statement 3 is wrong: BhashaNet (2022) is a MeitY-NIXI initiative, not ICANN's. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: BhashaNet = MeitY + NIXI (Indian bodies); ICANN is the global DNS coordinator.

13.s:
Which provisions are associated with governmental blocking of online content in India?
1. Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000
2. Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000
3. Section 3 of the Telegraph Act, 1885
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Sections 69A and 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 are associated with orders to ISPs and intermediaries for blocking content. Section 3 of the Telegraph Act is not the stated blocking provision.
13.tq: Eliminate the unrelated statutory provision.

13.s: Which legislation replaced the Telegraph Act, 1885 and contains the power to suspend Internet services?
13.x: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Telegraph Act and contains the power to suspend Internet services.
13.tq: Distinguish content-blocking provisions from the later telecommunications legislation.

13.s: An organisation notices that a particular website is inaccessible to users of one Internet service provider, while users of another provider can access it. Which explanation is consistent with this situation?
o: The provider may be using DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering
The OSI model has ceased to operate for that website
All websites have been permanently removed from the Internet
A PAN has automatically become a WAN
13.x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering on HTTPS. Consequently, blocklists and access results can differ between ISPs.
13.tq: Apply the technical mechanism to the observed provider-specific outcome.

13.s: BharatNet fibre, as indicated for 2025–26, reaches approximately how many gram panchayats?
13.x: BharatNet fibre reaches approximately 2.18 lakh gram panchayats according to the stated 2025–26 figure.
13.tq: Distinguish the lakh figure from crore and reversed-number distractors.

13.s: Which set of issues was discussed by Chief Minister Naidu and Sunil Mittal in relation to Andhra Pradesh?
o: Only the replacement of optical fibre by copper cable
Coal mining, irrigation dams and inland waterways
Last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station
Only satellite launching and missile testing
13.x: The discussion concerned last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station for Andhra Pradesh.
13.tq: Identify the complete issue cluster rather than a partial distractor.

14.s: What does the abbreviation SIM stand for in mobile telephony?
14.x: SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module, the card that identifies the subscriber on a mobile network. The other expansions are invented.
14.tq: Test the exact expansion of a commonly confused telecommunications abbreviation.

14.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Android?
o: A mobile operating system developed by Google and built on the Linux kernel
A payment protocol operating only through Bluetooth
A mobile network standard developed by Denso Wave
A mobile-number portability mechanism operated by RBI
14.x: Android is Google's mobile operating system and is built on the Linux kernel.
14.tq: Distinguish the operating system from network standards, payment technologies and portability services.

14.s: Which of the following statements regarding mobile-generation technologies is correct?
o: 4G runs on LTE, using OFDM and MIMO.
WiMAX replaced LTE as the dominant 4G technology.
14.x: 4G runs on LTE and uses OFDM and MIMO. WiMAX lost out to LTE; 1G dates from the 1980s, while 6G is expected in the early 2030s.
14.tq: Use the technology-generation sequence and the LTE–WiMAX comparison to eliminate reversals.

14.s: The first handheld mobile phone call was made on 3 April 1973 by:
14.x: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile call on 3 April 1973. Bell is linked with the telephone, Marconi with radio, and Jack Dorsey co-founded Twitter.
14.tq: First handheld call = Martin Cooper (Motorola), 1973.

14.s: Mobile Number Portability (MNP) within a telecom circle began in India on:
14.x: MNP within a circle began on 20 January 2011. 25 November 2010 was the date of the earlier Haryana pilot; 3 April 1973 is the date of the first handheld call; 1 January 2015 is unrelated.
14.tq: MNP: Haryana pilot Nov 2010, nationwide-in-circle 20 Jan 2011.

14.s:
With reference to QR codes, consider the following statements:
1. QR stands for Quick Response.
2. QR codes were designed by Denso Wave in Japan.
3. Their original design in 1994 was for the car industry.
4. They are read quickly by a phone camera.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: All four statements are correct. QR means Quick Response; Denso Wave designed the codes in Japan in 1994 for the car industry, and phone cameras can read them quickly.
14.tq: Check the expansion, origin, year, purpose and practical use together.

14.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of Near Field Communication (NFC) as described in mobile technology?
o: It supports data rates of about 106–424 kbps.
It generally works over a distance of a few centimetres.
It permits easier pairing and uses less power than Bluetooth.
It normally requires a greater operating range than Bluetooth.
14.x: NFC works over a few centimetres, supports approximately 106–424 kbps, and generally offers easier pairing and lower power use than Bluetooth. It does not require a greater operating range than Bluetooth.
14.tq: Reject the reversed comparison in the NFC–Bluetooth distinction.

14.s: Which institution allowed offline UPI Lite payments over NFC?
14.x: The Reserve Bank of India allowed offline UPI Lite payments over NFC.
14.tq: Identify the authority associated with the specified digital-payment measure.

14.s:
Consider the following statements about the Agrimarket app:
1. It uses GPS to find prices at markets within 50 kilometres.
2. Its data is obtained from Agmarknet.
3. It is available in English and Hindi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: All three statements are correct. Agrimarket uses GPS, obtains data from Agmarknet, covers markets within 50 km, and provides information in English and Hindi.
14.tq: Test the app through its coverage, data source and language features.

14.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
14.x: SWAYAM provides free online courses. Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, Sugamya Bharat concerns accessibility reporting, and UMANG is a governance application.
14.tq: Use the sector-purpose association to detect swapped application functions.

14.s: Which one of the following is an m-governance application that crowdsources reports of inaccessible places?
14.x: The Sugamya Bharat app crowdsources reports of inaccessible places and belongs to the m-governance sector.
14.tq: Identify the application from its distinctive real-world use.

14.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its digital-health function?
o: Doctor on Demand — United States health application
14.x: Agrimarket is an m-agriculture application. eSanjeevani provides telemedicine, Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, and Doctor on Demand is a US health application.
14.tq: Find the application placed in the wrong sector.

14.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SMTP — receiving e-mail from a mail server
POP3/IMAP — sending e-mail to a mail server
BCC — displaying all recipients to one another
14.x: SMTP is used for sending e-mail. POP3 and IMAP are used for receiving mail, while BCC hides recipients from one another.
14.tq: Discriminate between the sending protocol, receiving protocols and recipient-copy fields.

14.s: A sender wants to send copies of an e-mail to several recipients without revealing the recipients' addresses to one another. Which field should be used?
14.x: BCC, or blind carbon copy, sends copies while hiding the recipients' addresses from one another.
14.tq: Translate the privacy requirement in the scenario into the correct e-mail field.

14.s: An e-mail address such as name@gov.in is made up of:
14.x: An e-mail address has the form username @ domain name; in name@gov.in, 'name' is the username and 'gov.in' the domain. The reversed order is wrong, and protocols such as SMTP or a server address/port are not part of the address.
14.tq: E-mail address = user @ domain.

14.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the essentials of video conferencing?
14.x: Video conferencing needs a camera, microphone, speaker/display, a broadband link and conferencing software (codec). An RFID reader is used to read RFID tags and is not a video-conferencing component.
14.tq: VC kit: camera, mic, speaker/display, broadband, codec.

14.s: Who founded LinkedIn, which is primarily used for professional networking?
14.x: LinkedIn was founded by Reid Hoffman in 2003 and is used mainly for professional networking.
14.tq: Use the founder-purpose association and distinguish it from other social platforms.
