22.x: e-District is a State MMP providing district-level certificates and services. The other pairs assign functions of different MMPs.
22.tq: Start with the direct service-function pair and eliminate swapped functions.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about IVFRT:
1. It is a Ministry of Home Affairs project approved in 2010.
2. It is run by CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd with NIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: IVFRT is an MHA project approved in 2010. Statement 2 is wrong: IVFRT is run by the Bureau of Immigration with NIC; CSC e-Governance Services is the implementing agency of Common Service Centres. Hence only 1 is correct; B, C and D are wrong.
22.tq: Immigration project, so the Bureau of Immigration runs it (with NIC).

22.s: The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project provides which of the following?
22.x: The e-Panchayat MMP provides core panchayat software under the Panchayati Raj domain.
22.tq: Match the project with its sector-specific administrative function.

22.s: The GS NIRNAY application, launched in 2023, is associated with which activity?
22.x: The GS NIRNAY app covers Gram Sabha decisions and is associated with the e-Panchayat initiative.
22.tq: Use the year-and-function combination to distinguish the application from other MMP tools.

22.s: Which ministry coordinates the Digital India programme?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
22.x: The Digital India programme is coordinated by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, or MeitY.
22.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” test to identify the nodal ministry.

22.s:
With reference to implementation of Digital India, consider the following statements:
1. It is implemented by the whole government.
2. Public-private partnership is preferred wherever feasible.
3. Its implementation is confined to MeitY alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Digital India is implemented across the whole government, with PPP preferred wherever feasible. It is not confined to MeitY alone.
22.tq: Reject the absolute institutional claim that assigns a whole-of-government programme to one ministry.

22.s: The principal aim of Digital India is to transform India into a:
o: Digitally empowered society and knowledge economy
Centralised administrative state and industrial economy
Fully privatised economy and cashless market
22.x: Digital India aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
22.tq: Identify the precise paired formulation used for the programme’s overarching aim.

22.s: Universal digital literacy, documents on the cloud and services in Indian languages are associated with which vision area of Digital India?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility
22.x: These measures are components of the vision area called digital empowerment of citizens.
22.tq: Match concrete features to the correct broad vision area.

22.s: Which one of the following is the fourth pillar of Digital India?
22.x: The fourth pillar is e-Governance: reforming government through technology.
22.tq: Use the numbered pillar sequence to distinguish adjacent pillars.

22.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Digital India pillar)
A. Broadband Highways
B. Universal Access to Mobile/Phones
C. Public Internet Access Programme
D. Information for All

List-II (Pillar number)
1. 1
2. 2
3. 3
4. 6

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
22.x: Broadband Highways, Universal Access to Mobile/Phones, Public Internet Access Programme and Information for All are pillars 1, 2, 3 and 6 respectively.
22.tq: Start from the first three sequential pillars and verify the non-adjacent sixth pillar.

22.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
22.x: Early Harvest Programmes is the ninth pillar, not the seventh. The seventh pillar is Electronics Manufacturing: target net zero imports.
22.tq: Check the pillar number against the official sequence.

22.s: The target of “net zero imports” is associated with which Digital India pillar?
22.x: The seventh pillar, Electronics Manufacturing, carries the target of net zero imports.
22.tq: Match the distinctive policy target to its pillar.

22.s: Which of the following is included among the sub-schemes of Digital India?
22.x: Electronic Governance, National Knowledge Network, Cyber Security and the IndiaAI Mission are included among the stated Digital India sub-schemes.
22.tq: Select the technology-oriented sub-scheme from nearby government programmes.

22.s: Digital India completed ten years in:
22.x: Digital India was launched in 2015 and completed ten years in 2025.
22.tq: Calculate the milestone year from the launch year and confirm the stated figure.

22.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its Digital India pillar?
o: Early Harvest Programmes — long-term university research grants
IT for Jobs — skilling for IT and ITeS jobs
Information for All — Open Government Data platform
22.x: Early Harvest Programmes comprise quick-win projects such as biometric attendance and Wi-Fi in universities; they are not defined as long-term university research grants.
22.tq: Reject the option that swaps a pillar’s quick-win function with an unrelated activity.

22.s: The e-Kranti pillar of Digital India is associated with which of the following?
o: Universal biometric registration of all citizens
Manufacture of electronic goods to achieve net zero imports only
Electronic delivery of services through 44 Mission Mode Projects
Construction of rural roads through 44 projects
22.x: e-Kranti focuses on electronic delivery of services and includes 44 Mission Mode Projects.
22.tq: Identify the function that naturally belongs to the e-Kranti pillar.

22.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a Digital India vision area?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility — high-speed internet and cloud locker
Governance and services on demand — universal digital literacy only
Digital empowerment of citizens — GIS decision support only
Digital infrastructure as a core utility — cashless transactions only
22.x: High-speed internet, cradle-to-grave digital identity, Common Service Centre access and cloud locker are examples under digital infrastructure as a core utility.
22.tq: Match each example with the correct vision area rather than a neighbouring area.

22.s: The Digital India programme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on:
22.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 (APPSC 2025 key). 15 August 2014 and 25 September 2014 are associated with other announcements (Independence Day speech, Make in India), and 26 January 2016 is not its launch date.
22.tq: Digital India = 1 July 2015; 10 years in 2025.

22.s: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the Digital India programme?
22.x: Broadband Highways (pillar 1), e-Kranti (pillar 5) and Information for All (pillar 6) are pillars of Digital India. Issue of digital currency is not part of Digital India (APPSC 2024 key).
22.tq: Digital currency is RBI's domain, not a Digital India pillar.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about e-Kranti:
1. It is also known as NeGP 2.0.
2. It was approved in 2015 under Digital India.
3. It comprises 31 Mission Mode Projects.
4. Its vision is 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: e-Kranti is NeGP 2.0, approved in 2015 under Digital India, with the vision 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'. Statement 3 is wrong: e-Kranti has 44 MMPs; 31 is the expanded count of the original NeGP. So A is incomplete, and B and D include the wrong statement 3.
22.tq: NeGP: 27 → 31 MMPs; e-Kranti: 44 MMPs.

22.s: e-Kranti constitutes which pillar of Digital India?
22.x: e-Kranti is the fifth pillar of Digital India and concerns electronic delivery of services.
22.tq: Use the pillar-number distinction rather than confusing the initiative with the whole programme.

22.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle of e-Kranti?
22.x: The principles include transformation not translation, integrated not individual services, and cloud by default. Paper-first delivery is not an e-Kranti principle.
22.tq: Locate the one option that reverses the digital-first orientation.

22.s:
Which one of the following combinations contains only principles of e-Kranti?
1. Mobile first
2. Language localisation
3. Process re-engineering in every MMP
4. Cloud by default
22.x: Mobile first, language localisation, process re-engineering in every MMP and cloud by default are all stated principles of e-Kranti.
22.tq: Check whether every listed principle belongs to the same framework before selecting the all-inclusive code.

22.s:
Consider the following pairs of initiatives and launch years:
1. MyGov — July 2014
2. UPI and BHIM — 2016
3. UMANG — 2017
4. ONDC — 2020
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
22.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct: MyGov came in July 2014, UPI and BHIM in 2016, UMANG in 2017. Pair 4 is wrong: ONDC came in 2022; 2020 was PM eVIDYA. So A is incomplete, and C and D include the wrong pair 4.
22.tq: Ladder: Aadhaar 09, MyGov 14, DigiLocker 15, UPI 16, UMANG 17, eVIDYA 20, ONDC 22.

22.s: DigiLocker was launched in which year?
22.x: DigiLocker was launched in February 2015.
22.tq: Recall the year while avoiding confusion with adjacent digital initiatives.

22.s: PM eVIDYA was launched in 2020 primarily in the context of:
22.x: PM eVIDYA was launched in 2020 in response to the educational requirements arising during the pandemic.
22.tq: Link the initiative to its immediate context rather than its technology alone.

22.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
22.x: The DBT pilot was inaugurated on 1 January 2013. MyGov began in 2014, PM eVIDYA in 2020 and ONDC in 2022.
22.tq: Match each initiative with its exact year while rejecting near-year traps.

22.s: The correct chronological sequence of the following initiatives is: Aadhaar, MyGov, PM eVIDYA and ONDC.
22.x: Aadhaar was launched in 2009, MyGov in 2014, PM eVIDYA in 2020 and ONDC in 2022.
22.tq: Use the first and last items as chronological anchors before checking the middle pair.

22.s: Bhashini is best described as:
o: A biometric attendance system for universities
A digital locker for storing land records only
An AI language platform integrated with NIC tools such as CollabFiles
A network for electronic manufacturing units
22.x: Bhashini is an AI language platform integrated with NIC tools such as CollabFiles, supporting access to services in Indian languages.
22.tq: Use the exact function to distinguish Bhashini from other digital initiatives.

22.s: Which one of the following best describes India Stack?
o: A rural broadband project based exclusively on satellite connectivity
A manufacturing and investment promotion mission
A set of open and interoperable public digital rails including Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, CoWIN, ONDC and Account Aggregator
A closed government database used only for welfare payments
22.x: India Stack consists of open and interoperable public digital rails, including Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, CoWIN, ONDC and Account Aggregator.
22.tq: Identify the precise definition rather than a related digital mission.

22.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the three layers of India Stack:
1. Aadhaar represents the identity layer.
2. UPI represents the payments layer.
3. DEPA or Account Aggregator represents a consent-based data layer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: All three statements are correct: Aadhaar is the identity layer, UPI is the payments layer, and DEPA or Account Aggregator is the consent-based data layer.
22.tq: Match each layer with its exact digital function.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about UPI:
1. UPI is live in 11 countries.
2. The PayNow-UPI link was established with Singapore in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: UPI is live in 11 countries. Statement 2 is correct: PayNow is Singapore's system, linked with UPI in 2023. Hence both are correct; A, B and D are wrong.
22.tq: PayNow = Singapore.

22.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: DigiLocker — Public health and vaccination platform
22.x: Bhashini is the Translation Mission. DigiLocker is a cloud document wallet, CoWIN is a vaccination platform, and UPI/BHIM supports real-time payments.
22.tq: Start from the sure role-platform pair and eliminate swapped functions.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about BhashaNet:
1. It was unveiled on Universal Acceptance (UA) Day, 21 March 2024.
2. It was unveiled by NIXI and MeitY.
3. It is the Translation Mission launched in July 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: BhashaNet, the Universal Acceptance portal, was unveiled on UA Day, 21 March 2024, by NIXI and MeitY. Statement 3 is wrong: the Translation Mission of July 2022 is Bhashini, not BhashaNet. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
22.tq: BhashaNet = UA portal (NIXI); Bhashini = translation AI.

22.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Aarogya Setu and CoWIN from the other platforms listed?
o: They are public health and vaccination platforms.
They are cloud-based document storage platforms.
They are rural broadband connectivity platforms.
22.x: Aarogya Setu and CoWIN are public health and vaccination platforms.
22.tq: Discriminate between platforms by their functional domain.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about SWAYAM:
1. It offers free MOOCs for higher education, including courses from IITs, IIMs and central universities.
2. NPTEL is one of its national coordinators.
3. It is the national school e-content repository with QR-coded textbooks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: SWAYAM offers free higher-education MOOCs from IITs, IIMs and central universities. Statement 2 is correct: NPTEL is among its national coordinators (with UGC, AICTE, IGNOU, NCERT, NIOS, CEC). Statement 3 is wrong: the school repository with QR-coded textbooks is DIKSHA. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
22.tq: SWAYAM = higher-ed MOOCs; DIKSHA = school content.

22.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: DIKSHA — national school e-content repository with QR-coded textbooks and teacher training
SWAYAM — biometric attendance and Wi-Fi in universities
PM eVIDYA — only higher-education MOOCs from IITs
Bhashini — repository of QR-coded school textbooks
22.x: DIKSHA is the national school e-content repository and includes QR-coded textbooks and teacher training. The other descriptions belong to different platforms or programmes.
22.tq: Match each platform with its distinctive purpose and target group.

22.s: Which statement regarding PM eVIDYA is correct?
o: It provides One Class, One TV Channel through DTH, along with radio and podcasts, and integrates DIKSHA and SWAYAM.
It replaced all school e-content repositories with a single physical textbook system.
It is a platform exclusively for industrial BPO training.
It is restricted to bank and mobile KYC services.
22.x: PM eVIDYA uses the One Class, One TV Channel approach through DTH, radio and podcasts, and integrates DIKSHA and SWAYAM.
22.tq: Identify the option containing the complete service bundle of the platform.

22.s: UNESCO recognised India’s use of ICT in education during which period?
22.x: UNESCO recognised India’s use of ICT in education during the COVID-19 period.
22.tq: Connect the international recognition with its stated context.

22.s: Which combination best represents the major rural digital-divide gaps identified in the context of Digital India?
o: GP fibre connectivity through BharatNet and 4G coverage in villages
Only urban 5G availability and satellite television
Banking passwords and electronic voting machines
22.x: Rural digital gaps particularly concern Gram Panchayat fibre connectivity through BharatNet and 4G coverage in villages.
22.tq: Select the pair that directly addresses rural connectivity barriers.

22.s: Over the period referred to, UPI transaction volume increased approximately:
22.x: UPI transaction volume increased approximately 13,000-fold over the stated period, during which UPI became 10 years old.
22.tq: Preserve the exact magnitude and number of zeroes in a growth claim.

22.s: Aadhaar had reached more than how many people according to the cited indicator?
22.x: Aadhaar had reached more than 145 crore people.
22.tq: Distinguish crore-scale population figures by place value.

22.s: Approximately what proportion of the population was still offline according to the cited indicator?
22.x: Approximately 38% was still offline according to the cited indicator.
22.tq: Distinguish the remaining offline share from the share that came online.

22.s: Which statement best describes PMGDISHA?
o: It is a broadband fibre scheme targeting one Gram Panchayat per district.
It is a public Wi-Fi scheme targeting one device per village.
It is a rural digital literacy scheme targeting one person per household.
It is a vaccination platform targeting one dose per household.
22.x: PMGDISHA is a rural digital literacy scheme launched in 2017, with the aim of covering one person per household.
22.tq: Match the scheme's target group and objective rather than its digital-sounding name.

22.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NeSDA 2025 portal — launched by DARPG in June 2026
AP RTGS Data Lake — studied by a European delegation
e-Seva — introduced under the Make in India model
22.x: DARPG launched the NeSDA 2025 portal in June 2026. IVFRT was extended to 2031, a Singapore delegation studied AP's RTGS Data Lake and Command Centre, and AP pioneered e-Seva under the SMART governance model.
22.tq: Check each institutional actor, date and associated programme before selecting the fully correct pair.

22.s: The Immigration, Visa, Foreigners Registration and Tracking system (IVFRT) was extended up to:
22.x: IVFRT was extended up to 2031.
22.tq: Treat the terminal year as the key numerical distinction.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's e-governance:
1. A European Union delegation studied AP's RTGS Data Lake and Command Centre.
2. AP pioneered e-Seva under the SMART governance model.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is wrong: it was a Singapore delegation that studied AP's RTGS Data Lake and Command Centre (July 2026). Statement 2 is correct: AP pioneered e-Seva under the SMART governance model. Hence only 2 is correct; A, C and D are wrong.
22.tq: RTGS studied by Singapore; e-Seva = SMART model.

22.s: Which of the following represents the correct first-to-last sequence of major e-governance developments?
22.x: The sequence is NeGP in 2006, Digital India in 2015, and e-Kranti, or NeGP 2.0, in 2015.
22.tq: Use the first and last milestones to establish the sequence before resolving the two 2015 entries.

22.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism or debate associated with digital transformation?
o: Digital divide and data privacy concerns
Excessive dependence on paper records alone
Complete elimination of shared devices in rural areas
22.x: The identified concerns include the digital divide, shared devices in rural areas and data privacy.
22.tq: Select the substantive concern and reject absolute claims that deny the problem.

22.s: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) was reported to have raised the digital economy's share to approximately what proportion of GDP?
22.x: DPI was reported to have raised the digital economy's share to approximately 12–14% of GDP.
22.tq: Identify the correct range rather than a single approximate point estimate.

23.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Information Technology Act
B. National Informatics Centre
C. National e-Governance Plan
D. National Task Force on IT and Software Development
23.x: The milestones occurred in the order NIC in 1976, National Task Force in 1998, IT Act in 2000 and NeGP in 2006.
23.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 1998 and 2000 milestones between them.

23.s: C-DAC was set up at Pune in 1988 primarily to build the:
23.x: C-DAC was established at Pune in 1988 to build the PARAM supercomputer.
23.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive technology outcome.

23.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Information Technology Act, 2000 is correct?
1. It provided a legal basis for electronic records and digital signatures.
2. It was amended in 2008.
3. The 2008 amendment dealt, among other matters, with e-signatures and cybercrime.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: The IT Act, 2000 gave legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures, and its 2008 amendment addressed e-signatures and cybercrime-related provisions.
23.tq: Verify the legal function, amendment year and amendment subject together.

23.s: How many Mission Mode Projects are currently stated to operate under e-Kranti?
23.x: The stated number of Mission Mode Projects operating under e-Kranti is 44.
23.tq: Recall the exact programme count and distinguish it from policy targets measured in billions or millions.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Policy on Information Technology (NPIT), 2012:
1. It treats ICT as a driver of growth, jobs, governance reform and inclusion.
2. Its objectives include using ICT in education, health, skills, financial inclusion and governance, with e-literacy for all.
3. It sought to concentrate IT activity further in the six established hubs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statement 1 is correct: NPIT 2012 treats ICT as a driver of growth, jobs, governance reform and inclusion. Statement 2 is correct: its objectives cover ICT in education, health, skills, financial inclusion, governance and e-literacy for all. Statement 3 is wrong: the six hubs held ~90% of the industry and were near saturation, so NPIT pushed IT into Tier II and Tier III cities. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: Saturated hubs → spread to Tier II/III, never concentrate.

23.s:
The twin goals of the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 included which of the following?
1. Bringing the full power of ICT within reach of the whole of India
2. Making India a Global Hub and Destination for IT and ITES Services by 2020
3. Restricting IT services to six major metropolitan hubs
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: The twin goals were universal access to the benefits of ICT and making India a global hub and destination for IT and ITES services by 2020. Restricting IT to six metropolitan hubs was not a goal.
23.tq: Find the statement that reverses the policy’s inclusion and decentralisation objectives.

23.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian IT industry in 2011–12:
1. Approximately 80% of its revenue came from exports.
2. Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune and the NCR together accounted for nearly 90% of the industry.
3. These six hubs were considered to be near saturation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: All three statements are correct. The concentration and near-saturation of the six hubs encouraged the policy to promote IT in Tier II and Tier III cities.
23.tq: Use the complete cluster of baseline statistics and identify the option containing all correct statements.

23.s: The policy emphasis on Tier II and Tier III cities was primarily intended to:
o: Shift all IT institutions away from metropolitan areas
Reduce the export orientation of the IT industry
Expand IT activity beyond saturated major hubs
Restrict ITES services to state capitals
23.x: The policy sought to spread IT activity to Tier II and Tier III cities because the major established hubs were highly concentrated and nearing saturation.
23.tq: Link the policy measure to the problem it was designed to address.

23.s:
Which of the following initiatives are described as putting the vision of the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 into practice?
1. Digital India
2. Aadhaar
3. UPI
4. BharatNet
5. DigiLocker
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: Digital India, Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet and DigiLocker are all identified as initiatives that put the policy vision into practice.
23.tq: Check whether the comprehensive option correctly covers the full named list.

23.s: The target for IT-ITES revenue under the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 was to increase it from US$100 billion in 2012 to:
23.x: The policy target was to raise IT-ITES revenue from US$100 billion in 2012 to US$300 billion by 2020.
23.tq: Match the target year and target value, avoiding confusion with export and electronics figures.

23.s: The target for IT exports under the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 was:
o: An increase from US$100 billion to US$300 billion
An increase from US$190 billion to US$110 billion
An increase from US$69 billion to US$200 billion
An increase from US$69 billion to US$400 billion
23.x: The IT export target was to increase exports from US$69 billion to US$200 billion by 2020.
23.tq: Distinguish the export baseline and target from the separate IT-ITES revenue figures.

23.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the targets of the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012.

List-I (Target)
a. IT-ITES revenue
b. IT exports
c. Skilled manpower
d. E-literacy

List-II (Target by 2020)
i. At least one e-literate person in every household
ii. US$200 billion
iii. 10 million additional skilled ICT workers
iv. US$300 billion

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: IT-ITES revenue was targeted at US$300 billion; IT exports at US$200 billion; skilled manpower at 10 million additional workers; and e-literacy at one e-literate person in every household.
23.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes with mismatched categories.

23.s: India is regarded as one of the world's largest exporters of IT services. Which one of the following groups consists of Indian IT-service companies associated with this position?
23.x: TCS, Infosys and Wipro are identified as major Indian IT-service companies contributing to India's position as one of the world's largest IT-service exporters.
23.tq: Use the direct company-identification approach and distinguish service exporters from institutions and locations.

23.s: How many persons were employed by the IT and e-commerce sectors in 2022–23?
23.x: The IT and e-commerce sectors employed 14.67 million persons in 2022–23.
23.tq: Identify the exact employment figure and reject nearby numerical distractors.

23.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Global Capability Centres (GCCs):
1. They are offshore units operated by multinational corporations for their own functions.
2. Their activities may include engineering, research and development, and analytics.
3. They are the same as outsourcing vendors providing services to unrelated companies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. GCCs perform functions for their parent multinational corporations, whereas outsourcing vendors provide services to other organisations; therefore, statement 3 is false.
23.tq: Test the confusable distinction between captive multinational units and outsourcing vendors.

23.s: India's digital economy, currently about 12-14% of GDP, is projected to reach what share of GDP by 2029-30?
23.x: The digital economy is about 12-14% of GDP now and is projected to reach about 20% by 2029-30. 8% is below the current share, 14% is the current upper bound, and 35% overstates the projection.
23.tq: Digital economy: 12-14% now → 20% by 2029-30.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Policy on Electronics (NPE), 2019:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 20 February 2019.
2. It is a policy of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
3. It replaced the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NPE 2019 is a MeitY policy approved by the Cabinet on 20 February 2019. Statement 3 is wrong: NPE 2019 replaced NPE 2012, not NPIT 2012. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: NPE 2019 replaced NPE 2012 (same series); NPIT 2012 is a separate IT policy.

23.s: The principal aim of the National Policy on Electronics, 2019 was to make India a global hub for:
o: Only software exports without hardware production
23.x: NPE 2019 aimed to establish India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing, including chipsets.
23.tq: Choose the precise official scope rather than a software-only interpretation.

23.s:
Consider the following NPE 2019 targets for 2025:
1. Electronics manufacturing of US$400 billion
2. 1 billion mobile handsets a year, of which 600 million for export
3. Mobile exports of US$190 billion
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statement 1 is correct: US$400 billion (~₹26 lakh crore) electronics manufacturing. Statement 2 is correct: 1 billion handsets a year, 600 million for export. Statement 3 is wrong: US$190 billion is the mobile manufacturing value; mobile exports target is US$110 billion. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: Mobiles: make 190, export 110 (US$ bn).

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS):
1. It has an outlay of ₹62,500 crore for FY 2026-27 to 2030-31.
2. It replaces the PLI scheme for Large Scale Electronics.
3. It targets ₹39 lakh crore exports and ₹15 lakh crore production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: MPMS has ₹62,500 crore for FY 2026-27 to 2030-31 and replaces PLI (Large Scale Electronics). Statement 3 is wrong: the figures are reversed; targets are ₹39 lakh crore production and ₹15 lakh crore exports. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: Production is always the larger figure than exports.

23.s: Electronics production in India is stated to have reached what value in 2025–26?
23.x: Electronics production reached ₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025–26, described as sevenfold growth under PLI.
23.tq: Distinguish the achieved production figure from future scheme targets and policy estimates.

23.s: Electronics is stated to be India’s:
23.x: Electronics is stated to be India’s third-largest export item.
23.tq: Recall the ranking exactly and avoid upgrading a sector’s position to first or second.

23.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Scheme — Description
1. PLI — Large-scale electronics manufacturing
2. SPECS — Promotion of manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors
3. EMC 2.0 — Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters
4. MPMS — National e-Governance Plan Mission Mode Projects
23.x: MPMS is the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme; it is not a scheme for NeGP Mission Mode Projects. The first three pairs are correctly matched with NPE-related schemes.
23.tq: Find the single swapped programme description in a list of familiar schemes.

23.s: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) was launched in December 2021 under the:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
23.x: ISM was launched in December 2021 under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
23.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to identify the responsible ministry.

23.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the pillars of Semicon 2.0 and their support.

List-I (Pillar)
a. CMOS silicon fabs
b. Compound and display fabs
c. Advanced packaging
d. R&D

List-II (Maximum support)
i. 75% of project cost
ii. 35% capital subsidy
iii. 40% capital subsidy
iv. 35% support

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: CMOS silicon fabs receive up to 40% capital subsidy, compound and display fabs 35%, advanced packaging 35%, and R&D up to 75% of project cost.
23.tq: Start with the distinctive 75% R&D pair and then match the two fab subsidy rates.

23.s: Besides Fabs, Packaging and R&D, which of the following are the other two pillars of Semicon 2.0?
23.x: Design and Machines/Materials are the other two pillars in addition to Fabs, Packaging and R&D.
23.tq: Identify the remaining members of a classified list after excluding the familiar pillars.

23.s: RRP Electronics is associated with which of the following semiconductor facilities and locations?
o: Semiconductor and OSAT facility in Sri Sathya Sai district, Andhra Pradesh
First commercial fab at Dholera, Gujarat
23.x: RRP Electronics is associated with a semiconductor and OSAT facility in Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh.
23.tq: Discriminate the newer Andhra Pradesh entry from the Gujarat and Assam facilities.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chips to Start-up (C2S) programme:
1. It was launched in 2022 to build chip-design talent.
2. It targets 85,000 B.Tech, M.Tech and PhD students over five years.
3. It is implemented by NIELIT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: C2S (2022) builds chip-design talent, targeting 85,000 B.Tech/M.Tech/PhD students over five years. Statement 3 is wrong: C2S is implemented by C-DAC, not NIELIT. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: C2S → C-DAC (both start with C).

23.s: Which of the following semiconductor units is correctly matched with its company and location?
23.x: Tata's (TSAT) OSAT unit is at Jagiroad, Assam. The ATMP unit at Sanand, Gujarat belongs to Micron, not Tata (A), Micron is not at Jagiroad (B), and RRP Electronics is in Sri Sathya Sai district, AP (D).
23.tq: Micron–Sanand (ATMP); Tata–Jagiroad (OSAT); RRP–Sri Sathya Sai (AP).

23.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding IT institutions and their roles.

List-I (Institution)
a. MeitY
b. NASSCOM
c. STPI
d. NIC

List-II (Role)
i. Government IT/e-governance network and services
ii. Industry association of IT-BPM firms and partner in IoT CoEs
iii. Policy on IT, electronics, internet and cyber security; coordinates Digital India
iv. Export-oriented IT parks under MeitY and CoEs

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: MeitY handles policy and Digital India coordination; NASSCOM represents IT-BPM firms and partners in IoT CoEs; STPI runs export-oriented parks and CoEs; NIC provides government IT and e-governance services.
23.tq: Start with the distinctive NIC network role and eliminate codes with swapped institutional functions.

23.s: Which of the following is a stated role of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)?
o: Licensing all Internet Service Providers exclusively
Formulating policy on IT, electronics, internet except ISP licensing, and cyber security
23.x: MeitY handles policy on IT, electronics, the internet other than ISP licensing, and cyber security, and coordinates Digital India.
23.tq: Watch the explicit exception concerning ISP licensing while identifying the ministry’s policy role.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about C-DAC:
1. It has an R&D role involving PARAM supercomputers.
2. It implements the Chips to Start-up programme.
3. It has a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: C-DAC’s stated roles include R&D involving PARAM supercomputers, implementation of C2S and a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.
23.tq: Combine the institution’s historical R&D role with its current programme and location associations.

23.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with NIELIT?
o: Government e-governance network; national IT services
Industry association of IT-BPM firms; IoT CoEs
Deemed-to-be University under MeitY; IT and electronics training
Export-oriented IT parks; software export promotion
23.x: NIELIT is described as a deemed-to-be University under MeitY and is associated with IT and electronics training.
23.tq: Use the institutional status and training role together to distinguish NIELIT from allied bodies.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP IT & Global Capability Centers (GCC) Policy (4.0):
1. It covers the period 2024-29.
2. It came into force on 12 December 2024 for five years.
3. Its aim is to make Andhra Pradesh mainly a semiconductor manufacturing state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the policy covers 2024-29 and came into force on 12 December 2024 for five years. Statement 3 is wrong: its aim is to make AP a global knowledge economy hub and an IT and GCC powerhouse. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: AP IT & GCC 4.0: 2024-29, from 12 Dec 2024, knowledge-economy hub.

23.s: Which combination correctly identifies the workspaces promoted under the AP IT & Global Capability Centers (GCC) Policy 4.0?
o: IT parks, co-working spaces and neighbourhood workspaces
Only large industrial estates and export-processing zones
Data centres, semiconductor fabs and university laboratories only
Quantum campuses, cable landing stations and NIELIT centres
23.x: The policy promotes IT parks, co-working spaces and neighbourhood workspaces.
23.tq: Match the policy feature with its complete list rather than with associated infrastructure projects.

23.s: The Andhra Pradesh Data Centre Policy provides for adding data-centre capacity of up to:
23.x: The AP Data Centre Policy provides for adding up to 1 GW of data-centre capacity.
23.tq: Convert the stated capacity into the exact quantitative answer and watch the MW–GW scale distinction.

23.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with Visakhapatnam's information-technology initiatives?
o: Quantum Valley, NIELIT Quantum campus and Acharya Nagarjuna University classes
AI data projects with Anakapalli, a cable landing station, and an Infosys campus
NIELIT centre at Sri Venkateswara University and a 1 GW data-centre addition
Only a semiconductor research facility and a neighbourhood workspace
23.x: Visakhapatnam is associated with AI data projects with Anakapalli, a cable landing station and an Infosys campus expected to create about 7,000 jobs.
23.tq: Use location-based matching to separate Visakhapatnam initiatives from Tirupati and Amaravati projects.

23.s: The MeitY–NASSCOM IoT Centre of Excellence is associated with which city in Andhra Pradesh?
23.x: The MeitY–NASSCOM IoT Centre of Excellence is listed among the technology initiatives associated with Visakhapatnam.
23.tq: Identify the correct location by separating city-level projects from nearby district-level initiatives.

23.s: The 'Quantum Valley' in Andhra Pradesh, with a C-DAC centre, is being developed at:
23.x: Quantum Valley is at Amaravati, with a C-DAC centre. Visakhapatnam hosts the cable landing station, Infosys campus and IoT CoE; Anakapalli is linked with AI data projects; Tirupati is not named for it.
23.tq: Quantum = Amaravati; IoT CoE & cable landing = Vizag.

23.s: Which of the following correctly describes the policy developments identified as replacing the NPE-era schemes?
23.x: Semicon 2.0 (September 2026) and the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme, MPMS (August 2026), replace the NPE-era schemes; MPMS replaces the PLI scheme for Large Scale Electronics. GCC 4.0, Quantum Valley, IoT CoE, Digital India and SWAYAM are not replacements for NPE schemes.
23.tq: Discriminate between current policy labels and project or institution names.

23.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the criticism and continuing challenges associated with information-technology development:
1. Hub concentration and saturation were issues that NPIT sought to address.
2. Approximately 38% of the population remains offline.
3. These issues indicate that digital access has become universal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the continuing offline population shows that digital access is not yet universal.
23.tq: Find the false inference created by an extreme conclusion such as universal access.

23.s: In one Andhra Pradesh Cabinet round, the IT and electronics sectors attracted investment of more than:
23.x: IT and electronics attracted more than ₹18,210 crore in one Andhra Pradesh Cabinet round.
23.tq: Identify the exact investment magnitude and reject altered leading digits.

24.s: Which of the following correctly represents the four phases of the Gartner model?
24.x: The four Gartner phases are Information, Interaction, Transaction and Transformation, in that order.
24.tq: Recall the exact ordered framework rather than merely identifying its individual terms.

24.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Open Government Data — DBT for LPG subsidy
24.x: G2E is illustrated by CEMS, an employee-management system. G2P is illustrated by DBT, Open Government Data by data.gov.in, and m-Governance by services such as mPassport Seva and UMANG.
24.tq: Match each governance relationship with its specific example.

24.s: Which of the following is an example of G2P (Government-to-Person) service?
o: DBT for LPG subsidy and pensions
24.x: Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG subsidies and pensions is an example of G2P service delivery.
24.tq: Infer the relationship from the recipient of the service or benefit.

24.s: Which one of the following is associated with m-Governance?
o: Data Lake and Data Lens only
24.x: mPassport Seva and UMANG are examples of m-Governance. The m-Governance framework dates to 2012, while MSDG dates to 2011.
24.tq: Identify the mobile-governance examples and distinguish them from infrastructure platforms.

24.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three vision areas of Digital India mentioned below?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility
24.x: The three listed Digital India vision areas are digital infrastructure as a core utility, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens.
24.tq: Reject an extreme policy claim that is outside the stated vision areas.

24.s: Which of the following best expresses the role of ICT in e-governance?
o: It prevents real-time monitoring of public services.
It enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery.
It replaces all government institutions with private agencies.
It limits citizen participation to physical offices.
24.x: ICT enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery, including through transparency and real-time monitoring.
24.tq: Choose the option that states the positive functional role rather than an absolute consequence.

24.s: The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was formulated by which of the following combination of organisations?
24.x: The National e-Governance Plan was formulated by DeitY, now MeitY, in association with DARPG.
24.tq: Identify the agencies directly associated with formulation rather than implementation.

24.s:
With reference to the original structure of the National e-Governance Plan, consider the following statements:
1. It consisted of 27 Mission Mode Projects and 10 components.
2. The Mission Mode Projects were divided into 9 Central, 11 State and 7 Integrated projects.
3. The original plan contained 44 Mission Mode Projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: The original NeGP contained 27 MMPs and 10 components, divided into 9 Central, 11 State and 7 Integrated projects. The figure of 44 relates to e-Kranti, not the original plan.
24.tq: Separate the original structure from the later expanded figures.

24.s: Which one of the following is an Integrated Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan?
24.x: e-Courts is identified as an Integrated MMP. e-Panchayat is an MMP, while IT for Jobs and Early Harvest Programmes are Digital India pillars.
24.tq: Use the category distinction between NeGP MMPs and Digital India pillars.

24.s: Which of the following most accurately expresses the vision of the National e-Governance Plan?
o: To centralise all government files in the national capital
To make all government services accessible to the common man in his locality through common service delivery outlets
To replace all public authorities with private digital platforms
To restrict government services to mobile applications
24.x: NeGP aimed to make government services accessible locally through common service delivery outlets, with transparency, reliability, efficiency and affordable cost.
24.tq: Choose the option that retains the plan’s locality, access and service-delivery elements.

24.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of e-Kranti?
o: Integration of cloud, mobile and geospatial technologies
24.x: e-Kranti is integrated, outcome-oriented, fast and agile; it does not depend exclusively on paper-based files.
24.tq: Identify the option that reverses the digital and integrated character of the programme.

24.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: e-Courts — Ministry of Commerce and Industry — 2016
24.x: e-Courts is an Integrated Mission Mode Project under NeGP, not a Ministry of Commerce and Industry programme of 2016, so this pair is wrong. e-Panchayat is an MMP, IVFRT is an MHA MMP of 2010 and CCTNS an MHA MMP of 2009.
24.tq: Find the option that swaps the responsible ministry and adds an unsupported launch detail.

24.s: The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was approved by the Government of India on:
24.x: NeGP was approved on 18 May 2006. 1 July 2015 is the Digital India launch, 25 March 2015 is PRAGATI's launch, and 2001 is the year AP's e-Seva began; none is NeGP's approval.
24.tq: NeGP = 18 May 2006.

24.s: e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0) differs from the original NeGP in that it:
o: Has 44 Mission Mode Projects and is a pillar of Digital India
Has 27 Mission Mode Projects and is a stand-alone national plan
Has 31 Mission Mode Projects and replaced Digital India
Has 10 Mission Mode Projects run only by States
24.x: e-Kranti has 44 MMPs and is a pillar of Digital India. 27 MMPs in a stand-alone plan describes the original NeGP 2006; 31 is the later expanded NeGP count; 10 is the number of NeGP components, not e-Kranti MMPs.
24.tq: NeGP 27 (stand-alone) → e-Kranti 44 (Digital India pillar).

24.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as core infrastructure of the National e-Governance Plan?
24.x: State Data Centres, SWAN and village-level Common Service Centres formed the core infrastructure of NeGP. The National Investment and Infrastructure Fund is unrelated to this framework.
24.tq: Find the unrelated institutional component among the three stated infrastructure pillars.

24.s: Common Service Centres are generally operated by Village Level Entrepreneurs and extend down to the level of:
24.x: CSCs are operated by Village Level Entrepreneurs and reach down to the Gram Panchayat level.
24.tq: Use the delivery-chain endpoint to distinguish grassroots access from higher administrative levels.

24.s: Which of the following is NOT among the broad categories of services delivered through Common Service Centres?
24.x: CSCs provide more than 400 services, including government, financial, Aadhaar, welfare, education, telemedicine, travel and utility-bill services. Constitutional amendment drafting is not a listed CSC service.
24.tq: Find the single function outside the established service basket rather than choosing a familiar CSC category.

24.s: As of April 2025, which of the following figures correctly represents the number of functional Common Service Centres and those at Gram Panchayat level, respectively?
24.x: There were 5.97 lakh functional CSCs, of which 4.73 lakh were at the Gram Panchayat level as of April 2025.
24.tq: Read the larger total first and distinguish it from the included Gram Panchayat-level subset.

24.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its role in NeGP infrastructure?
o: SDC — converged backbone for data, voice and video
CSC — hosts State e-governance applications and data
24.x: Common Service Centres are village-level front-end delivery outlets. SWAN is the converged backbone network, while SDC hosts State e-governance applications and data.
24.tq: Match each infrastructure pillar with its functional layer.

24.s: Which of the following correctly represents the relationship among G2G, G2C and G2B services and NeGP infrastructure?
o: They are enabled only by CSCs without any network or hosting infrastructure.
They are enabled together by SWAN, SDC and CSC.
They refer exclusively to mobile governance applications.
They are unrelated to State Data Centres.
24.x: SWAN, State Data Centres and Common Service Centres together enable seamless Government-to-Government, Government-to-Citizen and Government-to-Business services.
24.tq: Link each service relationship to the complete infrastructure stack instead of one component alone.

24.s: Government cloud hosting for e-governance applications in India is now provided by:
24.x: MeghRaj, the GI Cloud, now provides government cloud hosting. SWAN is the state backbone network, e-Taal gives e-transaction statistics, and CSCs are village-level front-end outlets.
24.tq: Cloud = MeghRaj (GI Cloud).

24.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. UMANG provides access to services of central, state and local governments through one mobile application.
2. DigiLocker is primarily a cloud locker for digital documents.
3. e-Sign enables Aadhaar-based signing of electronic documents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: All three statements are correct. UMANG is a unified service app, DigiLocker stores documents, and e-Sign facilitates Aadhaar-based electronic signatures.
24.tq: Match each platform with its distinctive core service before selecting the coded combination.

24.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
24.x: e-Pramaan is the national e-Authentication framework. SARATHI concerns driving licences, VAHAN concerns vehicle registration, and Bhavishya is an integrated pensioners’ portal.
24.tq: Check the precise function of each neighbouring transport, pension and authentication platform.

24.s: Meri Pehchaan is associated with which of the following?
o: A digital life certificate service for pensioners
A national single sign-on service integrating 15,024 services
A national telemedicine service for remote consultations
24.x: Meri Pehchaan is a MeitY single sign-on service, with 15,024 services integrated. Its backend includes Parichay or Jan-Parichay, e-Pramaan and DigiLocker.
24.tq: Use the stated scale and backend relationship to identify the single-sign-on platform.

24.s: MyGov, launched in 2014, is primarily a platform for:
24.x: MyGov is a MeitY citizen-engagement platform focused on participation and engagement relating to government policy.
24.tq: Identify the platform by its participatory policy function rather than by a transactional service.

24.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Platform)
a. UMANG
b. e-Office
c. GeM
d. CPGRAMS
List-II (Ministry or body)
i. DARPG
 ii. MeitY
 iii. Ministry of Commerce and Industry
 iv. MeitY through the NIC platform
24.x: UMANG is under MeitY; e-Office is a MeitY-NIC platform; GeM belongs to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; CPGRAMS is associated with DARPG.
24.tq: Start with CPGRAMS–DARPG and GeM–Commerce, then resolve the two MeitY-related pairs.

24.s: Jeevan Pramaan is associated with:
o: Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificates for pensioners
24.x: Jeevan Pramaan is a MeitY initiative providing Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificates for pensioners.
24.tq: Identify the beneficiary group and authentication method of the pension-related service.

24.s: PRAGATI, launched on 25 March 2015, is associated with:
o: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs and company registration
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry and public procurement
The Prime Minister’s Office and proactive governance, grievance handling and project monitoring
24.x: PRAGATI is associated with the PMO and stands for Pro-Active Governance And Timely Implementation; it deals with grievances and project monitoring.
24.tq: Use the acronym, launch date and institutional setting together to identify the programme.

24.s: e-Taal 3.0 is related to:
o: Digital signatures based only on paper certificates
24.x: e-Taal 3.0, operated by NIC and MeitY, provides statistics on e-transactions and e-services.
24.tq: Identify the monitoring-and-statistics platform rather than a citizen-service delivery portal.

24.s: A citizen who wants to apply online for a new driving licence would use which portal of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways?
24.x: SARATHI handles driving licence applications. VAHAN is for vehicle registration (the classic trap), Bhavishya is the pensioners' portal, and e-Pramaan is the national e-authentication framework.
24.tq: SARATHI = licence (driver); VAHAN = vehicle.

24.s: Which platform functions as a cloud locker for storing digital documents and was launched in February 2015?
24.x: DigiLocker is MeitY’s cloud-based document locker, launched in February 2015.
24.tq: Use the service-function association to distinguish document storage from authentication and pension services.

24.s:
Which of the following statements regarding DigiLocker is correct?
1. It provides each citizen with a cloud account linked to Aadhaar.
2. Driving licences and vehicle Registration Certificates can be included in it.

25.tq: Use direct person-identification recall.

25.s: Tembhli village, associated with the first Aadhaar number, is located in:
25.x: Tembhli village in Nandurbar district of Maharashtra was the first Aadhaar village and was the place where the first Aadhaar number was issued.
25.tq: Combine person, place and district carefully to avoid location swaps.

25.s: Aadhaar was launched in:
25.x: Aadhaar was launched in 2009, while the first Aadhaar number was issued in 2010.
25.tq: Discriminate between the launch year and the first-number year.

25.s:
With reference to UIDAI, consider the following statements:
1. UIDAI became a statutory body under the Aadhaar Act, 2016.
2. UIDAI works under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
3. The Aadhaar Act was amended in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
25.x: All three statements are correct. UIDAI became statutory under the Aadhaar Act, 2016, functions under MeitY, and the Act was amended in 2019.
25.tq: Check each institutional statement before selecting the complete combination.

25.s:
The Aadhaar Act primarily covers which of the following functions?
1. Enrolment
2. Authentication
3. Targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services
Select the correct answer using the code below.
25.x: The Aadhaar Act covers enrolment, authentication and targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services.
25.tq: Test the full statutory scope rather than one isolated function.

25.s: Which of the following correctly represents the biometric information captured for Aadhaar?
o: Ten fingerprints, two iris scans and a face photograph
Eight fingerprints, one iris scan and a voice sample
Ten fingerprints, two iris scans and a DNA sample
All biometric traits without any facial photograph
25.x: Aadhaar captures ten fingerprints, two irises and a face photograph.
25.tq: Use the exact numerical combination in a biometric list.

25.s: Which of the following statements regarding open APIs and Aadhaar is correct?
o: API Setu was developed by NPCI exclusively for card payments.
Aadhaar e-KYC can be used only for election-related services.
The Policy on Open APIs was issued by RBI in 2015 and prohibited integration with public services.
MeitY's Policy on Open APIs, 2015, led to API Setu; Aadhaar e-KYC simplified banking and public services.
25.x: MeitY's Policy on Open APIs, 2015, led to API Setu. Aadhaar e-KYC simplified banking and public services.
25.tq: Identify the correct authority, year and practical application together.

25.s: UPI was launched in April 2016 by:
25.x: The Unified Payments Interface was launched in April 2016 by NPCI.
25.tq: Apply the who-launched-what institutional trap.

25.s: Which one of the following best describes the functioning of UPI?
o: It permits cash withdrawals only through Aadhaar-enabled micro-ATMs.
It permits a single application to route payments from several bank accounts using a VPA such as name@bank.
It is a wallet system that operates without bank accounts or virtual payment addresses.
It is a card network that cannot link more than one bank account.
25.x: UPI allows one application to route payments from several bank accounts through a Virtual Payment Address such as name@bank.
25.tq: Match the digital-payment mechanism with its defining operational feature.

25.s:
Which of the following features is associated with UPI 2.0?
1. Linking of overdraft accounts
2. Pre-authorised payments
3. Signed merchant QR codes
4. A daily limit of Rs 2 lakh
Select the correct answer using the code below.
25.x: UPI 2.0 includes overdraft-account linking, pre-authorised payments, signed merchant QR codes and a daily limit of Rs 2 lakh.
25.tq: Recognise a complete feature set and avoid omitting the numerical limit.

25.s: Which product is correctly matched with its description?
o: BHIM — NPCI's UPI app launched on 30 December 2016
e-RUPI — a permanent cash transfer account with no specified purpose
UPI Lite — a large-value payment system requiring a UPI PIN for every transaction
Bharat QR — a non-interoperable QR code restricted to one card network
25.x: BHIM is NPCI's UPI app and was launched on 30 December 2016. Bharat QR is interoperable, UPI Lite is designed for small-value payments without a UPI PIN, and e-RUPI is a one-time purpose-specific voucher.
25.tq: Find the correctly matched product while rejecting swapped or reversed descriptions.

25.s:
Consider the following statements about e-RUPI:
1. It is a one-time, cashless, person- and purpose-specific voucher.
2. It was developed by NPCI with the Department of Financial Services, MoHFW and the National Health Authority.
3. It was launched on 30 December 2016 as part of the post-demonetisation push.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
25.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: e-RUPI was launched in August 2021; 30 December 2016 is the launch date of BHIM. Hence '1 only' is incomplete and the options containing 3 are wrong.
25.tq: 30 Dec 2016 = BHIM; Aug 2021 = e-RUPI.

25.s: Which country was the first in Europe to accept UPI?
25.x: France was the first country in Europe to accept UPI.
25.tq: Use geographical discrimination among named international UPI markets.

25.s: The PayNow-UPI linkage was established between India and Singapore in:
25.x: The PayNow-UPI linkage between India and Singapore was established in 2023.
25.tq: Distinguish the bilateral-link year from the wider international acceptance facts.

25.s: UPI accounted for approximately what share of digital payments by volume in FY 2025–26?
25.x: UPI accounted for approximately 85% of digital payments by volume in FY 2025–26.
25.tq: Recall the reported percentage and distinguish it from UPI's global real-time-payment share.

25.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
25.x: NEFT and RTGS are operated by RBI. IMPS and UPI are NPCI products, wallets are issued by RBI-authorised banks and non-banks, and BBPS is operated by NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd.
25.tq: Start from the sure operator-authority pair and reject neighbouring-body swaps.

25.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
25.x: FASTag (NETC) is operated by NPCI with NHAI and IHMCL, not by RBI alone. IMPS, AePS and RuPay are NPCI-operated systems.
25.tq: Find the wrong operator by checking the authority responsible for each system.

25.s: AePS enables which of the following through micro-ATMs?
o: Only cheque clearing between RBI offices
Only international card settlement without identity verification
Issuance of government bonds through a QR code
Cash withdrawal and balance enquiry using Aadhaar
25.x: AePS enables cash withdrawal and balance enquiry at micro-ATMs using Aadhaar-based authentication.
25.tq: Link the payment product with its practical service and authentication method.

25.s: Bharat BillPay (BBPS) is operated by:
25.x: BBPS is operated by NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd.
25.tq: Identify the operating entity rather than the regulator or end-use organisation.

25.s:
With reference to RBI's New Umbrella Entities (NUEs), consider the following statements:
1. They are meant to end NPCI's monopoly in retail payments.
2. The minimum capital required for an NUE is Rs 100 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
25.x: Statement 1 is correct: NUEs are RBI's move to end NPCI's monopoly in retail payments. Statement 2 is wrong: the minimum capital is Rs 500 crore, not Rs 100 crore. So '2 only' and 'Both' are wrong, and 'Neither' ignores the correct statement 1.
25.tq: NUE: anti-NPCI-monopoly, Rs 500 crore capital.

25.s: At present, the nodal responsibility for digital payments rests with:
o: MeitY under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
NPCI under the Ministry of Railways
Department of Financial Services under the Ministry of Finance
RBI under the Ministry of Commerce
25.x: Digital payments currently come under the Department of Financial Services in the Ministry of Finance, which also gives the Digital Payments Awards. Earlier, MeitY was the nodal department for promoting digital payments.
25.tq: Distinguish present responsibility from the earlier nodal arrangement.

25.s:
The Digital Payments Index of RBI has which of the following characteristics?
1. Its base period is March 2018.
2. The base value is 100.
3. It is published half-yearly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
25.x: The RBI Digital Payments Index uses March 2018 as its base period with a base value of 100 and is published half-yearly.
25.tq: Verify the base period, base value and publication frequency as separate facts.

25.s: The 'iPay' payment gateway is operated by:
25.x: iPay is IRCTC's own payment gateway. NPCI runs UPI, IMPS, AePS and BBPS; RBI runs NEFT and RTGS; NHAI is linked with FASTag, not iPay.
25.tq: iPay = IRCTC (rail tickets).

25.s: The first major application of JAM was associated with which scheme?
25.x: PAHAL, the LPG subsidy scheme, was the first application of JAM.
25.tq: Use the scheme-purpose pair to distinguish DBT from other digital initiatives.

25.s:
DBT payments are routed through which of the following mechanisms?
1. CPSMS, now PFMS
2. NPCI’s Aadhaar Payment Bridge
3. ONDC’s e-commerce network
4. DEPA consent architecture
25.x: DBT routing uses CPSMS, now known as PFMS, and NPCI’s Aadhaar Payment Bridge. ONDC and DEPA serve different digital functions.
25.tq: Identify the actual payment-routing mechanisms and reject neighbouring digital platforms.

25.s: The DBT Mission is presently located in the:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
25.x: The DBT Mission is now located in the Cabinet Secretariat.
25.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the coordinating authority.

25.s: The coverage of Direct Benefit Transfer extends to more than:
25.x: DBT covers more than 300 central schemes.
25.tq: Select the correct order of magnitude rather than a superficially similar figure.

25.s: By May 2025, the cumulative amount transferred through DBT was reported to be approximately:
25.x: The cumulative amount transferred through DBT was reported as approximately Rs 44 lakh crore by May 2025.
25.tq: Separate the cumulative transfer figure from the savings and deposit figures.

25.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported gender composition of PMJDY accounts?
o: Less than one-fourth were held by women
Exactly half were held by women
More than half were held by women
Women were not included as account holders
25.x: More than half of PMJDY accounts were reported to be held by women.
25.tq: Distinguish a qualitative majority from an exact numerical proportion.

25.s: Which of the following correctly states the inauguration details of DBT in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It was inaugurated at Amaravati on 6 January 2016 by UIDAI.
It was inaugurated at Tembhli, Maharashtra, on 29 September 2010.
It was inaugurated at Gollaprolu, East Godavari, on 6 January 2013.
It was inaugurated at Gollaprolu on 1 January 2014 by NPCI.
25.x: DBT was inaugurated at Gollaprolu in East Godavari on 6 January 2013 by Jairam Ramesh along with Chief Minister Kiran Kumar Reddy.
25.tq: Combine venue, district, date and associated persons without swapping the event with Aadhaar.

25.s: Which of the following correctly describes e-Seva in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It is an NPCI payment network established in 2016.
It was launched in 2019 as a replacement for Aadhaar enrolment.
It was launched in 2001 as India's first integrated citizen service centres.
It was the first Aadhaar village in Maharashtra.
25.x: e-Seva was introduced in 2001 and constituted the first integrated citizen service centres in India.
25.tq: Distinguish the AP service-delivery platform from later systems and national payment networks.

25.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the recent relevance of UPI?
o: It accounted for 49% of the world’s real-time payments and recorded a FY 2025–26 high.
It was limited to offline transactions during FY 2025–26.
It accounted for 49% of India’s GDP and had no global share.
It was replaced by ONDC as the principal real-time payment system.
25.x: UPI recorded a FY 2025–26 record and accounted for 49 percent of the world’s real-time payments.
25.tq: Separate the global real-time-payment share from unrelated GDP and platform figures.

25.s:
Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate concerning digital public infrastructure?
1. Biometric failures that may exclude elderly persons and labourers
2. Privacy and data-centralisation concerns
3. The digital divide
4. Guaranteed universal access without any implementation challenge
25.x: Biometric exclusion, privacy and data-centralisation concerns, and the digital divide are identified criticisms. Guaranteed universal access without implementation challenges is not a criticism or debate.
25.tq: Find the statement that reverses the direction of the documented criticism.

26.s: The National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN), later associated with BharatNet, was approved on 25 October 2011 with an initial target of connecting:
26.x: NOFN was approved on 25 October 2011 with the objective of connecting 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
26.tq: Recall the original programme name, date and numerical target together.

26.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional history of BharatNet's special purpose vehicle?
o: BBNL was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with BSNL in February 2023.
BBNL was registered on 25 October 2011 and merged with RailTel in February 2023.
BBNL was registered in February 2023 and merged with BSNL in 2012.
BBNL was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with PGCIL in February 2024.
26.x: Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL) was registered on 25 February 2012 and merged with BSNL in February 2023.
26.tq: Use the sequence of registration and merger to reject swapped dates and organisations.

26.s: BharatNet has been laid by which group of Central Public Sector Undertakings?
26.x: The BharatNet network has been laid by the CPSUs BSNL, RailTel and Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL).
26.tq: Identify the correct implementing-agency combination rather than a related ministry or institution.

26.s: The target bandwidth under BharatNet is:
o: 10 Mbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 100 Mbps
100 Mbps per village, fixed without scalability
100 Mbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 1 Gbps
1 Gbps per gram panchayat, scalable to 10 Gbps
26.x: BharatNet targets 100 Mbps for each gram panchayat, with scalability up to 1 Gbps.
26.tq: Distinguish the base capacity from the scalable capacity in a two-number technical target.

26.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Phases I and II of BharatNet?
o: They focused on fibre connectivity to gram panchayats through CPSUs and States.
They focused exclusively on upgrading 480 new gram panchayats.
They were limited to last-mile Wi-Fi through private cloud providers.
They primarily introduced a PPP model with revenue sharing and 5G links.
26.x: Phases I and II, beginning from 2011, focused on providing fibre connectivity to gram panchayats through CPSUs and States.
26.tq: Separate the focus of the earlier phases from the features of the amended programme.

26.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature associated with Phase III or the Amended BharatNet Programme?
o: Exclusive implementation through CPSUs without private participation
Revenue sharing and last-mile links with 5G
26.x: The Amended BharatNet Programme provides for a PPP model, a greater role for States, revenue sharing, last-mile connectivity and links with 5G. It is not exclusively implemented through CPSUs without private participation.
26.tq: Find the option that contradicts the distinguishing features of the amended phase.

26.s: The approved outlay associated with Phase III or the Amended BharatNet Programme is:
26.x: The Amended BharatNet Programme is associated with an outlay of Rs 1.39 lakh crore.
26.tq: Distinguish the programme-wide outlay from the separate Andhra Pradesh commitment.

26.s: In February 2026, Andhra Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Cooperation under the Amended BharatNet Programme. Which of the following statements about it is correct?
o: It was signed with the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator and covers 13,426 village panchayats.
It was signed with BSNL and covers 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
It was signed with RailTel and covers only 480 new gram panchayats.
It was signed with MeitY and is implemented by AP FiberNet as the Central SPV.
26.x: The MoC (22 Feb 2026, Amaravati) was signed between the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator and the AP government for 13,426 village panchayats, with the Centre committing Rs 2,432 crore and the state SPV being Andhra Pradesh BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd. 2.5 lakh GPs was the original NOFN target; 480 new GPs is only one part of the scope; the SPV is a state SPV, not a Central one.
26.tq: AP ABP MoC = DBN + 13,426 panchayats + Rs 2,432 cr.

26.s: The Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) was primarily intended to support telecommunications in:
o: commercially unviable rural and remote areas
government offices located only in State capitals
foreign markets with high private investment
26.x: USOF is a non-lapsable fund intended to support telecommunications in commercially unviable rural and remote areas.
26.tq: Apply the purpose of a public connectivity fund to an area-selection scenario.

26.s: Which of the following statements about USOF and Digital Bharat Nidhi is correct?
o: USOF was renamed Digital Bharat Nidhi under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and it funded NOFN.
Digital Bharat Nidhi was renamed USOF under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and it funded PMGDISHA.
USOF is a lapsable fund used only for urban 5G deployment.
Digital Bharat Nidhi is administered only by State governments and has no relation to BharatNet.
26.x: USOF funded NOFN and was renamed Digital Bharat Nidhi under the Telecommunications Act, 2023. Digital Bharat Nidhi also runs the Amended BharatNet Memoranda of Cooperation.
26.tq: Track the renaming direction and distinguish the fund's actual connectivity uses.

26.s: The Memoranda of Cooperation for the Amended BharatNet Programme are run through which fund?
26.x: Digital Bharat Nidhi runs the Memoranda of Cooperation for the Amended BharatNet Programme.
26.tq: Identify the funding channel linked to a specific infrastructure programme.

26.s: Which of the following correctly describes PM-WANI?
o: A digital-literacy programme launched in December 2020, covering 6 crore households.
A fibre-laying programme launched in October 2011, covering 2.5 lakh gram panchayats.
A cloud deployment model launched in March 2024, with 3.15 crore applications.
A public Wi-Fi programme launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots reported.
26.x: PM-WANI is a public Wi-Fi initiative launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots reported.
26.tq: Separate the programme's technology, launch date and scale from other digital initiatives.

26.s: Under the Digital Bharat Nidhi, 5% of collections (about Rs 500 crore a year) is allocated to which of the following?
26.x: 5% of DBN collections (~Rs 500 crore a year) goes to the Telecom Technology Development Fund. PM-WANI is a public Wi-Fi programme, PMGDISHA is a digital-literacy scheme and MeghRaj is the government cloud; none is the stated destination of this 5%.
26.tq: DBN 5% -> TTDF.

26.s: MeghRaj refers to which of the following?
o: A public Wi-Fi programme initiated by DoT
A rural optical-fibre programme initiated by BSNL
The GI Cloud initiated by DeitY
A digital-literacy mission initiated by NCERT
26.x: MeghRaj is the GI Cloud initiative started by the Department of Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY).
26.tq: Expand and identify the exact identity and originating authority of an ICT initiative.

26.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five characteristics of cloud computing identified under MeghRaj?
o: Mandatory physical installation for every user
26.x: The five characteristics are on-demand self-service, ubiquitous network access, metered use, elasticity and resource pooling. Mandatory physical installation for every user is not one of them.
26.tq: Find the non-cloud characteristic among the standard feature list.

26.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. IaaS — Infrastructure as a Service
2. PaaS — Platform as a Service
3. SaaS — Software as a Service
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
26.x: All three pairs are correctly matched and constitute the three service models listed for MeghRaj: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.
26.tq: Expand technical abbreviations and verify each pair before selecting the combined option.

26.s: Which of the following is NOT a deployment model of MeghRaj GI Cloud?
26.x: The four deployment models are public, private, hybrid and community cloud. Satellite cloud is not one of the listed deployment models.
26.tq: Use the exact four-item classification and reject the invented category.

26.s: Which of the following correctly describes the architecture and empanelment arrangements under MeghRaj?
o: Only private clouds are permitted and no application store is included.
MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers; the architecture includes national and State clouds and an e-Gov App Store.
State governments empanel foreign providers without involvement of MeitY.
The architecture consists only of a single national cloud operated by BSNL.
26.x: MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers for government use. The architecture includes national and State clouds along with an e-Gov App Store.
26.tq: Check the responsible authority and the complete architecture rather than accepting a partial description.

26.s: Which of the following is a cloud deployment model rather than a cloud service model?
26.x: Public, private, hybrid and community are deployment models, whereas IaaS, PaaS and SaaS are service models.
26.tq: Separate the service-model column from the deployment-model column.

26.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (Programme) — List-II (Description)
a. NDLM — i. Digital literacy scheme preceding PMGDISHA
b. DISHA — ii. Digital Saksharta Abhiyan
c. ICT@Schools — iii. Centrally sponsored scheme for computer labs and ICT learning

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
26.x: NDLM and DISHA refer to the digital literacy initiatives that preceded PMGDISHA, with DISHA expanded as Digital Saksharta Abhiyan. ICT@Schools was a centrally sponsored scheme for computer labs and ICT learning in government schools.
26.tq: Start from the sure acronym expansion and eliminate mismatched programme descriptions.

26.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its focus?
o: e-Pathshala — optical-fibre connectivity to gram panchayats
Vidya Vahini — school project focused on computer education
26.x: Vidya Vahini was a school project focused on computer education. ICT@Schools concerned computer labs and ICT learning, NDLM concerned digital literacy, and e-Pathshala provided digital educational resources.
26.tq: Use nearby education and ICT schemes to detect the swapped programme descriptions.

26.s: e-Pathshala was launched in November 2015 by which combination of organisations?
26.x: e-Pathshala was launched in November 2015 by MHRD and NCERT to provide e-textbooks and other educational resources.
26.tq: Recall the implementing institutions and launch period of an education platform.

26.s: PMGDISHA was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at:
26.x: PMGDISHA was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Gandhinagar.
26.tq: Recall the launch venue of a named government digital-literacy scheme.

26.s: Which of the following correctly describes the target and age group under PMGDISHA?
o: Two crore rural households, one person per household, aged 14–50 years
Six crore rural households, all persons per household, aged 18–59 years
Six crore urban households, two persons per household, aged 18–60 years
Six crore rural households, one person per household, aged 14–60 years
26.x: PMGDISHA targeted six crore rural households, with one person from each household, in the age group of 14 to 60 years.
26.tq: Check target population, household coverage and age range as separate components.

26.s: PMGDISHA closed on 31 March 2024. Which set of figures correctly represents its registered, trained and certified beneficiaries, respectively?
26.x: At closure, PMGDISHA had 7.35 crore registered beneficiaries, 6.39 crore trained beneficiaries and 4.78 crore certified beneficiaries.
26.tq: Preserve the order of registration, training and certification while comparing close figures.

26.s: The E&ICT Academy Phase-II scheme of MeitY aims to:
o: train 1,35,000 faculty members through 14 agencies such as IITs, NIT, NIELIT and CDAC
make one person in each of 6 crore rural households digitally literate
set up computer labs in all government schools
26.x: E&ICT Academy Phase-II (MeitY, 5 years) targets training 1,35,000 faculty through 14 agencies including IITs, NIT, NIELIT and CDAC. The 6 crore households target is PMGDISHA, computer labs in government schools is ICT@Schools, and e-textbooks via NCERT is e-Pathshala.
26.tq: E&ICT Academy = faculty training (1.35 lakh, 14 agencies).

26.s: The primary objective of the BhashaNet portal is to promote which of the following?
26.x: BhashaNet was launched to promote digital inclusion by advancing Universal Acceptance, including support for diverse languages and scripts.
26.tq: Match the named initiative with its principal objective rather than a neighbouring ICT programme.

26.s: Universal Acceptance means that:
o: domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script should function in every application
all internet services must be provided free of cost
all citizens must use one standard language on the internet
only government websites should accept Indian-language content
