36.s: NASA has flagged which of the following as a top risk to Starship's Moon-landing plan?
o: The use of an endothermic hydrocarbon fuel in an HSTDV combustor
The absence of a solid stage in Vikram-1
36.x: Cryogenic propellant transfer in orbit has been identified as a top risk to Starship's Moon-landing plan.
36.tq: Use the distinctive risk-technology association rather than confusing it with propulsion tests on other vehicles.

37.s: Which one of the following statements about a geostationary satellite is NOT correct?
o: Its orbital plane is the equatorial plane with zero inclination.
Its orbital period is approximately 24 hours.
It orbits at approximately 35,786 km above the equator.
Its fixed orbital height varies according to the mass of the satellite.
37.x: The geostationary orbital height is fixed and does not depend on the satellite’s mass. The other statements correctly describe geostationary orbit.
37.tq: Find the exception by checking the physical condition that does not affect orbital height.

37.s: A geostationary satellite appears stationary to an observer because it
o: moves from east to west in a polar plane
moves from west to east in the equatorial plane with a period matching Earth’s rotation
remains permanently fixed above the North Pole
moves randomly around the Earth at a very low altitude
37.x: A geostationary satellite moves west to east in the equatorial plane and has a 24-hour period, matching Earth’s rotation.
37.tq: Combine direction, plane and period to explain the apparent stationary position.

37.s: Which of the following correctly describes the usual process of placing a communication satellite in geostationary orbit?
o: The launcher places it in an elliptical GTO, after which the satellite’s own motor raises it to GEO.
The satellite first descends into the atmosphere and is then lifted by solar radiation.
The launcher directly places it in a circular polar orbit and the satellite remains there.
The launcher places it directly in a sub-GTO and no onboard propulsion is required.
37.x: Launch vehicles generally inject satellites into an elliptical geostationary transfer orbit (GTO); the satellite’s own motor raises it to geostationary orbit (GEO).
37.tq: Distinguish the transfer orbit from the final geostationary orbit.

37.s: Which one of the following correctly explains APPLE?
o: Asian Public Platform for Long-distance Education, launched in 2004 as EDUSAT
Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment, launched in 1981 as India’s first experimental communication satellite
Aerial Payload and Propulsion Laboratory Experiment, launched in 2002 as a navigation satellite
Advanced Polar Payload Launch Experiment, launched in 1992 as India’s first meteorological satellite
37.x: APPLE stands for Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment and was India’s first experimental communication satellite, launched in 1981.
37.tq: Expand the acronym and match it with its historical role.

37.s: Which of the following is a feature of the multipurpose INSAT design?
o: Telecommunication, television broadcasting, meteorology, disaster warning and search-and-rescue are integrated on one geostationary platform.
Only military communication is provided through a network of polar satellites.
Only weather imaging is performed, without broadcasting or disaster services.
Education and telemedicine are excluded from the satellite-based service framework.
37.x: INSAT integrates telecommunications, television broadcasting, meteorology, disaster warning and search-and-rescue on one geostationary platform. It is regarded as one of the largest domestic systems in the Asia-Pacific region.
37.tq: Select the option that captures the full multipurpose design rather than a single service.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about the INSAT system:
1. It is a joint venture of DoS, DoT, IMD, All India Radio and Doordarshan.
2. It is coordinated by the INSAT Coordination Committee (ICC).
3. It is controlled from the Master Control Facility at Sriharikota.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: INSAT is a joint venture of DoS, DoT, IMD, AIR and Doordarshan, coordinated by the ICC. Statement 3 is wrong: the MCF is at Hassan, Karnataka. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options include statement 3 or omit a true one.
37.tq: Launches from Sriharikota, but satellites are controlled from MCF Hassan.

37.s: INSAT-4C was lost because
o: GSLV-F01 failed during the EDUSAT mission
Falcon 9 failed during the GSAT-N2 mission
37.x: INSAT-4C was lost in 2006 when GSLV-F02 failed. It was replaced by INSAT-4CR, launched in September 2007 by GSLV-F04.
37.tq: Link the failed satellite with the correct launch vehicle and year.

37.s: The Indian National Satellite (INSAT) system is best described as a:
o: Combined communication and meteorological satellite system
37.x: INSAT serves both communication and meteorology from geostationary orbit (JPSC 2021 keyed it as a 'meteorological satellite'), and also carries broadcasting, disaster warning and search-and-rescue. It is not purely military, not a sun-synchronous remote-sensing system (that is IRS), and not a navigation system (that is NavIC).
37.tq: INSAT = comms + weather, from GEO.

37.s: In 2022, India's in-orbit communication satellites (10 of them) were transferred to which entity?
37.x: In 2022, 10 in-orbit communication satellites were transferred to NSIL, ISRO's commercial-arm CPSE, which now operates them. Antrix is the older commercial arm; IN-SPACe is the regulator; DoT was one of the original INSAT partners but is not the operator.
37.tq: Satcom operator today = NSIL (2022).

37.s: Which one of the following statements about GSAT-11 is correct?
o: It is a dedicated Navy satellite launched in 2013.
It was the first operational satellite of the INSAT system in 1983.
It is a 2015 satellite with a large deployable antenna for mobile communication.
It is India’s heaviest communication satellite, weighing approximately 5.8 tonnes, and supports high-speed rural broadband.
37.x: D is correct: GSAT-11 (2018), about 5.8 tonnes, is the heaviest ISRO-built communication satellite and serves high-speed internet and rural broadband. A describes GSAT-7 'Rukmini' (Navy, 2013), B describes INSAT-1B (system commissioned 1983) and C describes GSAT-6 (2015).
37.tq: Use the distinctive weight and broadband function to separate GSAT-11 from the other satellites.

37.s:
Consider the following statements regarding INSAT-1 series:
1. The first INSAT satellites were bought abroad.
2. The INSAT system was commissioned in 1983.
3. The series began from 1992 with INSAT-2A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: The INSAT-1 satellites were procured from abroad and the INSAT system was commissioned in 1983. Statement 3 is false because the INSAT-2 series began in 1992.
37.tq: Split the options by checking the series start dates before considering the combined code.

37.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: GSAT-8 — Cyclone-warning satellite without communication payloads
37.x: EDUSAT, also designated GSAT-3, was intended for education and provided two-way classroom links. The other satellites have been matched with incorrect functions.
37.tq: Start with the sure purpose-satellite pair and reject swapped applications.

37.s: Which one of the following combinations regarding INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR is correct?
o: INSAT-3D—1983; television broadcasting; INSAT-3DR—1992; mobile communication
INSAT-3D—2013; advanced meteorology; INSAT-3DR—2016; advanced meteorology
37.x: INSAT-3D was launched in 2013 and INSAT-3DR in 2016; both serve advanced meteorological purposes.
37.tq: Compare the two closely named satellites by year and common application.

37.s: Which one of the following statements about GSAT-8 is correct?
o: It was launched on 21 May 2011 by Ariane-5 and carried a GAGAN payload.
It was launched in 2020 by GSLV-F01 for two-way classroom links.
It was launched in 2018 by Falcon 9 and carried only a military payload.
It was launched in 2004 by PSLV and functioned as an exclusive weather satellite.
37.x: GSAT-8 was launched on 21 May 2011 by Ariane-5 and carried a GAGAN payload; GSAT-10 and GSAT-15 also carried GAGAN payloads.
37.tq: Use the date-launcher-payload combination to distinguish GSAT-8 from nearby GSAT missions.

37.s:
Arrange the following satellites in chronological order of their stated launch dates:
A. GSAT-30
B. KALPANA-1
C. EDUSAT
D. GSAT-8
37.x: KALPANA-1 was launched in 2002, EDUSAT in 2004, GSAT-8 in 2011 and GSAT-30 in 2020.
37.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the middle satellites by year.

37.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: INSAT-2 — first fully indigenous INSAT series
KALPANA-1 — first South Asia regional communication satellite
INSAT-3DR — first fully indigenous INSAT series
37.x: INSAT-2 was the first fully indigenous INSAT series. KALPANA-1, not GSAT-9 or INSAT-3DR, was the first exclusive weather satellite.
37.tq: Start with the sure satellite-series and first-achievement pair.

37.s: Which satellite was described as the heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil, weighing 4,410 kg and intended for the Navy?
37.x: CMS-03, also designated GSAT-7R, weighed 4,410 kg and was described as the heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil for the Navy.
37.tq: Combine payload mass, satellite identity and user organisation.

37.s: GSAT-30, launched on 17 January 2020 from Kourou, French Guiana, is primarily a:
37.x: GSAT-30 is a telecommunication satellite launched by Ariane from Kourou on 17 Jan 2020 (APPSC 2018 PYQ theme). Navigation is NavIC/NVS, earth observation is EOS/IRS, and the exclusive weather satellite was KALPANA-1.
37.tq: GSAT = communication; Kourou 2020 = GSAT-30.

37.s: Which one of the following sets contains only Indian communication satellites launched from Kourou by Ariane?
37.x: INSAT-3A, INSAT-4A, INSAT-4B and GSAT-8 are among the Indian communication satellites launched from Kourou by Ariane.
37.tq: Group the satellites by launcher and location, rejecting satellites associated with Indian or US launchers.

37.s: GSAT-N2 was launched by
o: US Space Shuttle from Kennedy Space Center
37.x: GSAT-N2 was launched by SpaceX’s Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral.
37.tq: Separate the recent commercial foreign launch from the earlier Ariane launches.

37.s: Which satellite is correctly matched with its principal use?
o: GSAT-6 — Large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic communication
GSAT-11 — First operational satellite of the INSAT system
37.x: GSAT-6, launched in 2015, has a large deployable antenna and supports mobile and strategic communication. GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7A serves the Air Force, and INSAT-1B marked operationalisation of INSAT.
37.tq: Start with the satellite-use pair and watch for swapped defence roles and chronology.

37.s:
Arrange the following satellites in chronological order of the years stated for them:
A. GSAT-7
B. GSAT-6
C. GSAT-7A
D. GSAT-11
37.x: The sequence is GSAT-7 (2013), GSAT-6 (2015), GSAT-7A (2018) and GSAT-11 (2018).
37.tq: Fix the earliest satellite first and then distinguish the two 2018 entries by their stated sequence.

37.s:
Match the strategic satellites with their users:

a. GSAT-7 'Rukmini'
b. GSAT-7A 'Angry Bird'
c. GSAT-7B (proposed)

i. Indian Air Force
ii. Indian Army
iii. Indian Navy
37.x: GSAT-7 'Rukmini' (2013) is the Navy satellite (later replaced by CMS-03), GSAT-7A 'Angry Bird' (2018) is the dedicated Air Force satellite, and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army. The other codes swap the Navy and Air Force or the Army.
37.tq: Rukmini = Navy; Angry Bird = Air Force; 7B = Army.

37.s:
Match List-I (Band) with List-II (Typical use):
List-I
a. C / extended C
b. Ku
c. Ka
d. S
List-II
i. High-throughput broadband
ii. DTH and VSAT
iii. Telecom and TV distribution
iv. Mobile satellite services and DWS downlink
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
37.x: C/extended C is used for telecom and TV distribution (iii), Ku for DTH and VSAT (ii), Ka for high-throughput broadband such as GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 (i), and S for mobile satellite services and the DWS downlink (iv). Option B swaps C and Ku, option C swaps Ku and Ka, option D swaps C and S.
37.tq: Higher band letter, higher frequency, more bandwidth: Ka is the broadband band.

37.s: Which of the following satellites is associated with UHF, S and C bands in the stated communication configuration?
37.x: CMS-03 has UHF, S and C bands in the stated configuration; UHF is associated with military applications.
37.tq: Identify the satellite from the unusual combination of three transponder bands.

37.s: Which of the following sets contains only high-throughput or broadband satellites?
37.x: GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 are identified with high-throughput broadband services for underserved areas, in-flight links and defence, complementing BharatNet.
37.tq: Group satellites by service category and reject meteorological, educational and strategic-only sets.

37.s: Which one of the following frequency bands is NOT used for INSAT/GSAT satellite communication?
37.x: MF is not used in INSAT/GSAT communication (RPSC 2021). C/extended C serves telecom and TV distribution, Ku serves DTH and VSAT, and S serves mobile satellite services and the DWS downlink.
37.tq: Satellites use C, Ku, Ka, S, UHF; not MF.

37.s: Which of the following best describes the stated role of Starlink’s proposed Indian satellite internet service in 2025?
o: Registering newspapers through a satellite-based portal
Replacing all terrestrial fibre networks in urban areas
Providing broadband to remote, disaster-hit and mobile areas
37.x: Starlink’s India launch was imminent in 2025 and its stated advantage was broadband access for remote, disaster-hit and mobile areas.
37.tq: Apply the service’s coverage advantage to the locations and situations described.

37.s: Which of the following is NOT an application served by the INSAT/GSAT system?
o: Extraction of petroleum directly from underground reservoirs
37.x: INSAT/GSAT applications include DSNG, mobile satellite services and satellite-aided search and rescue, but satellites do not directly extract petroleum from underground reservoirs.
37.tq: Find the unrelated activity among the recognised communication and service applications.

37.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Application)
A. DTH
B. VSAT
C. DSNG
D. MSS

List-II (Description)
I. Mobile satellite services
II. Satellite news gathering
III. Direct-to-Home broadcasting
IV. Business networks through very small aperture terminals

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: DTH means Direct-to-Home broadcasting, VSAT supports business networks, DSNG means satellite news gathering, and MSS means mobile satellite services.
37.tq: Begin with the unambiguous acronym expansions and complete the matching code.

37.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Swayam Prabha is correct?
o: It uses INSAT-4CR to provide satellite-aided search-and-rescue services.
It uses KALPANA-1 to transmit cyclone warnings to coastal receivers.
It uses GSAT-11 to provide only military broadband channels.
It uses GSAT-15 to beam 40 free DTH education channels.
37.x: Swayam Prabha uses GSAT-15 to provide 40 free Direct-to-Home education channels.
37.tq: Match the named education initiative with its satellite and channel count.

37.s: In the Disaster Warning System, cyclone warnings from the Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai are
o: sent upward through S-band and received through C-band by all receivers without selection
sent upward through UHF and received through MF by television households
sent upward through C-band and received through S-band by selectively addressable receivers
sent upward through Ku-band and received through Ka-band only by military stations
37.x: The warning signal goes up on C-band and comes down on S-band to selectively addressable DWS receivers along the coast.
37.tq: Trace the communication path in order: uplink band, downlink band and receiver type.

37.s: Which organisation receives Bay of Bengal cyclone-track data supplied by SDSC-SHAR for disaster-management purposes?
37.x: SDSC-SHAR supplies Bay of Bengal cyclone-track data to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA).
37.tq: Identify the receiving disaster-management authority rather than the supplying centre.

37.s: INSAT’s search-and-rescue transponders operate under the international programme known as
37.x: INSAT carries search-and-rescue transponders under the international COSPAS-SARSAT programme.
37.tq: Separate search-and-rescue terminology from navigation and education programmes.

37.s: The South Asia Satellite is designated as which of the following?
37.x: The South Asia Satellite is designated as GSAT-9.
37.tq: Direct identification of a satellite designation.

37.s: GSAT-9, the South Asia Satellite, was launched in which month and year using GSLV-F09?
37.x: GSAT-9 was launched in May 2017 by the GSLV-F09 launch vehicle.
37.tq: Distinguish the closely placed launch year and vehicle details.

37.s: Which South Asian country opted out of the South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9) launched by India in May 2017?
37.x: Pakistan opted out of the South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9, GSLV-F09, May 2017). Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka are among the neighbours meant to benefit from it.
37.tq: GSAT-9 = South Asia Satellite; Pakistan out.

37.s: Which one of the following correctly describes CMS-03, also designated GSAT-7R?
o: A weather satellite launched by GSLV-F09 for cyclone-warning services
A commercial communication satellite placed in low Earth orbit by LVM3-M6
An encrypted satellite providing anti-jam naval links up to 2,000 km from the coast, launched by LVM3-M5
A navigation satellite providing regional positioning services through PSLV
37.x: CMS-03/GSAT-7R is associated with encrypted, anti-jam naval links extending up to 2,000 km from the coast and was launched using LVM3-M5.
37.tq: Match the satellite with its specific defence application and launch vehicle.

37.s: The early-warning capability of INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR has had which of the following effects?
o: It sharply reduced cyclone-related deaths on the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
It provided encrypted naval communication up to 2,000 km from the coast.
It made BlueBird Block-2 the largest satellite in low Earth orbit.
It enabled the South Asian countries to opt out of satellite services.
37.x: INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR early warnings sharply reduced cyclone deaths along the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
37.tq: Identify the concrete consequence of a satellite-based warning system.

37.s: KALPANA-1 holds which distinction in the Indian satellite programme?
o: First fully indigenous communication satellite series
First satellite for encrypted naval links
First commercial communication satellite in low Earth orbit
37.x: KALPANA-1 was India's first exclusive weather satellite.
37.tq: Direct recall of a first-in-category distinction.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about GPS:
1. It was started by the US Department of Defense in 1973.
2. Its original design has 24 satellites in 6 orbits at about 20,200 km.
3. Each GPS satellite circles the Earth once a day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: GPS began in 1973 under the US DoD, with 24 satellites in 6 orbits at 20,200 km. Statement 3 is wrong: each satellite circles the Earth twice a day (once a day would be geosynchronous). So '1 and 2 only'; the other options include statement 3 or omit a true one.
38.tq: 20,200 km is well below 36,000 km, so the period is shorter than a day - 12 hours.

38.s: An error of approximately one microsecond in an atomic clock used for positioning may produce a position error of about:
38.x: A one-microsecond clock error can produce an approximate position error of 300 metres, illustrating the importance of atomic clocks in navigation.
38.tq: Convert the stated clock-error relationship without changing the unit scale.

38.s: Which of the following statements about GPS signals is correct?
o: GPS signals are confined to marine navigation.
GPS uses signals on L1 at 1,575.42 MHz and on L2.
GPS operates only on NavIC’s S band.
GPS transmits only a civilian L5 signal and no L1 signal.
38.x: GPS uses the L1 signal at 1,575.42 MHz and the L2 signal. Its applications extend well beyond marine navigation.
38.tq: Match the exact frequency and bands while rejecting scope and system swaps.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about NavIC:
1. It was formerly called IRNSS.
2. It became fully operational in 2013.
3. Its genesis lies in the US denial of GPS data during the 1999 Kargil War.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: NavIC was formerly IRNSS. Statement 2 is wrong: NavIC became fully operational in 2018 (navigation satellites have been launched since 2013). Statement 3 is correct: GPS data denial in the 1999 Kargil War prompted it. So '1 and 3 only'; options including 2 are wrong and '1 and 2 only' also drops 3.
38.tq: Kargil 1999 -> idea; 2013 first launches; 2018 fully operational.

38.s:
With reference to the NavIC constellation, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of seven satellites.
2. Three satellites are in geostationary orbit.
3. Four satellites are in inclined geosynchronous orbit at about 29° to the equator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: NavIC’s planned constellation has seven satellites: three in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit at about 29° to the equator.
38.tq: Verify the total and split the constellation into its two orbital groups.

38.s: The primary service area of NavIC extends over India and approximately:
38.x: NavIC provides coverage over India and approximately 1,500 km beyond India’s borders.
38.tq: Distinguish the regional coverage figure from global-system coverage.

38.s: Which frequency bands are associated with the original NavIC services?
38.x: NavIC traditionally provides signals in the L5 and S bands. The NVS series additionally introduces an L1 civilian signal.
38.tq: Avoid importing the familiar GPS bands into the NavIC question.

38.s: The major signal-related improvement introduced by the NVS series is the addition of:
38.x: The NVS series adds a civilian L1 signal compatible with other GNSS systems, helping mobile-phone adoption.
38.tq: Identify the exact new band and its civilian-use implication.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes NavIC’s Standard Positioning Service?
o: It is available only to authorised military users and is encrypted.
It is available only outside India and offers accuracy better than 100 metres.
It is a timing-only service without positioning capability.
It is available to all civilians and offers accuracy better than 20 metres.
38.x: The Standard Positioning Service is available to all civilian users and has a design positioning accuracy better than 20 metres.
38.tq: Contrast civilian SPS with the authorised and encrypted Restricted Service.

38.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First GPS satellite launched
B. GPS programme initiated
C. NavIC became fully operational
D. NVS-01 launched
38.x: The GPS programme began in 1973, its first satellite was launched in 1978, NavIC became fully operational in 2018, and NVS-01 was launched in 2023.
38.tq: Place the events by their years, using the first two close milestones carefully.

38.s: Which statement regarding the IRNSS satellite launches is correct?
o: All IRNSS satellites were launched from a foreign spaceport using only GSLV vehicles.
All IRNSS satellites were launched from Sriharikota, and the IRNSS-1 series used PSLV launch vehicles.
The IRNSS-1 series was launched only by reusable spaceplanes.
The IRNSS satellites were placed in orbit without launch vehicles.
38.x: The IRNSS satellites were launched from Sriharikota, and the IRNSS-1 series was launched using PSLV vehicles.
38.tq: Combine launch-location and launch-vehicle facts while rejecting absolute but unsupported alternatives.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes NVS-01?
o: It was launched in January 2025 by GSLV-F15 and suffered a valve glitch.
It was launched in March 2016 by PSLV and was decommissioned above GEO.
It was launched in May 2023 by GSLV-F12 and was the first satellite with an indigenous rubidium atomic clock.
It was launched in 2018 by a foreign launch vehicle without an atomic clock.
38.x: NVS-01, the second-generation satellite, was launched in May 2023 on GSLV-F12 and was the first to carry an indigenous rubidium atomic clock.
38.tq: Match the satellite with its launch date, vehicle and distinctive payload.

38.s: NVS-02 was launched by GSLV-F15 in January 2025, but a valve glitch:
o: left it in the wrong orbit, after which it was salvaged for alternate use
prevented it from carrying any navigation payload
caused it to land in the Bay of Bengal
38.x: A valve glitch left NVS-02 in the wrong orbit, but the satellite was salvaged for alternate use. The launch was also the 100th Sriharikota launch.
38.tq: Track the failure consequence without confusing it with total mission destruction.

38.s: The launch of NVS-02 in January 2025 was significant because it marked the:
38.x: The NVS-02 mission marked the 100th launch from Sriharikota.
38.tq: Retain the milestone number separately from the satellite’s technical failure.

38.s: Which statement correctly describes the change in atomic clocks used in IRNSS satellites?
o: IRNSS satellites never used rubidium clocks.
ISRO replaced indigenous clocks with Swiss clocks in 2018 because the indigenous clocks failed.
The clock issue concerned only GPS satellites and not IRNSS satellites.
ISRO replaced repeatedly failing Swiss SpectraTime rubidium clocks with indigenous clocks in 2018.
38.x: First-generation IRNSS satellites used rubidium clocks supplied by Swiss firm SpectraTime, which repeatedly failed; ISRO switched to indigenous clocks in 2018.
38.tq: Track the direction of the technology switch and the supplier’s identity.

38.s: On 13 March 2026, the failure of the last clock on IRNSS-1F resulted in which situation?
o: IRNSS-1F immediately became a new GEO satellite.
Only three PNT-capable satellites remained, below the four needed for the required service.
The constellation gained two additional PNT-capable satellites.
All seven satellites became fully operational.
38.x: After the last clock on IRNSS-1F failed, only IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable—three satellites, below the four needed.
38.tq: Count the surviving satellites and compare the number with the service threshold.

38.s: Which company developed India’s first NavIC-based device intended to provide precise directions for infrastructure projects?
38.x: Elena Geo Systems developed India’s first NavIC-based device for precise directions on infrastructure projects.
38.tq: Match the specialised company with its specific technological product.

38.s: Which of the following statements regarding NavIC adoption in mobile devices is correct?
o: NavIC adoption in phones is unrelated to the signals carried by NVS satellites.
The L1 signal was removed from newer NVS satellites to restrict civilian use.
NavIC can be received only through dedicated military terminals.
38.x: Qualcomm Snapdragon chipsets support NavIC. Newer NVS satellites add a civilian L1 signal, making integration with other GNSS-enabled phones easier.
38.tq: Select the positive technology-adoption statement and reject reversed signal claims.

38.s: The AIS-140 requirement relating to NavIC primarily concerns:
o: replacement of all GPS satellites by NavIC satellites
mandatory NavIC-enabled location trackers in public transport vehicles
use of NavIC only in military aircraft
mandatory NavIC receivers for all private household appliances
38.x: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ AIS-140 rule made NavIC-enabled location trackers compulsory in public transport vehicles.
38.tq: Identify the regulatory application from the vehicle-tracking context.

38.s:
Which of the following is an appropriate application of GPS?
1. Precise timing for power, telecommunications and banking
2. Surveying and geodetic mapping
3. Vehicle tracking and fleet management
4. Precision farming and disaster management
38.x: GPS supports all the listed applications, including precise timing, surveying, vehicle and fleet tracking, precision farming and disaster management.
38.tq: Recognise the broad multi-sector application set and select the complete combination.

38.s: Reconfigured IRNSS-1A helped fishermen at sea by broadcasting warnings relating to:
38.x: Reconfigured IRNSS-1A broadcasts cyclone, tsunami and high-wave warnings to fishermen at sea.
38.tq: Match the satellite function with the specific maritime-warning group.

38.s: In March 2026, the Government of India urged electronics manufacturers to use NavIC for which purpose?
o: Replacing all mobile-tower clocks with GPS receivers
Broadcasting television signals in the S band
38.x: The Government urged electronics makers to use NavIC for Indian Standard Time (Mar 2026), reflecting NavIC's precise-timing capability. Replacing clocks with GPS would defeat the indigenous purpose; NavIC is not a TV-broadcast or encryption system.
38.tq: NavIC timing = Indian Standard Time push (Mar 2026).

38.s: GAGAN is an augmentation system whose full form is:
38.x: GAGAN stands for GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation.
38.tq: Use exact expansion discrimination among similar navigation terms.

38.s: The principal function of a Satellite-Based Augmentation System is to:
o: replace every navigation satellite with a ground-based radar
broadcast real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay
increase satellite altitude without correcting navigation data
38.x: An SBAS broadcasts real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay, improving accuracy, integrity and availability.
38.tq: Identify the correction functions that define SBAS operation.

38.s: GAGAN was developed jointly by:
o: AAI and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
ISRO and the United States Department of Defense
ISRO and the Airports Authority of India
38.x: GAGAN was jointly developed by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India.
38.tq: Apply the developer-agency matching method to distinguish GAGAN from GPS.

38.s:
GAGAN payloads are carried on which of the following satellites?
1. GSAT-8
2. GSAT-10
3. GSAT-15
38.x: GAGAN payloads are carried on GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.
38.tq: Check all listed satellite platforms before selecting the complete combination.

38.s: The service area of GAGAN is the:
38.x: GAGAN serves the Indian Flight Information Region.
38.tq: Match the augmentation system with its aviation region.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the GAGAN ground segment?
38.x: The GAGAN ground segment includes Indian Reference Stations (INRES), the Indian Master Control Centre (INMCC) and uplink stations (INLUS).
38.tq: Decode the institutional abbreviations and match them with the ground segment.

38.s: GAGAN was certified by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation for aviation approach guidance in:
38.x: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation certified GAGAN for aviation approach guidance in 2015.
38.tq: Distinguish the aviation-certification year from system-development and operational years.

38.s: Which organisation is the nodal authority for both NavIC and GAGAN?
o: Satellite Navigation Programme Office under ISRO
Directorate General of Civil Aviation alone
Ministry of Defence’s Integrated Defence Staff
38.x: The Satellite Navigation Programme Office under ISRO is the nodal authority for NavIC and GAGAN.
38.tq: Identify the coordinating authority rather than an implementing or certifying agency.

38.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
38.x: MSAS is the SBAS associated with Japan. WAAS serves the USA and North America, EGNOS serves Europe and GAGAN serves India.
38.tq: Use region-based elimination among similarly named augmentation systems.

38.s: The primary aviation use of GAGAN is to support:
o: Military satellite communication for the Navy
Tracking of ocean currents for fisheries
Precision approach and landing for civil aviation
38.x: GAGAN supports precision approach and landing for civil aviation by providing augmented navigation information over the Indian Flight Information Region.
38.tq: Link the augmentation function to its practical civil-aviation application.

38.s: Which of the following is a structural limitation of NavIC when compared with GPS?
o: NavIC has no satellite-based positioning service.
NavIC is global, whereas GPS covers only India.
NavIC is regional, covering India and about 1,500 km beyond its borders, whereas GPS is global.
Both systems are limited to the Indian Flight Information Region.
38.x: NavIC is a regional system, while GPS is global. NavIC’s stated coverage is India plus approximately 1,500 km beyond its borders.
38.tq: Use the regional-versus-global contrast to identify the limitation.

38.s: The thin ecosystem of NavIC receivers was initially related mainly to the fact that:
o: L5 and S bands were not commonly included in mobile-phone chipsets
NavIC had no satellites in orbit
GPS prevented all receivers from using satellite signals
NavIC signals were transmitted only through optical fibre
38.x: Receiver adoption was constrained because L5 and S bands were not commonly supported in phone chipsets; the newer civilian L1 signal helps address this limitation.
38.tq: Connect the receiver limitation with the relevant frequency-band issue.

38.s: Which combination best explains why NavIC could not fully replace GPS over India as reported in March 2026?
o: Absence of any regional coverage and lack of satellites since 1999
Excessive global coverage and too many civilian receivers
Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure
Only the use of geostationary satellites, with no clock problems
38.x: Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure reduced the effective constellation, preventing NavIC from fully replacing GPS over India.
38.tq: Combine the operational failure causes rather than choosing a coverage or orbit distraction.

38.s: The failure of the clock in which satellite was associated with the reduction of the operational NavIC constellation to three working satellites on 13 March 2026?
38.x: The reduction of the working NavIC constellation was attributed to the clock failure in IRNSS-1F.
38.tq: Identify the satellite directly linked with the stated technical failure.

38.s:
Assertion (A): NavIC is important for India’s strategic autonomy.
Reason (R): During a conflict, Indian forces and emergency responders need not depend entirely on foreign navigation systems when an indigenous system is available.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
38.x: Both statements are true. Reduced dependence on foreign navigation systems during conflict directly explains NavIC’s importance for strategic autonomy.
38.tq: Test whether the Reason explains the strategic significance stated in the Assertion.

38.s: GPS jamming reported near the Strait of Hormuz during the West Asia conflict most directly illustrates which risk?
o: The restriction of satellite navigation to maritime transport
The complete failure of all regional navigation systems
The inability of satellites to provide weather information
The vulnerability created by dependence on foreign navigation systems during conflict
38.x: GPS jamming near the Strait of Hormuz illustrates the operational risk of relying on foreign navigation systems in a conflict situation.
38.tq: Apply the strategic-autonomy concept to a conflict-related navigation disruption.

38.s: NavIC-based alerts are of particular practical importance to Andhra Pradesh because they assist which group during cyclones?
o: Mountain rescue teams in the Eastern Himalayas
Air traffic controllers at international airports
Fishermen operating along the long coastline
38.x: NavIC-based fishermen alerts can support the large fishing community along Andhra Pradesh’s long coastline during cyclones.
38.tq: Link the regional application with the geographic feature and affected community.

39.s: Which one of the following most appropriately describes remote sensing?
o: Preparation of maps only through manual surveying
Measurement of only the chemical composition of rocks by direct sampling
Recording of atmospheric pressure exclusively through ground instruments
Collection of information about the Earth without physical contact, using reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation
39.x: Remote sensing obtains information about the Earth without physical contact by detecting reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation.
39.tq: Use the precise definition and eliminate options that restrict the concept to one application or instrument.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component or stage of a standard remote sensing system?
o: Interaction of radiation with the target
39.x: Interaction of energy with minimisation is not a component of the remote sensing system. The relevant stage is interaction of energy or radiation with the target.
39.tq: Find the look-alike phrase that substitutes an incorrect term for the standard process stage.

39.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sensor type)
a. Passive sensor
b. Active sensor
c. Optical sensor
d. SAR sensor

List-II (Characteristic)
i. Uses its own signal and reads the echo
 ii. Uses reflected light and is affected by cloud cover
 iii. Detects natural sunlight or emitted heat
 iv. Uses microwave energy and can operate through cloud and darkness

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Passive sensors detect natural sunlight or emitted heat; active sensors transmit their own signal. Optical sensors use reflected light, while SAR uses microwaves and can observe through clouds and in darkness.
39.tq: Start from the sure pair—active sensor with its own signal—and complete the remaining pairs by elimination.

39.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: SAR — optical sensor blocked by cloud
IRS — passive sensor using reflected or emitted natural energy
RISAT radar — passive sensor dependent only on sunlight
LiDAR — passive sensor receiving only natural heat
39.x: IRS is an example of a passive remote sensing system. RISAT SAR and LiDAR are active systems, while optical sensing is vulnerable to cloud cover.
39.tq: Separate passive and active sensors by asking who supplies the energy—the target or the sensor.

39.s: Hyperspectral remote sensing is particularly useful for:
o: Producing radar echoes from a single microwave band
Identifying materials or chemicals using hundreds of narrow spectral bands
Measuring only the revisit interval of a satellite
Determining satellite launch velocity without imaging
39.x: Hyperspectral sensing uses hundreds of narrow spectral bands, enabling identification of materials and their chemical characteristics.
39.tq: Link the prefix ‘hyper’ with numerous narrow bands and material discrimination.

39.s: Which one of the following is an example of an active remote-sensing system?
39.x: LiDAR sends its own laser pulse and reads the echo, so it is active (APPSC 2023: laser is active). Multispectral cameras, infrared radiometers and visible cameras record sunlight reflected or heat emitted by the target, so they are passive.
39.tq: Own pulse + echo = active: RISAT SAR, LiDAR.

39.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents a type of remote sensing resolution and its meaning?

1. Spatial resolution — size of the smallest ground detail distinguishable
2. Spectral resolution — ability to distinguish wavelength bands
3. Temporal resolution — frequency of coverage of an area
4. Radiometric resolution — sensitivity to differences in energy intensity
39.x: Spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric are the four recognised resolution types. Their meanings correspond to the four statements.
39.tq: Match each resolution term with the dimension it measures: space, wavelength, time or energy intensity.

39.s: Which technique is most suitable for mapping ground deformation due to subsidence, earthquakes and volcanic uplift?
39.x: InSAR maps ground deformation, including subsidence, earthquake-related movement and volcanic uplift.
39.tq: Match the technique to its characteristic output—in this case, surface displacement.

39.s: LiDAR is primarily used for:
o: Measuring vegetation health from red and near-infrared reflectance
Laser ranging, elevation measurement and three-dimensional terrain or forest-canopy mapping
Detecting only subsidence through radar phase differences
Recording only emitted heat from fires
39.x: LiDAR uses laser ranging to derive elevation, three-dimensional terrain and forest canopy height.
39.tq: Use the energy clue—laser ranging—to separate LiDAR from radar, vegetation and thermal techniques.

39.s: The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is used to assess:
o: Forest-canopy height from laser pulses alone
Volcanic temperature from long-wave infrared alone
Vegetation health from red and near-infrared reflectance
Ground deformation from microwave phase differences
39.x: NDVI assesses vegetation health by comparing red and near-infrared reflectance.
39.tq: Remember the distinctive spectral pair—red and near-infrared—for vegetation-index questions.

39.s: Which technique is most directly suited to detecting heat from volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat?
39.x: Thermal infrared sensing records emitted heat and is therefore useful for volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat mapping.
39.tq: Link emitted heat with thermal infrared and eliminate techniques measuring vegetation, elevation or deformation.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT a type of resolution in remote sensing?
39.x: The four resolution types are spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric. 'Chemical resolution' does not exist (APPSC 2025 trap). Radiometric, temporal and spectral are all genuine resolution types.
39.tq: Resolutions: spatial, spectral, temporal, radiometric - no 'chemical'.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sun-synchronous polar orbits:
1. They are near-polar orbits.
2. A satellite passes a given place at approximately the same local solar time.
3. They provide consistent lighting conditions for imaging.
4. Their path covers the whole globe.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All four statements correctly describe sun-synchronous polar orbits used for Earth observation.
39.tq: Test a cluster of linked features by checking whether the orbit’s geometry supports each statement.

39.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trade-off between LEO and geosynchronous imaging satellites?
o: LEO provides finer detail with periodic revisit, whereas geosynchronous imaging provides coarser detail with frequent observation of priority targets.
LEO is used only for navigation, whereas geosynchronous orbit is used only for communication.
LEO provides continuous observation of one region, whereas geosynchronous satellites provide only occasional observation.
Both provide the same image detail and revisit frequency because they operate at similar altitudes.
39.x: LEO satellites generally provide finer detail but revisit periodically. Geosynchronous imagers provide coarser detail but can observe priority targets very frequently.
39.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by separating image detail from revisit frequency.

39.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MEO — 35,786 km over the Equator; communication
SSPO — equatorial orbit; satellite appears fixed
39.x: LEO extends approximately from 200 to 2,000 km and is widely used for Earth observation. MEO is associated with navigation, GEO with communication and weather, and SSPO with polar imaging.
39.tq: Start from the sure altitude-use pair and eliminate swapped orbital categories.

39.s:
Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its principal use?
1. LEO — Earth observation
2. MEO — GPS navigation
3. GEO — communication and weather
4. GSO — satellite appears permanently fixed over one equatorial point
Select the correct answer using the code below.
39.x: Statement 4 is incorrect. A satellite appears permanently fixed over one equatorial point only in the geostationary special case, not in every geosynchronous orbit.
39.tq: Find the overbroad statement created by applying a special GEO property to all GSO orbits.

39.s: Which of the following is the correct altitude range associated with a sun-synchronous polar orbit used for imaging?
39.x: Sun-synchronous polar imaging orbits generally operate at approximately 500–900 km.
39.tq: Compare the numerical altitude bands of LEO, MEO, GEO and SSPO.

39.s: EOS-05 is reported to image priority targets every five minutes and the entire Indian landmass every:
39.x: EOS-05 images priority targets every five minutes and the whole Indian landmass every 30 minutes.
39.tq: Separate the two revisit intervals instead of applying the shorter interval to the entire coverage area.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about geostationary (GEO) and geosynchronous (GSO) orbits:
1. A geostationary satellite orbits at about 35,786 km over the Equator.
2. Both GEO and GSO have an orbital period of one sidereal day, about 23 h 56 min.
3. Every geosynchronous satellite appears fixed in the sky.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: GEO is at 35,786 km over the Equator, and GEO and GSO share a period of one sidereal day (~23 h 56 min). Statement 3 is wrong: only the geostationary special case (zero inclination, circular) appears fixed; an inclined GSO traces a figure-8. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options include statement 3 or drop a true one.
39.tq: GEO = GSO with zero inclination; 35,786 km; 23 h 56 min.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the early IRS satellites:
1. IRS-1A, launched on 17 March 1988, was India's first operational remote-sensing satellite.
2. IRS-1C (1995) was the first IRS satellite launched on PSLV from Sriharikota.
3. IRS-P2 (1994) was the first IRS satellite launched on PSLV from Sriharikota.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: IRS-1A (17 Mar 1988) was the first operational remote-sensing satellite. Statement 2 is wrong: IRS-1A, 1B (1991) and 1C (1995) all went from Baikonur on Soviet rockets. Statement 3 is correct: IRS-P2 (1994) was the first on PSLV. So '1 and 3 only' (B) is right; A and D include the false statement 2, and C wrongly drops statement 1.
39.tq: IRS-1A/1B/1C = Baikonur (Soviet); IRS-P2 1994 = first on PSLV.

39.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of India's early Earth-observation satellite milestones?
o: IRS-1A operational satellite, followed by Bhaskara I experimental satellite
Bhaskara I experimental satellite, followed by IRS-1A as the first operational IRS satellite
APPLE experimental communication satellite, followed by EOS-03 as the first operational IRS satellite
INSAT-3D weather satellite, followed by Bhaskara I as the first operational IRS satellite
39.x: Bhaskara I, launched in 1979, was the first experimental Earth-observation satellite. IRS-1A, launched on 17 March 1988, was the first operational IRS satellite.
39.tq: Use the first-experimental versus first-operational distinction to establish the sequence.

39.s: IRS-1A, launched on 17 March 1988, was carried by which launcher?
39.x: IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988 using a Soviet Vostok launcher and was India's first operational IRS satellite.
39.tq: Match the satellite's exact launch date with its foreign launch vehicle.

39.s: Which of the following statements about India's IRS programme is correct?
o: It began with IRNSS-1A in 1988 and is designed mainly for navigation.
It began with Cartosat-3 in 2023 and is primarily a military communication constellation.
It began with GSAT-15 in 2015 and is dedicated exclusively to television broadcasting.
It began with IRS-1A in 1988 and is regarded as the world's largest civilian remote-sensing constellation.
39.x: India's IRS programme began with IRS-1A in 1988 and is regarded as the largest civilian remote-sensing constellation in the world.
39.tq: Combine the starting satellite, year and distinguishing superlative in one precise statement.

39.s: Which one of the following is the principal application of the Resourcesat series?
o: Natural-resource management, including crop acreage and watershed studies
39.x: Resourcesat-1, Resourcesat-2 and Resourcesat-2A are used for natural-resource applications such as crop acreage, watershed studies and precision farming.
39.tq: Identify the application from the series name and its resource-oriented function.

39.s: Cartosat satellites are primarily designed for:
39.x: Cartosat-1, Cartosat-2 and Cartosat-3 are high-resolution mapping satellites also used for surveillance.
39.tq: Match the satellite series with its dominant operational function.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Oceansat — ocean colour and sea-surface temperature
39.x: HySIS is a hyperspectral-imaging satellite. Direct-to-home broadcasting is associated with communication satellites, not HySIS.
39.tq: Find the mismatched application by separating EO functions from communication functions.

39.s: The Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories generated from ocean-observation data are most directly useful to:
39.x: Oceansat observations support PFZ advisories, which help fishermen identify areas likely to have higher fish availability.
39.tq: Translate the technical abbreviation PFZ into its practical user group.

39.s: RISAT satellites use which technology for imaging under cloudy conditions and at night?
39.x: RISAT-1, RISAT-2 and RISAT-2B use Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), enabling all-weather, day-and-night imaging through clouds.
39.tq: Distinguish radar-based RISAT imaging from optical Earth observation.

39.s: SCATSAT-1 is equipped with a scatterometer primarily for measuring:
39.x: SCATSAT-1 uses a scatterometer to measure ocean-surface wind vectors, supporting cyclone forecasting.
39.tq: Match the sensor type with the parameter it measures.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the renamed EOS satellites:
1. EOS-04 (formerly RISAT-1A) is a SAR satellite that can observe crops under cloud cover.
2. EOS-06 is the new name of Oceansat-2.
3. EOS-04 data were used in NRSC's CROP wheat estimate for 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: EOS-04 = RISAT-1A, a SAR satellite that sees crops under cloud. Statement 2 is wrong: EOS-06 is Oceansat-3 (used for PFZ fishing advisories), not Oceansat-2. Statement 3 is correct: EOS-04 SAR fed NRSC's CROP wheat estimate 2024-25. Hence B; A and D include the false statement 2, C omits the true statement 1.
39.tq: EOS-04 = RISAT-1A (SAR, crops); EOS-06 = Oceansat-3 (PFZ).

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: SARAL — hyperspectral imaging of agricultural fields
39.x: SARAL is an ISRO-CNES altimetry mission using the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter to measure sea-surface height; hyperspectral agricultural imaging is associated with HySIS.
39.tq: Find the single application belonging to another satellite series.

39.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (Satellite group)
a. INSAT-3DS and Kalpana-1
b. Oceansat series
c. RISAT, Cartosat, EMISAT and EOS-N1
d. GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2

List-II (Application domain)
i. Broadband
 ii. Weather monitoring
 iii. Strategic surveillance
 iv. Ocean studies

Codes:
a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i
 a–iv, b–ii, c–i, d–iii
 a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i
 a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i
39.x: INSAT-3DS and Kalpana-1 are weather satellites; Oceansat serves ocean studies; RISAT, Cartosat, EMISAT and EOS-N1 are associated with strategic surveillance; and the GSAT satellites listed provide broadband services.
39.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with reversed application domains.

39.s: Cartosat-1 was primarily designed for:
o: Topographic mapping using stereo imagery for three-dimensional maps and elevation models
Measuring ocean waves and cyclone intensity
Providing dual-band radar observations of glaciers
Real-time crop monitoring through microwave radar only
39.x: Cartosat-1, launched in 2005, was intended for topographic mapping and supplied stereo images for 3D maps and elevation models.
39.tq: Associate stereo imagery with three-dimensional mapping and elevation modelling.

39.s: Which one of the following applications is most closely associated with the Cartosat-2 series?
o: Monitoring only volcanic heat through thermal infrared
Tracking crop harvest exclusively through EOS-04 SAR
Smart Cities, transport and border management using sub-metre imagery
Mapping only ocean colour and marine phytoplankton
39.x: The Cartosat-2 series, operational from 2007 onward, provides sub-metre resolution imagery for Smart Cities, transport, border management and infrastructure corridors.
39.tq: Use the application cluster associated with high-resolution mapping satellites.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about Cartosat-3:
1. It provides imagery of about 25 cm resolution.
2. It was launched on GSLV-F16 along with 13 US nanosatellites.
3. It was launched in 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: Cartosat-3 gives ~25 cm resolution. Statement 2 is wrong: it flew on PSLV-C47 (with 13 US nanosatellites); GSLV-F16 launched NISAR. Statement 3 is correct: launch was in 2019. Hence B; A and D include the false statement 2, C omits statement 1.
39.tq: Cartosat-3 = 25 cm, PSLV-C47, 2019, 13 US nanosats.

39.s:
Cartosat-3 imagery is associated with which of the following applications?
1. Smart Cities
2. PM Gati Shakti
3. Border surveillance
4. Heritage applications such as KASTURI and Bharat Darshan

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Cartosat-3 imagery supports Smart Cities, PM Gati Shakti, border surveillance and heritage applications including KASTURI and Bharat Darshan.
39.tq: Group all applications belonging to the same high-resolution Earth observation mission.

39.s: Which mission formed part of the record launch of 104 satellites into a 506 km sun-synchronous orbit on 15 February 2017?
39.x: The Cartosat-2 series was launched by PSLV-C37 on 15 February 2017 and formed part of the record 104-satellite launch into a 506 km SSO. Its mass was 714 kg.
39.tq: Combine the date, launch vehicle, orbit and record number to identify the mission.

39.s: EOS-03, also known as GISAT-1, was intended primarily for:
o: Near-real-time geo-imaging of floods and cyclones
Measuring ocean winds for cyclone forecasting
39.x: EOS-03, formerly GISAT-1, was designed for geo-imaging and near-real-time observation of events such as floods and cyclones.
39.tq: Separate the intended mission application from the later launch outcome.

39.s:
Which of the following statements regarding EOS-05 is correct?
1. It was formerly known as GISAT-1A.
2. It was launched by GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026.
3. It was the first Earth-observation imager working from geosynchronous orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: EOS-05 was formerly GISAT-1A, was launched on GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026, and became the first EO imager working from geosynchronous orbit.
39.tq: Verify the former name, launch details and unique orbital achievement together.

39.s: The sensor suite of EOS-05 spans which of the following bands?
o: Visible, near-infrared, short-wave infrared and long-wave infrared bands
39.x: EOS-05 sensors span visible, near-infrared, short-wave infrared and long-wave infrared portions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
39.tq: Select the option that gives the complete spectral range rather than a partial range.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about EOS-03:
1. It was also known as GISAT-1.
2. It was launched by GSLV-F10 in August 2021.
3. It successfully entered orbit and began geostationary imaging.
4. Its mission failed because of a cryogenic-stage problem.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: EOS-03 was also called GISAT-1 and was launched by GSLV-F10 in August 2021. The mission failed because of a cryogenic-stage problem, so statement 3 is false.
39.tq: Test a mission’s identity, launch details and outcome, with success-versus-failure as the trap.

39.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the reported launch failure?
1. EOS-09 — PSLV-C61, May 2025
2. EOS-N1 ‘Anvesha’ — PSLV-C62, January 2026
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: EOS-09, a C-band SAR satellite, failed to reach orbit on PSLV-C61 in May 2025. DRDO's hyperspectral EOS-N1, named Anvesha, failed on PSLV-C62 in January 2026.
39.tq: Check each failure against its launch vehicle and date before choosing the code.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about NISAR:
1. It was launched on 30 July 2025 by GSLV-F16.
2. It is the world's first dual-frequency radar satellite.
3. It uses L-band radar from NASA and S-band radar from ISRO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: NISAR was launched on GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025 and carries NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band radars, making it the first dual-frequency radar satellite of its kind.
39.tq: Combine mission date, record and agency-wise instrument contribution.

39.s: Which of the following correctly states the coverage and antenna features of NISAR?
o: It scans only the oceans every 12 months using a Ka-band altimeter.
It scans India every 3 days using a 1-metre communication antenna.
It scans nearly the whole Earth every 12 days and has a 12-metre antenna reflector deployed in orbit.
It scans the whole Earth every 24 hours using a 25-centimetre optical reflector.
39.x: NISAR scans nearly the whole Earth every 12 days and carries a 12-metre antenna reflector deployed in orbit.
39.tq: Pair the coverage interval with the distinctive antenna dimension.

39.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GSAT-7 'Rukmini' is the Indian Navy's dedicated communication satellite.
2. GSAT-7 was launched by PSLV from Sriharikota.
3. GSAT-30, a C/Ku-band communication satellite, replaced INSAT-4A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: GSAT-7 'Rukmini' serves the Navy (GSAT-7A serves the IAF). Statement 2 is wrong: GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou (2013). Statement 3 is correct: GSAT-30 (Ariane-5, Jan 2020) is C/Ku-band and replaced INSAT-4A. Hence B; A and D include the false statement 2, C omits statement 1.
39.tq: GSAT-7, GSAT-10, GSAT-30 all flew on Ariane-5 from Kourou.

39.s: Which one of the following statements regarding GSAT-10 is correct?
o: It was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou in 2012 and carried a GAGAN payload.
It was launched by GSLV-F10 for geostationary imaging.
It was launched by PSLV-C47 for high-resolution mapping.
It was launched in 2024 as a weather satellite fully funded by MoES.
39.x: GSAT-10 was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou in 2012 and carried a GAGAN payload.
39.tq: Match the satellite with its launch year, vehicle, site and distinctive payload.

39.s: Which satellite was fully funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and launched by GSLV-F14 on 17 February 2024?
39.x: INSAT-3DS is a weather satellite fully funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and was launched by GSLV-F14 on 17 February 2024.
39.tq: Match the funding ministry with the satellite’s weather function and launch date.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the INSAT system:
1. It was commissioned in 1983 with INSAT-1B.
2. INSAT-1B was launched on Ariane-1 from Kourou.
3. It is one of the largest domestic geostationary communication systems in the Asia-Pacific region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: INSAT was commissioned in 1983 with INSAT-1B. Statement 2 is wrong: INSAT-1B went up on the US Space Shuttle Challenger; Ariane-1 carried APPLE (1981). Statement 3 is correct. Hence B; A and D include the false statement 2, C omits statement 1.
39.tq: Ariane-1 = APPLE 1981; Challenger = INSAT-1B 1983.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the INSAT system:
1. It is managed by the inter-ministerial INSAT Coordination Committee (ICC).
2. Its satellites are controlled from the Master Control Facility at Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: the inter-ministerial ICC manages INSAT. Statement 2 is wrong: the Master Control Facility is at Hassan, Karnataka (Hyderabad hosts NRSC). Hence A; B and C wrongly accept statement 2, D wrongly rejects statement 1.
39.tq: MCF = Hassan; NRSC = Hyderabad.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the services provided through the INSAT system:
1. It supports telecommunication and television services.
2. It provides meteorological services.
3. It supports telemedicine and tele-education.
4. It has no role in search-and-rescue operations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: INSAT supports telecommunication, television, meteorology, telemedicine and tele-education. It also supports COSPAS-SARSAT search-and-rescue operations, so statement 4 is false.
39.tq: Find the one reversed service statement and select the corresponding coded combination.

39.s: Which of the following frequency bands are carried by the INSAT system?
o: L, X, V, W and Y bands
C, L, M, N and P bands
C, extended-C, Ku, Ka and S bands
39.x: The INSAT system carries C, extended-C, Ku, Ka and S bands.
39.tq: Recall the complete named list; do not confuse carried bands with bands used by other systems.

39.s: EDUSAT, launched in 2004, was primarily associated with which INSAT service?
39.x: EDUSAT (2004) delivered the INSAT system's tele-education service, giving schools and colleges two-way satellite links to virtual classrooms. Disaster warning, hyperspectral land imaging and COSPAS-SARSAT search and rescue are separate functions that EDUSAT did not perform.
39.tq: Identify the satellite from its application-specific name and service association.

39.s: India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite, APPLE (1981), was launched by:
39.x: APPLE was launched in 1981 on Ariane-1 from Kourou. SLV-3 launched Rohini (1980); the Space Shuttle Challenger carried INSAT-1B (1983); the Vostok launcher carried IRS-1A (1988).
39.tq: APPLE 1981 = Ariane-1, Kourou; INSAT-1B = Challenger.

39.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
39.x: GLONASS is owned by Russia. GPS belongs to the USA, Galileo to the European Union and BeiDou to China.
39.tq: Use owner-country discrimination and reject swapped global systems.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding satellite navigation systems:
1. GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou are global systems.
2. NavIC and QZSS are regional systems.
3. QZSS is owned by Japan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou are global systems, whereas NavIC and QZSS are regional systems; QZSS belongs to Japan.
39.tq: Check the system type first and then verify the owner-country statement.

39.s: India’s NavIC is distinctive among developing countries because it is:
o: the only system using both civilian and military signals
the only developing country operating a global navigation system
the only developing country with an independent regional navigation system
the first system jointly owned by India and the United States
39.x: India is described as the only developing country with its own independent regional navigation system.
39.tq: Identify the precise comparative claim rather than confusing regional and global status.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about IRNSS/NavIC:
1. IRNSS stands for Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System.
2. NavIC has been operational since 2018.
3. Its nominal constellation consists of three GEO and four GSO satellites.
4. It covers India and an area extending up to 1,500 km beyond India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All four statements are correct. NavIC is the operational Indian regional navigation system, with a seven-satellite constellation of three GEO and four GSO satellites and coverage extending up to 1,500 km beyond India.
39.tq: Verify the system’s name, operational date, constellation composition and coverage together.

39.s: NavIC signals are broadcast in which of the following frequency bands?
39.x: NavIC provides signals in the L5 and S bands.
39.tq: Distinguish navigation signal bands from communication payload bands such as C and Ku.

39.s: Which one of the following statements regarding NVS-02 is correct?
o: It was launched by PSLV-C47 in 2019 and entered a sun-synchronous orbit.
It was launched by GSLV-F15 on 29 January 2025 but did not reach its circular orbit.
It was launched by GSLV-F14 in 2024 and became a weather satellite.
It was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou in 2020 and replaced INSAT-4A.
39.x: NVS-02 was launched by GSLV-F15 on 29 January 2025, the 100th launch from Sriharikota, but did not reach its circular orbit. A review panel attributed the failure to a loose pyro connector.
39.tq: Match the navigation satellite with its launch vehicle, date and mission outcome.

39.s: Following the stoppage of the last rubidium atomic clock on IRNSS-1F on 13 March 2026, which one of the following describes NavIC's status?
o: Five PNT-capable satellites remained, enough for a position fix
All seven satellites lost navigation capability
Only three PNT-capable satellites remained, while a PNT fix needs at least four
IRNSS-1F was replaced the same week by NVS-02
39.x: After IRNSS-1F's last clock stopped (3 days after its 10-year design life), only IRNSS-1B, 1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable: three, below the minimum four needed. 'Five' and 'all seven lost' are wrong counts, and NVS-02 never reached its circular orbit (Jan 2025).
39.tq: Mar 2026: 3 PNT satellites (1B, 1I, NVS-01) < 4 needed.

39.s: In the Indian remote sensing data chain, processing is carried out at the nodal centre located at:
39.x: After collection and reception at a ground station, remote sensing data are processed at the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad, which functions as the nodal centre.
39.tq: Test the institutional location by distinguishing the processing centre from the launch and headquarters locations.

39.s: Which platform is the ISRO geoportal through which Earth-observation data are made openly accessible?
39.x: Bhuvan is the ISRO geoportal through which Earth-observation data are made openly accessible along with NRSC data services.
39.tq: Identify the platform by matching the service with its specific function.

39.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Bhoonidhi — ISRO-hosted Earth-observation data platform
2. VEDAS — ISRO-hosted data platform
3. Yuktdhara — planning MGNREGA assets for gram panchayats
4. MOSDAC — ISRO-hosted data platform
Select the correct answer using the code below.
39.x: Bhoonidhi, VEDAS and MOSDAC are hosted by ISRO as data platforms, while Yuktdhara supports gram panchayats in planning MGNREGA assets.
39.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after verifying each platform-function pairing.

39.s: Which of the following is NOT a national Earth-observation application listed for NRSC and related platforms?
o: Operation of civil aviation precision-landing systems
39.x: Groundwater mapping, FASAL crop forecasting and INFFRAS forest-fire monitoring are listed Earth-observation applications. Civil aviation precision landing is associated with GAGAN, not this list of NRSC applications.
39.tq: Separate the application domain of NRSC platforms from the aviation function of GAGAN.

39.s: The Landslide Atlas of India was released by:
o: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
39.x: The Landslide Atlas of India was released by the National Remote Sensing Centre in 2023.
39.tq: Use the responsible-agency trap by distinguishing the remote sensing agency from neighbouring scientific organisations.

39.s: Joshimath subsidence was mapped by NRSC using images from:
39.x: NRSC mapped the Joshimath subsidence using Cartosat-2S images in 2023.
39.tq: Discriminate between closely related Cartosat and EOS satellite designations.

39.s: CROP, the NRSC framework, uses EOS-04 SAR data primarily to monitor:
o: Satellite launch trajectories and orbital debris
Urban heat islands and volcanic eruptions
Sowing, crop growth and harvesting near real time
Only ocean salinity and sea-surface temperature
39.x: CROP stands for Comprehensive Remote Sensing Observation on Crop Progress and uses EOS-04 SAR to track sowing, growth and harvest near real time.
39.tq: Expand the acronym and connect the named framework with its agricultural application.

39.s: Bhuvan provides flood-inundation maps and cyclone tracks using data from:
39.x: Bhuvan uses RISAT and INSAT-3DS data to provide flood-inundation maps and cyclone tracks.
39.tq: Match the application platform with the specific satellite data sources.

39.s: The AP Space Applications Centre, or APSAC, is primarily the remote-sensing agency of which State?
39.x: APSAC is Andhra Pradesh’s State remote-sensing agency.
39.tq: Use the location clue embedded in the institutional name and context.

39.s: The coastal location of SDSC-SHAR enables it to contribute data for tracking cyclones over which water body for APSDMA?
39.x: SDSC-SHAR contributes data for Bay of Bengal cyclone tracking for APSDMA.
39.tq: Link the geographic location of the centre with the nearby cyclone-monitoring region.

39.s: Which of the following applications is NOT associated with EOS-05?
39.x: EOS-05 is intended for applications such as floods, cyclones, forest fires, crops and security. Deep-sea submarine communication is not listed among its applications.
39.tq: Find the option outside the satellite's Earth-imaging application set.

39.s:
With reference to India's geostationary satellite applications, consider the following statements:
1. The earlier geostationary 'eyes' of India were weather satellites of the INSAT-3D series.
2. EOS-05 is intended for land imaging rather than being merely a weather satellite.
3. EOS-03 became India's first operational geostationary land-imaging satellite after a successful launch.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: The INSAT-3D series represented India's earlier geostationary weather satellites, while EOS-05 is India's first geosynchronous land-imaging satellite. Statement 3 is false because EOS-03 was lost at launch.
39.tq: Reject the false success claim and compare the roles of the INSAT-3D series, EOS-03 and EOS-05.

39.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. IIRS and CSSTEAP, both located in Dehradun, contribute to space-application capacity building.
2. The Integrated Mission for Sustainable Development began in 2002.
3. EOS-05 was launched by GSLV-F10.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: IIRS and CSSTEAP are both in Dehradun. Statement 2 is wrong: the Integrated Mission for Sustainable Development dates to 1992 (covering 174 districts). Statement 3 is wrong: EOS-05 flew on GSLV-F17 (4 Sep 2026); GSLV-F10 lost EOS-03 in 2021. Hence A; B, C and D all include a false statement.
39.tq: Dehradun = IIRS + CSSTEAP; IMSD = 1992.

39.s: All the launches referred to in the context of India's space programme are stated to take place from SDSC-SHAR, located in:
39.x: SDSC-SHAR is located at Sriharikota in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh.
39.tq: Identify the launch-site location rather than confusing it with the control or training centres.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about the RISAT satellites:
1. RISAT-2BR1, launched by PSLV-C48 in December 2019, serves radar imaging, disaster management and surveillance.
2. RISAT-1 carries an L-band SAR.
3. RISAT-1 provides day-night, all-weather imaging.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
40.x: Statement 1 is correct per the launch table. Statement 2 is wrong: RISAT-1 (PSLV-C19) carries a C-band (5.35 GHz) SAR. Statement 3 is correct: SAR gives day-night, all-weather imaging. Hence B; A and D include the false statement 2, C omits statement 1.
40.tq: RISAT-1 = C-band 5.35 GHz SAR; RISAT-2BR1 = PSLV-C48.

40.s: EOS-07, launched by SSLV-D2 on 10 February 2023, was intended mainly for:
40.x: EOS-07 was an Earth-observation and technology-demonstration mission launched by SSLV-D2.
40.tq: Use the purpose to distinguish an Earth-observation satellite from communication and navigation satellites.

40.s: Which satellite was intended for NavIC navigation but missed its intended orbit?
40.x: NVS-02, launched by GSLV-F15 in January 2025, was intended for NavIC navigation but missed its intended orbit.
40.tq: Link the unusual mission outcome with the correct navigation satellite.

40.s: NISAR, launched by GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025, is associated with:
o: Earth observation in a sun-synchronous polar orbit with NASA
40.x: NISAR is an Earth-observation mission with NASA and was placed in a sun-synchronous polar orbit.
40.tq: Use the mission's international partnership and orbit-purpose combination.

40.s: EOS-05, launched by GSLV-F17 in September 2026, is described as an ‘eye in the sky’ for which purposes?
40.x: EOS-05 is a geo-platform imaging satellite intended for agriculture, environmental monitoring and disaster applications.
40.tq: Interpret the mission description through its stated application areas.

40.s: Which one of the following launch-date statements is correct?
o: NISAR was launched by PSLV-C56 in 2023.
INSAT-3DS was launched by GSLV-F14 in 2024.
Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C48 in 2019.
DS-SAR was launched by PSLV-C59 in 2024.
40.x: INSAT-3DS was launched by GSLV-F14 in 2024. Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57 in 2023, DS-SAR by PSLV-C56 in 2023, and NISAR by GSLV-F16 in 2025.
40.tq: Find the correctly matched vehicle and year among closely related launch facts.

40.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SpaDeX was launched by PSLV-C60 on 30 December 2024.
2. SpaDeX achieved docking on 16 January 2025.
3. PSLV-C60 holds India's record for the most satellites launched in one mission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
40.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: PSLV-C60 launched SpaDeX on 30 Dec 2024 and docking came on 16 Jan 2025. Statement 3 is wrong: the record is PSLV-C37 with 104 satellites (2017). Hence A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
40.tq: Most satellites = PSLV-C37 (104); SpaDeX = PSLV-C60.

40.s: India became the fourth country to dock in space through SpaDeX. Which of the following countries were identified as the earlier three?
40.x: The United States, Russia and China had achieved space docking before India, making India the fourth country through SpaDeX.
40.tq: Use the stated ordinal ranking and identify the complete preceding group.

40.s: The SpaDeX capability is particularly needed for which proposed Indian space facility?
40.x: Space docking capability demonstrated by SpaDeX is needed for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.
40.tq: Connect a technology demonstration with its stated future application.

40.s: The heaviest payload launched by an Indian rocket, BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg), was launched on 24 December 2025 by:
40.x: LVM3-M6 launched the 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2 (223 sq m phased array, direct-to-smartphone broadband) on 24 Dec 2025. PSLV-C60 launched SpaDeX, GSLV-F17 launched EOS-05, and SSLV is a small-satellite launcher.
40.tq: Heaviest = BlueBird Block-2, 6,100 kg, LVM3-M6.

40.s: Duchifat-3, a foreign customer satellite launched by PSLV-C48, belonged to which country?
40.x: Duchifat-3 was an Israeli satellite launched by PSLV-C48.
40.tq: Pair the foreign satellite with its country and vehicle.

40.s: Proba-3 was launched by PSLV-C59 in December 2024 for which agency?
40.x: Proba-3 was an ESA satellite mission launched by PSLV-C59 in December 2024.
40.tq: Distinguish the European agency from the agencies involved in other joint missions.

40.s: As reported for the Indian space programme, ISRO had launched how many foreign satellites of more than 34 countries?
40.x: ISRO had launched 433 foreign satellites from more than 34 countries; more than half were from the United States.
40.tq: Distinguish the overall ISRO total from the smaller NSIL figures.

40.s: Which mission and lost payload are correctly matched?
40.x: GSLV-F02 lost INSAT-4C in 2006. GSLV-F10 lost EOS-03, SSLV-D1 lost EOS-02 and AzaadiSAT, and PSLV-C61 lost EOS-09.
40.tq: Find the correctly matched failure and payload among swapped mission pairs.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about PSLV-C61:
1. It was launched on 18 May 2025.
2. It lost EOS-09, also known as RISAT-1B.
3. EOS-09 carried a C-band SAR payload.
4. The failure occurred at the third stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: All four statements are correct regarding the PSLV-C61 failure and EOS-09/RISAT-1B.
40.tq: Verify date, alternate name, payload type and failure stage independently.

40.s: Which one of the following statements about PSLV-C62 is correct?
o: It successfully placed NISAR into its intended orbit.
It failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of its third stage, losing the loss of EOS-N1 ‘Anvesha’ and 15 co-passengers.
It failed because the first stage did not ignite and lost INSAT-4C.
It carried only a Spanish re-entry capsule and no satellite payload.
40.x: On 12 January 2026, PSLV-C62 failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of its third stage and lost EOS-N1 ‘Anvesha’ along with 15 co-passengers.
40.tq: Use the failed stage and payload count to separate PSLV-C62 from earlier failures.

40.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with the PSLV-C62 co-passengers?
o: AayulSAT was a navigation satellite, while MOI-1 was a solar coronagraph.
AayulSAT was a weather satellite, while MOI-1 was a lunar lander.
AayulSAT was the first on-orbit refuelling demonstrator, while MOI-1 was an AI image laboratory.
Both AayulSAT and MOI-1 were foreign communication satellites.
40.x: AayulSAT was identified as the first on-orbit refuelling demonstrator and MOI-1 as an AI image laboratory among the PSLV-C62 co-passengers.
40.tq: Match each unusual payload description with its correct satellite name.

40.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a re-entry experiment?
40.x: SRE-1 was associated with PSLV-C7 in 2007. CARE was associated with LVM3 in 2014, and POEM-3 with PSLV-C58 in 2024.
40.tq: Match each experiment with its vehicle and year before considering the distractors.

40.s: POEM platforms are best described as:
o: Spent PS4 stages used as orbital laboratories
Reusable crew capsules for ISS missions
Foreign customer satellites launched by PSLV
40.x: POEM platforms use the spent PS4 stage as an orbital laboratory.
40.tq: Interpret the platform’s function from its structural origin and orbital use.

40.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Indian satellites used for military communication is correct?
o: GSAT-7, GSAT-7A and GSAT-7B are all operational satellites exclusively used by the Navy.
