49.tq: Identify the system from its strategic role rather than its name alone.

49.s: Which one of the following statements about Kinzhal is correct?
o: It is a Pakistani 450 km surface-to-surface missile.
It is an Iranian ballistic missile series.
It is a North Korean ship-launched cruise missile.
It is a Russian air-launched hypersonic missile.
49.x: Kinzhal is a Russian air-launched hypersonic missile. Six Kinzhal missiles were reportedly intercepted by Patriot systems in one night over Kyiv in May 2023.
49.tq: Distinguish Kinzhal from the ship-launched Zircon by launch platform.

49.s: The ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for which of the following purposes?
o: Testing of the Astra export configuration
Demonstration of the first indigenous anti-radiation missile
49.x: Ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for LRAShM validation rounds.
49.tq: Match the distinctive geographical clue with the specific validation activity rather than with a missile name alone.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s long-range missile capability:
1. Agni, Nirbhay LR-LACM and BrahMos are identified as long-range systems that are not yet fully integrated.
2. India’s rocket force is still described as a concept rather than an established force.
3. The long-range missile systems are described as fully integrated into an operational rocket force.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the assessment states that the systems are not yet fully integrated and that the rocket force remains only a concept.
49.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reported assessment by changing an incomplete capability into a fully operational one.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's defence 'firsts':
1. Mission Shakti made India the fourth country with anti-satellite capability, after the USA, Russia and China.
2. Indonesia was the first export buyer of BrahMos.
3. The Philippines was the first export buyer of the Astra missile.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mission Shakti (2019) made India the 4th ASAT nation after the USA, Russia and China. Statements 2 and 3 swap the buyers: the Philippines was the first BrahMos buyer, and Indonesia the first Astra buyer (Jul 2026). So '1 only'; the other codes accept one or both swapped statements.
49.tq: Philippines = BrahMos first; Indonesia = Astra first; Shakti = 4th ASAT.

50.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its approximate U-235 enrichment level?
50.x: Natural uranium contains about 0.7% U-235. Reactor-grade LEU is about 3–5%, HEU is 20% or more, and weapons-grade uranium is about 90%.
50.tq: Compare the enrichment categories in ascending order rather than relying on the labels alone.

50.s: In U-235 fission, the impact of a neutron can produce:
o: Electrons that directly sustain a chemical reaction
Two smaller nuclei and two or three neutrons that help sustain the chain reaction
One larger nucleus and no additional neutrons
Hydrogen isotopes and a fusion primary only
50.x: A neutron striking U-235 can split it into two smaller nuclei, such as barium and krypton, while releasing two or three neutrons that sustain the chain reaction.
50.tq: Follow the particle-level sequence from neutron impact to chain reaction.

50.s: Which device is described as a high-speed switch used to fire the detonators of a nuclear bomb?
50.x: A krytron is a high-speed switch used to fire nuclear-bomb detonators. MOSFETs, solid-state relays and solenoids are specifically distinguished from it in this context.
50.tq: Use precise technical terminology to distinguish the specialised device from ordinary switching components.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a fission weapon from a fusion (thermonuclear) weapon?
o: A fission weapon splits heavy nuclei such as U-235 or Pu-239 in a chain reaction, while a fusion weapon fuses light hydrogen isotopes using a fission primary as trigger.
A fission weapon fuses hydrogen isotopes, while a fusion weapon splits U-235 nuclei.
Both weapons work only by splitting heavy nuclei; they differ only in yield.
A fusion weapon needs no trigger, while a fission weapon needs a fusion primary to start.
50.x: Fission (atomic) weapons split heavy nuclei (U-235/Pu-239) in a neutron chain reaction, as in Pokhran-I. Fusion (hydrogen) weapons fuse light hydrogen isotopes, with a fission 'primary' supplying the heat to trigger fusion, as tested in Pokhran-II. The second option reverses the two, the third ignores fusion, and the fourth reverses the trigger relationship.
50.tq: Fission splits heavy; fusion joins light, lit by a fission primary.

50.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Pokhran-I is correct?
o: It comprised five fission and fusion devices led by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
It was conducted on 18 May 1974 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and was described as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
It was conducted on 11 May 1998 under Prime Minister A.B. Vajpayee as a thermonuclear test.
It was conducted at Pokhran under Prime Minister Morarji Desai as Operation Shakti.
50.x: Pokhran-I took place on 18 May 1974 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and was officially described as a peaceful nuclear explosion. The other options refer to features of Pokhran-II or contain incorrect details.
50.tq: Use the date, Prime Minister and official description together to eliminate mixed-up details.

50.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Pokhran-II:
1. It was conducted under Prime Minister A.B. Vajpayee.
2. The scientific leadership included A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and R. Chidambaram.
3. It involved both fission and fusion devices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements are correct. Pokhran-II was conducted under A.B. Vajpayee, involved A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and R. Chidambaram, and included fission as well as fusion devices.
50.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.

50.s: 11 May is observed in India as:
50.x: 11 May is observed as National Technology Day in India, commemorating the 1998 Pokhran tests.
50.tq: Use the exact official observance name rather than a plausible substitute.

50.s: Pokhran-II was conducted on:
50.x: Pokhran-II, known as Operation Shakti, was conducted on 11 and 13 May 1998 under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
50.tq: Distinguish the two 1998 test dates from the single date of Pokhran-I.

50.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Pokhran-I (1974) - Smiling Buddha
2. Pokhran-II (1998) - Operation Shakti
3. Pokhran-II - a single fission device
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
50.x: Pokhran-I (18 May 1974) was code-named 'Smiling Buddha' and Pokhran-II (11 and 13 May 1998) 'Operation Shakti', so pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: Pokhran-II tested five devices, both fission and fusion. '1 only' misses pair 2, while the other two codes wrongly include pair 3.
50.tq: Buddha smiled in 1974; Shakti (5 devices) in 1998.

50.s: India's nuclear doctrine was officially adopted by the Cabinet Committee on Security on
50.x: The nuclear doctrine was officially adopted by the Cabinet Committee on Security on 4 January 2003.
50.tq: Distinguish the official adoption date from the draft-doctrine year and Pokhran-II date.

50.s: The draft of India's nuclear doctrine was issued in
50.x: India's draft nuclear doctrine was issued in 1999; it was officially adopted in 2003.
50.tq: Separate the draft year from the later year of official adoption.

50.s: The 'No First Use' principle in India's nuclear policy is associated with the Vajpayee government after
50.x: The No First Use principle dates from the Vajpayee government after Pokhran-II.
50.tq: Link the policy tenet to the correct nuclear milestone rather than to a diplomatic summit.

50.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's nuclear doctrine:
1. India maintains credible minimum deterrence.
2. India has a No First Use policy.
3. The doctrine provides for massive retaliation causing unacceptable damage.
4. India has declared that it will use nuclear weapons against every non-nuclear-weapon state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are tenets of the doctrine. Statement 4 is false because the doctrine provides for no use against non-nuclear-weapon states, subject to the stated doctrine concerning major biological or chemical attacks.
50.tq: Watch for an absolute statement that reverses the no-use commitment.

50.s: India's nuclear doctrine retains the nuclear option against a major attack involving
50.x: The doctrine retains the nuclear option against a major biological or chemical attack.
50.tq: Recall the specific exception rather than broadening it to every form of attack.

50.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Body)
a. Political Council of the Nuclear Command Authority
b. Executive Council of the Nuclear Command Authority
c. Strategic Forces Command
d. Cabinet Committee on Security

List-II (Function or head)
i. Manages nuclear forces
ii. Headed by the Prime Minister
iii. Supervised civilian political control
iv. Headed by the National Security Adviser
50.x: The Political Council is headed by the Prime Minister, the Executive Council by the National Security Adviser, the Strategic Forces Command manages nuclear forces, and civilian political control is supervised by the CCS.
50.tq: Start from the sure institutional pairs and eliminate codes with a mismatched head or function.

50.s: Who is the sole authority empowered to order the use of nuclear weapons under the Nuclear Command Authority structure?
o: The Prime Minister as head of the Political Council
50.x: The Prime Minister, as head of the Political Council, is the sole authority to order nuclear use.
50.tq: Use the question 'who would do this job?' to distinguish political authority from advisory and executive roles.

50.s: Under India’s No First Use policy, nuclear weapons may be used in retaliation against
o: any conventional attack on Indian territory
a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces
a cyberattack on India’s strategic infrastructure
any military alliance formed against India
50.x: India’s No First Use policy permits nuclear weapons only in retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces.
50.tq: Distinguish the exact condition attached to a strategic policy from broader military contingencies.

50.s:
Which of the following is associated with India’s continuing nuclear policy?
1. Continued moratorium on nuclear testing
2. Strict export controls
3. Support for disarmament and the Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
50.x: India’s nuclear policy includes a continued testing moratorium, strict export controls and support for disarmament and the FMCT.
50.tq: Recognise a cluster of related policy commitments rather than an operational doctrine alone.

50.s: The Strategic Forces Command is best described as
o: a joint research body of DRDO and ISRO
a civilian body regulating nuclear exports
a tri-service command managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal
a parliamentary committee supervising defence expenditure
50.x: The Strategic Forces Command is a tri-service command responsible for managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal.
50.tq: Match the organisation with its precise institutional role.

50.s: Agni user trials are conducted under the aegis of which organisation?
50.x: Agni user trials are conducted under the aegis of the Strategic Forces Command.
50.tq: Identify the operational agency rather than the policy-making authority.

50.s:
With reference to the legs of India's nuclear triad, consider the following statements:
1. The land leg comprises the Prithvi and Agni series, including canisterised road- and rail-mobile missiles.
2. The air leg comprises Su-30MKI and Rafale aircraft carrying free-fall nuclear bombs.
3. The sea leg comprises K-15 and K-4 SLBMs fired from Arihant-class SSBNs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
50.x: Statement 1 is correct: Prithvi and Agni (canisterised, road- and rail-mobile) form the land leg. Statement 2 is wrong: the air leg is Jaguar and Mirage 2000 with free-fall bombs. Statement 3 is correct: K-15/K-4 SLBMs from Arihant-class SSBNs form the sea leg. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 2.
50.tq: Air leg = Jaguar + Mirage 2000; watch for Su-30MKI/Rafale swapped in.

50.s: Which of the following statements about Dhanush is correct?
o: It is a free-fall nuclear bomb delivered by Mirage 2000.
It is an SLBM carried by Arihant-class SSBNs.
It was fired from ships including INS Subhadra and INS Rajput.
It is an intercontinental ballistic missile launched from rail platforms.
50.x: Dhanush was fired from ships, including INS Subhadra and INS Rajput; it is distinct from the K-15 and K-4 SLBMs deployed on SSBNs.
50.tq: Separate an earlier ship-launched system from submarine-launched ballistic missiles.

50.s: Why are SSBNs regarded as the most survivable leg of the nuclear triad?
o: They eliminate the need for land-based deterrence.
They remain permanently visible to adversaries.
Their concealment supports a guaranteed second-strike capability.
50.x: SSBNs are difficult to detect and destroy, thereby supporting a reliable second-strike capability that underpins India’s No First Use posture.
50.tq: Connect survivability with the strategic purpose of assured retaliation.

50.s: The next strategic step associated with India’s SSBN-based deterrence is
o: ending the No First Use policy
replacement of all missiles by free-fall bombs
50.x: Continuous at-sea deterrence is identified as the next step in strengthening India’s SSBN-based nuclear deterrence.
50.tq: Identify the policy objective that follows from the capability already described.

50.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
50.x: K-15 Sagarika has an approximate range of 750 km. K-4 has an approximate range of 3,500 km, while K-5 is described as a longer-range SLBM.
50.tq: Find the range reversal between the two K-series missiles.

50.s: The K-4 missile is correctly described as a
o: short-range conventional cruise missile for aircraft
1,000 km-range land-attack missile powered by a turbojet
3,500 km-range, nuclear-capable missile for Arihant-class submarines
50.x: K-4 is a nuclear-capable submarine-launched ballistic missile with an approximate range of 3,500 km, intended for Arihant-class submarines.
50.tq: Combine range, nuclear capability and platform to identify the missile.

50.s: The letter 'K' in the K-series of submarine-launched missiles honours
50.x: The K-series designation honours former President and missile scientist Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.
50.tq: Use the naming-convention clue rather than confusing it with a platform designation.

50.s:
Arrange the following Arihant-class submarines in chronological order of their commissioning or indicated commissioning sequence:
A. INS Aridhaman
B. INS Arihant
C. INS Arighat
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
50.x: INS Arihant was associated with 2016, INS Arighat with 2024, and INS Aridhaman is the third boat whose commissioning was signalled in 2026.
50.tq: Fix the sequence using the years 2016, 2024 and 2026.

50.s: INS Arihant is designated S2 and is best described as:
50.x: INS Arihant, commissioned in 2016, is India’s first indigenous SSBN. The other options refer to conventional or leased submarine categories.
50.tq: Distinguish submarine type and origin instead of treating every naval submarine as an SSBN.

50.s: Which of the following statements regarding INS Arighaat is correct?
o: It is designated S4 and has eight vertical launch systems.
It is designated S3, was commissioned in 2024, and had the K-4 tested from it.
It is a German Type 209 conventional submarine commissioned before 1988.
It is designated S2 and was commissioned in 2016 as the first indigenous SSBN.
50.x: INS Arighaat is designated S3, was commissioned in 2024, is of similar size to Arihant, and had the K-4 tested from it.
50.tq: Match the boat designation, commissioning year and distinguishing test event.

50.s: The ATV project was undertaken primarily to develop:
o: Indigenous SSBNs with DRDO and private-sector participation and Russian assistance
A network of anti-drone systems with Israel Aerospace Industries
A long-range air-defence radar with the United States
A conventional submarine fleet based entirely on German designs
50.x: The Advanced Technology Vessel project was initiated more than three decades ago by DRDO and private firms, with Russian assistance, to build SSBNs.
50.tq: Identify the project from its objective and institutional partnership.

50.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: INS Chakra — leased Charlie-class submarine; INS Chakra II — leased Russian Akula-class submarine
INS Chakra — German Type 209; INS Chakra II — Kilo-class submarine
INS Chakra — indigenous SSBN; INS Chakra II — conventional diesel-electric submarine
INS Chakra — Arihant-class boat; INS Chakra II — Barak-class submarine
50.x: INS Chakra was a leased Charlie-class submarine obtained in 1988, while INS Chakra II was the Russian Akula-class boat formerly known as Nerpa.
50.tq: Start from the sure pair linking each leased submarine with its class.

50.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: INS Shishumar — German Type 209 conventional submarine
INS Sindhuvir — Russian Kilo-class, Sindhughosh-class submarine
INS Shalki — German Type 209 conventional submarine
50.x: INS Shalki is a German Type 209 conventional diesel-electric submarine, not an Arihant-class SSBN. INS Shishumar is also Type 209, while INS Sindhuvir belongs to the Russian Kilo/Sindhughosh class.
50.tq: Find the wrong submarine classification among closely related naval platforms.

50.s: INS Aridhaman, the third Arihant-class boat commissioned in April 2026, differs from INS Arihant chiefly in that it
o: is about 7,000 t with 8 vertical launch tubes for up to 24 K-15 or 8 K-4/K-5 missiles
is a leased Russian Akula-class nuclear attack submarine
is a German Type 209 diesel-electric submarine
carries only 2 launch tubes for Dhanush missiles
50.x: INS Aridhaman (S4), commissioned at Visakhapatnam in April 2026, is larger than INS Arihant (about 6,000 t, 4 VLS): about 7,000 t with 8 VLS for 24 K-15 or 8 K-4/K-5. The Akula class is the leased INS Chakra II, Type 209 boats are Shalki and Shishumar, and Dhanush was ship-fired, not from SSBNs.
50.tq: Arihant 4 tubes; Aridhaman 8 tubes, 7,000 t.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the BMD interceptor with its tier?
o: PAD — exo-atmospheric interception at higher altitude
PAD — endo-atmospheric interception at lower altitude
AAD — exo-atmospheric interception at higher altitude
50.x: PAD, or Prithvi Air Defence, is the higher-altitude exo-atmospheric interceptor. AAD is the lower-altitude endo-atmospheric interceptor, while Swordfish is a tracking radar.
50.tq: Start with the altitude clue and then distinguish interceptor from radar.

50.s: AD-1 and AD-2 are associated with which phase of India’s BMD programme?
o: Phase II, aimed at longer-range threats of about the 5,000-km class
The initial exo-atmospheric tier for short-range threats only
50.x: AD-1 and AD-2 are Phase II BMD interceptors intended to address longer-range threats, including those in approximately the 5,000-km class.
50.tq: Separate the Phase II interceptor pair from the first-tier PAD/AAD systems.

50.s: The Swordfish radar is primarily used to:
o: Jam drone-control signals at short range
Track ballistic missiles and space objects at distances exceeding 1,500 km
50.x: The Long-Range Tracking Radar, known as Swordfish, tracks ballistic missiles and space objects at distances of more than 1,500 km.
50.tq: Identify the sensor by its tracking function and range rather than by the interceptor it supports.

50.s: Which of the following statements about the June 2026 BMD demonstration is correct?
o: It was the maiden test of the K-15 from INS Arihant.
It concerned only the procurement approval of MRSAM by the DAC.
It demonstrated a multi-layered BMD system in which interceptors destroyed their targets and indicated capability against threats up to ICBM class.
It demonstrated only a conventional submarine-launched missile with no interception component.
50.x: In June 2026, DRDO demonstrated a multi-layered BMD system with interceptors destroying targets, placing India among the few countries capable of engaging threats up to ICBM class.
50.tq: Separate a live capability demonstration from procurement, submarine and anti-ship events.

50.s:
With reference to the S-400 Triumf, consider the following statements:
1. China was its third operator after Russia and Belarus.
2. Turkey and India are among its operators.
3. The Indian Air Force refers to its S-400 system as ‘Sudarshan Chakra’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: Statement 1 is wrong: China was the first foreign buyer (after Russia); Belarus came later. Turkey and India are operators, and the IAF calls its system Sudarshan Chakra. So '2 and 3 only'.
50.tq: Combine operator-list facts with the Indian designation without reversing the sequence.

50.s: Barak-1 is best described as a:
o: High-power laser weapon developed by DRDO
Indigenous anti-drone electronic-warfare system of the Air Force
Long-range ballistic missile interceptor of the Indian Army
Ship-based point-defence surface-to-air missile system of the Indian Navy
50.x: Barak-1 is an Israeli-origin, ship-based point-defence surface-to-air missile system operated by the Navy.
50.tq: Identify the correct combination of platform, role and service operator.

50.s: MRSAM or Barak-8 has been developed through cooperation between:
50.x: MRSAM/Barak-8 is an India-Israel programme involving DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI).
50.tq: Use the development-agency trap to distinguish DRDO-IAI cooperation from other partnerships.

50.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Akashteer — BEL and the Indian Army
Akash Tarang — anti-drone soft-kill electronic-warfare system
IADWS — ship-based point-defence system of the Navy
IADWS — DRDO indigenous integrated air-defence system
50.x: IADWS is an indigenous, multi-layered integrated air-defence weapon system developed by DRDO; it is not a ship-based point-defence system. Akashteer is associated with BEL and the Army, while Akash Tarang jams drone-control signals.
50.tq: Find the mismatched authority or platform rather than selecting the familiar system name.

50.s: The Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) comprises:
o: QRSAM, VSHORADS and a high-power laser directed-energy weapon
PAD, AAD and Swordfish radar only
MRSAM, BrahMos and a nuclear-powered interceptor
50.x: IADWS is a multi-layered indigenous system comprising QRSAM, VSHORADS and a high-power laser directed-energy weapon.
50.tq: Test the system’s component combination instead of its country of origin.

50.s: Mission Sudarshan Chakra, under Vision 2035, is intended to create a comprehensive national shield integrating:
o: Coastal radar, naval aviation and aircraft carriers
Space launch vehicles, weather satellites and navigation satellites
Only nuclear weapons and submarine-launched missiles
50.x: Mission Sudarshan Chakra is envisaged as a networked national shield integrating air defence, cybersecurity and surveillance.
50.tq: Reject the ‘only’ formulation and select the stated multi-domain purpose.

50.s: Which of the following systems are identified as building blocks of Mission Sudarshan Chakra?
o: INS Arihant, INS Arighaat and INS Aridhaman
50.x: Akash Tarang, MRSAM and VSHORADS are identified as building blocks of Mission Sudarshan Chakra.
50.tq: Match the mission with its component systems, not with unrelated strategic platforms.

50.s: Project Kusha is associated with a DRDO long-range air-defence project having interceptor ranges of approximately:
50.x: Project Kusha is reported as a long-range air-defence project with M1, M2 and M3 interceptors of about 150, 250 and 350–400 km ranges, respectively.
50.tq: Read the range progression carefully and avoid confusing interceptor ranges with missile ranges.

50.s: With reference to Mission Sudarshan Chakra, which one of the following was keyed as its stated aim in the UPSC 2026 question?
o: To enhance air defence, ballistic missile defence and aerial offensive capabilities
To build a fleet of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers
To replace the nuclear triad with space-based weapons
To create a national satellite navigation system for civil aviation
50.x: UPSC 2026 keyed as correct only that Mission Sudarshan Chakra aims to enhance air defence, BMD and aerial offensive capabilities; it is a networked national shield (Vision 2035). It is not about aircraft carriers, replacing the triad or civil satellite navigation.
50.tq: Sudarshan Chakra = air defence + BMD + aerial offence.

50.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Regime)
a. MTCR
b. Wassenaar Arrangement
c. Australia Group
d. Hague Code of Conduct

List-II (India's status)
i. Joined in 2018
ii. Joined in 2016 as the 35th member
iii. Joined in 2016
iv. Joined in 2017

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
50.x: India joined the MTCR as its 35th member in 2016, Wassenaar in 2017, Australia Group in 2018 and the Hague Code of Conduct in 2016.
50.tq: Start with the sure MTCR and Australia Group pairs, then eliminate the codes.

50.s: India's status in relation to the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) is that it:
o: is not a member; its 2016 application was blocked by China
50.x: India is not an NSG member. It applied in 2016, but its membership was blocked by China.
50.tq: Distinguish membership from a waiver or participation in guidelines.

50.s: India follows the guidelines of the NSG, MTCR, Wassenaar Arrangement and Australia Group through the:
o: Atomic Energy Act and the Union List alone
National Security Act and the IT Rules
Foreign Exchange Management Act and SEZ list
50.x: India implements or follows the relevant guidelines through the WMD Act and the SCOMET list. United States support helped India enter three of these regimes.
50.tq: Match the regulatory instruments with the export-control arrangements.

50.s: India has not signed the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty primarily because it regards the treaty as
o: a treaty limited only to chemical weapons
a treaty that requires membership of the NSG
an agreement that prohibits civilian nuclear energy
50.x: India considers the NPT discriminatory because it creates an unequal division between recognised nuclear-weapon states and other states, a position often described as opposition to nuclear apartheid.
50.tq: Link a non-membership status with the stated reason rather than confusing it with another regime.

50.s: India’s position regarding the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty is that it will not sign the treaty until it is linked to
o: automatic membership of the UN Security Council
a ban on all conventional weapons
the abolition of the Nuclear Suppliers Group
50.x: India has not signed the CTBT because it seeks a link between the treaty and time-bound global nuclear disarmament; it nevertheless observes a voluntary test moratorium.
50.tq: Test the precise reason for non-signature and distinguish it from membership conditions of other regimes.

50.s: India supports a universal and verifiable Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty provided that it
o: does not cap India’s existing stockpile
50.x: India supports a universal and verifiable FMCT, but its position is that the treaty should not cap its existing stockpile.
50.tq: Focus on the qualification attached to India’s support for an international treaty.

50.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding India's domestic pressurised heavy water reactors and the NSG?
o: India's 700 MW PHWRs use domestic uranium and therefore need no NSG clearance.
India's 700 MW PHWRs use imported uranium and require individual NSG approval.
Only military PHWRs are covered by the 2008 NSG waiver.
All Indian reactors are exempt from IAEA safeguards because of NSG membership.
50.x: India's 700 MW PHWRs use domestic uranium and do not need NSG clearance. India is also not an NSG member.
50.tq: Apply the distinction between domestic fuel use and NSG clearance.

50.s: The operational deployment of Indian warheads cited in the June 2026 assessment was linked particularly to
o: Dhanush missiles mounted exclusively on aircraft carriers
only free-fall bombs carried by Jaguar aircraft
SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni missiles
civilian nuclear reactors and space launch vehicles
50.x: The cited deployment was linked to SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni missiles.
50.tq: Match a current quantitative assessment with the two capabilities associated with it.

50.s: INS Aridhaman was commissioned in
50.x: INS Aridhaman (S4), the third Arihant-class SSBN (about 7,000 t, 8 VLS), was commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 3 April 2026. April 2024 was INS Arighaat (S3).
50.tq: Distinguish closely spaced years and months in a current-affairs fact.

50.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the United States nuclear triad?
o: Minuteman III ICBMs, strategic bombers and Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs
Tomahawk missiles, aircraft carriers and attack submarines
Trident submarines, Agni missiles and Mirage 2000 aircraft
Prithvi missiles, Jaguar aircraft and Arihant-class SSBNs
50.x: The US triad consists of Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missiles, strategic bombers and Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs.
50.tq: Match a country-specific triad with all three of its stated components.

50.s: India is described as having a fully operational nuclear triad along with which of the following countries?
o: France, the United Kingdom and Pakistan
The United States, Russia and China
50.x: India is described as having a fully operational triad alongside the United States, Russia and China.
50.tq: Use the membership comparison rather than selecting other nuclear-capable states.

51.s: Which organisation designed the Tejas Light Combat Aircraft, and which organisation built it?
o: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited; Aeronautical Development Agency
Aeronautical Development Agency; Hindustan Aeronautics Limited
51.x: The Tejas LCA was designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency and built by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited.
51.tq: Test the developer–builder distinction rather than identifying only the aircraft.

51.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. LCH Prachand — High-altitude light combat helicopter
2. HTT-40 — Basic turboprop trainer
3. Do-228 — Light transport and maritime patrol aircraft
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
51.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Prachand is a high-altitude light combat helicopter, HTT-40 is a basic turboprop trainer, and Do-228 serves light transport and maritime patrol roles.
51.tq: Split the options by checking each aircraft’s role.

51.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: C-17 Globemaster III — Boeing, United States
C-130J Super Hercules — Lockheed Martin, United States
51.x: The IL-76 was developed by Ilyushin of Russia. Dassault of France developed the Rafale.
51.tq: Find the swapped developer–aircraft pair.

51.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Aircraft)
A. C-130J Super Hercules
B. C-17 Globemaster III
C. IL-76
D. IL-78

List-II (Role)
1. Mid-air refuelling tanker
2. Tactical transport and special operations
3. Strategic heavy-lift transport
4. Heavy transport

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
51.x: The C-130J is used for tactical transport and special operations; the C-17 for strategic heavy lift; the IL-76 for heavy transport; and the IL-78 as a mid-air refuelling tanker.
51.tq: Start from the sure pair, especially the distinctive tanker role of IL-78.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about the C-295 aircraft:
1. It is built by Airbus (Spain) with Tata.
2. It is a strategic heavy-lift transport aircraft.
3. The first 'Made in India' C-295 rolls out in 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is correct: the C-295 is an Airbus (Spain) aircraft built with Tata. Statement 2 is wrong: the C-295 is a medium tactical transport; the C-17 Globemaster III is the strategic heavy-lift transport. Statement 3 is correct: the first Made-in-India C-295 rolls out in 2026. So '1 and 2 only', '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' all wrongly accept statement 2.
51.tq: C-295 = medium tactical (Airbus + Tata); C-17 = strategic heavy lift.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about HAL's 2025 contract for LCA Mk1A aircraft:
1. It covers 97 aircraft: 68 fighters and 29 twin-seaters.
2. Deliveries run from 2027-28 and the aircraft carry the UTTAM AESA radar.
3. It is the first order placed for the Mk1A variant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is correct: 97 aircraft (68 fighters + 29 twin-seaters), Rs 62,370 crore, signed 25 Sep 2025. Statement 2 is correct: deliveries from 2027-28 over six years, over 64% indigenous content, UTTAM AESA radar. Statement 3 is wrong: it came after an earlier order of 83 Mk1A. Hence '1 only' misses 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 3.
51.tq: 97 = 68 + 29; it followed the earlier 83 Mk1A order.

51.s: Which feature is specifically associated with Tejas?
o: It was India's first automated air-defence network
It was India's first licence-built Russian tank
It was India's first 300 km universal rocket launcher
It was India's first indigenous fly-by-wire aircraft
51.x: Tejas is identified as India's first indigenous fly-by-wire aircraft.
51.tq: Test the distinctive technological feature rather than the broad platform category.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tejas variants:
1. Mk-1A has the Uttam AESA radar, an EW suite and air-to-air refuelling.
2. Mk-2, with a GE F414 engine and canards, is under development.
3. Mk-2 came first and was followed by Mk-1 and Mk-1A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as stated. Statement 3 is wrong: the sequence is Mk-1, then Mk-1A, then Mk-2 (still under development). So '1 only' misses 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly accept 3.
51.tq: Mk-1 -> Mk-1A (Uttam AESA) -> Mk-2 (GE F414, canards).

51.s: How many Rafale fighter jets does the Indian Air Force operate, as asked in a 2025 examination?
51.x: The IAF operates 36 Rafale jets from Dassault, France. 83 was the earlier Tejas Mk1A order and 97 the 2025 Mk1A contract; 26 is a distractor (the number of Rafale-M jets ordered for the Navy, not the IAF figure).
51.tq: IAF Rafale = 36.

51.s: Lakshya, developed by DRDO’s Aeronautical Development Establishment, is a:
o: Light combat helicopter for high-altitude operations
Pilotless target drone used for weapon tests
51.x: Lakshya is a pilotless target drone developed by DRDO-ADE for weapon testing.
51.tq: Identify the platform from its developer and operational purpose.

51.s: Rustom-II, also known as TAPAS-BH-201, belongs to which UAV class?
51.x: Rustom-II or TAPAS-BH-201 is a Medium Altitude Long Endurance UAV.
51.tq: Expand the acronym and match it with the correct UAV class.

51.s: Nishant is primarily a:
o: Pilotless target aircraft for weapon training
51.x: Nishant is a tactical UAV intended for battlefield reconnaissance.
51.tq: Distinguish reconnaissance, target-training and armed UAV roles.

51.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Ghatak—stealth UCAV with a flying-wing configuration
Ghatak—pilotless target aircraft for weapon training
51.x: Ghatak is a stealth UCAV with a flying-wing configuration; its demonstrator is a high-speed flying-wing UAV.
51.tq: Use configuration and role together to distinguish the UCAV from other UAV classes.

51.s: Archer-NG is classified as an:
51.x: Archer-NG is an armed Medium Altitude Long Endurance UAV.
51.tq: Separate the armed MALE category from reconnaissance and target UAV categories.

51.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Arjun Mk-1A—Russia, licence-built at HVF Avadi
51.x: Arjun Mk-1A was developed by DRDO through CVRDE, Chennai.
51.tq: Identify the developer-origin pair rather than the production location of another tank.

51.s: The T-90 Bhishma is best described as a tank of which origin and production arrangement?
o: Russian origin and licence-built at HVF Avadi
Indigenous design by DRDO and built only at Chennai
French origin and assembled by HAL
Israeli origin and produced by NIBE
51.x: The T-90 Bhishma is of Russian origin and is licence-built at the Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi.
51.tq: Separate origin from Indian licence production.

51.s: The Zorawar is a light tank developed by:
o: Ordnance Factory Board with Russia for plains
HAL with Bharat Forge for desert warfare
DRDO with Larsen & Toubro for high-altitude areas
DRDO with Israel for naval operations
51.x: The Zorawar light tank is being developed by DRDO with L&T for high-altitude areas.
51.tq: Use the developer-purpose-location relationship as the discriminator.

51.s: ATAGS is associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: A multi-barrel rocket launcher developed only by HAL
An automated air-defence network developed by the Navy
A 155 mm towed gun developed by DRDO's ARDE with Indian industry
A universal rocket launcher developed by Russia
51.x: ATAGS is a 155 mm towed gun developed by DRDO's ARDE with Indian industry.
51.tq: Distinguish artillery-gun systems from rocket launchers and command networks.

51.s: Dhanush is correctly described as:
o: A 155 mm gun based on the Bofors design, associated with the Ordnance Factory Board at Jabalpur
A 155 mm gun based on the Bofors design, developed by HAL at Bengaluru
A Russian tank licence-built at Avadi
A 300 km universal rocket launcher made by NIBE
51.x: Dhanush is a 155 mm gun based on the Bofors design and was associated with the Ordnance Factory Board at Jabalpur.
51.tq: Check both the weapon description and the developer-origin pair.

51.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Suryastra—NIBE with Israel; universal rocket launcher; 300 km
Suryastra—DRDO with Russia; 155 mm towed gun; 120 km
Suryastra—HAL with France; light combat helicopter; 300 km
Suryastra—BEL with the Army; air-defence network; 120 km
51.x: Suryastra is a universal rocket launcher developed by NIBE with Israel, with a stated range of 300 km.
51.tq: Use the three-part match: developer, weapon type and range.

51.s: The maximum range of the Pinaka LRGR-120 is:
51.x: The LRGR-120 has a maximum range of 120 km.
51.tq: Distinguish the rocket's range from the 300 km range of another launcher.

51.s: What is PINAKA?
o: An Indian multi-barrel rocket launcher developed by DRDO
A Russian-origin main battle tank licence-built at Avadi
A light combat helicopter built by HAL
51.x: Pinaka is a multi-barrel rocket launcher (MBRL) developed by DRDO (ARDE Pune with HEMRL), as keyed in APPSC 2018. The T-90 Bhishma is the licence-built Russian tank, Astra is the BVR air-to-air missile, and Prachand is HAL's light combat helicopter.
51.tq: Pinaka = MBRL (APPSC 2018).

51.s: INS Vikrant is correctly described as:
o: India’s first indigenous aircraft carrier, IAC-1, built by Cochin Shipyard
A Project 15B destroyer built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders
India’s first nuclear ballistic-missile submarine, built by Mazagon Dock
A Project 75 submarine built by Hindustan Shipyard
51.x: INS Vikrant is India’s first indigenous aircraft carrier, designated IAC-1, and was built by Cochin Shipyard.
51.tq: Match the platform with its project identity and builder.

51.s: Which one of the following is the correct composition of Project 15B destroyers?
51.x: Project 15B comprises the Visakhapatnam-class destroyers Visakhapatnam, Mormugao, Imphal and Surat.
51.tq: Use the class roster to distinguish destroyers from frigates and submarines.

51.s:
Which of the following statements about the Nilgiri class is/are correct?
1. It is associated with Project 17A.
2. Seven multi-mission stealth frigates are included in the class.
3. The ships use CODOG propulsion and can exceed 28 knots.
4. BrahMos and MRSAM/Barak-8 are among the specified weapon systems.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
51.x: All four statements are correct. Project 17A consists of seven multi-mission stealth frigates with CODOG propulsion, speeds above 28 knots, and systems including BrahMos and MRSAM/Barak-8.
51.tq: Break a dense platform description into project, number, propulsion, speed and weapon features.

51.s: The Nilgiri-class frigates are being built by:
51.x: The Nilgiri-class Project 17A frigates are being built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders and Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers.
51.tq: Test the joint-builder relationship.

51.s: INS Tamal was commissioned on 1 July 2025 at which shipyard?
51.x: INS Tamal was commissioned on 1 July 2025 at Yantar Shipyard in Kaliningrad, Russia.
51.tq: Pair the precise commissioning date with the unusual foreign shipyard location.

51.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Tavasya — Stealth frigate launched at Goa Shipyard in March 2025
2. Dunagiri — Fifth Nilgiri-class ship delivered by GRSE in March 2026
3. Taragiri — Fourth Nilgiri-class ship commissioned at Visakhapatnam in April 2026
4. Mahendragiri — Seventh P17A warship and sixth to be commissioned
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
51.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Tavasya was launched in March 2025, while Dunagiri, Taragiri and Mahendragiri reached the stated milestones in 2026.
51.tq: Check the vessel, project position, location and date in each pair.

51.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of the other naval inductions listed for 2026?
o: Varunastra, TAL, Maareech, USHUS, SMART and ERASR
Agray, Malwan, Anjadip, Sanshodhak, Sanghmitra and Shachi
Cheetah, Guldar, Kumbhir, Tamal, Surat and Imphal
Nilgiri, Udaygiri, Himgiri, Vaghsheer, Taragiri and Dunagiri
51.x: The 2026 inductions included ASW shallow-water craft Agray, Malwan and Anjadip, survey vessel Sanshodhak, and NGOPVs Sanghmitra and Shachi.
51.tq: Select the group whose members share the same induction-year classification.

51.s: The three vessels INS Cheetah, INS Guldar and INS Kumbhir were decommissioned on 12 January 2024 at:
51.x: INS Cheetah, Guldar and Kumbhir were decommissioned on 12 January 2024 at Port Blair.
51.tq: Combine the exact date, vessel trio and location while avoiding the similar but incorrect vessel name Magar.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian naval ship projects:
1. Project 17A consists of seven Nilgiri-class stealth frigates.
2. Project 15B includes INS Imphal.
3. INS Surat is the fourth and last ship of Project 15B.
4. Project 17A consists of seven stealth destroyers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Project 17A consists of Nilgiri-class stealth frigates, whereas Project 15B consists of stealth destroyers; therefore statement 4 is false.
51.tq: Catch the reversed comparison between frigates and destroyers.

51.s: Tavasya is associated with which of the following?
o: An indigenously built stealth frigate launched by the Navy, belonging to the P-1135.6 follow-on project at Goa Shipyard
A Nilgiri-class frigate constructed at GRSE under Project 17A
A Scorpene submarine built at MDL under Project-75
A Kamorta-class corvette built at Cochin Shipyard
51.x: Tavasya is an indigenously built stealth frigate launched by the Navy, associated with the P-1135.6 follow-on project at Goa Shipyard.
51.tq: Identify the platform from its project, yard and class description.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kalvari class:
1. It is associated with Project 75.
2. The submarines are diesel-electric Scorpene-class submarines based on a French design.
3. Six boats are planned or built under the programme.
4. INS Vaghsheer is the last boat of the class.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All four statements are correct. The Kalvari class belongs to Project 75, comprises six French-design Scorpene diesel-electric submarines, and INS Vaghsheer is the last boat.
51.tq: Verify the project, propulsion, number and terminal vessel separately.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Varunastra?
o: An indigenous heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo designed by NSTL, Visakhapatnam
A submarine sonar integrated by DRDO-NMRL
A lightweight helicopter-launched torpedo designed by ARDE, Pune
An anti-torpedo decoy system developed by GRSE, Kolkata
51.x: Varunastra is an indigenous heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo designed by NSTL at Visakhapatnam.
51.tq: Distinguish the heavyweight torpedo from decoys, sonar and lightweight torpedoes.

51.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Naval system)
A. TAL
B. Maareech
C. USHUS
D. ERASR

List-II (Description)
1. Integrated submarine sonar
2. Anti-submarine rocket
3. Lightweight torpedo
4. Anti-torpedo decoy system

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
51.x: TAL is a lightweight torpedo, Maareech is an anti-torpedo decoy, USHUS is an integrated submarine sonar, and ERASR is an anti-submarine rocket.
51.tq: Start with the distinctive sonar and decoy pairs before completing the code.

51.s:
Assertion (A): An Air Independent Propulsion system allows a diesel-electric submarine to remain submerged for extended periods without snorkelling.
Reason (R): The DRDO-NMRL system uses fuel-cell technology to provide underwater endurance.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
51.x: Both statements are true, and the fuel-cell-based DRDO-NMRL system explains how AIP extends submerged operation without snorkelling.
51.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the operational advantage stated in the assertion.

51.s: Which statement regarding the Indian AIP system is correct?
o: It is a nuclear propulsion system developed by NSTL for SSBNs.
It was developed by DRDO-NMRL and has been cleared for retrofit in diesel-electric submarines.
It is based on a Russian partnership and is used only in aircraft carriers.
It enables submarines to remain submerged only while snorkelling continuously.
51.x: The AIP system was developed by DRDO-NMRL using fuel-cell technology and has been cleared for retrofit in diesel-electric submarines.
51.tq: Use the authority and propulsion-type traps to eliminate swapped descriptions.

51.s: INS Arihant is India’s first:
o: Indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel
51.x: INS Arihant is India’s first SSBN, or nuclear ballistic-missile submarine, commissioned in 2016.
51.tq: Distinguish the strategic submarine category from other naval platforms.

51.s: INS Astradharini is best described as a:
o: Torpedo launch and recovery vessel used to trial DRDO underwater weapons
Project 17A stealth frigate armed with BrahMos
Survey vessel operated by Garden Reach Shipbuilders
Nuclear ballistic-missile submarine used for deterrence patrols
51.x: INS Astradharini is an indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel used for trials of DRDO underwater weapons; it was commissioned in 2024 at Visakhapatnam.
51.tq: Identify the vessel by its specialised test and recovery function.

51.s: Khanderi and Vagir are respectively the:
o: Second and fifth Project-75 Kalvari-class submarines
51.x: Khanderi is the second and Vagir the fifth Project-75 Kalvari-class submarine.
51.tq: Test ordinal positions within the same project rather than the ship names alone.

51.s: Project-75(I) is associated with which of the following arrangements?
o: AIP-equipped conventional submarines and a Navantia–L&T teaming agreement
Stealth frigates and a Russia–L&T agreement
Nuclear submarines and a France–GRSE agreement
Aircraft carriers and a Spain–MDL agreement
51.x: Project-75(I) concerns next-generation conventional submarines with air-independent propulsion, with Navantia of Spain and L&T signing a teaming agreement in July 2023.
51.tq: Separate the project’s propulsion feature, partners and platform type.

51.s: Which shipyard was founded in 1941 by Scindia Steam Navigation and built the first Indian-built ship, Jala Usha, in 1948?
o: Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers, Kolkata
51.x: Hindustan Shipyard Limited at Visakhapatnam was founded in 1941 by Scindia Steam Navigation and built Jala Usha, the first Indian-built ship, in 1948.
51.tq: Link the founding year, founder, first ship and location to the correct yard.

51.s: Hindustan Shipyard Limited is presently a:
o: Private shipyard jointly owned by Airbus and Tata
Ministry of Defence public sector undertaking
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways undertaking
51.x: Hindustan Shipyard Limited is now a Ministry of Defence public sector undertaking.
51.tq: Apply the ownership-authority trap to distinguish central ministries.

51.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders — Mumbai — builds destroyers, P17A frigates and Scorpene submarines
GRSE — Kochi — builds only aircraft carriers
Goa Shipyard — Kolkata — builds Scorpene submarines
Cochin Shipyard — Visakhapatnam — builds Adamya-class fast patrol vessels
51.x: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is located in Mumbai and builds destroyers, Project 17A frigates and Scorpene submarines.
51.tq: Check the yard’s location, ownership role and characteristic construction portfolio together.

51.s: Which Indian shipyard was the first Indian yard to export a warship, sending one to Mauritius in 2014?
51.x: GRSE was the first Indian shipyard to export a warship; the export to Mauritius took place in 2014.
51.tq: Identify the ‘FIRST’ achievement and its export destination.

51.s: Cochin Shipyard is under which ministry and is associated with which distinction?
o: Ministry of Home Affairs; builder of Scorpene submarines
Ministry of Heavy Industries; first exporter of a warship
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways; builder of INS Vikrant and India’s largest shipyard
Ministry of Defence; India’s oldest shipyard
51.x: Cochin Shipyard is under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. It built INS Vikrant and is India’s largest shipyard.
51.tq: Separate ministry ownership from the shipyard’s major construction achievement.

51.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Goa Shipyard?
o: Vasco da Gama, Goa; defence PSU that builds Adamya-class fast patrol vessels for the Coast Guard
Mumbai; builds only commercial cargo ships
51.x: Goa Shipyard is located at Vasco da Gama in Goa, is a defence PSU, and builds Adamya-class fast patrol vessels for the Coast Guard.
51.tq: Use the location–ownership–product combination to identify the shipyard.

51.s: The Indian Coast Guard was set up in:
51.x: The Indian Coast Guard was established in 1977.
51.tq: Recall the establishment year while avoiding nearby institutional dates.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels:
1. Eight vessels are being built by Goa Shipyard.
2. Three were commissioned in 2025.
3. ICGS Achal was commissioned in 2026.
4. Their roles include coastal surveillance, anti-smuggling and search and rescue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All four statements are correct. The Adamya-class vessels are being built by Goa Shipyard and perform surveillance, anti-smuggling and SAR roles.
51.tq: Verify the class through builder, commissioning timeline and operational roles.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about the Coast Guard's Hovercraft H-561:
1. It is an Adamya-class fast patrol vessel built by Goa Shipyard.
2. It is the first indigenous air cushion vehicle.
3. It can work over mudflats and sandbars such as the Rann of Kutch and the Sundarbans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Adamya-class FPVs (eight by Goa Shipyard) are a separate class; H-561 is a hovercraft. Statement 2 is correct: H-561 (2026) is the first indigenous air cushion vehicle. Statement 3 is correct: it works over mudflats and sandbars. So only '2 and 3 only' fits; the other codes include statement 1 or leave out 2.
51.tq: H-561 = first indigenous hovercraft; Adamya = FPV class.

51.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated role of the Indian Coast Guard?
o: Operating intercontinental ballistic missile launch facilities
51.x: The Coast Guard performs coastal security, anti-poaching, anti-smuggling and search-and-rescue roles. Operating intercontinental ballistic missile launch facilities is not a stated Coast Guard role.
51.tq: Find the unrelated defence function among the Coast Guard’s maritime roles.

51.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The IFC-IOR was set up by the Navy at Gurugram in 2018.
2. The IFC-IOR is the ICG's chain of 84 coastal radar stations.
3. The IFC-IOR shares white-shipping and maritime-security data with partner countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is correct: Navy, Gurugram, 2018. Statement 2 is wrong: the 84 radar stations are the ICG's coastal radar chain set up after 26/11, a separate network. Statement 3 is correct: IFC-IOR shares white-shipping and maritime-security data. So '1 and 3 only'; the other codes include 2 or miss 1 or 3.
51.tq: IFC-IOR = Navy, Gurugram 2018, data sharing; 84 radars = ICG chain.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's coastal surveillance network:
1. It consists of 84 radar stations of the Indian Coast Guard.
2. It was set up after the 26/11 attacks.
3. It forms part of the coastal surveillance network.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: The Indian Coast Guard's 84 radar stations form a coastal surveillance network established after 26/11.
51.tq: Combine the number, institutional agency and cause without importing unrelated radar facts.

51.s: The headquarters of the Eastern Naval Command is located at:
51.x: The Eastern Naval Command has its headquarters at Visakhapatnam.
51.tq: Test the headquarters-location pair directly.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Naval Command:
1. INS Dega is a naval air station.
2. The Eastern Fleet received INS Mahendragiri at Mumbai.
3. A new submarine base is being built at Rambilli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is correct: INS Dega is a naval air station. Statement 2 is wrong: Mahendragiri joined the Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam, the HQ of the Eastern Naval Command. Statement 3 is correct: a new submarine base is being built at Rambilli. So '1 and 3 only'.
51.tq: Eastern Naval Command = Visakhapatnam; Dega (air), Rambilli (submarines).

51.s: The SAGAR and MAHASAGAR visions are associated with guiding India's:
51.x: The SAGAR and MAHASAGAR visions guide India's maritime and naval capabilities.
51.tq: Apply the vision to the domain with which it is institutionally associated.

51.s: Which type of radar measures the speed of an object from the frequency shift of the reflected signal and is used in weather radars?
51.x: Doppler radar measures speed through the frequency shift of the returned signal and is used in weather radars.
51.tq: Identify the radar from its distinctive operating principle and application.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR):
1. It is used for imaging at night.
2. It can produce images through clouds.
3. It depends exclusively on visible light.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: SAR enables imaging at night and through clouds. It does not depend exclusively on visible light.
51.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ and identify the two valid capabilities.

51.s: With reference to AESA radar, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It requires a mechanically rotating antenna for beam steering.
It has a transmit/receive module on every antenna element and electronically steers the beam.
It uses HF waves reflected from the ionosphere.
It is used only for measuring rainfall.
51.x: Active Electronically Scanned Array radar has a transmit/receive module on each element and steers its beam electronically without a moving antenna.
51.tq: Use the defining hardware feature to distinguish AESA from mechanically scanned radar.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the operating principle of an over-the-horizon radar?
o: It uses HF waves bounced off the ionosphere to observe targets beyond the horizon.
It uses Doppler shift exclusively to map clouds.
It uses only underwater acoustic signals.
It uses visible laser beams to detect targets beyond mountains.
51.x: Over-the-horizon radar uses high-frequency waves reflected by the ionosphere, enabling observation beyond the geometric horizon.
51.tq: Match the radar name with the unusual propagation path stated in the options.

51.s:
Match List-I (Indigenous radar) with List-II (Role):
List-I
A. Swordfish
B. Swathi
C. Rajendra
D. Surya
List-II
1. Fire-control radar of the Akash SAM system
2. VHF radar for tracking stealth aircraft
3. Long-range tracking radar of the BMD shield
4. Weapon-locating radar for enemy guns, mortars and rockets
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
51.x: Swordfish is the long-range tracking radar of the BMD shield (1,500+ km); Swathi (BEL, exported to Armenia) is the weapon-locating radar; Rajendra is the phased-array fire-control radar of Akash (80 km); Surya is the VHF radar for tracking stealth aircraft. So A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2. The second code swaps Swathi and Rajendra, the third swaps Swordfish and Surya, the fourth is wrong for all.
51.tq: Swathi = weapon locating; Rajendra = Akash; Surya = stealth (VHF).

51.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Ashwini — Low-level lightweight 3D radar detecting cruise missiles and drones
Swathi — Fire-control radar of the Akash system
Rajendra — Weapon-locating radar exported to Armenia
Swordfish — Low-level surveillance radar of the IAF
51.x: Ashwini is a low-level lightweight 3D radar capable of detecting cruise missiles and drones. Swathi is weapon-locating, Rajendra is associated with Akash, and Swordfish performs long-range tracking.
51.tq: Find the correctly matched role by separating surveillance, fire-control and weapon-location functions.

51.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Arudhra — Medium-Power 4D surveillance radar for the IAF
Ashwini — Low-Level Transportable Radar for the IAF
Surya — Weapon-locating radar for enemy guns and mortars
51.x: Surya is a VHF-band surveillance radar for tracking stealth aircraft. Swathi, not Surya, is the weapon-locating radar for enemy guns, mortars and rockets.
51.tq: Find the swapped role among closely related indigenous radar systems.

51.s:
Which of the following statements about Netra AEW&C is correct?
1. It was built by DRDO-CABS in Bengaluru.
2. It carries an AESA radar on an Embraer EMB-145 aircraft.
3. It can track aircraft, drones, cruise missiles and ships.
4. It provides IFF and can guide friendly fighters.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
51.x: All four statements correctly describe Netra AEW&C, including its developer, platform, tracking functions, IFF and fighter-guidance role.
51.tq: Check each statement against the system’s developer, platform and operational functions.

51.s: Which statement best distinguishes AWACS from Netra AEW&C?
o: AWACS is a smaller jet with shorter range, whereas Netra is a larger platform for complete air-battle control.
Netra is used only for weather observation, whereas AWACS is used only for naval patrol.
AWACS is a larger platform for long-range surveillance and full control of the air battle, whereas Netra is a smaller jet providing early warning and command-and-control.
Both systems are identical in platform size, range and function.
51.x: AWACS is the larger, longer-range platform with full air-battle control, while Netra is a smaller jet offering early warning and command-and-control over a shorter range.
51.tq: Compare the two systems across platform size, range and degree of control.

51.s: Netra AEW&C has a stated detection range of approximately:
51.x: Netra AEW&C has a detection range of approximately 250–500 km or more, with 300–360° coverage.
51.tq: Select the range band associated with the airborne early-warning platform.

51.s: The Final Operational Clearance for Netra AEW&C was handed over to the Indian Air Force in:
51.x: Netra AEW&C (DRDO-CABS, AESA radar on Embraer EMB-145) received Final Operational Clearance, handed to the IAF on 27 June 2026.
51.tq: Distinguish the closely placed year and month-based current-affairs dates.

51.s: The Indrajaal system is best described as:
o: An AI-powered anti-drone grid developed by a Hyderabad start-up
A DRDO ballistic missile tracking radar
51.x: Indrajaal is an AI-powered anti-drone grid developed by a Hyderabad start-up. It can cover up to 4,000 sq km and has been deployed at naval sites in Gujarat and Karnataka.
51.tq: Identify the system from its developer type and anti-drone function.

51.s: D4, developed by DRDO, combines which of the following capabilities?
o: Only infrared imaging and underwater sonar
51.x: D4 means Drone Detect, Deter and Destroy. It uses 360° radar, soft-kill jamming and hard-kill laser; it detects drones at 4 km and neutralises them within 1 km.
51.tq: Expand the acronym and connect each component with its soft-kill or hard-kill function.

51.s: Which indigenous system fires 64 micro-rockets against drone swarms?
51.x: Bhargavastra is an indigenous counter-drone system that fires 64 micro-rockets at drone swarms.
51.tq: Use the distinctive numerical payload to identify the system.

51.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Akash Tarang is an indigenous anti-drone electronic-warfare system.
2. It jams drone-control signals as a soft-kill measure.
3. Its procurement was approved by the DAC in July 2026.
4. It forms part of the Sudarshan Chakra layered air shield.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All four statements are correct. Akash Tarang is an indigenous anti-UAV EW system using soft-kill jamming, approved for procurement in July 2026 and included in the Sudarshan Chakra layered air shield.
51.tq: Combine system identity, method, approval date and wider defence architecture.

51.s: Vayu Astra is associated with which of the following?
o: An indigenous loitering munition developed by NIBE Ltd
A VHF radar for stealth aircraft
51.x: Vayu Astra is an indigenous loitering munition developed by NIBE Ltd.
51.tq: Distinguish a munition from similarly named radar and anti-drone systems.

51.s: Which statement correctly describes a kamikaze or suicide drone?
o: It is a manned aircraft used for air-sea rescue.
It continuously returns to its base after releasing a non-explosive sensor.
It loiters over an area and crashes into the target carrying a warhead.
It can operate only underwater and has no warhead.
51.x: A kamikaze drone loiters over an area and then crashes into its target with a warhead. The DAC approved jet-based kamikaze drones in July 2026.
51.tq: Apply the operational definition to a short battlefield scenario.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about electronic warfare (EW):
1. EW is the use of electromagnetic energy to control the spectrum, deny it to the enemy and protect own sensors.
2. Samyukta is the Army's mobile integrated ground-based EW system.
3. Himshakti, an integrated EW system for mountainous terrain, was developed by BEL.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as stated in the notes. Statement 3 is wrong: Himshakti was developed by DLRL Hyderabad, not BEL. So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly accept statement 3.
51.tq: Himshakti = mountains, DLRL Hyderabad.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about radar cross-section (RCS):
1. RCS indicates how big a target looks to radar.
2. Shaping, radar-absorbent coatings and flush-mounted weapons reduce RCS.
3. Larger exposed metal surfaces and external weapon mounts reduce RCS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is correct: RCS is how 'big' a target looks to radar. Statement 2 is correct: shaping, radar-absorbent coatings and flush-mounted weapons (as on P17A frigates) cut RCS. Statement 3 is wrong: exposed surfaces and external mounts increase reflections. So '1 and 2 only'.
51.tq: Stealth = shaping + RAM + flush weapons.

51.s: The load-bearing stealth structures referred to in connection with stealth technology are made by:
51.x: ASL makes load-bearing stealth structures.
51.tq: Match the specialised laboratory with its defence-material capability.

51.s: HMX is also known as:
51.x: HMX is known as octogen and is a high-melting, powerful military explosive.
51.tq: Test the exact alternate name of the explosive.

51.s: Which of the following correctly describes LLM-105?
o: An insensitive high explosive designed to be safer against accidental detonation
A pilotless target aircraft for weapon training
51.x: LLM-105 is an insensitive high explosive with greater safety against accidental detonation.
51.tq: Distinguish the material's safety property from unrelated defence products.

51.s: Which one of the following laboratories is associated with CL-20, described as the most powerful non-nuclear explosive?
51.x: CL-20 is associated with the High Energy Materials Research Laboratory (HEMRL), Pune, and is described as the most powerful non-nuclear explosive.
51.tq: Use the laboratory–material association directly.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding high-energy materials and armour technologies:
1. Ultra-fine beta-HMX and fine RDX are associated with TBRL.
2. Kanchan armour is a composite armour developed for the Arjun tank.
3. Carbon-carbon and C-SiC composites are used in re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All three statements are correct. TBRL is associated with ultra-fine beta-HMX and fine RDX, Kanchan is composite armour for the Arjun tank, and carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites serve high-temperature aerospace applications.
51.tq: Check each material against its stated use and laboratory association.

51.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Material or technology)
a. Kanchan armour
b. Carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites
c. Super-alloys and tungsten heavy alloys
d. Maraging steel

List-II (Application)
i. Rocket motor casings and submarine hulls
ii. Engines and penetrator rods
iii. Composite armour for Arjun tank
iv. Re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles

Code:
51.x: Kanchan armour is used on the Arjun tank; carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites are used for re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles; super-alloys and tungsten heavy alloys serve engines and penetrator rods; maraging steel is used in rocket motor casings and submarine hulls.
51.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with a wrong material–use match.

51.s: Kanchan armour, the composite armour used on the Arjun tank, was developed by which DRDO laboratory?
51.x: Kanchan composite armour for the Arjun tank was developed by the Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL), Hyderabad, named after Kanchanbagh where DMRL is located. HEMRL Pune synthesised CL-20, TBRL works on HMX/RDX, and CVRDE Chennai designed the Arjun tank itself, not its armour.
51.tq: Kanchan = DMRL Hyderabad (Kanchanbagh).

51.s: Lukoskin is used as a:
o: Polyherbal ointment for leucoderma or vitiligo
51.x: Lukoskin is a polyherbal ointment used for leucoderma, also called vitiligo.
51.tq: Match the product with its specific medical use.

51.s: Bio-toilets based on bio-digesters are used for:
o: Waste treatment in high-altitude areas and have been adopted by the Railways
Detecting chemical agents in NBC warfare
51.x: Bio-toilets treat waste in high-altitude environments and have been adopted by the Railways.
51.tq: Connect the product with both its use and adoption context.

51.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with DIPAS?
51.x: DIPAS is associated with high-altitude physiology products such as the Bukhari space heater, oxygenated solar shelter and Cognobar. A chemical agent monitor is associated with DRDE.
51.tq: Find the one product belonging to the neighbouring NBC-defence laboratory.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about DRDO life-science labs:
1. DIHAR, Leh is known for the Bukhari space heater and Cognobar.
2. DRDE Gwalior works on NBC defence, e.g. the NBC haversack and chemical agent monitor.
3. INMAS works on nuclear medicine and developed the bike ambulance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
51.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Bukhari space heater and Cognobar are DIPAS (high-altitude physiology); DIHAR, Leh works on high-altitude agriculture and herbal products. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So '2 and 3 only'.
51.tq: DIPAS = physiology gear; DIHAR = high-altitude farming and herbals.

51.s: Mahendragiri was commissioned into which fleet in July 2026?
51.x: Mahendragiri, the 7th Project 17A (Nilgiri-class) frigate and the 6th to be commissioned, joined the Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam on 18 July 2026.
51.tq: Test the commissioning event through the fleet-location association.

51.s: In March 2026, which organisation delivered three ships at once?
51.x: Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) delivered three ships at once in March 2026.
51.tq: Identify the organisation connected with the specific recent defence milestone.

51.s:
Which of the following were identified as AI platforms unveiled by DRDO in the stated current-affairs context?
1. Kautilya
2. Q-FORCE
3. Varunastra
4. RudraM-II
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
51.x: Kautilya and Q-FORCE were identified as AI platforms. Varunastra is associated with NSTL, while RudraM-II is a separate DRDO defence system.
51.tq: Separate systems by their stated category instead of grouping all DRDO names together.

51.s: Which one of the following places is correctly matched with the defence-related establishment or activity associated with it?
o: Mahendragiri — Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers headquarters
Visakhapatnam — Eastern Naval Command, HSL and NSTL
Sri Sathya Sai district — Eastern Naval Command headquarters
Kurnool — Hindustan Shipyard Limited and INS Dega
51.x: Visakhapatnam is associated with the Eastern Naval Command, Hindustan Shipyard Limited and NSTL, which is linked with Varunastra. The other combinations incorrectly shift these establishments to different locations.
51.tq: Match the location with the correct cluster of nearby defence establishments.

51.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the specified naval platform milestones?
o: H-561 is the last indigenous hovercraft.
INS Tamal was built indigenously at Visakhapatnam.
Vaghsheer is the last P75 boat.
Surat is the first P15B destroyer.
51.x: Vaghsheer is identified as the last P75 boat. INS Tamal was built abroad in Russia, Surat is the last P15B destroyer, and H-561 is the first indigenous hovercraft.
51.tq: Use first-versus-last and indigenous-versus-foreign distinctions carefully.

51.s: What was the significance of the June 2026 milestone concerning Netra?
o: Netra was transferred to the Defence Materials and Stores Research Laboratory.
Netra achieved its first test flight by the Navy.
Netra received full operational clearance for the Indian Air Force.
Netra was inducted into the Eastern Naval Command as a frigate.
51.x: In June 2026 (27 Jun) Netra AEW&C's Final Operational Clearance (FOC) was handed to the Indian Air Force; option C's 'full operational clearance' refers to this FOC. Netra is a DRDO-CABS airborne early-warning system for the IAF, not a Navy test or a frigate.
51.tq: Identify the exact service and stage of induction rather than the platform’s general function.

51.s: A DRDO test range mentioned in connection with recent Andhra Pradesh defence infrastructure is located near
51.x: The notes place a DRDO test range near Kurnool (21 May 2026) as part of AP's defence ecosystem; Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command, NSTL and HSL, and Sri Sathya Sai district has BEL Palasamudram and the ADA complex.
51.tq: Use the Andhra Pradesh location association to identify the test facility.

51.s: Which one of the following is correct about DRDO?
o: It was formed in 1958 and its motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam'.
It was formed in 1969 and its motto is 'Sha No Varunah'.
It was formed in 1947 and its motto is 'Nabhah Sprisham Deeptam'.
It was formed in 1980 and its motto is 'Satyameva Jayate'.
51.x: DRDO was formed in 1958 and its motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' (the source of strength is science). The other options pair wrong years with mottoes of other bodies or the national motto (Nabhah Sprisham Deeptam is the IAF motto; Sha No Varunah the Navy's).
51.tq: DRDO: 1958, Balasya Mulam Vigyanam.

52.s: In which month and year was the defence sector opened to Indian private participation with foreign direct investment up to 26 per cent under licensing?
52.x: The defence sector was opened to 100 per cent Indian private participation in May 2001, with FDI up to 26 per cent under the licensing route.
52.tq: Direct recall of a date and policy change.

52.s: With reference to foreign direct investment in the defence sector, which one of the following is correct?
o: 100 per cent FDI is permitted through the automatic route for all defence activities.
74 per cent FDI is permitted only through the government route and investment above it is not allowed.
26 per cent is permitted through the automatic route and any higher investment is prohibited.
74 per cent is permitted through the automatic route, while investment above 74 per cent up to 100 per cent requires the government route in cases involving access to modern technology.
52.x: The current provision allows 74 per cent FDI through the automatic route. Investment above 74 per cent and up to 100 per cent requires the government route where modern technology access is involved.
52.tq: Discriminate between automatic and government routes and their limits.

52.s: The cumulative FDI received in the defence sector from May 2001 to June 2025 was approximately:
52.x: Cumulative defence-sector FDI from May 2001 to June 2025 amounted to ₹5,730.55 crore.
52.tq: Direct recall of a cumulative figure.

52.s: Since 2013–14, how many defence licences have been issued to private firms?
52.x: Since 2013–14, 576 defence licences have been issued to private firms.
52.tq: Number-based elimination using closely spaced figures.

52.s: In 2021, the Ordnance Factory Board was reorganised by dissolving it and regrouping its factories into:
52.x: The 200-year-old OFB was dissolved in 2021, and its 41 factories were regrouped into seven DPSUs.
52.tq: Test the linked count of factories and successor DPSUs.

52.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the seven DPSUs formed after the dissolution of the Ordnance Factory Board?
52.x: The seven DPSUs included Munitions India, AVNL, AWEIL, Troop Comforts, Yantra India, India Optel and Gliders India. Bharat Electronics Limited was not one of them.
52.tq: Find the one organisation outside the specified successor group.

52.s: With reference to the procurement categories under DAP 2020, which one has the HIGHEST priority?
52.x: Buy (Indian-IDDM) is the highest-priority procurement category under DAP 2020.
52.tq: Use the priority-order clue and distinguish the two closely related Indian procurement categories.

52.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Buy (Indian-IDDM):
1. IDDM stands for Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured.
2. The category was first added in DPP 2016.
3. It was introduced on the advice of the Dhirendra Singh Committee.
4. It is the least preferred category under DAP 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Buy (Indian-IDDM) is the most preferred category under DAP 2020.
52.tq: Find the single reversed-priority statement among the otherwise precise factual statements.

52.s: Which of the following correctly describes the review initiated by the Ministry of Defence in 2025?
o: It declared 2025 the Year of Reforms and began reviewing DAP 2020 to support joint ventures and technology transfer for the private sector.
It reviewed DPP 2013 to expand only government-to-government procurement.
It declared 2025 the Year of Indigenisation and discontinued DAP 2020 completely.
It introduced DPM 2025 exclusively for capital procurement by the armed forces.
52.x: The Ministry of Defence declared 2025 the Year of Reforms and began reviewing DAP 2020 to support JVs and technology transfer for the private sector.
52.tq: Match the reform year with its stated objective and avoid confusing DAP with DPM.

52.s: An Expression of Interest for 600 indigenous 1,000-kg aerial bombs was associated with which procurement category?
52.x: The EoI for 600 indigenous 1,000-kg aerial bombs was issued under Buy (Indian-IDDM).
52.tq: Apply the procurement-category definition to an indigenous manufacturing example.

52.s: Under DAP 2020, offset clauses were dropped in which types of deals?
o: All Indian private-sector deals and all export contracts
52.x: DAP 2020 dropped offset clauses in government-to-government and single-vendor deals.
52.tq: Distinguish the two specified deal types from broader procurement categories.

52.s: The Defence Procurement Manual (DPM) 2025, released on 23 October 2025, governs which kind of procurement?
o: Revenue procurement of about Rs 1 lakh crore
Only procurement under the Strategic Partnership model
52.x: DPM 2025 (released 23 Oct 2025, effective 1 Nov 2025) covers revenue procurement of about Rs 1 lakh crore. Capital acquisition is governed by DAP 2020; exports and the SP model are not what the DPM covers.
52.tq: DPM = revenue; DAP = capital.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about Positive Indigenisation Lists:
1. Five Positive Indigenisation Lists have been issued.
2. They bar imports of listed items after specified dates.
3. The SRIJAN portal is associated with their implementation and indigenisation efforts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct. Five lists have been issued, imports of listed items are barred after set dates, and SRIJAN supports indigenisation.
52.tq: Check whether all components of a policy description belong to the same indigenisation framework.

52.s: What is the principal function of the SRIJAN portal?
o: To provide export licences for defence equipment
To conduct recruitment for the armed forces
To enable DPSUs and the Services to list imported items that Indian industry can manufacture
52.x: SRIJAN is the indigenisation portal through which DPSUs and the Services list import items that Indian industry can manufacture.
52.tq: Use the portal-function distinction and avoid confusing SRIJAN with a funding scheme.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about iDEX:
1. It was launched by the Prime Minister in April 2018.
2. It works with MSMEs, start-ups, innovators and academia.
