58.x: LPG mainly consists of propane and butane, is obtained as a by-product of oil refining and gas processing, and is heavier than air.
58.tq: Combine composition, origin and physical-property statements.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Piped Natural Gas (PNG)?
o: It contains 85–95 per cent methane and is supplied continuously through CGD networks
It contains mainly propane and butane and is stored in cylinders
It is natural gas liquefied below −160°C and transported by tankers
It is a heavy residual fuel supplied only to boilers
58.x: PNG contains approximately 85–95 per cent methane and is supplied through City Gas Distribution networks on a continuous basis.
58.tq: Separate PNG from LPG, LNG and furnace oil using composition and delivery mode.

58.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Furnace oil — light fuel for household cooking
58.x: Brent is the North Sea crude-price benchmark, while WTI is the United States benchmark. Furnace oil is a heavy residual fuel used in boilers.
58.tq: Discriminate between two commonly confused crude-price benchmarks.

58.s: India has approximately how many LPG connections?
58.x: India has approximately 33 crore LPG connections. Domestic gas could supply around 30 crore consumers if they switched to PNG.
58.tq: Direct recall of a large sectoral figure.

58.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Product)
A. LPG
B. CNG
C. Naphtha
D. Furnace oil

List-II (Main use)
1. Petrochemicals and fertilisers
2. Household cooking
3. Industrial boilers and furnaces
4. Vehicles

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
58.x: LPG is mainly used for household cooking, CNG for vehicles, naphtha for petrochemicals and fertilisers, and furnace oil in industrial boilers and furnaces.
58.tq: Start with the sure product-use pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Petrochemicals — Plastics, synthetic fibres and rubber
Furnace oil — Industrial boilers and furnaces
58.x: CNG is mainly used in vehicles and produces lower pollutants. Industrial boilers and furnaces mainly use furnace oil in the given classification.
58.tq: Identify the product whose stated use has been swapped with a neighbouring product.

58.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding LNG, CNG and LPG?
o: LNG is natural gas cooled below −160°C; CNG is compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm²; LPG mainly contains propane and butane.
LNG is propane cooled below −16°C; CNG is compressed to 20–25 kg/cm²; LPG mainly contains methane.
LNG and LPG are identical forms of methane, while CNG is a mixture of propane and butane.
LNG is coal bed methane, whereas LPG is methane frozen in deep-sea sediments.
58.x: LNG is methane-rich natural gas cooled below −160°C, CNG is compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm², and LPG mainly consists of propane and butane from refining.
58.tq: Separate the three similar fuel terms using their state, pressure and composition.

58.s: India has been a net exporter of petroleum products since
58.x: India became a net exporter of petroleum products in 2001-02. 1991-92 (the reform year), 2011-12 and 2016-17 are distractors with no link to this milestone. India still imports most of its crude oil; it exports refined products.
58.tq: Net exporter of PRODUCTS (not crude) since 2001-02.

58.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the cleanest fossil fuel?
58.x: Natural gas is the cleanest fossil fuel. Coal is the most polluting. Furnace oil is a heavy residual fuel used in boilers. Naphtha is a refinery feedstock for petrochemicals and fertilisers.
58.tq: Cleanest fossil fuel = natural gas.

58.s: India's targeted share of gas in the energy mix by 2030 is approximately
58.x: The target is to raise the share of gas in the energy mix from about 6.7 percent to 15 percent by 2030.
58.tq: Distinguish the present approximate share from the future target.

58.s: The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline passes through which states?
o: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal
58.x: The HVJ pipeline of GAIL connects Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; Maharashtra is not on this route.
58.tq: Use route sequencing and the excluded-state trap to identify the correct corridor.

58.s:
Which of the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga project is correct?

1. It is also known as the Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra pipeline.
2. Its authorised length is 3,546 km.
3. Its running length is 3,272 km.
4. It links the eastern and north-eastern regions to the gas grid.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: All four statements correctly describe Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga, including its JHBDPL identity, authorised and operating lengths, and regional linkage function.
58.tq: Check the project name, both numerical lengths and its stated connectivity before selecting the complete combination.

58.s:
Which of the following organisations constitute the joint venture for the Indradhanush North-East Gas Grid?

1. IOCL
2. ONGC
3. GAIL
4. OIL
5. NRL

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The joint venture comprises IOCL, ONGC, GAIL, OIL and NRL.
58.tq: Verify the full institutional composition instead of stopping at the first three familiar entities.

58.s: One Nation One Gas Grid was initiated in
58.x: The One Nation One Gas Grid initiative began in 2014.
58.tq: Distinguish the initial year of the gas-grid idea from the later implementation dates.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly states the target associated with One Nation One Gas Grid?
o: A network of 25,429 km linking all districts by 2025
A national network of 3,200 km linking only the eastern States by 2030
A national network of more than 32,000 km linking all States by 2027
A network of 34,223 km restricted to the eight North-Eastern States by 2027
58.x: The target is a national pipeline network exceeding 32,000 km and linking all States by 2027.
58.tq: Combine the target length, coverage and deadline in one precise option.

58.s: The idea of a national gas grid was first proposed in 1955 by
58.x: S. H. Zaheer first proposed the idea of a national gas grid in 1955.
58.tq: Test the person-year association without confusing the proposal with later implementation.

58.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. HVJ — Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
2. Trishna gas project — Tripura
3. East-West pipeline — Kakinada to Bharuch
4. PM Urja Ganga — Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha
58.x: All four pairings are correct. The East-West pipeline runs from Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh to Bharuch in Gujarat, while PM Urja Ganga covers the five listed eastern and north-central States.
58.tq: Check each route against its states and endpoints before selecting the complete matching set.

58.s: As on 31 March 2025, the natural gas pipeline network authorised by PNGRB and the length in operation were respectively about
58.x: PNGRB had authorised 34,223 km of pipelines, of which 25,429 km were operating. Swapping the two numbers is the trap. 3,546/3,272 km are the authorised/running lengths of PM Urja Ganga alone, and 1,656 km is the Indradhanush NE grid.
58.tq: Authorised 34k > operating 25k; target >32,000 km by 2027.

58.s:
With reference to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), consider the following statements:

1. It is a statutory body under the PNGRB Act, 2006.
2. It authorises geographical areas for city gas distribution.
3. It sets pipeline tariffs.
4. It regulates crude oil production.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: PNGRB is a statutory body under the 2006 Act, authorises CGD geographical areas and sets pipeline tariffs. It does not regulate crude oil production among the activities specified here.
58.tq: Apply the authority test: identify the powers expressly assigned to PNGRB and reject the overextended production claim.

58.s:
According to the specified regulatory division, PNGRB regulates which two activities among the following?

1. Production of crude oil
2. Refining, storage and distribution of petroleum
3. Marketing and sale of petroleum products
4. Production of natural gas

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The two regulated activities specified are refining, storage and distribution of petroleum, and marketing and sale of petroleum products. Crude oil and natural gas production are not included in these two activities.
58.tq: Separate regulated downstream activities from upstream production activities.

58.s: Oil marketing companies had established how many Energy Stations by 1 August 2025?
58.x: Oil marketing companies had established 799 Energy Stations by 1 August 2025.
58.tq: Retain the exact count and date together; nearby figures are scale-based distractors.

58.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Phase I locations of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
58.x: Phase I of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves comprises Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur in Karnataka.
58.tq: Use location-based elimination among closely related energy projects.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR):
1. Phase I reserves cover about 9.5 days of India's imports.
2. The IEA norm for strategic reserve cover is 60 days of imports.
3. The reserves are operated by ISPRL under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas through OIDB.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: Phase I (Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur) gives about 9.5 days of import cover. Statement 2 is wrong: the IEA norm is 90 days, not 60. Statement 3 is correct: ISPRL operates the reserves under MoPNG through OIDB. So 1 and 3 only.
58.tq: India about 9.5 days against the IEA norm of 90 days; the gap is the point the exam tests.

58.s:
Under the new strategic fuel reserve plan, which of the following combinations is correct?
1. It is planned to hold about two months of crude and LNG.
2. It is planned to hold about six weeks of LPG.
3. It is proposed to be funded partly through levies on LPG and gas.
58.x: The proposed reserve covers about two months of crude and LNG and about six weeks of LPG, with funding through levies on LPG and gas.
58.tq: Use the coverage periods and financing mechanism together to test a policy proposal.

58.s: The Andhra Pradesh Gas Infrastructure Corporation holds what share in a consortium with ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas for four KG-basin blocks?
58.x: APGIC holds a 10 per cent share in the consortium involving ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas for four KG-basin blocks.
58.tq: Direct recall of consortium participation and percentage.

58.s: Which of the following pairs of KG-basin fields and participating entities is correctly matched?
58.x: Ravva is an offshore KG field associated with Cairn-ONGC, whereas KG-D6 is associated with Reliance-BP.
58.tq: Swap-the-owner trap involving two prominent KG-basin fields.

58.s: The target for PNG connections in Andhra Pradesh under the City Gas Distribution expansion is:
58.x: The target is 83.61 lakh PNG connections by March 2032.
58.tq: Read the quantity and deadline together to avoid a partial-number or date trap.

58.s: The Supreme Court’s cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 was followed by which legislative measure for auction-based allocation?
o: Mines and Minerals Act, 1957, without amendment
58.x: The cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 led to the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, which enabled auction-based allocation.
58.tq: Match the judicial event with the specific corrective legislation that followed it.

58.s:
Which of the following functions is performed by the Coal Controller’s Organisation?
1. Compilation of coal statistics
2. Monitoring of captive coal blocks
3. Hearing objections relating to acquisition of coal-bearing land

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The Coal Controller’s Organisation performs all three functions: maintaining coal statistics, monitoring captive blocks and hearing objections concerning acquisition of coal-bearing land.
58.tq: Group the body’s technical, monitoring and quasi-adjudicatory functions before choosing the code.

58.s: The publication titled ‘Energy Statistics’ is brought out by the:
o: Coal Controller’s Organisation under the Ministry of Coal
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Power
National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
58.x: Energy Statistics is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
58.tq: Identify the publishing authority and avoid swapping it with a sectoral regulator or ministry.

58.s: The coal associated with the Godavari valley is:
58.x: The Godavari valley coalfields are associated with Singareni, which is now in Telangana. The historical observation was that Andhra lacked coal and would draw on Singareni.
58.tq: Location-resource association using a nearby regional distractor.

58.s: The Coal Council of India was set up in
58.x: The Coal Council of India was established in 1956.
58.tq: Distinguish institutional formation dates from later nationalisation dates.

58.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of coal-sector nationalisation?
o: Non-coking coal in 1971-72, coking coal in 1973, Coal India Ltd in 1975
Coking coal in 1971-72, non-coking coal in 1973, Coal India Ltd in 1975
Coking coal in 1973, non-coking coal in 1975, Coal India Ltd in 1971-72
Coal India Ltd in 1971-72, coking coal in 1973, non-coking coal in 1975
58.x: Coking coal was nationalised in 1971-72, non-coking coal in 1973, and Coal India Ltd was established in 1975.
58.tq: Fix the first and last milestones before checking the middle event.

58.s: Commercial mining auctions for coal commenced from
58.x: Commercial mining auctions for coal began in 2020.
58.tq: Separate the year of the special-provisions legislation from the year commercial auctions began.

58.s: Which of the following is NOT a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Coal mentioned in the context of the coal sector?
58.x: The listed Ministry of Coal PSUs are Coal India Limited, NLC India and Singareni Collieries Company Limited. Oil India Limited belongs to the petroleum sector.
58.tq: Find the organisation belonging to the neighbouring petroleum sector.

58.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First coal mine at Sitarampur, Raniganj
B. Beginning of India's oil industry at Digboi
C. Proposal of a national gas grid to Nehru
D. Establishment of Coal India Ltd
58.x: The events occurred in 1774, 1889, 1955 and 1975 respectively.
58.tq: Place the earliest and latest events first, then order the two middle dates.

58.s: The equity of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) is held as follows:
58.x: SCCL is a joint company of Telangana and the Centre: Telangana holds 51% and the Government of India 49%. Reversing the split is the usual trap. It is neither wholly State-owned nor majority Central.
58.tq: SCCL: State 51 : Centre 49.

58.s: Coal gasification primarily produces syngas containing
o: Carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide
58.x: Coal gasification produces syngas containing carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide.
58.tq: Break the process output into its named chemical constituents.

58.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a possible product or downstream application of coal gasification?
58.x: Coal gasification can support production of SNG, methanol, ethanol, ammonia or urea, hydrogen and petrochemicals. Nuclear fuel enrichment is not a stated application.
58.tq: Identify the unrelated industrial application among the gasification products.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about coal gasification in India:
1. The National Coal Gasification Mission targets 100 MT by 2030.
2. The first coal-gasification fertiliser plant is planned at Angul (Odisha) by December 2027.
3. JSPL's Angul plant is the only commercial-scale coal-gasification plant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: the mission target is 100 MT by 2030. Statement 2 is wrong: the first gasification fertiliser plant is planned at Talcher (Odisha), not Angul, by December 2027. Statement 3 is correct: JSPL Angul is the only commercial-scale plant. So 1 and 3 only.
58.tq: Talcher = the fertiliser plant to come; Angul (JSPL) = the plant already running. Both are in Odisha, which is the trap.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about India's coal sector:
1. Coal output crossed 1,000 million tonnes in FY 2025-26.
2. India is the world's largest producer of coal.
3. Coking coal is imported mainly from Australia and Indonesia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: output was 1,040.08 MT in FY 2025-26. Statement 2 is wrong: India is the second-largest producer (about 10%) after China (51%). Statement 3 is correct: coking coal is imported from Australia and Indonesia. So 1 and 3 only.
58.tq: Coal: 1,040 MT; 2nd after China; coking coal imported.

58.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the stated estimates of India's import dependence?
o: Crude oil about 80% and gas about 25% only
Crude oil about 25% and gas about 80%
Crude oil about 50% and gas about 88%
Crude oil about 88% and gas about 50%
58.x: The cited estimate places India's import reliance at about 88% for crude oil and 50% for gas. Another cited estimate gives lower figures of 80% and 25%, showing the difference between sources.
58.tq: Keep the two fuels and their percentages in the correct order.

58.s: IUCN Motion 042 of 2025 describes fossil-fuel production as
58.x: IUCN Motion 042 (2025) calls fossil-fuel production a direct threat to nature.
58.tq: Identify the exact wording of the environmental criticism.

58.s:
Which of the following events were linked to West Asia supply shocks in the stated current-affairs context?
1. Samudra Manthan in August 2026
2. The strategic petroleum reserve levy plan in August 2026
3. The Dandewala find in May 2026
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Samudra Manthan, the strategic reserve levy plan and the Dandewala find were all presented as current developments driven by West Asia supply shocks.
58.tq: Group multiple current developments under their common cause.

58.s: Following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March 2026, India reportedly relied more on
o: Imported coal while stopping domestic production
Only imported crude oil while stopping gas imports
Nuclear power alone while suspending LPG imports
Domestic coal and gas while accelerating LNG and LPG imports
58.x: The Hormuz closure led India to lean on domestic coal and gas and accelerate LNG and LPG imports.
58.tq: Apply the supply-disruption scenario to the stated energy response.

58.s: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board approved how many geographical areas in Andhra Pradesh in the stated city-gas-distribution context?
58.x: PNGRB approved 10 geographical areas in Andhra Pradesh.
58.tq: Distinguish the number of approved geographical areas from connection targets.

59.s: According to the latest reported figures, India's total installed electricity generation capacity and the share of non-fossil sources are approximately
59.x: India's total installed capacity is about 552 GW, of which non-fossil sources account for more than 54%.
59.tq: Match the current total with its associated percentage rather than an older capacity figure.

59.s: Which of the following is the largest renewable-energy component in India's installed capacity?
59.x: Solar capacity was 164.59 GW in the latest cited figures and is the largest renewable-energy component.
59.tq: Identify the largest item by comparing the renewable-source figures.

59.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the latest cited installed capacity?
1. Large hydro — 51.96 GW
2. Nuclear — 8.78 GW
3. Coal and lignite thermal — about 247 GW
59.x: Large hydro was 51.96 GW, nuclear 8.78 GW and coal plus lignite thermal capacity was about 247 GW.
59.tq: Check the source-wise values individually; all three correspond to the stated capacity figures.

59.s: India's installed capacity reached the 50 per cent non-fossil threshold approximately
59.x: The 50 per cent non-fossil share was reached about five years before 2030.
59.tq: Read the relative date carefully instead of treating 2030 as the achievement year.

59.s:
Arrange the following sources in descending order of their shares in the source-wise capacity table:
A. Wind
B. Coal including lignite
C. Large hydro
D. Solar
59.x: The descending order is coal including lignite at 42.43 per cent, solar at 28.96 per cent, wind at 10.47 per cent and large hydro at 9.58 per cent.
59.tq: Compare the percentages first and arrange from the highest to the lowest.

59.s: Which of the following statements about capacity additions during 2025-26 is correct?
o: Total non-fossil capacity declined by 44.6 GW.
59.x: A record 44.6 GW of solar capacity was added during 2025-26.
59.tq: Distinguish the decimal placement and the source to which the addition relates.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly states the installed capacity distribution in April 2023 among the private, State and Central sectors?
59.x: In April 2023, the private sector accounted for 50.6 per cent, the State sector 25.4 per cent and the Centre 24 per cent.
59.tq: Keep the three-sector order intact while comparing closely related percentages.

59.s:
Consider the following projections of the National Generation Adequacy Plan for 2035-36:
1. Installed capacity of 1,121 GW
2. Non-fossil share of 70 per cent
3. Peak demand of 459 GW
4. Storage requirement of 174 GW/888 GWh
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: The plan projects all four figures: 1,121 GW capacity, 70 per cent non-fossil share, 459 GW peak demand and 174 GW/888 GWh storage.
59.tq: Check whether all projected figures belong to the same planning horizon before selecting the complete code.

59.s: India's global ranking in renewable-energy capacity, solar capacity and wind capacity, respectively, is
59.x: The latest cited ranking places India third in renewable and solar capacity and fourth in wind capacity.
59.tq: Preserve the order of the three categories while distinguishing current rankings from older figures.

59.s: What percentage of India’s electricity generation in 2024-25 came from thermal sources and renewable-energy sources, respectively?
59.x: Thermal sources contributed about 75% and renewable-energy sources about 22% of generation in 2024-25.
59.tq: Read the two percentages in the order asked.

59.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the approximate capacity factors or operating ranges of different power sources in India?
1. Coal plants: 60–85%
2. Nuclear plants: above 84%
3. Wind: 20–35%
4. Solar: 20–25%
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: The stated ranges are coal 60–85%, nuclear above 84% or roughly 85–90%, wind 20–35% and solar 20–25%.
59.tq: Compare operating ranges source by source rather than assuming capacity equals generation.

59.s: Which region had the highest plant load factor according to the APPSC 2019 key?
59.x: The Southern Region was identified as having the highest plant load factor.
59.tq: Discriminate among similarly named regional grids or regions.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the capacity–generation relationship in India:
1. Non-fossil sources account for over 54% of installed capacity.
2. Coal accounts for about 42% of installed capacity.
3. Coal produces over 70% of electricity generation.
4. Nuclear accounts for about 1.6% of capacity and about 3% of generation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All four are correct. Non-fossil sources are over 54% of capacity, yet coal, with only about 42% of capacity, gives over 70% of electricity; nuclear is about 1.6% of capacity but about 3% of generation (57 TWh in 2024-25). This is the capacity-generation paradox, so 1, 2, 3 and 4.
59.tq: Separate installed-capacity shares from actual-generation shares.

59.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes coal-based generation in 2025-26?
o: It fell by 5.39%, but its share rose for the first time in 50 years.
It fell by 3.69%, and its share fell for the first time in 50 years.
It remained unchanged, although its capacity share fell.
It increased by 3.69% and reached its highest share in five decades.
59.x: Coal generation fell by 3.69% in 2025-26, and its share fell for the first time in 50 years.
59.tq: Check both the direction and the magnitude of change.

59.s: India is the world’s ____ largest producer of electricity.
59.x: India is the third-largest electricity producer in the world.
59.tq: Test the global rank directly without confusing production with renewable capacity.

59.s: India’s electricity generation increased from 1,020.2 billion units in 2013–14 to approximately how much in 2024–25?
59.x: Electricity generation rose from 1,020.2 BU in 2013–14 to 1,830 BU in 2024–25.
59.tq: Use the two-endpoint comparison and identify the later value.

59.s: The Indian power system is described as “One Nation-One Grid-One Frequency” because it is
o: a grid used only for renewable-energy transmission
a distribution network controlled exclusively by state utilities
a collection of isolated state grids operating at different frequencies
59.x: India operates the world’s largest synchronous grid under the One Nation-One Grid-One Frequency framework.
59.tq: Identify the defining feature rather than a related institutional claim.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about India’s regional grids:
1. There are five regional grids.
2. They are Northern, Eastern, Western, North-Eastern and Southern.
3. The Southern Grid was synchronised last.
4. The Southern Grid was synchronised in December 2013.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: India had five named regional grids, and the Southern Grid was the last to be synchronised, in December 2013.
59.tq: Test the list and the chronological detail together.

59.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Southern Grid synchronisation
B. PGCIL study for the Green Energy Corridor
C. Implementation of the Green Energy Corridor
D. APERC approval for procurement of 1,600 MW of coal power
59.x: The PGCIL study was conducted in 2012, the Southern Grid was synchronised in December 2013, the Green Energy Corridor was implemented from 2015, and the APERC approval came in 2026.
59.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle events.

59.s: Which of the following gives the correct funding pattern for Intra-State Green Energy Corridor-I?
59.x: The funding pattern is MNRE 40%, KfW 40% and the State Transmission Utility 20%.
59.tq: Compare the percentages while preserving the order of the funding agencies.

59.s: Which organisation functions as the Central Transmission Utility of India?
59.x: POWERGRID, or PGCIL, functions as the Central Transmission Utility.
59.tq: Match the statutory transmission role with the correct organisation.

59.s: India recorded a peak power demand of 270.82 GW on
59.x: The record peak demand was 270.82 GW on 21 May 2026.
59.tq: Match the record figure with its precise date.

59.s: According to the Economic Survey reference, the demand–supply gap in electricity had become zero by
59.x: The demand–supply gap was reported to be zero by November 2025.
59.tq: Distinguish the zero-gap date from the separate shortage figures.

59.s: The transmission network associated with India’s One Nation-One Grid-One Frequency system exceeds
59.x: The network exceeds 5 lakh circuit km.
59.tq: Identify the order of magnitude rather than confusing it with recent additions.

59.s: India’s peak power shortage declined from approximately 4.2% in 2014 to what level in 2025?
59.x: The peak shortage fell sharply from 4.2% in 2014 to 0.03% in 2025.
59.tq: Pay attention to the decimal placement in a near-zero deficit figure.

59.s: The Intra-State Green Energy Corridor Phase-I covers how many States, including Andhra Pradesh?
59.x: Intra-State GEC-I covers 8 States including Andhra Pradesh, with about 9,700 ckm of lines and 24 GW of RE, costing Rs 10,141.68 crore and funded MNRE 40%, KfW 40% and STU 20%. Five is the number of regional grids, not GEC States; ten and twelve are not the stated figure.
59.tq: GEC-I: 8 States; 40-40-20 funding.

59.s: The Electricity Act, 2003 was notified on which date?
59.x: The Electricity Act, 2003 was notified on 10 June 2003.
59.tq: Use the precise date rather than the year alone.

59.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Electricity Act, 2003?
59.x: The Act introduced or facilitated electricity trading; it did not abolish it. It also delicensed generation, required unbundling of SEBs and introduced open access and SERCs.
59.tq: Find the option that reverses a major provision of the Act.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Electricity Act, 2003:
1. It consolidates laws relating to generation, transmission, distribution and trading of electricity.
2. It established the Central Electricity Authority, regulatory commissions and an appellate tribunal.
3. It required State Electricity Boards to remain fully integrated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Act required SEBs to be unbundled.
59.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the unbundling provision.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC):
1. It was set up under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998.
2. After bifurcation, it served both successor States for up to two years under the AP Reorganisation Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: APERC was set up under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998, which came before the Electricity Act 2003. Statement 2 is wrong: after bifurcation APERC served both States for up to six months, not two years. So 1 only.
59.tq: APERC: 1998 Reform Act; shared after bifurcation for six months.

59.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body)
a. CERC
b. SERCs
c. APTEL
d. CEA
List-II (Function or feature)
i. Reports on installed capacity and National Electricity Plan
 ii. Central tariffs and inter-State matters
 iii. State retail tariffs, licensing and standards
 iv. Appeals against CERC and SERC orders
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: CERC handles central tariffs and inter-State matters; SERCs handle State retail tariffs and licensing; APTEL hears appeals; CEA publishes technical power-sector reports.
59.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched regulatory functions.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL):
1. It was established on 24 August 2004.
2. It hears appeals against orders of CERC and SERCs.
3. Its Chairperson is usually a retired High Court judge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004 under the Electricity Act 2003. Statement 2 is correct: it hears appeals against CERC and SERC orders. Statement 3 is wrong: its Chairperson is usually a retired Supreme Court judge, not a High Court judge. So 1 and 2 only.
59.tq: APTEL sits above CERC and SERCs, so it is headed by a retired Supreme Court judge.

59.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the following developments?
A. Establishment of CERC
B. Notification of the Electricity Act, 2003
C. Establishment of APTEL
D. Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020
59.x: CERC was set up in 1998, the Electricity Act was notified in 2003, APTEL was established in 2004, and the Consumer Rules were issued in 2020.
59.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intervening dates.

59.s: The Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020 primarily provide for
o: allocation of coal to thermal plants
time limits for new connections and service standards
59.x: The 2020 Rules prescribe time limits for new electricity connections and service standards for consumers.
59.tq: Match the consumer-rights rules with their service-delivery function.

59.s:
Which of the following are recognised power exchanges in India?
1. Indian Energy Exchange
2. Power Exchange India Limited
3. Hindustan Power Exchange
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: IEX, PXIL and HPX are the power exchanges identified in the electricity market framework.
59.tq: Use the complete-list option when all three named exchanges belong to the group.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about India's power markets:
1. The Real-Time Market was introduced in 2020.
2. The Green Day-Ahead Market was introduced in 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Real-Time Market began in 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: the Green Day-Ahead Market began in 2021, a year later. So 1 only.
59.tq: RTM 2020, then GDAM 2021: real-time first, green next.

59.s: The Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge and Related Matters) Rules, 2022 enable discoms to
o: fix tariffs without approval of the regulator
obtain free power from renewable generators
clear old dues in instalments and face restriction of power-exchange access for defaulting entities
59.x: The 2022 Rules permit discoms to clear old dues in instalments and provide for cutting power-exchange access for defaulters.
59.tq: Apply the rule to a defaulting discom rather than confuse it with tariff regulation.

59.s: Under the Rights of Consumers Rules, a new electricity connection is to be provided within which maximum periods in metropolitan, municipal and rural areas respectively?
59.x: The prescribed periods are 3 days in metropolitan areas, 7 days in municipal areas and 15 days in rural areas.
59.tq: Retain the geographical order while matching each area with its time limit.

59.s: The payment cycle for electricity-sector dues changed from 178 days in FY 2020-21 to how many days in FY 2024-25?
59.x: The payment cycle declined from 178 days in FY21 to 113 days in FY25.
59.tq: Compare the initial and latest values in the stated time sequence.

59.s: The amended Electricity Rules provide for automatic pass-through of fuel-cost changes. What is the principal intended effect of this provision?
o: It prevents generating companies from changing fuel sources.
It prevents new deficits from arising due to unrecovered fuel-cost changes.
It abolishes all electricity tariffs for agricultural consumers.
It transfers all distribution losses to consumers without regulation.
59.x: Automatic pass-through of fuel-cost changes is intended to prevent new deficits caused by delays in recovering such costs.
59.tq: Infer the financial consequence from the mechanism described in the rule.

59.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as a cause of the financial sickness of State Electricity Boards?
o: Autonomy of State Governments over power generation and distribution
Sale of electricity to agricultural and domestic consumers below cost
59.x: State autonomy over power generation and distribution was identified as not being a problem. Below-cost sales, high T&D losses and poor cost recovery were causes of financial sickness.
59.tq: Find the exception by separating a governance feature from genuine financial problems.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial sickness of State Electricity Boards:
1. Commercial losses, including theft, contributed to their sickness.
2. Delays in commissioning projects were identified as a problem in the power sector.
3. Power sold to agricultural and domestic consumers below cost contributed to their sickness.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: Commercial losses, project delays and below-cost sale of power were all identified as sector problems or causes of financial weakness.
59.tq: Combine the financial and project-related causes without treating them as mutually exclusive.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about State power subsidies:
1. States spend about ₹2.4 lakh crore a year subsidising farm and domestic power.
2. Since FY 2021-22, States pay only half of the current subsidy and defer the legacy subsidy dues.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: States spend about ₹2.4 lakh crore a year on farm and domestic power subsidies. Statement 2 is wrong: since FY 2021-22 States must pay the full subsidy and also clear legacy subsidy dues. So 1 only; 'both' and '2 only' include the wrong statement, and 'neither' rejects a true one.
59.tq: The reform is full payment plus clearing old dues, not half.

59.s: A discom with fixed long-term power-purchase agreements faces a shortfall during a demand spike. It is most likely to procure the additional electricity
o: only from nuclear plants at fixed prices
from the Finance Commission without purchase contracts
from exchanges at volatile peak prices
59.x: Discoms with fixed long-term PPAs buy shortfalls on power exchanges, where prices can be volatile during peak demand.
59.tq: Apply the demand-pressure problem to the operational choice available to a discom.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about DISCOM loss metrics:
1. AT&C loss covers technical and commercial losses, including theft and inefficiency in billing and collection.
2. The ACS-ARR gap is the average revenue realised minus the average cost of supply per unit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: AT&C loss means technical plus commercial losses (theft, billing and collection inefficiency). Statement 2 is wrong because the order is reversed: the ACS-ARR gap is the average cost of supply minus the average revenue realised per unit. So 1 only.
59.tq: ACS-ARR is read in order: cost minus revenue, and a positive gap means a loss per unit.

59.s: AT&C losses declined from 22.62% in FY 2013-14 to what level in FY 2024-25?
59.x: AT&C losses declined to 15.04% in FY25 from 22.62% in FY14. The figure of 16.12% relates to FY24 in an older set of values.
59.tq: Match the exact percentage with the correct financial year and reject the nearby-year figure.

59.s: The ACS-ARR gap decreased from ₹0.78 per kWh in FY 2013-14 to what level in FY 2024-25?
59.x: The ACS-ARR gap fell to ₹0.06 per kWh in FY25 from ₹0.78 per kWh in FY14. This equals 6 paise per unit, not 0.06 paise.
59.tq: Check both the unit and the decimal placement in a small financial figure.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the financial performance of DISCOMs?
o: They posted a profit of ₹67,962 crore in FY25 after a loss of ₹2,701 crore in 2013-14.
They posted identical profits in both years.
They posted a loss of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 after a profit of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
They posted a profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 after a loss of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
59.x: DISCOMs posted a profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25, compared with a loss of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
59.tq: Track both the direction of change and the year attached to each amount.

59.s: The PFC Integrated Rating and Ranking exercise grades DISCOMs annually on which basis?
o: Only the number of rural households connected
59.x: PFC annually grades DISCOMs on their financial and operational performance through its Integrated Rating and Ranking exercise.
59.tq: Identify the two-dimensional basis of the institutional rating.

59.s: Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY), launched in November 2015, was primarily intended for which of the following purposes?
o: Financial turnaround and revival of DISCOMs
Universal installation of nuclear power plants
Privatisation of all State Electricity Boards
59.x: UDAY was launched in November 2015 to achieve the financial turnaround and revival of distribution companies.
59.tq: Directly identify the purpose associated with the named scheme.

59.s: Which one of the following is a demand-side intervention under UDAY?
59.x: The use of energy-efficient LED bulbs is a demand-side intervention. Coal swapping, transformer upgrades and feeder metering are operational interventions.
59.tq: Separate operational measures from measures that reduce consumer-side energy demand.

59.s:
Which of the following is a set of distribution-sector schemes mentioned in connection with electricity reforms?
1. DDUGJY
2. IPDS
3. SAUBHAGYA
4. RDSS
59.x: DDUGJY, IPDS, SAUBHAGYA and RDSS are all identified as distribution-sector schemes.
59.tq: Recognise the complete scheme cluster and avoid excluding a less familiar acronym.

59.s: The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) was conveyed on 3 December 2014. Which one of the following correctly describes it?
o: A scheme exclusively for nuclear-power generation
A scheme for last-mile household connections in urban areas only
A rural power scheme that subsumed RGGVY and aimed at 24x7 power in rural India
A scheme for privatisation of rural DISCOMs
59.x: DDUGJY was conveyed on 3 December 2014, subsumed the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana and aimed at providing 24x7 power in rural India.
59.tq: Combine the date, predecessor scheme and principal objective of a government programme.

59.s: Which organisation is the nodal agency for DDUGJY?
59.x: Rural Electrification Corporation, or REC, is the nodal agency for DDUGJY.
59.tq: Use the institutional-association approach to identify the nodal agency.

59.s:
Consider the following components of DDUGJY:
1. Separation of agricultural and non-agricultural feeders
2. Strengthening of sub-transmission and distribution systems
3. Development of micro-grids and off-grid systems
4. Metering of distribution transformers, feeders and consumers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All four are components of DDUGJY. The scheme also includes rural electrification as a major component.
59.tq: Test the completeness of a scheme by checking whether each listed component belongs to its design.

59.s: Under DDUGJY, the normal grant component and the additional milestone-linked support are respectively:
59.x: DDUGJY provides a 60% grant and additional support of up to 15% linked to milestones. For special-category States, the corresponding figures are 85% and 5%.
59.tq: Recall the paired percentage structure and distinguish ordinary from special-category States.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between feeder separation, RDSS and PM-KUSUM?
o: Feeder separation ended with DDUGJY and has no connection with later schemes.
Feeder separation continues under RDSS, and separated agricultural feeders are subsequently solarised under PM-KUSUM.
PM-KUSUM separates urban commercial feeders under RDSS.
RDSS replaced feeder separation with only off-grid micro-grids.
59.x: Feeder separation continues under RDSS, while separated agricultural feeders can subsequently be solarised under PM-KUSUM.
59.tq: Trace the policy sequence from an infrastructure intervention to its later application.

59.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I
(a) Date of electrification milestone
(b) Number of inhabited census villages electrified
(c) Last village electrified
(d) State of the last village

List-II
(i) Manipur
(ii) 28 April 2018
(iii) Leisang
(iv) 18,374
59.x: The milestone occurred on 28 April 2018; 18,374 inhabited census villages were electrified; the last village was Leisang in Manipur.
59.tq: Start from the sure date-place pair and eliminate incompatible codes.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Saubhagya scheme (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana)?
o: Launched in 2017 with REC as nodal agency for last-mile household connections; about 2.86 crore households electrified
Conveyed in 2014, subsumed RGGVY and focused on separating agricultural feeders
Launched in 2021 as a results-linked scheme for smart prepaid meters with REC and PFC as nodal agencies
Launched in 2015 for the financial turnaround of DISCOMs through debt takeover
59.x: Saubhagya (2017, nodal REC) gave last-mile household connections to about 2.86 crore households. Option B describes DDUGJY, option C describes RDSS and option D describes UDAY.
59.tq: Villages = DDUGJY (2014); households = Saubhagya (2017).

59.s: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) was introduced in which year, and what is its stated total outlay?
59.x: RDSS was introduced in 2021 with an outlay of ₹3.03 lakh crore.
59.tq: Match the programme year with its distinctive outlay figure.

59.s:
Which of the following features characterises RDSS?
1. It is reform-based.
2. It is results-linked.
3. It has been extended by two years up to FY 2027-28.
4. REC and PFC are its nodal agencies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: All four statements are correct. RDSS is reform-based and results-linked, has been extended to FY 2027-28, and uses REC and PFC as nodal agencies.
59.tq: Use a four-part scheme profile rather than relying on its name alone.

59.s:
Under RDSS, smart metering is implemented on which model, with priority given to which consumers?

1. TOTEX model under a public-private partnership framework
2. Government offices
3. Commercial consumers
4. Commercial and industrial consumers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: RDSS smart metering follows the TOTEX model under PPP, with priority for government offices and commercial and C&I consumers.
59.tq: Link the implementation model with the priority consumer categories.

59.s: Which of the following correctly represents the smart-metering figures under RDSS?
59.x: Approximately 4.7 crore smart meters had been installed, while 20.34 crore had been sanctioned under RDSS.
59.tq: Compare installed and sanctioned quantities without reversing their status.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL):
1. It undertakes demand aggregation for large smart-metering programmes.
2. It signed an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic PNG meters.
3. It has replaced REC as the nodal agency of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: EESL aggregates demand for large smart-metering programmes. Statement 2 is correct: it signed an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic piped natural gas meters. Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal agencies of RDSS are REC and PFC, not EESL. So 1 and 2 only.
59.tq: RDSS nodal agencies = REC + PFC; EESL only aggregates demand.

59.s: Repayment associated with the SPVs created to warehouse discom debt would qualify for
o: the Special Incentive Scheme for Capital Investment
59.x: Repayment of the warehoused discom debt qualifies for the Special Incentive Scheme for Capital Investment.
59.tq: Distinguish the incentive linked to debt repayment from the names of other electricity schemes.

59.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Delhi DISCOMs — Privatised in 2002
2. Odisha DISCOMs — Taken over by Tata Power in 2020-21
3. Bhiwandi input-based franchise model — Torrent, 2007
4. Sixteenth Finance Commission — Recommendation for active DISCOM privatisation by States

Select the correct answer using the code below.
59.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Delhi’s DISCOMs were privatised in 2002, Odisha’s were taken over by Tata Power in 2020-21, Bhiwandi pioneered the cited franchise model in 2007, and the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended active State-led privatisation.
59.tq: Start with the sure historical pair and verify the remaining institutional associations.

59.s: The input-based franchisee model in electricity distribution was first implemented at Bhiwandi by:
59.x: The input-based franchisee model was first implemented at Bhiwandi by Torrent in 2007.
59.tq: Match the place, implementing entity and year in a reform-history question.

59.s: Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah Thermal Power Station is associated with:
59.x: Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS is owned by APPDCL.
59.tq: Apply the owner-function distinction among NTPC, APGENCO and APPDCL.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s coal supply:
1. Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own.
2. It depends on coal from Singareni and MCL.
3. Its thermal power plants therefore depend entirely on imported coal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own and draws coal from Singareni and MCL. Statement 3 is wrong: because its supply comes from these domestic sources (Singareni and MCL), its plants do not depend entirely on imported coal. So 1 and 2 only.
59.tq: Reject the extreme word “entirely” and distinguish domestic external sources from imports.

59.s: What was the installed and contracted electricity capacity of Andhra Pradesh, as indicated for 2025-26?
59.x: Andhra Pradesh had an installed and contracted capacity of 21,297 MW.
59.tq: Use the exact capacity figure rather than approximating the total.

59.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Power plant)
a. Simhadri STPP
b. Dr NTTPS
c. Dr M.V.R. RTPP
 d. Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS

List-II (Location)
i. Muddanur, Kadapa district
 ii. Krishnapatnam, Nellore district
 iii. Visakhapatnam district
 iv. Ibrahimpatnam, near Vijayawada

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: Simhadri is in Visakhapatnam, Dr NTTPS is at Ibrahimpatnam, RTPP is at Muddanur, and Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS is at Krishnapatnam.
59.tq: Start from the sure location–plant pairs and eliminate the codes.

59.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dr M.V.R. RTPP — APGENCO — 600 MW unit
Dr NTTPS — APGENCO — 500 MW and 800 MW units
59.x: Hinduja National Power in Visakhapatnam is owned by the Hinduja group, not APGENCO. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
59.tq: Find the swapped owner in a plant–location–capacity association.

59.s: Which of the following correctly describes the power procurement approved in principle by APERC on 6 August 2026?
o: 5,588 MW of thermal power through nominated allocation under Section 63
2,600 MW of solar power through reverse auction under Section 86
1,600 MW of coal power through tariff-based bidding under Section 63 on the DBFOO model
1,000 MW of gas power through cost-plus regulation under Section 62
59.x: APERC approved in principle the purchase of 1,600 MW of coal power through tariff-based bidding under Section 63 on the DBFOO model.
59.tq: Split the option into capacity, fuel, procurement method and legal provision.

59.s: According to the stated Andhra Pradesh demand projection, the demand CAGR and peak demand projected for 2035–36 are respectively:
59.x: The projected demand CAGR is 6.90%, and peak demand is expected to reach 30,927 MW by 2035–36.
59.tq: Match the growth rate with the corresponding projected peak figure.

59.s: The transmission and distribution (T&D) losses of Andhra Pradesh's power system are reported at about
59.x: AP's T&D losses are 9.25%, with 376 EHT substations and 33,379.72 ckm of transmission lines. 15.04% and 22.62% are the national AT&C losses for FY25 and FY14, and 4.2% was India's peak power shortage in 2014.
59.tq: AP T&D 9.25% vs national AT&C 15.04%.

59.s: Who introduced free electricity for farmers in Andhra Pradesh after becoming Chief Minister on 14 May 2004?
59.x: Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy introduced free electricity for farmers after becoming Chief Minister on 14 May 2004.
59.tq: Match the policy decision with the correct office-holder and date.

59.s: Under PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh, approximately how many farm pump sets are proposed to be solarised?
59.x: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh aims to solarise 2.93 lakh farm pump sets.
59.tq: Distinguish closely related lakh-based target figures.

59.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding Andhra Pradesh DISCOMs?
o: APSPDCL — Headquartered at Hyderabad after its 2020 re-formation
59.x: APSPDCL is headquartered at Tirupati. APCPDCL was re-formed in 2020 at Vijayawada; the older pre-2014 APCPDCL was associated with Hyderabad.
59.tq: Find the single location and organisational-history mismatch.

59.s: Which statement correctly describes the change involving APSPDCL after bifurcation under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: It was re-formed at Vijayawada in 2020.
It took over all districts formerly served by APEPDCL.
It took over Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL.
59.x: At bifurcation under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, APSPDCL took over Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL.
59.tq: Identify the specific territorial transfer rather than the headquarters of the DISCOM.

59.s: In Andhra Pradesh, BPL SC/ST households receive free electricity up to how many units a month?
59.x: About 20.79 lakh BPL SC/ST households get free power up to 200 units a month. 100, 150 and 300 units are not the stated limit. Aqua farmers, by contrast, get a concessional tariff of Rs 1.50 per unit.
59.tq: SC/ST BPL: 200 units free; aqua: Rs 1.50/unit.

59.s: Which one of the following publications is correctly matched with its publisher?
o: World Energy Outlook — Central Electricity Authority
Statistical Review of World Energy — International Energy Agency
World Energy Outlook — International Energy Agency
59.x: The World Energy Outlook is published by the International Energy Agency in Paris. The Statistical Review of World Energy is published by the Energy Institute.
59.tq: Identify the publication whose publisher is correctly paired rather than swapping international agencies.

59.s:
Which of the following publications are associated with NITI Aayog?
1. India Energy Security Scenarios 2047
2. Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero
3. National Electricity Plan
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: NITI Aayog is associated with India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 and the 2026 Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero. The National Electricity Plan is a CEA report.
59.tq: Reject the statement that assigns a CEA publication to NITI Aayog.

59.s: The annual publication 'Energy Statistics (India)' is brought out by
o: Central Statistics Office, now the National Statistics Office (MoSPI)
59.x: Energy Statistics is published by the CSO, now the NSO under MoSPI (UPSC 2009; APPSC-GS 2019). CEA publishes installed-capacity reports and the National Electricity Plan, the IEA publishes the World Energy Outlook, and the Energy Institute publishes the Statistical Review of World Energy.
59.tq: Energy Statistics = CSO/NSO, MoSPI.

59.s: Which one of the following best illustrates the distinction between installed capacity and actual electricity generation in India?
o: Coal accounts for 6–10% of present electricity generation and over 50% of installed capacity.
Non-fossil sources account for about 22% of installed capacity but over 50% of electricity output.
Non-fossil sources account for over 50% of installed capacity but only about 22% of electricity output.
Solar curtailment ensures that installed capacity and generation remain equal.
59.x: Non-fossil sources constitute more than half of installed capacity, but their share in actual output is only about 22%, demonstrating the capacity-generation gap.
59.tq: Comparison-table reasoning: distinguish the capacity share from the generation share.

59.s: Approximately how much renewable-energy capacity is reported to have no power-purchase agreement (PPA)?
59.x: Around 40 GW of renewable-energy projects are reported to have no PPAs.
59.tq: Figure-based recall using nearby electricity-sector numbers as distractors.

59.s: NITI’s long-term projection regarding coal’s share in India’s electricity generation envisages that it may fall from about 74% to:
59.x: NITI projects that coal’s share of electricity generation could decline from about 74% to 6–10% by 2070.
59.tq: Trend-and-end-point trap: match the starting share, projected range and target year.

59.s:
Assertion (A): An El Niño year can adversely affect wind and hydropower generation.
Reason (R): Variations associated with El Niño can reduce wind availability and hydrological conditions relevant to power generation.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
59.x: Both statements are true, and the reason explains why El Niño conditions can hurt wind and hydropower output.
59.tq: Causal assertion–reason test linking a climate phenomenon with two electricity sources.

59.s:
Which of the following developments is associated with the present electricity-sector debate?
1. Solar curtailment
2. Stranded gas-based power plants of approximately 25 GW
3. A gap between installed capacity and actual generation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: Solar curtailment, approximately 25 GW of stranded gas plants and the capacity-versus-generation gap are all identified as important electricity-sector concerns.
59.tq: All-of-the-above option tests whether each listed criticism has been retained.

59.s: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are particularly relevant to the electricity system for:
o: Replacing all transmission and distribution networks
Meeting the evening peak in demand
Eliminating the need for power-purchase agreements
59.x: BESS is highlighted as a means of managing the evening peak in electricity demand, especially alongside variable renewable generation.
59.tq: Scenario application: identify the system role naturally associated with storage.

59.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Initiative/feature)
 a. UDAY
 b. RDSS
 c. ICEP-2024 in Andhra Pradesh
 d. PM JANMAN through AP DISCOMs

List-II (Description)
 i. Electrification of 24,691 tribal households
 ii. Target of 160 GW of renewable energy
 iii. Debt takeover by the States
 iv. Results-linked infrastructure and reform grant

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
59.x: UDAY is associated with debt takeover, RDSS with results-linked infrastructure and reform grants, ICEP-2024 with the 160 GW renewable-energy target, and PM JANMAN with electrification of 24,691 tribal households.
59.tq: Start from the sure programme-feature pairs and eliminate codes containing a wrong match.

60.s: In a hydroelectric power plant, which sequence correctly represents the conversion of energy?
o: Electrical energy → potential energy → kinetic energy → mechanical energy
Potential energy → kinetic energy → mechanical energy of turbine → electrical energy
Kinetic energy → chemical energy → mechanical energy → electrical energy
Mechanical energy → potential energy → thermal energy → electrical energy
60.x: Stored water has potential energy; falling water gains kinetic energy, turns the turbine through mechanical energy, and the generator produces electricity by electromagnetic induction.
60.tq: Follow the physical sequence from stored water to turbine motion and then generation.

60.s: A hydroelectric plant uses stored water in a reservoir, whose release can be regulated to meet changing electricity demand. Such a plant is classified as a:
60.x: A storage or reservoir plant uses a dam to store water and regulate power output.
60.tq: Identify the plant type from its operational feature rather than from its energy source.

60.s: Which of the following correctly describes a run-of-the-river hydroelectric plant?
o: It requires a very large reservoir and completely changes the watercourse.
It operates only with nuclear-generated electricity.
It uses natural river flow with little or no storage and does not require a large dam or reservoir.
It stores surplus electricity by pumping water uphill.
60.x: Run-of-the-river plants use the natural flow of water with little or no storage and require no large dam or reservoir.
60.tq: Distinguish run-of-the-river generation from reservoir and pumped-storage systems.

60.s: Pumped-storage hydropower functions most appropriately as which of the following?
o: A run-of-the-river system that avoids all storage
A thermal plant that converts coal directly into electricity
A grid battery that stores surplus power by pumping water uphill and releases it during peak demand
A dam designed only for flood control and not power generation
60.x: Pumped storage uses surplus electricity to pump water to an upper reservoir and releases it during peak demand; it is regarded as a grid battery and a fast large-scale storage option.
60.tq: Infer the technology from the charge–discharge cycle and its grid function.

60.s: According to the classification specified for hydro projects, which statement is correct?
o: Small hydro means projects above 25 MW, while large hydro means projects up to 3 MW.
Small hydro means projects up to 25 MW, while large hydro means projects above 25 MW.
Large hydro is defined as projects between 3 MW and 25 MW only.
Both small and large hydro are limited to projects below 3 MW.
60.x: MNRE treats projects up to 25 MW as small hydro, while the Ministry of Power treats projects above 25 MW as large hydro.
60.tq: Discriminate between adjacent threshold categories using the exact numerical cutoff.

60.s: Which sequence correctly represents the change in the small-hydro threshold mentioned in the policy history?
o: Up to 25 MW in 1989 and up to 3 MW in November 1999
Up to 3 MW in 1989 and up to 25 MW in November 1999
Up to 3 MW in 1999 and up to 25 MW in 2005
Up to 25 MW in 1989 and above 25 MW in November 1999
60.x: Small hydro plants up to 3 MW were transferred to MNRE in 1989, and the ceiling was raised to 25 MW in November 1999; today small hydro means up to 25 MW (MNRE) and large hydro above 25 MW (Ministry of Power). Options that reverse the two thresholds or dates are wrong.
60.tq: Arrange policy changes by date and verify the associated numerical threshold.

60.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the March 2019 large-hydro reforms?
o: Abolition of all renewable purchase obligations for discoms
Budgetary support for flood moderation and storage hydroelectric projects
Declaration of large hydro above 25 MW as renewable energy
60.x: The March 2019 package included renewable-energy status, tariff rationalisation and budgetary support; abolition of all renewable purchase obligations was not included.

61.x: Enrichment raises the share of U-235, the fissile isotope, by isotope separation; it does not increase U-238.
61.tq: Discriminate between the fissile isotope U-235 and the fertile isotope U-238.

61.s: Low-enriched uranium used in light-water reactors generally contains approximately:
61.x: Light-water reactor fuel is generally enriched to about 3–5% U-235. About 90% U-235 is associated with weapons-grade enrichment.
61.tq: Separate the reactor-fuel range from natural uranium and weapons-grade enrichment values.

61.s: Which one of the following is NOT a nuclear fuel but may serve as a moderator, coolant or absorber in a reactor?
61.x: Graphite is a reactor moderator, not a nuclear fuel. U-235, Pu-239 and U-233 are fissile fuels.
61.tq: Find the non-fuel by separating reactor-support materials from fissile isotopes.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about hydrogen isotopes:
1. Deuterium contains one proton and one neutron.
2. Tritium is produced by bombarding lithium with neutrons.
3. Tritium is a stable isotope and does not emit beta particles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is correct: deuterium (heavy hydrogen, stable) has 1 proton and 1 neutron. Statement 2 is correct: tritium (1 proton + 2 neutrons) is made by bombarding lithium with neutrons. Statement 3 is wrong: tritium is radioactive, a beta emitter with a half-life of 12.3 years. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '2 and 3 only', '1 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' all wrongly include statement 3.
61.tq: Deuterium is stable; tritium is radioactive (beta, 12.3 years) and bred from lithium.

61.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes nuclear fission from nuclear fusion?
o: Fission joins light nuclei, whereas fusion splits heavy nuclei.
Fission splits a heavy nucleus, whereas fusion joins two light nuclei.
Both fission and fusion involve only chemical changes.
Both processes require the same temperature and pressure conditions.
61.x: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus, while fusion is the joining of two light nuclei.
61.tq: Use the reversed-process trap to distinguish splitting from joining.

61.s: In the fission of U-235, the principal products and released particles represented in the simplified reaction are:
o: Thorium, radium and alpha particles only
61.x: The simplified U-235 fission reaction produces barium, krypton and approximately 2–3 neutrons, along with energy.
61.tq: Identify the option containing the characteristic fission fragments and neutrons.

61.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nuclear fission occurs in present-day nuclear power reactors.
2. Fusion occurs naturally in the Sun and stars.
3. Fusion-based electricity generation is already the source of all present nuclear electricity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. All present-day nuclear electricity is generated through fission; fusion power remains at the research-and-development stage.
61.tq: Check the present status of technology before accepting the broad claim about fusion electricity.

61.s: The minimum mass of fissile material required to sustain a nuclear chain reaction is known as:
61.x: Critical mass is the minimum quantity of fissile material needed to sustain a chain reaction.
61.tq: Match the quantity-related definition with the exact technical term.

61.s:
Consider the following statements comparing nuclear fission and nuclear fusion:
1. Fusion requires extremely high temperature and pressure.
2. Fission releases more energy per unit mass than fusion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is correct: fusion needs extremely high temperature and pressure, whereas fission needs a neutron hit and critical mass. Statement 2 is wrong: fusion releases more energy per unit mass than fission. Hence '1 only' is right; '2 only' and 'Both 1 and 2' accept the false statement 2, and 'Neither 1 nor 2' rejects the true statement 1.
61.tq: Fusion: harder conditions, bigger energy per unit mass.

61.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes an atomic bomb from a hydrogen bomb?
o: An atomic bomb uses thorium fusion, whereas a hydrogen bomb uses uranium moderation.
An atomic bomb involves uncontrolled fission, whereas a hydrogen bomb involves fusion initiated by a fission bomb.
An atomic bomb uses controlled fusion, whereas a hydrogen bomb uses controlled fission.
Both are based exclusively on chemical explosions.
61.x: An atomic bomb is based on an uncontrolled fission reaction. A hydrogen bomb uses fusion, with a fission explosion serving as the trigger.
61.tq: Separate the primary reaction from the triggering mechanism.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
61.x: The Hiroshima bomb, Little Boy, used U-235. The Nagasaki bomb, Fat Man, used Pu-239.
61.tq: Match the city, bomb name and fissile material as a three-part pair.

61.s:
Which of the following are emissions associated with radioactivity?
1. Alpha particles
2. Beta particles
3. Gamma rays
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
61.x: The principal emissions associated with radioactivity are alpha, beta and gamma radiation.
61.tq: Recognise the complete standard classification of radioactive emissions.

61.s: Alpha radiation consists essentially of:
o: A stream of neutrons and positrons
Electromagnetic waves of very high frequency
A helium-4 nucleus containing two protons and two neutrons
A stream of fast electrons only
61.x: An alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus containing two protons and two neutrons.
61.tq: Break the radiation into its particle composition before comparing penetration properties.

61.s: Which one of the following correctly matches radiation with its usual shielding requirement?
o: Beta — a few millimetres of aluminium
Gamma — a thin layer of aluminium only
61.x: Beta radiation can generally be stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium. Alpha is stopped by paper or skin, whereas gamma requires dense shielding such as lead or concrete.
61.tq: Use penetration order to reject swapped shielding materials.

61.s: The half-life of a radioactive substance is the time required for:
o: Its atomic mass to become zero
Its radiation to lose half its penetrating power
Half of its radioactive nuclei to decay
61.x: Half-life is the time required for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to undergo decay.
61.tq: Choose the definition involving nuclei, not the intensity or mass of the sample.

61.s:
Consider the following statements regarding radioactive series:
1. The uranium series begins with U-238 and ends with Pb-206.
2. The thorium series begins with Th-232 and ends with Pb-208.
3. The actinium series begins with U-235 and ends with Pb-207.
4. The neptunium series is a natural radioactive series.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the neptunium series is artificial.
61.tq: Find the exception in an otherwise standard list of natural decay series.

61.s: Radioactivity was discovered in 1896 by:
61.x: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896; its emissions are alpha, beta and gamma. Marie Curie later worked on radium and polonium, Rutherford classified alpha and beta rays and studied the nucleus, and Roentgen discovered X-rays (1895), not radioactivity.
61.tq: Becquerel 1896 = radioactivity; Roentgen 1895 = X-rays.

61.s:
Match List-I (reactor component) with List-II (function):
List-I: a. Moderator  b. Coolant  c. Control rods
List-II: i. Absorb neutrons and control the rate of the chain reaction  ii. Slow neutrons so that U-235 can undergo fission  iii. Carry heat from the core to make steam
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
61.x: Moderator (heavy water, light water, graphite) slows neutrons (ii); coolant (heavy water, light water, liquid sodium) carries heat to make steam (iii); control rods (boron, cadmium) absorb neutrons and control the rate (i). So a-ii, b-iii, c-i. 'a-iii, b-ii, c-i' swaps moderator and coolant; 'a-i, b-iii, c-ii' swaps moderator and control rods; 'a-ii, b-i, c-iii' swaps coolant and control rods.
61.tq: Moderator slows, coolant carries heat, control rods absorb.

61.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally used as a moderator in a nuclear reactor?
61.x: Heavy water, light water and graphite can act as moderators. Liquid sodium is used as a coolant in FBRs, not as a moderator.
61.tq: Find the component that belongs to coolant rather than moderator.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: BWR — light water as moderator and coolant
AHWR — no moderator and no coolant
61.x: A BWR uses light water both as moderator and coolant, with the water boiling in the core. PHWRs use heavy water, while FBRs use sodium and no moderator.
61.tq: Compare the moderator-coolant combinations across reactor types.

61.s: In a Pressurised Water Reactor or VVER, the coolant is:
61.x: PWRs and VVERs use low-enriched uranium fuel, light water as moderator and pressurised light water as coolant.
61.tq: Use the reactor acronym and its characteristic coolant together.

61.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Removal of control rods can allow the chain reaction to run away.
2. A runaway chain reaction increases the risk of meltdown.
3. A thermal reactor cannot function normally without a moderator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Control rods restrain the chain reaction, so their absence can cause a runaway reaction and meltdown risk. A thermal reactor also requires a moderator to slow neutrons.
61.tq: Link each safety statement to the role of the corresponding reactor component.

61.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Light Water Reactors is correct?
o: They use only natural uranium and heavy water.
They account for more than 85% of world nuclear power capacity and use light water as moderator and coolant.
They use liquid sodium and have no moderator.
They are restricted to India's Stage III thorium programme.
61.x: LWRs account for more than 85% of global nuclear capacity and use light water for both moderation and cooling. India is prioritising them for rapid capacity addition.
61.tq: Combine the global share with the defining reactor characteristics.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
61.x: Tarapur is associated with BWR technology, whereas Kudankulam uses VVER reactors.
61.tq: Use the reactor-technology pair to distinguish the two well-known sites.

61.s: The term 'criticality' in nuclear reactor operation refers to:
o: boiling of coolant outside the reactor core
conversion of all uranium into plutonium
61.x: Criticality is the condition in which the nuclear chain reaction sustains itself.
61.tq: Discriminate between critical mass, criticality and reactor overheating.

61.s: Xenon-135 is called a nuclear poison because it:
o: converts light water into heavy water
acts as a moderator in every reactor
61.x: Xenon-135 absorbs neutrons and can therefore affect the reactivity of a nuclear reactor.
61.tq: Identify the effect associated with the specialised term 'nuclear poison'.

61.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of India's three-stage nuclear power programme?
61.x: India's programme begins with PHWRs using natural uranium, proceeds to FBRs using plutonium-based fuel, and culminates in thorium-based AHWRs or other thorium reactors.
61.tq: Use the fuel-cycle sequence to identify the correct order.

61.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Stage I of India's three-stage nuclear programme:
1. It uses Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors.
2. Natural uranium is used as fuel.
3. Plutonium-239 is obtained from the spent fuel.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Stage I uses PHWRs with natural uranium. Its spent fuel yields Pu-239, which is required for the subsequent stage.
61.tq: Match each statement with the defining features of the first stage.

61.s: In the second stage of India's nuclear programme, the fuel known as MOX consists of:
61.x: MOX fuel used in the second stage consists of plutonium-239 and uranium-238.
61.tq: Split the options by identifying the fuel associated with FBRs.

61.s: Which one of the following statements about the second stage of India's nuclear programme is correct?
o: It uses liquid sodium as coolant and does not use a moderator.
It uses heavy water as both moderator and coolant.
It directly converts thorium-232 into electricity without an intermediate fuel.
It uses only natural uranium and produces no plutonium.
61.x: Fast Breeder Reactors use liquid sodium as coolant and do not require a moderator. They breed more plutonium than they consume, while a thorium blanket produces U-233.
61.tq: Use the reactor-component combination to distinguish FBRs from PHWRs.

61.s: The thorium blanket in a Fast Breeder Reactor is intended to produce:
61.x: Thorium-232 in the blanket is converted into uranium-233, an important fuel for the third stage.
61.tq: Trace the conversion of the blanket material into its product.

61.s: Who conceived India's three-stage nuclear power programme during the 1950s?
61.x: The three-stage programme was conceived by Homi J. Bhabha in the 1950s.
61.tq: Apply the person-and-contribution recall pattern.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about ANEEL fuel:
1. It combines thorium with HALEU and was developed by the US firm Clean Core Thorium Energy.
2. It can be used only in new fast breeder reactors, not in existing PHWRs.
3. It could hasten India's move to Stage III of the nuclear programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Statement 1 is correct: ANEEL is thorium + HALEU, from Clean Core Thorium Energy (USA). Statement 2 is wrong: it works in existing PHWRs (high-burnup tests done at Idaho National Laboratory). Statement 3 is correct: because it runs in PHWRs it could hasten Stage III. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' omits statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.
61.tq: ANEEL = thorium + HALEU in existing PHWRs: a shortcut to Stage III.

61.s: The Atomic Energy Act of 1948 primarily limited atomic energy in India to:
61.x: The Atomic Energy Act, 1948, limited the use of atomic energy to peaceful purposes.
61.tq: Identify the stated policy purpose without importing later legal changes.

61.s:
Assertion (A): Homi Bhabha's three-stage nuclear programme was designed to achieve self-reliance through a closed fuel cycle.
Reason (R): The programme was intended to overcome India's scarcity of uranium by making use of its abundant thorium resources.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
61.x: Both the assertion and reason are true. The need to overcome scarce uranium through abundant thorium underlies the programme's objective of self-reliance and a closed fuel cycle.
61.tq: Check whether the resource constraint directly explains the programme's strategic objective.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear-mineral resource position:
1. India possesses about 2% of the world's uranium.
2. India possesses about 25% of the world's thorium.
3. India is described as having the world's third-largest thorium reserves.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: India has approximately 2% of global uranium and about 25% of global thorium, and is described as having the third-largest thorium reserves.
61.tq: Retain the numerical shares together with the ranking.

61.s: Jaduguda and Tummalapalle uranium mines are operated by:
61.x: Both the Jaduguda and Tummalapalle uranium mines are run by Uranium Corporation of India Limited.
61.tq: Identify the organisation directly responsible for mining rather than reactor operation.

61.s: The approximate quantities of thorium and natural uranium available in India are:
o: 70,000 tonnes of thorium and 3,60,000 tonnes of uranium
3,60,000 tonnes of thorium and 70,000 tonnes of natural uranium
25,000 tonnes of thorium and 2,000 tonnes of uranium
61.x: The estimated quantities are approximately 3,60,000 tonnes of thorium and 70,000 tonnes of natural uranium.
61.tq: Compare the order of magnitude and avoid swapping the two resources.

61.s: Monazite is best described as a beach-sand mineral that is a source of:
o: Thorium and rare earths, along with phosphate and a small quantity of uranium
61.x: Monazite is a source of thorium and rare earths; it also yields phosphate and a small amount of uranium.
61.tq: Select the option retaining all the associated mineral products without the word 'only'.

61.s:
With reference to monazite in India, consider the following statements:
1. It occurs along the entire Indian coast without exception.
2. It is found in beach sands of Kerala and Odisha.
3. Only government bodies such as IREL may process and export monazite.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
