71.tq: Discriminate between closely related electricity-metering concepts.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the rooftop-solar targets announced in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The target is six lakh connections.
2. The target is 6,000 connections in each constituency.
3. A model solar village is proposed in every district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct. The announced targets include six lakh connections, 6,000 connections per constituency and one model solar village in every district.
71.tq: Check whether the numerical target and the geographical targets all belong to the same policy announcement.

71.s: Who announced the targets of six lakh rooftop-solar connections, 6,000 connections per constituency and one model solar village in every district of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission
The Chairperson of the Central Electricity Authority
71.x: Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar announced these rooftop-solar targets for Andhra Pradesh.
71.tq: Identify the responsible authority associated with a specific policy announcement.

71.s: The installed renewable-energy capacity of Andhra Pradesh is 10,639.75 MW. Which component-wise distribution is correct?
71.x: Andhra Pradesh had 10,639.75 MW of renewable-energy capacity, comprising 5,614.52 MW of solar and 4,397.67 MW of wind capacity.
71.tq: Match the component figures with their correct labels before checking the total.

71.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the broad evolution of electricity-related policy emphasis in India?
o: Prosumers → quality and discom viability → household connections
Household connections → quality and discom viability → prosumers
Household connections → prosumers → quality and discom viability
71.x: The emphasis moved from providing connections through DDUGJY and Saubhagya, to quality and discom viability through UDAY and RDSS, and subsequently to prosumers through PM Surya Ghar.
71.tq: Arrange the policy stages from basic access to system viability and then consumer participation.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the current electricity-sector position:
1. India's installed capacity was 509.74 GW.
2. Renewable energy accounted for 49.83 per cent of installed capacity.
3. These figures relate to November 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct: installed capacity was 509.74 GW and renewable energy constituted 49.83 per cent in November 2025.
71.tq: Link the quantitative values with the correct reference date instead of considering them in isolation.

71.s: Which of the following is identified as a continuing criticism of electricity distribution and rooftop-solar expansion?
o: Absence of renewable-energy potential and surplus loan availability
Weak discom finances, slow rooftop uptake and difficulties in accessing loans
Universal adoption of rooftop solar without financing constraints
Complete financial strength of all discoms and excessive rooftop adoption
71.x: The continuing concerns are weak discom finances, slow uptake of rooftop solar and difficulties in accessing loans.
71.tq: Select the option that combines all the stated challenges without reversing their direction.

71.s: Which village in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified?
71.x: Leisang in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified.
71.tq: Use the distinctive place-name association to distinguish the first/last fact from nearby locations.

72.s: The Solar Park Scheme was launched by MNRE on:
72.x: The Solar Park Scheme was launched by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy on 12 December 2014.
72.tq: Direct date recall using nearby scheme milestones as distractors.

72.s: An Ultra Mega Solar Park is defined as a solar park having a capacity of at least:
72.x: An Ultra Mega Solar Park has a capacity of 500 MW or more at one location.
72.tq: Discriminate the official threshold from the higher 1,000 MW figure.

72.s:
Consider the following statements about floating solar power in India:
1. India has an estimated floating-solar potential of about 102 GW.
2. The existing floating-solar capacity is approximately 0.7 GW.
3. Omkareshwar in Madhya Pradesh is associated with a 278 MW floating solar project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: India has about 0.7 GW of floating solar capacity against an estimated 102 GW potential, and the 278 MW Omkareshwar project in Madhya Pradesh is the largest identified project.
72.tq: Compare existing capacity, potential and the largest project without reversing units.

72.s: The subsidy mentioned for BC households consuming less than 200 units under the Andhra Pradesh rooftop programme is:
72.x: A subsidy of ₹20,000 is provided for 27.59 lakh BC households using less than 200 units.
72.tq: Direct recall of the subsidy amount with scaled distractors.

72.s: The estimated national potential of pumped storage projects is approximately:
72.x: The national pumped-storage potential is estimated at approximately 267 GW.
72.tq: Distinguish total potential from installed and operational components.

72.s: Which of the following correctly represents the national pumped-storage position?
o: 58 GW on-stream, 209 GW off-stream and approximately 7 GW installed
7 GW on-stream, 58 GW off-stream and 209 GW installed
267 GW on-stream, 7 GW off-stream and 58 GW installed
209 GW on-stream, 58 GW off-stream and 267 GW installed
72.x: The national potential includes about 58 GW on-stream and 209 GW off-stream components, while installed capacity is approximately 7 GW.
72.tq: Separate potential categories from the installed-capacity figure.

72.s: Andhra Pradesh opened 50,000 acres of barren land for solar leases primarily to:
o: replace all wind projects with nuclear projects
restrict private participation in solar generation
72.x: The barren land was opened for solar leases to avoid diversion of farmland for renewable-energy projects.
72.tq: Identify the policy rationale behind land-use decisions.

72.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW, which one of the following correctly represents the approximate shares of solar and wind energy, respectively?
72.x: Solar energy accounts for approximately 53% and wind energy for approximately 41% of Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW.
72.tq: Split the options by comparing the order and approximate shares of the two energy sources.

72.s: Ananthapuram-I Solar Park, with a capacity of 1,500 MW, is located at which place?
72.x: Ananthapuram-I Solar Park is located at NP Kunta in Ananthapuramu district.
72.tq: Direct location recall using nearby project locations as distractors.

72.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kadapa Ultra Mega Solar Park — Galiveedu
72.x: Ananthapuram-I Solar Park is located at NP Kunta, not Galiveedu. Galiveedu is the location of Kadapa Ultra Mega Solar Park.
72.tq: Find the swapped location among closely related projects.

72.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Tata Renewable hybrid project in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 800 MW wind at Kanekallu and no solar component
400 MW solar at Pathikonda and 400 MW wind at Kanekallu
400 MW wind at Pathikonda and 400 MW solar at Kanekallu
800 MW solar at Pathikonda and no wind component
72.x: The project comprises 400 MW of solar capacity at Pathikonda in Kurnool and 400 MW of wind capacity at Kanekallu in Anantapur.
72.tq: Separate the two equal capacities by their technology and location.

72.s: The 1,000 MW Ultra Mega Solar Park at Gani-Sakunala in Panyam mandal, once the world's largest single-location solar park, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
72.x: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park (1,000 MW) is at Gani-Sakunala, Panyam mandal, Kurnool (APPSC 2019). Ananthapuramu hosts NP Kunta, Talaricheruvu and Ramagiri; YSR Kadapa hosts the Galiveedu park; Nellore is not linked to these parks.
72.tq: Gani-Sakunala/Panyam = Kurnool UMSP, once world's largest

72.s: NTPC's 25 MW floating solar plant in Andhra Pradesh, operational by July 2022, is at:
72.x: The 25 MW floating solar plant is at NTPC Simhadri in Visakhapatnam (APPSC 2021). Omkareshwar (MP) is India's largest floating solar project (278 MW); Krishnapatnam has an APPDCL thermal plant; Ramagiri has the hybrid solar-wind park.
72.tq: AP floating solar = Simhadri (NTPC, 25 MW)

72.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Srisailam Right Bank hydel — APPDCL — Kurnool
72.x: Simhadri STPS at Visakhapatnam is operated by NTPC and has a capacity of 2,000 MW. Krishnapatnam is operated by APPDCL, while Dr NTTPS and Srisailam Right Bank hydel are associated with APGENCO.
72.tq: Match plant, operator and capacity while detecting swapped authorities.

72.s: The combined thermal capacity of NTTPS and RTPP under APGENCO is:
72.x: The combined APGENCO thermal capacity of NTTPS and RTPP is 4,210 MW.
72.tq: Distinguish a sub-total from broader generation totals.

72.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, which factor contributed to increased coal-related difficulty in power generation?
o: Abolition of transmission charges for coal-based power
Excess availability of high-quality coal within Andhra Pradesh
Replacement of all thermal plants by nuclear plants
Loss of coal mines, resulting in long-distance coal haulage and poor coal quality
72.x: Andhra Pradesh lost its coal mines after bifurcation, causing long coal haulage and exposure to poor coal quality.
72.tq: Apply the stated cause-and-effect chain to an energy-sector situation.

72.s: Which agency functions as the State nodal agency for renewable energy in Andhra Pradesh and handles land, clearances and single-window facilitation?
72.x: NREDCAP is the State nodal agency for renewable energy and facilitates land, clearances and single-window services.
72.tq: Identify the agency by its functional responsibility.

72.s: APTRANSCO is associated with which of the following activities?
o: Operation of the Simhadri thermal power station
Transmission and 13 ongoing 400 kV works worth ₹3,698 crore
Preparation of solar park DPRs under MNRE
Energy conservation and efficiency certification only
72.x: APTRANSCO handles transmission and had 13 ongoing 400 kV works valued at ₹3,698 crore.
72.tq: Match the infrastructure agency with its sectoral responsibility and project figure.

72.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: NREDCAP — operation of all thermal power plants
72.x: NREDCAP is the renewable-energy nodal agency; it does not operate all thermal power plants. APGENCO and APPDCL are associated with State generation.
72.tq: Reject the exaggerated authority assigned to a specialised agency.

72.s: The agency primarily associated with energy conservation in Andhra Pradesh is:
72.x: APSECM is the agency associated with energy conservation.
72.tq: Direct agency-role recall with closely related energy bodies as distractors.

72.s: The 600 MW Kadapa renewable-energy project associated with SAEL is a current-relevance development under which policy framework?
o: Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023
72.x: The 600 MW SAEL project in Kadapa is identified as a development under the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 (ICEP-2024).
72.tq: Use the project-to-policy association and distinguish the State’s recent policy from older solar and green-hydrogen policies.

72.s: With reference to PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following figures represents the target number of farm pumps?
72.x: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh targets 2.93 lakh farm pumps. The figure of 32,000 refers to solar pumps installed earlier.
72.tq: Separate the target figure from the already-installed solar-pump figure before choosing the numerical option.

72.s: The policy of leasing barren land for renewable-energy projects is particularly associated with addressing which concern?
o: Declining wind speeds in coastal areas
Shortage of uranium for nuclear power generation
Excess generation from rooftop solar systems
72.x: Leasing barren land is suggested as a response to food-versus-fuel conflicts, since renewable-energy projects may compete with agriculture for land.
72.tq: Apply the stated policy response to the underlying land-use conflict rather than to a technical energy problem.

72.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Wind energy in Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy mix — approximately 41%
India’s solar capacity in June 2026 — 162.15 GW
Andhra Pradesh’s solar capacity in the cited comparison — 32,000 MW
Solar energy in Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy mix — approximately 53%
72.x: Andhra Pradesh’s solar capacity in the cited comparison was 5.6 GW, not 32,000 MW. The figure 32,000 refers to solar pumps installed earlier under the State’s renewable-energy initiatives.
72.tq: Find the mismatched numerical unit and distinguish capacity figures from the number of solar pumps.

73.s: Which one of the following best describes the environment?
o: The genetic composition of a species only
The geographical distribution of a single population
The physical structure of an organism
The surroundings and conditions in which organisms live
73.x: Environment comprises the surroundings and conditions in which organisms live. It includes interactions between biotic and abiotic factors and is never static.
73.tq: Use the precise definition rather than a narrower biological term.

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composite nature of the environment:
1. The physical component includes nutrients, water and air.
2. The biological component consists of organisms.
3. Chemical interactions include the carbon and nitrogen cycles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements correctly describe the physical, biological and chemical components of the environment.
73.tq: Check each statement against the three components of a composite system.

73.s:
The physical category of the environment consists of which of the following?
1. Lithosphere
2. Hydrosphere
3. Atmosphere
4. Microbes
73.x: Lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere constitute the physical category. Microbes belong to the biotic category.
73.tq: Separate physical components from living components.

73.s: Which of the following is included in the cultural category of the environment?
73.x: The cultural environment is man-made and includes social, economic and political aspects.
73.tq: Identify the man-made category rather than a natural component.

73.s:
With reference to habitat and environment, consider the following statements:
1. A habitat always has life.
2. A habitat is suited to a particular species.
3. An environment may exist even in the absence of life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: A habitat is a living place suited to a species, whereas environment is broader and may include conditions without life.
73.tq: Discriminate between two closely related ecological terms.

73.s: Which one of the following is NOT a primary function of the environment?
73.x: The primary functions of the environment are providing resources, assimilating wastes and serving as a habitat for biodiversity. Generating synthetic chemicals is not one of them (APPSC 2024 trap).
73.tq: Resources, waste assimilation, habitat - synthetic chemicals is the odd one out.

73.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. An ecological community consists of all populations of different species living in an area.
2. A biome is a large region defined chiefly by its population density and sex ratio.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: a community is all populations of different species in an area. Statement 2 is wrong: a biome is a large region defined by climate and dominant vegetation (rainforest, tundra, desert); density and sex ratio are population attributes. Hence '1 only'; the other options are wrong.
73.tq: Community = many species' populations together; biome = climate + dominant vegetation; density/sex ratio = population attributes.

73.s: Which one of the following represents the correct ecological order from the smallest to the largest level?
o: Organism → community → population → ecosystem → biome → biosphere
Organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere
Population → organism → community → biome → ecosystem → biosphere
Organism → ecosystem → population → community → biome → biosphere
73.x: The ecological order is organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome and biosphere.
73.tq: Check the hierarchy sequentially from the individual level upward.

73.s:
Which of the following gives the complete hierarchy of ecological organisation in the correct order?

1. Atoms
2. Molecules
3. Protoplasm
4. Cells
5. Tissues
6. Organs
7. Organisms
8. Populations
9. Communities
10. Ecosystems
11. Biomes
12. Biosphere
73.x: The complete sequence proceeds from atoms to molecules, protoplasm, cells, tissues, organs, organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, biomes and biosphere.
73.tq: Arrange the levels by moving from molecular organisation to global ecological organisation.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the biosphere:
1. It is absent at the poles, the highest peaks and the deepest oceans.
2. Fungal and bacterial spores occurring above 8,000 metres are dormant.
3. Energy enters the biosphere from the Sun, while nutrients are recycled within it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements correctly describe the limits and functioning of the biosphere. Solar energy enters the system, whereas nutrients undergo internal recycling.
73.tq: Combine three independent factual statements and identify the inclusive option.

73.s: The term 'ecology' was coined by
73.x: Ernst Haeckel coined the term 'ecology' (1869; the ecologists table gives 1866). Tansley coined 'ecosystem' (1935), Elton wrote Animal Ecology (1927) and Odum wrote Fundamentals of Ecology (1953).
73.tq: Haeckel - ecology; Tansley - ecosystem.

73.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes habitat from niche?
o: Habitat and niche are identical terms.
Habitat is the physical place, whereas niche is the functional role of a species.
Habitat is the functional role, whereas niche is the physical place.
A niche can be occupied by unlimited species with identical roles.
73.x: Habitat is the physical place or address of an organism. Niche is its functional role or profession in that habitat.
73.tq: Separate the address concept from the profession concept.

73.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. One habitat may contain many species.
2. All habitats are environments.
3. All environments are habitats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: A habitat is a particular physical place within the broader concept of environment. Thus, one habitat can contain many species and all habitats are environments, but all environments are not habitats.
73.tq: Spot the reversed universal statement in a definition-based question.

73.s: The fundamental niche of a species refers to
o: the actual range occupied after competition
the full range of conditions and resources it could use in the absence of other species
73.x: Fundamental niche is the potential range of conditions and resources available to a species when competition and other biological limitations are absent.
73.tq: Distinguish potential range from actual range.

73.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
73.x: Grinnell proposed the habitat niche concept in 1917. Elton is associated with the functional niche, while Hutchinson proposed the n-dimensional niche.
73.tq: Match proponents with the specific form of niche concept.

73.s: A koala, which feeds mainly on eucalyptus, is best described as a
73.x: A specialist uses a narrow range of resources. Dependence of the koala mainly on eucalyptus is an example of narrow niche breadth.
73.tq: Infer niche breadth from the range of resources used.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the ecological niche:
1. A niche is the functional role of a species in its habitat.
2. No two species occupy exactly the same niche.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: the niche is the functional role ('profession') of a species, set by habitat, food, reproduction and physical-chemical factors. Statement 2 is correct: a niche is unique to each species, so no two species occupy the same niche (APPSC 2022: both correct). Hence 'Both 1 and 2'.
73.tq: Niche = profession, and it is unique to each species.

73.s: Natality in a population is concerned with
o: the number of individuals dying in a population
the number of births in a population
the proportion of males and females in a population
the distribution of individuals among age groups
73.x: Natality means births in a population. Its rate may be expressed as the number of individuals produced per female per unit time.
73.tq: Match the population attribute with the process it measures.

73.s: Which of the following is NOT a population attribute?
73.x: Density, mortality, age structure and sex ratio are population attributes. Dominant vegetation is associated with the description of a biome.
73.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring ecological level rather than the population level.

73.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Mortality — births per female per unit time
Carrying capacity — number of predators only
73.x: Population density is the number of individuals per unit area. Mortality refers to deaths per unit time, while natality refers to births.
73.tq: Separate the basic population attributes by their measured quantities.

73.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
73.x: A triangular age pyramid indicates an expanding population. Bell-shaped and urn-shaped pyramids indicate stable and declining populations respectively.
73.tq: Compare the three age-pyramid forms with their population trends.

73.s: A population showing a J-shaped growth curve is characterised by
73.x: The J-curve represents exponential growth, expressed as dN/dt = rN, when resources are assumed to be unlimited.
73.tq: Associate the curve shape with the growth equation and resource condition.

73.s: The S-shaped growth curve of a population is associated with
o: logistic growth approaching carrying capacity K
73.x: The S-curve represents logistic growth, in which population growth slows as it approaches carrying capacity K; it is expressed as dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K.
73.tq: Distinguish logistic growth from exponential growth by the role of K.

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding r-selected and K-selected species:
1. Insects and weeds commonly show r-selected characteristics.
2. Elephants and humans commonly show K-selected characteristics.
3. K-selected species generally produce few large offspring and provide considerable parental care.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. r-selected species include many insects and weeds, whereas elephants and humans illustrate the K-selected strategy of fewer offspring and greater care.
73.tq: Combine examples with the contrasting reproductive strategies.

73.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Radiation is an abiotic component of an ecosystem.
2. Fire and gravity may function as abiotic factors.
3. Parasites and symbionts are abiotic components.
4. Topography and wind are abiotic components.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Radiation, fire, gravity, topography and wind are abiotic factors. Parasites and symbionts are living, biotic components.
73.tq: Use the living-versus-non-living test to identify the incorrect statement.

73.s: Which of the following correctly describes an ecosystem?
o: A biotic community and its non-living surroundings linked by energy flow and nutrient cycling
A group of abiotic factors independent of living organisms
A collection of animals without their physical surroundings
Only the plant community present in a geographical region
73.x: An ecosystem includes a biotic community and its non-living environment, connected through energy flow and nutrient cycling.
73.tq: Select the option containing both the living community and its physical environment.

73.s: Arthur Tansley defined an ecosystem in 1935 as a system resulting from the integration of which of the following?
o: Only the physical and chemical components of an area
All food chains present in a biome
Only the living organisms of a habitat
All living and non-living factors of the environment
73.x: In 1935, Arthur Tansley described an ecosystem as a system resulting from the integration of all living and non-living factors of the environment.
73.tq: Test the precise wording of a definition along with its associated year and scientist.

73.s:
Which of the following is included in the structural aspect of an ecosystem?

1. Biotic community
2. Abiotic materials
3. Species composition
4. Trophic levels

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Ecosystem structure includes the biotic community, abiotic materials, species composition and trophic levels. Energy flow and nutrient cycling are functional aspects.
73.tq: Separate structural components from ecosystem processes before choosing the code.

73.s: Which one of the following represents a functional process of an ecosystem rather than its structure?
73.x: Nutrient cycling is an ecosystem function. Species composition, trophic levels and abiotic materials are elements of ecosystem structure.
73.tq: Discriminate between the structure and function columns of an ecosystem.

73.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the exchange characteristics of ecosystems and the Earth?
o: Ecosystems are open for energy and matter, while the Earth is open for energy but nearly closed for matter
Ecosystems are open only for matter, while the Earth is closed for energy
Ecosystems are closed for both energy and matter, while the Earth is open for both
Both ecosystems and the Earth are completely closed systems
73.x: Ecosystems exchange both energy and matter with their surroundings. The Earth receives energy from outside but is nearly closed with respect to matter.
73.tq: Compare open and closed characteristics across ecosystems and the Earth.

73.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the basic functional unit of ecology?
73.x: The ecosystem - a biotic community plus its non-living surroundings linked by energy flow and nutrient cycling - is the basic functional unit of ecology (APPSC PYQ). A population is one species in an area; a biome is a large climatic-vegetation region; the biosphere is the sum of all ecosystems.
73.tq: Functional unit of ecology = ecosystem.

73.s: An abiotic factor is best defined as which one of the following?
o: An organism that obtains food from dead organic matter
Any non-living component that affects organisms or their environment
A living component occupying the highest trophic level
A biological interaction between two species
73.x: An abiotic factor is any non-living component that affects organisms or their environment, such as light, temperature, water or soil.
73.tq: Use the precise definition rather than examples alone.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Type of abiotic factor)
(a) Climatic
(b) Edaphic
(c) Topographic

List-II (Examples)
(i) Altitude, slope and aspect
(ii) Light, temperature and rainfall
(iii) Soil texture, pH and minerals

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Climatic factors include light, temperature and rainfall; edaphic factors relate to soil; topographic factors include altitude, slope and aspect.
73.tq: Start from the meaning of edaphic and topographic before matching the remaining pair.

73.s: Liebig’s Law of the Minimum states that the growth of an organism is limited by which of the following?
o: The factor that changes most rapidly
The factor present in greatest quantity
The average value of all environmental factors
73.x: Liebig’s Law of the Minimum states that growth is limited by the nutrient or factor in shortest supply.
73.tq: Distinguish the minimum-law principle from the broader law of tolerance.

73.s: Which statement correctly expresses Shelford’s Law of Tolerance?
o: An organism is unaffected by excessive quantities of environmental factors
Only deficiency of a factor can limit an organism
Growth depends exclusively on the nutrient in shortest supply
Both too little and too much of an environmental factor can limit an organism
73.x: Shelford’s Law of Tolerance holds that both insufficient and excessive levels of an environmental factor can limit an organism.
73.tq: Separate the two limiting-factor laws by focusing on deficiency versus both extremes.

73.s: Abiotic factors may perform which of the following roles in determining the distribution of organisms?
o: They are always limiting and never enabling
They affect only the reproductive stage of organisms
They can be limiting or enabling factors
73.x: Abiotic factors can either enable the distribution of organisms or limit it when conditions fall outside suitable ranges.
73.tq: Apply the factor-distribution relationship rather than treating all abiotic factors as harmful.

73.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
73.x: Lions are tertiary consumers when they feed on other carnivores such as wolves. They are not primary consumers, which feed directly on producers.
73.tq: Check each organism against its usual feeding position and identify the reversed consumer level.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organism or group)
 a. Humans
 b. Saprotrophs
 c. Reptiles
 d. Camel

List-II (Characteristic)
 i. Cold-blooded
 ii. Desert-adapted
 iii. Feed on dead matter
 iv. Omnivores

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Humans are omnivores, saprotrophs feed on dead matter, reptiles are cold-blooded, and camels are adapted to desert conditions.
73.tq: Begin with the distinctive camel and saprotroph pairs, then complete the remaining matches.

73.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes macroconsumers from microconsumers?
o: Macroconsumers are phagotrophs, whereas microconsumers are saprotrophs.
Macroconsumers are abiotic, whereas microconsumers are biotic.
Macroconsumers manufacture inorganic nutrients, whereas microconsumers consume sunlight.
Macroconsumers are decomposers, whereas microconsumers are herbivores.
73.x: Macroconsumers, or phagotrophs, ingest food particles or organisms. Microconsumers, or saprotrophs, obtain nutrients by decomposing organic matter.
73.tq: Use the feeding mode—ingestion versus saprotrophic absorption—to distinguish the two groups.

73.s: Which of the following correctly represents producers in a terrestrial ecosystem?
o: Sulphur bacteria at deep-sea vents only
73.x: Herbs, shrubs and trees are the principal producers in terrestrial ecosystems.
73.tq: Match the producer group with its ecosystem rather than with an aquatic or vent environment.

73.s: In an aquatic ecosystem, the producer group includes
o: phytoplankton, algae, and submerged and floating plants
73.x: Aquatic producers include phytoplankton, algae, and submerged and floating plants.
73.tq: Identify organisms capable of primary production in water and exclude aquatic consumers.

73.s: The primary producers at deep-sea vents are chiefly
73.x: Chemosynthetic bacteria, including sulphur bacteria, use chemical energy rather than light at deep-sea vents.
73.tq: Apply the light-versus-chemical-energy distinction to a lightless ecosystem.

73.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Photoautotrophs — Chemical oxidation as the energy source
Chemoautotrophs — Sunlight as the energy source
Photoautotrophs — Green plants, algae and cyanobacteria
Archaea — All members depend on photosynthesis
73.x: Photoautotrophs use sunlight and include green plants, algae and cyanobacteria. Chemoautotrophs obtain energy through chemical oxidation, while many archaea are chemoautotrophic.
73.tq: Use the energy-source distinction to separate photoautotrophs from chemoautotrophs.

73.s: Chemoautotrophic bacteria inhabiting deep ocean trenches may obtain energy by oxidising which substance released from sea-floor cracks?
73.x: Chemoautotrophic bacteria in deep ocean trenches can use hydrogen sulphide released from cracks on the sea floor as an energy source.
73.tq: Direct recall of the specialised energy source used by deep-sea chemoautotrophs.

73.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nitrifying bacteria are examples of chemoautotrophs.
2. Many chemoautotrophic archaea, including methanogens, live in extreme habitats.
3. All archaea obtain energy through photosynthesis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Nitrifying bacteria are chemoautotrophs, and many chemoautotrophic archaea such as methanogens inhabit extreme environments. Statement 3 is false because archaea are not all photosynthetic.
73.tq: Use the absolute word 'all' as a warning, then verify the two positive associations.

73.s: Earthworms differ from decomposer bacteria and fungi chiefly because earthworms:
o: Fragment dead organic matter as detritivores
Occupy the producer level in every food chain
73.x: Earthworms are detritivores that fragment dead organic matter. Bacteria and fungi chemically decompose it into inorganic nutrients.
73.tq: Discriminate between physical fragmentation by detritivores and chemical decomposition by microbes.

73.s: Decomposers are regarded as a link between the biotic and abiotic components because they:
o: Convert dead organic matter into inorganic nutrients reused by producers
Prevent nutrient cycling in the soil
73.x: Decomposers release inorganic nutrients from dead organic matter, making them available again to producers and linking living and non-living components.
73.tq: Apply the link concept by tracing nutrients from dead organisms back to producers.

73.s:
Which of the following is the correct sequence of decomposition processes?

1. Fragmentation
2. Leaching
3. Catabolism
4. Humification
5. Mineralisation
73.x: Decomposition proceeds through fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.
73.tq: Arrange the decomposition stages in their process sequence.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about decomposition:
1. Bacteria and fungi act as decomposers.
2. Earthworms, nematodes and arthropods assist in decomposition.
3. Catabolism involves the action of enzymes produced by bacteria and fungi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Bacteria and fungi are the principal decomposers, while earthworms, nematodes and arthropods act as helpers. Bacterial and fungal enzymes carry out catabolism.
73.tq: Separate principal decomposers from their detritivore and enzyme-assisted roles.

73.s: The rate of decomposition is likely to be fastest under which of the following conditions?
o: Detritus rich in nitrogen and sugars, with a warm and moist climate
Detritus rich in chitin, with cold and dry conditions
Detritus rich in lignin, with low temperature and anaerobic conditions
Detritus poor in nitrogen, with persistent waterlogging
73.x: Decomposition is rapid when detritus contains nitrogen and sugars and the climate is warm and moist. Lignin, chitin, low temperature and anaerobic conditions slow it down.
73.tq: Identify the combination of favourable and unfavourable decomposition conditions.

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding food chains:
1. A grazing food chain begins with living green plants.
2. A detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter.
3. In a grazing food chain, energy captured by autotrophs is transferred to herbivores.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. Grazing chains begin with living producers, whereas detritus chains begin with dead leaves, remains or other dead organic matter.
73.tq: Test the defining starting point and energy-transfer direction of each food-chain type.

73.s: A food chain beginning with leaf litter and proceeding through earthworms to birds is classified as a:
73.x: A detritus food chain starts with dead organic matter such as leaf litter and proceeds through detritivores such as earthworms to higher consumers.
73.tq: Distinguish the two chains by asking whether the first component is living vegetation or dead organic matter.

73.s: In the sequence ‘tiger, grass, snake, frog’, which trophic level is missing?
73.x: Grass represents the first trophic level and the remaining animals are consumers. The second trophic level, occupied by herbivores or primary consumers, is absent.
73.tq: Locate the producer first and identify the absent feeding group between producer and carnivore.

73.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence in an aquatic food chain?
o: Zooplankton → phytoplankton → large fish → small fish
Large fish → small fish → zooplankton → phytoplankton
Phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → large fish
Small fish → phytoplankton → zooplankton → large fish
73.x: Phytoplankton are producers, zooplankton are primary consumers, and small and large fish occupy progressively higher trophic positions.
73.tq: Arrange the organisms from producer to successively larger consumers.

73.s:
Which of the following organisms occupies the first trophic level in an ecosystem?
1. Phytoplankton
2. Seaweeds
3. Green plants
4. Zooplankton
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Phytoplankton, seaweeds and green plants are producers and occupy the first trophic level. Zooplankton are primary consumers at the second trophic level.
73.tq: Separate producers from primary consumers before selecting the coded combination.

73.s: With reference to trophic levels, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: A trophic level denotes the functional position of an organism in a food chain.
Each species can occupy only one trophic level in every ecosystem.
A trophic level denotes the geographical location of an organism.
Decomposers always occupy the highest trophic level.
73.x: A trophic level is the functional position occupied by an organism in a food chain. A species may occupy more than one trophic level in different feeding relationships.
73.tq: Choose the precise definition and reject statements using absolute terms such as ‘only’ and ‘always’.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organism)
 a. Phytoplankton
 b. Zooplankton
 c. Carnivores
 d. Earthworms

List-II (Role)
 i. Primary consumers
 ii. Producers
 iii. Detritivores
 iv. Secondary or tertiary consumers

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Phytoplankton are producers, zooplankton are primary consumers, carnivores occupy higher consumer levels, and earthworms are detritivores.
73.tq: Start with the sure producer pair and then match the feeding roles of consumers and detritivores.

73.s: Which one of the following represents a grassland food chain mentioned in ecological examples?
o: Grass → grasshopper or rabbit → snake or hawk
73.x: A grassland chain begins with grass, followed by herbivores such as grasshoppers or rabbits, and then predators such as snakes or hawks.
73.tq: Read the chain from producer to herbivore and then to predator.

73.s: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a food web?
o: It excludes decomposers from energy relationships.
It begins exclusively with dead organic matter.
It contains only one pathway of energy transfer.
It represents interlinked food chains and provides alternative food sources.
73.x: A food web consists of interconnected food chains. It provides species with alternative food sources and generally improves the chances of survival.
73.tq: Identify the defining feature of a web—multiple interconnected feeding pathways.

73.s: Why is an ecosystem with a more complex food web generally more stable?
o: It has more alternative feeding pathways
It eliminates all competition among organisms
73.x: A complex food web provides alternative pathways for energy and feeding relationships, increasing ecosystem stability.
73.tq: Link structural complexity with redundancy and alternative pathways.

73.s: Which environmental stresses are specifically associated with disruption of food chains through coral bleaching?
73.x: Warming and ocean acidification can cause coral bleaching and disrupt marine food chains.
73.tq: Match the stated stressors with their marine ecosystem consequence.

73.s: In an ecosystem, the primary source of energy is
73.x: The Sun is the primary energy source for ecosystems. Producers capture solar energy through photosynthesis and transfer it to consumers.
73.tq: Use the direct source-identification approach and distinguish energy input from nutrient cycling.

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding energy flow in an ecosystem:
1. Energy flow is unidirectional.
2. Energy is cycled in an ecosystem in the same manner as nutrients.
3. Energy flow obeys the laws of thermodynamics.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Energy flows in one direction and obeys the laws of thermodynamics. Statement 2 is false because nutrients are cycled, whereas energy is not.
73.tq: Find the incorrect statement by separating energy flow from nutrient cycling.

73.s:
With reference to incident sunlight and photosynthesis, which of the following statements is correct?
1. Less than 50% of incident sunlight is photosynthetically active radiation.
2. Plants fix approximately 2–10% of photosynthetically active radiation.
3. Plants capture all incident sunlight for photosynthesis.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Less than 50% of incident sunlight is photosynthetically active radiation, and plants fix only about 2–10% of that PAR. Statement 3 is false because plants do not capture all incident sunlight.
73.tq: Reject the extreme statement containing 'all' and retain the two quantified facts.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about total primary production efficiency of an ecosystem:
1. It is the share of incoming solar energy that is captured and used in photosynthesis.
2. On average, it is about 10% of the incoming solar energy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: primary production efficiency is the share of incoming solar energy captured and used in photosynthesis. Statement 2 is wrong: on average it is only about 1-2%; 10% is the share passed between trophic levels (ten percent law). Hence '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
73.tq: 1-2% = solar energy fixed by plants; 10% = transfer between trophic levels. Do not mix them.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I
(a) Gross primary productivity
(b) Net primary productivity
(c) Secondary productivity

List-II
(i) New organic matter formed by consumers
(ii) Total organic matter made through photosynthesis
(iii) GPP minus producer respiration

Code:
73.x: GPP is the total organic matter produced through photosynthesis; NPP is GPP minus producer respiration; secondary productivity is new organic matter formed by consumers.
73.tq: Start from the sure pair linking secondary productivity with consumers.

73.s: Raymond Lindeman’s ten per cent law of energy transfer was formulated in
73.x: Raymond Lindeman formulated the ten per cent law in 1942. The law states that only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.
73.tq: Use the year-based numerical distinction among closely spaced values.

73.s: According to the ten per cent law, approximately what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
73.x: Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next level. The remaining approximately 90% is lost through respiration, excretion, locomotion and heat.
73.tq: Separate the transferred fraction from the much larger fraction lost at each trophic transfer.

73.s:
Assertion (A): Food chains generally do not extend beyond four or five trophic levels.
Reason (R): About 90% of energy is lost at each trophic transfer through processes such as respiration, excretion, locomotion and heat.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
73.x: Both statements are true, and the large energy loss at each transfer leaves insufficient energy to support many successive trophic levels. This explains why food chains are generally limited to four or five levels.
73.tq: Test whether the energy-loss statement directly explains the limited length of food chains.

73.s: Which one of the following ecosystems is generally the most productive in terms of net primary productivity per unit area?
73.x: Tropical rainforests are the standard highest-productivity ecosystem among the alternatives. Estuaries, coral reefs and swamps also have high productivity.
73.tq: Identify the standard high-yield answer while distinguishing productivity per unit area from total output.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about oceanic productivity:
1. Open oceans have low net primary productivity per unit area.
2. The total output of oceans can still be large because of their extensive area.
3. Oceans are necessarily the most productive ecosystems when productivity is measured per unit area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Open oceans have low productivity per unit area, but their enormous area gives them a large total output. Statement 3 is false because tropical rainforests and certain aquatic ecosystems are more productive per unit area.
73.tq: Watch the reversed comparison between total productivity and productivity per unit area.

73.s: Which of the following statements regarding ecological pyramids is correct?
o: The base represents top consumers and the apex represents producers.
The base generally represents producers and the apex represents top consumers.
Ecological pyramids have only two types.
All organisms occupy only one trophic level.
73.x: The base of an ecological pyramid represents producers and the apex represents top consumers. The three types are pyramids of number, biomass and energy.
73.tq: Use the structural rule of ecological pyramids: producers at the base and top consumers at the apex.

73.s: An inverted pyramid of numbers may also occur in
o: a forest floor litter chain only
73.x: Parasitic food chains can have fewer hosts supporting numerous parasites, resulting in an inverted pyramid of numbers.
73.tq: Recognise the host–parasite pattern as a standard exception to an upright number pyramid.

73.s: Why can the biomass pyramid in an aquatic ecosystem be inverted?
o: Fish do not consume zooplankton in aquatic ecosystems.
Energy increases at every aquatic trophic level.
Phytoplankton have a small standing crop but rapidly support larger zooplankton and fish biomass.
73.x: Phytoplankton have a small standing crop but reproduce and are consumed rapidly, allowing them to support a larger standing biomass of zooplankton and fish.
73.tq: Distinguish standing biomass from productivity and identify the fast-turnover producer explanation.

73.s: Which ecological pyramid can NEVER be inverted?
73.x: The energy pyramid is always upright because energy is lost as heat at every trophic transfer and cannot increase at higher levels.
73.tq: Look for the absolute exception and connect it with energy loss at each trophic transfer.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Pyramid)
a. Number
b. Biomass
c. Energy
List-II (Characteristic)
i. Always upright
 ii. May be inverted in aquatic ecosystems
 iii. May be inverted in a tree ecosystem

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
73.x: The pyramid of number may be inverted in a tree ecosystem, the biomass pyramid may be inverted in aquatic systems, and the energy pyramid is always upright.
73.tq: Start from the sure pair that energy is always upright, then match the two inversion cases.

73.s: Which one of the following is a limitation of ecological pyramids?
o: They always include decomposers at every trophic level
They place each species at several trophic levels simultaneously
They accurately represent every feeding relationship
They assume a simple food chain, although food webs are common in nature
73.x: Ecological pyramids assume a simple food chain and therefore do not adequately represent the complexity of food webs.
73.tq: Select the genuine limitation and reject statements that reverse the limitation.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about limitations of ecological pyramids:
1. A species cannot be placed at two trophic levels in a pyramid.
2. Saprophytes and decomposers receive no place in ecological pyramids despite their vital role.
3. Organism size is ignored in pyramids of numbers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Ecological pyramids cannot place one species at two trophic levels, generally omit decomposers and may ignore organism size; counting organisms is also difficult.
73.tq: Group the structural, decomposer and measurement limitations before choosing the code.

73.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes bioaccumulation from biomagnification?
o: Bioaccumulation is the rise of concentration across trophic levels, whereas biomagnification is accumulation within one organism
Bioaccumulation occurs only in apex predators, whereas biomagnification occurs only in producers
Bioaccumulation is the build-up of a pollutant within one organism over its life, whereas biomagnification is the rise in concentration at successive higher trophic levels
Both terms refer only to the accumulation of biodegradable pollutants in soil
73.x: Bioaccumulation is the lifetime build-up of a pollutant inside one organism. Biomagnification refers to increasing concentration at each higher trophic level.
73.tq: Discriminate between two closely related environmental terms by focusing on organism-level and food-chain-level accumulation.

73.s:
Consider the following pollutants:
1. DDT
2. Mercury
3. Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)
Which of the pollutants listed above can undergo biomagnification?
73.x: DDT, mercury and PCBs are persistent, fat-soluble and non-biodegradable pollutants, which are the characteristics favouring biomagnification.
73.tq: Use the common property shared by all listed pollutants to identify the inclusive option.

73.s: Which one of the following is the most appropriate set of characteristics of a pollutant that biomagnifies?
o: Radioactive, gaseous and readily converted into oxygen
Highly soluble in water, biodegradable and short-lived
73.x: Only persistent, fat-soluble and non-biodegradable pollutants are identified as biomagnifying pollutants in this context.
73.tq: Identify the exact qualifying characteristics rather than selecting a broad pollution-related description.

73.s: DDT contamination in an aquatic food chain is most directly associated with which of the following effects?
o: Thinning of bird eggshells and crashes in seabird populations
Thickening of bird eggshells and increase in seabird populations
Conversion of mercury into oxygen in seabirds
Immediate destruction of all aquatic vegetation
73.x: DDT causes thinning of bird eggshells and has been associated with crashes in seabird populations.
73.tq: Link a named pollutant with its characteristic ecological impact in an applied situation.

73.s: Methyl mercury is particularly likely to reach high concentrations in which of the following organisms?
o: Apex predators such as dolphins and orcas
Primary producers such as algae only
Organisms at the lowest trophic level only
73.x: Methyl mercury concentrates through the food chain and reaches high levels in apex predators such as dolphins and orcas.
73.tq: Use trophic-level reasoning to identify where a persistent pollutant reaches its highest concentration.

73.s: Minamata disease, first reported in Japan, was caused by biomagnification of which pollutant?
73.x: Methylmercury concentrated up the marine food chain and caused Minamata disease in Japan. DDT is linked to eggshell thinning in fish-eating birds; PCBs are another persistent biomagnifying pollutant but not the cause of Minamata disease; cadmium is not among the examples in the notes (it is associated with itai-itai disease).
73.tq: Minamata = mercury.

73.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Commensalism — Orchid growing as an epiphyte on mango
2. Parasitism — Cuscuta on a host plant
3. Amensalism — Penicillium inhibiting bacteria
4. Competition — Tiger and deer
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
73.x: Orchid on mango is commensalism, Cuscuta is parasitism and Penicillium inhibiting bacteria is amensalism. Tiger and deer illustrate predation, not competition.
73.tq: Find the swapped example by distinguishing predation from competition.

73.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
73.x: Neutralism denotes an interaction in which neither species is significantly affected, represented by 0/0. Amensalism is -/0, predation is +/- and commensalism is +/0.
73.tq: Discriminate closely related interaction signs.

73.s: The association between a fig tree and a fig wasp is an example of
73.x: The fig wasp pollinates the fig and obtains a breeding site, making the association a coevolved mutualistic relationship.
73.tq: Apply the benefit-benefit relationship to a specialised natural association.

73.s: Which of the following pairs is associated with sexual deceit during pollination?
73.x: The Ophrys orchid attracts bees through sexual deceit, thereby facilitating pollination.
73.tq: Test a distinctive feature of a coevolved pair.

73.s:
With reference to ecological interactions, consider the following statements:
1. Intraspecific interactions occur among members of the same species.
2. Interspecific interactions occur among members of different species.
3. Interspecific interactions can be beneficial, harmful or neutral.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Intraspecific interactions occur within a species. Interspecific interactions occur between different species and may have positive, negative or neutral effects.
73.tq: Build the answer by separating same-species and different-species relationships.

73.s: Competing species may coexist when they
o: avoid all interaction with other species
use different parts or forms of a shared resource
73.x: Resource partitioning permits competing species to coexist by using different portions of a resource, such as different parts of the same plant.
73.tq: Apply the ecological principle of resource partitioning.

73.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Lichen (alga and fungus) — Mutualism
2. Cattle egret feeding near grazing cattle — Commensalism
3. Large tree shading a small plant — Parasitism
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
73.x: Pair 1 is correct: in a lichen the alga and fungus both benefit (+/+). Pair 2 is correct: the cattle egret gains insects disturbed by cattle, which are unaffected (+/0). Pair 3 is wrong: a large tree shading a small plant is amensalism (-/0), not parasitism. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
73.tq: Lichen +/+, egret +/0, shading tree -/0.

73.s: A species whose effect on a community is far greater than would be expected from its abundance is called a
73.x: A keystone species has an ecological effect far larger than its abundance; its removal may cause the community to collapse.
73.tq: Use the defining phrase ‘effect far larger than abundance’ to identify a keystone species.

73.s: The sea star Pisaster ochraceus is regarded as a keystone species because it
73.x: Pisaster ochraceus is a keystone sea star that controls mussels in intertidal zones. This example is associated with the work of Robert Paine.
73.tq: Use the species–ecological effect association rather than the general definition alone.

73.s: Which one of the following is a foundation species?
73.x: Foundation species create or shape the habitat itself; corals and kelp are examples.
73.tq: Distinguish habitat-building species from charismatic and environmental-indicator species.

73.s: Lichens are commonly used as indicators of
73.x: Lichens can indicate environmental health and are particularly used as indicators of sulphur dioxide pollution.
73.tq: Match the indicator organism with the environmental condition it signals.

73.s: Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
o: Keystone species — effect much larger than its abundance
Umbrella species — attracts public support mainly through charisma
Foundation species — creates or shapes habitat
73.x: Attracting public support through charisma is the role of a flagship species. An umbrella species is wide-ranging, and its protection benefits many other species.
73.tq: Find the swapped definition among closely related conservation roles.

73.s: The ability of an ecosystem to withstand a disturbance is known as
73.x: Resistance is the ability to withstand disturbance. Resilience is the ability to recover after disturbance.
73.tq: Separate the two similar terms by asking whether the ecosystem withstands or recovers from disturbance.

73.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Resistance — Ability to recover after a disturbance
Resilience — Ability to withstand a disturbance without change
Homeostasis — Self-regulation through feedback within limits
Resistance — Permanent elimination of all ecosystem changes
73.x: Homeostasis is the self-regulatory capacity by which an ecosystem resists stress through feedback up to a limit. Resistance means withstanding disturbance without change, whereas resilience means recovery after disturbance.
73.tq: Discriminate the closely related terms resistance, resilience and homeostasis.

73.s: An ecosystem that returns to its earlier condition after a forest fire is displaying which property?
73.x: Resilience is the ability of an ecosystem to recover after a disturbance. Resistance, by contrast, is the ability to withstand disturbance without change.
73.tq: Use the disturbance scenario to distinguish recovery from resistance.

73.s: Which one of the following ecosystems is generally the most stable?
73.x: Diverse and complex systems such as rainforests are generally more stable than simple systems such as tundra, deserts and monoculture croplands.
73.tq: Use diversity and structural complexity as the basis of comparison.

73.s: An ecotone is best described as
o: the centre of a climax community
a region having no species interaction
a uniform stand of a single forest type
a transition zone where two communities or biomes meet and integrate
73.x: An ecotone is a transition zone between two biological communities or biomes, generally having intermediate conditions.
73.tq: Identify the transition-zone definition without confusing it with a single community.

73.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Uniform forest stand — ecotone between two communities
Estuary — fresh water and salt water interface
73.x: A uniform stand of one forest type is a single community, not an ecotone. Mangroves, estuaries and riverbanks represent the stated transition zones.
73.tq: Find the exception by rejecting a single-community area.

73.s: Which of the following correctly represents the habitat transition associated with a grassland ecotone?
73.x: Grassland is identified as an ecotonal region between forest and desert conditions.
73.tq: Discriminate among ecotone pairs by matching the habitat combination.

73.s: The edge effect refers to the phenomenon in which an ecotone generally has
o: fewer species than either adjoining community
only species from the larger adjoining community
more species and higher density of some species than either adjoining community
73.x: The edge effect is the increased number of species and increased density of some species in an ecotone. Such organisms are called edge species.
73.tq: Use the comparison with adjoining communities to identify the edge effect.

73.s: Which of the following statements about natural and artificial ecosystems is correct?
o: Artificial ecosystems develop without appreciable human influence.
Natural ecosystems are created and maintained exclusively by humans.
Natural ecosystems develop with little human influence, whereas artificial ecosystems are man-made.
Artificial ecosystems cannot contain producers or decomposers.
73.x: Natural ecosystems develop with little human influence. Artificial ecosystems, such as crop fields and urban parks, are created or substantially managed by humans.
73.tq: Compare the ecosystems by their degree of human creation and management.

73.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Artificial or man-modified ecosystem — crop field
73.x: Crop fields are artificial or man-modified ecosystems. Forests, oceans, lakes, deserts and grasslands are natural ecosystems, while a city is an extreme artificial example.
73.tq: Use the human-disturbance distinction to eliminate mismatched examples.

73.s:
Natural terrestrial ecosystems include which of the following?
1. Tundra
2. Forest
3. Grassland
4. Desert
5. Mountain
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Tundra, forest, grassland, desert and mountain are all terrestrial ecosystem types.
73.tq: Test completeness of a classification list.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Aquatic class)
a. Freshwater
b. Brackish
c. Marine
List-II (Salinity)
i. 35 ppt or more
ii. Less than 5 ppt
iii. 5–35 ppt

Codes:
73.x: Freshwater has salinity below 5 ppt, brackish water has 5–35 ppt, and marine water has 35 ppt or more.
73.tq: Start with the sure salinity pair and complete the classification.

73.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Freshwater — open oceans and shallow seas
Marine water — coral reefs and open oceans
Brackish water — estuaries and mangrove swamps
73.x: Open oceans and shallow seas are marine ecosystems, not freshwater ecosystems. Springs and rivers are lotic freshwater examples, while lakes and ponds are lentic examples.
73.tq: Find the reversed category-example pair.

73.s: Which forest ecosystem generally has the highest species richness on land?
73.x: Tropical rainforests have the highest species richness among terrestrial ecosystems.
73.tq: Use the characteristic feature directly associated with the ecosystem type.

73.s: Why is soil in tropical rainforests often thin and nutrient-poor despite high biological productivity?
o: There is no litter production in rainforests
Fast litter decay removes organic matter rapidly
Thick acidic litter accumulates for long periods
73.x: Rapid litter decay in tropical rainforests leaves the soil relatively thin and nutrient-poor.
73.tq: Link the ecological process of litter decay with its soil consequence.

73.s: Which one of the following correctly describes taiga or boreal forest conditions?
o: Slow decay, thick litter and acidic soil
Fast decay, thin litter and highly fertile soil
73.x: Taiga forests have slow decomposition, which produces thick litter and acidic soil.
73.tq: Contrast the taiga pattern with the opposite decomposition pattern of rainforests.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about mature forests:
1. They generally provide little net oxygen because respiration balances photosynthesis.
2. They remain important carbon sinks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
73.x: In mature forests, photosynthesis and respiration approximately balance with respect to net oxygen production, but the forests continue to function as important carbon sinks.
73.tq: Avoid the trap that equates low net oxygen production with low ecological importance.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about desert ecosystems:
1. Both hot and cold deserts have low precipitation.
2. The Thar occurs in western Rajasthan and Kutch.
3. Ladakh and the Gobi are examples of cold deserts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Low precipitation is common to hot and cold deserts; the Thar occurs in western Rajasthan and Kutch, while Ladakh and the Gobi are cold deserts.
73.tq: Test the common feature and the examples together rather than relying on one keyword.

73.s: Which of the following is NOT a typical adaptation of desert flora?
o: Broad, thin leaves that increase water loss
73.x: Desert plants commonly have deep roots, small or spiny leaves and waxy cuticles. Broad, thin leaves would generally increase water loss.
73.tq: Identify the option that contradicts the water-conservation principle.

73.s: Desert fauna such as camels, lizards, snakes and scorpions are commonly adapted by being:
73.x: Many desert animals are mostly nocturnal and possess water-saving adaptations.
73.tq: Connect the behavioural adaptation with the principal environmental constraint.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Grassland)
a. Prairie
b. Pampas
c. Veld
d. Downs

List-II (Region)
i. Australia
ii. South Africa
iii. North America
iv. Argentina/South America

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
73.x: Prairie is associated with North America, Pampas with Argentina or South America, Veld with South Africa and Downs with Australia.
73.tq: Start from the sure geographical pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong regional association.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about grasslands:
1. Steppe is the temperate grassland of Eurasia.
2. Savanna is a temperate grassland of Australia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: Steppe is the Eurasian temperate grassland. Statement 2 is wrong: Savanna is a tropical wet-and-dry grassland (e.g. Africa); Australia's grasslands are the Downs. Hence '1 only'; the other options are wrong.
73.tq: Savanna = tropical (Africa); Downs = Australia; Steppe = Eurasia.

73.s: Shola vegetation in India is associated with:
o: The Himalayan foothills of Assam alone
The salt marshes of coastal Gujarat alone
The Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
73.x: Shola consists of high-altitude grasslands and stunted forests in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
73.tq: Use the location-based identification method for a regional ecosystem.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the Terai grasslands:
1. They are tall wet grasslands.
2. They occur along the Himalayan foothills.
3. They are associated with Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Assam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Terai refers to tall wet grasslands along the Himalayan foothills, including areas of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Assam.
73.tq: Verify the habitat, location and state distribution separately.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the Banni grassland:
1. It lies in Kutch, Gujarat, at the edge of a salt marsh.
2. It is home to Maldhari pastoralists and the Banni buffalo.
3. Its main invasive threat is Lantana camara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: Banni is in Kutch, Gujarat, at the edge of a salt marsh, one of Asia's largest natural grasslands. Statement 2 is correct: it supports Maldhari pastoralists and the Banni buffalo. Statement 3 is wrong: the invasive threat named for Banni is Prosopis juliflora. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong.
73.tq: Banni = Kutch + Maldharis + Prosopis juliflora.

73.s: Which one of the following is a lentic ecosystem?
73.x: Lentic ecosystems contain still water, including ponds, lakes, pools, ditches and marshes. Springs, streams and rivers are lotic systems.
73.tq: Apply the still-water versus flowing-water distinction.

73.s: Which lake zone is characterised by shallow water, light reaching the bottom and rooted plants?
73.x: The littoral zone is the shallow edge of a lake where light reaches the bottom and rooted plants commonly grow.
73.tq: Match the zone with its physical features and vegetation.

73.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the profundal zone of a lake?
o: Deep, dark water below the limnetic zone with decomposers
Sunlit open water dominated by plankton
73.x: The profundal zone lies below the limnetic zone, is deep and dark, does not support photosynthesis, and is associated with decomposers.
73.tq: Use the vertical sequence of lake zones to identify the deepest zone.

73.s: A clear lake with low nutrient levels and abundant dissolved oxygen is classified as:
73.x: Oligotrophic lakes are nutrient-poor, clear and oxygen-rich. Eutrophic lakes are nutrient-rich and commonly experience algal blooms and low oxygen at depth.
73.tq: Match the trophic category with its nutrient and oxygen characteristics.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about eutrophic lakes:
1. They are nutrient-rich.
2. They may experience algal blooms.
3. They generally have high oxygen levels at depth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Eutrophic lakes are nutrient-rich and may develop algal blooms. Oxygen levels at depth are often low rather than high.
73.tq: Identify the reversed oxygen trend in the false statement.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about oceanic zones:
1. The disphotic zone is approximately 200–1,000 metres deep.
2. The aphotic zone is permanently dark and lies below approximately 1,000 metres.
3. The benthic zone refers to the open water column.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The benthic zone is the sea floor and its organisms; the open water column is the pelagic zone.
73.tq: Catch the swapped meanings of benthic and pelagic zones.

73.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the epipelagic zone?
o: The freshwater zone surrounding a lake
The permanently dark zone below 1,000 metres
The deepest part of the benthic region
The upper layer of the open water column containing the most marine habitats
73.x: The epipelagic is the upper layer of the pelagic, or open-water, zone and contains the greatest number of marine habitats.
73.tq: Move from the broad pelagic category to its upper sub-zone.

73.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes phytoplankton from zooplankton?
o: Phytoplankton are producers, whereas zooplankton are primary consumers.
Phytoplankton are primary consumers, whereas zooplankton are producers.
Both phytoplankton and zooplankton are decomposers.
Both are secondary consumers in marine food chains.
73.x: Phytoplankton form the producer base of marine food chains, while zooplankton generally act as primary consumers.
73.tq: Separate the producer and primary-consumer roles of similar-sounding groups.

73.s: Which one of the following does NOT belong to marine ecosystems?
73.x: Rivers are freshwater ecosystems. Coral reefs, hydrothermal vents and tidal zones are marine ecosystems.
73.tq: Find the freshwater item among marine ecosystem examples.

73.s:
Assertion (A): Coral reefs are called the 'rainforests of the sea'.
Reason (R): Coral reefs break storm waves and prevent coastal erosion.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
73.x: A is true: coral reefs are called the rainforests of the sea because of their very high species richness. R is also true: reefs break storm waves and prevent coastal erosion. But this protective role does not explain the 'rainforest' label, which rests on species richness. Hence both true, R not the explanation.
73.tq: 'Rainforests of the sea' = species richness; wave-breaking is a separate service.

73.s: An estuary is best described as a region where:
o: A freshwater lake is separated from a river by a dam
A river meets the sea and freshwater mixes with saltwater
Two tributaries join before entering a river
A glacier meets a river in a mountainous region
73.x: An estuary is formed where a river meets the sea, creating a transition between freshwater and saltwater.
73.tq: Use the precise definition rather than confusing an estuary with a lake or river confluence.

73.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the usual salinity gradient in an estuary?
o: 35 ppt upstream and nearly zero at the mouth
Uniformly zero salinity throughout the estuary
Nearly freshwater upstream and about 35 ppt at the mouth
73.x: Salinity generally increases from near-freshwater conditions upstream to approximately 35 ppt near the sea-facing mouth.
73.tq: Track the direction of the gradient and place the numerical value at the correct end.

73.s: Which of the following is NOT a climate-resilience function of mangroves?
o: Increasing the salinity of all freshwater lakes
73.x: Mangroves buffer cyclones and storm surges, reduce coastal erosion and store carbon. They do not increase the salinity of all freshwater lakes.
73.tq: Find the option that falls outside the stated group of ecosystem services.

73.s: Which of the following pairs of Indian estuaries is located on the west coast?
73.x: Narmada and Tapi are major west-coast estuaries. Hooghly, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery are east-coast estuaries.
73.tq: Separate the east-coast and west-coast groups before choosing the pair.

73.s: Which of the following is a coastal wetland rather than an inland wetland?
73.x: Lagoons, estuaries and mangroves are coastal wetlands. Lakes, marshes and floodplains are inland wetlands.
73.tq: Distinguish coastal and inland members of a classification.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about wetlands:
1. They moderate floods.
2. They help purify water.
3. They conserve biodiversity.
4. They store carbon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Flood moderation, water purification, biodiversity conservation and carbon storage are all important wetland functions.
73.tq: Recognise the full set of ecosystem services rather than selecting only one.

73.s: Wetlands in India are specifically protected under which of the following?
73.x: The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 provide the specific legal framework for wetland protection in India.
73.tq: Match the subject with the exact legal instrument and year.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ramsar Convention:
1. It was signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.
2. India became a party to it in 1992.
3. Threatened Ramsar sites are placed on the Montreux Record.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Convention was signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran (World Wetlands Day, 2 February, marks the signing). Statement 2 is wrong: India joined in 1982, not 1992. Statement 3 is correct: parties designate sites and practise wise use, and threatened sites go on the Montreux Record. So '1 and 3 only'; options including 2 are wrong.
73.tq: Ramsar 1971, India 1982, Montreux Record = threatened sites. Watch the swapped year.

73.s: According to the stated current figures, India has how many Ramsar sites?
73.x: India has 96 Ramsar sites, whose fauna ZSI has documented at 8,213 species. India joined the Ramsar Convention (signed 1971 at Ramsar, Iran) in 1982.
73.tq: Handle a current numerical fact by distinguishing nearby counts.

73.s: World Wetlands Day is observed every year on
73.x: World Wetlands Day is on 2 February, the date the Ramsar Convention was signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran. 22 March is World Water Day, 5 June World Environment Day and 17 June the World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought.
73.tq: 2 Feb = Ramsar signing date.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about plant adaptations:
1. Halophytes of saline soils and mangroves show pneumatophores, vivipary and salt glands.
2. Hydrophytes show a thick cuticle, sunken stomata and CAM.
3. Hydrophytes show aerenchyma, reduced roots and floating leaves.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: halophytes (e.g. Rhizophora) have pneumatophores, vivipary and salt glands. Statement 2 is wrong: thick cuticle, sunken stomata and CAM are xerophyte (desert) features; hydrophytes have a thin cuticle. Statement 3 is correct: aerenchyma, reduced roots and floating leaves mark hydrophytes (Hydrilla, lotus). So '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 are wrong.
73.tq: Water plant = thin cuticle + air tissue; desert plant = thick cuticle + sunken stomata + CAM; salt plant = breathing roots + vivipary.

73.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with xerophytes?
o: Thin cuticle and reduced roots for floating
Thick cuticle, sunken stomata, spines, succulence and CAM
73.x: Xerophytes are adapted to deserts through features such as thick cuticles, sunken stomata, spines, succulence and CAM; Opuntia is an example.
73.tq: Recognise the water-conservation package typical of desert plants.

73.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Rhizophora — halophyte
2. Opuntia — xerophyte
3. Hydrilla — hydrophyte
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
73.x: All three pairs are correct. Rhizophora is a salt-tolerant mangrove plant, Opuntia is a desert plant, and Hydrilla is an aquatic plant.
73.tq: Verify each organism against its habitat adaptation before selecting the coded combination.

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding halophytes:
1. They can tolerate salt spray and saline conditions around their roots.
2. Salt-excreting glands and succulent leaves are adaptations found in some halophytes.
3. Pneumatophores and vivipary are associated with adaptations of some mangrove plants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Halophytes tolerate saline conditions, and salt-excreting glands, succulent leaves, pneumatophores and vivipary are important adaptations found among estuarine and mangrove plants.
73.tq: Check each adaptation independently before selecting the combined code.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Site)
a. Kolleru
b. Pulicat
c. Coringa
d. Eastern Ghats

List-II (Description)
i. Mangrove-estuary and wildlife sanctuary in the Godavari delta
ii. Freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna deltas
iii. Dense tropical forests grading into thorn forests on the Rayalaseema plateau
iv. Brackish-water lagoon on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
73.x: Kolleru is the freshwater lake, Pulicat the brackish lagoon, Coringa the mangrove-estuary sanctuary and the Eastern Ghats the forest-to-thorn-forest transition region.
73.tq: Start with the distinctive Kolleru and Pulicat water types, then complete the remaining pairs.

73.s:
Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. It has a coastline of 1,053 km.
2. It has the second-largest mangrove ecosystem in India.
3. The major mangrove ecosystems occur in the Godavari and Krishna estuaries.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
73.x: Andhra Pradesh has a 1,053 km coastline and the second-largest mangrove ecosystem in India, concentrated in the Godavari and Krishna estuaries.
73.tq: Combine the numerical figure, rank and locations before selecting the code.

73.s: Pulicat is best described as a:
o: Mangrove-estuary wildlife sanctuary associated with marine turtles
Freshwater lake between two river deltas
73.x: Pulicat is a brackish-water lagoon on the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border and is associated with flamingos.
73.tq: Distinguish Pulicat from Kolleru and Coringa by combining water type with fauna.

73.s: Coringa is associated with which one of the following combinations?
