2. The Centre may give Environmental Relief Fund money to CPCB/SPCBs for restoration.
3. Penalty rates are now fixed in the Act itself rather than in rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: offences were decriminalised (penalty instead of imprisonment). Statement 2 is correct: Environmental Relief Fund money may go to CPCB/SPCBs for restoration. Statement 3 is wrong: rates were shifted to rules. Hence 1 and 2 only.
76.tq: Jan Vishwas = decriminalise + rates moved to rules; relief for death Rs 25,000 -> Rs 5 lakh.

76.s: The relief payable in cases involving death was raised to what amount under the Jan Vishwas-related amendment?
76.x: The relief for death was increased from ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh.
76.tq: Distinguish the revised figure from the earlier compensation amount.

76.s: The imprisonment term prescribed for offences under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 ranges from:
76.x: The Water Act provides imprisonment of 1.5 to 6 years. 'Up to 5 years' is the original Environment (Protection) Act penalty, often wrongly placed under the Water Act. 6 months to 3 years and 2 to 7 years are not the stated terms.
76.tq: Water Act 1.5-6 years; EPA up to 5 years + Rs 1 lakh.

76.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the institutional status of the CPCB?
o: It is a judicial body constituted under the National Green Tribunal Act.
It is a private regulatory organisation functioning without statutory authority.
It is a constitutional body under the Ministry of Finance.
It is a statutory body under MoEFCC and provides technical services to the Ministry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
76.x: The CPCB is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and also provides technical services to the Ministry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
76.tq: Identify the correct institutional status and parent ministry together.

76.s: Who nominates the chairperson of the CPCB and the chairperson of an SPCB, respectively?
76.x: The CPCB chairperson is nominated by the Central Government, while the SPCB chairperson is nominated by the concerned State Government.
76.tq: Compare the appointing authority at the Union and State levels.

76.s: Which one of the following is primarily a function of the CPCB rather than an operational function of an SPCB?
o: Inspecting individual industrial plants within the State
Granting consent to individual industries in the State
Analysing samples collected for State-level enforcement
76.x: Coordination of SPCBs is a CPCB function. Inspection, sample analysis and granting consents to industries are among the operational functions of SPCBs.
76.tq: Separate the coordinating role of the central body from field-level State functions.

76.s: For the purpose of environmental enforcement under the Environment (Protection) Act framework, which body is identified as the enforcement body?
76.x: The Central Pollution Control Board is identified as the enforcement body under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.
76.tq: Distinguish the pollution enforcement agency from other environment-related attached bodies.

76.s: Real-time air-quality information from the monitoring network is available through which application?
76.x: Real-time air-quality information is provided through the SAMEER app. SAFAR is a separate air-quality and weather forecasting system.
76.tq: Discriminate between two similarly associated air-quality applications.

76.s: The National Air Quality Index was launched in:
76.x: The National Air Quality Index was launched in 2015.
76.tq: Recall the launch year independently from the later NCAP target year.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):
1. It was launched in 2019.
2. It targets a 40% cut in PM10 by 2025-26 compared with 2019-20.
3. It covers 130 cities in 29 States/UTs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: NCAP dates from 2019. Statement 2 is correct: the target is a 40% PM10 reduction by 2025-26 vs 2019-20. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs (older notes say 131 cities). Hence 1 and 2 only.
76.tq: NCAP: 2019, 40% PM10, 2025-26, 130 cities, 24 States/UTs.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of the environment ministry:
1. The Department of Environment was set up in 1980.
2. It became the Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985.
3. The Ministry was renamed MoEFCC in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: Department of Environment, 1980. Statement 2 is correct: Ministry of Environment and Forests, 1985. Statement 3 is wrong: renaming to MoEFCC came in 2014. Hence 1 and 2 only.
76.tq: 1980 Department -> 1985 Ministry -> 2014 'Climate Change' added.

76.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
o: Central Pollution Control Board — statutory body
National Tiger Conservation Authority — established in 2005
Forest Survey of India — body unrelated to the Ministry
Central Zoo Authority — established in 1992 under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972
76.x: Option C is wrong: the Forest Survey of India is one of the bodies under MoEFCC (with BSI, ZSI and NTCA), not unrelated to it. CPCB is a statutory body under the Ministry, NTCA dates from 2005 and the Central Zoo Authority from 1992 under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
76.tq: Find the incorrect association among bodies connected with the Ministry.

76.s: Which of the following set consists entirely of bodies listed under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
76.x: The Botanical Survey of India, Zoological Survey of India and Forest Survey of India are listed among the bodies under MoEFCC.
76.tq: Identify the common institutional parent from a same-sector group.

76.s: Which of the following is a common requirement under both the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981?
o: Compulsory registration under the Water Cess Act
Declaration of every industrial site as an air pollution control area
Prior consent of the concerned Board to establish and operate a polluting unit
Prior approval of the National Green Tribunal for every industrial unit
76.x: Both Acts require prior consent of the Pollution Control Board for establishing and operating a unit that may cause pollution.
76.tq: Find the common legal mechanism rather than a feature belonging exclusively to one Act.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the consent mechanism for polluting industries:
1. Consent to Establish (CTE) is needed before setting up the unit.
2. Both CTE and Consent to Operate (CTO) are granted by the Central Pollution Control Board.
3. Consent to Operate (CTO) is needed before production begins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: CTE is the first stage, before setting up. Statement 2 is wrong: both consents are given by the State Pollution Control Board, not the CPCB. Statement 3 is correct: CTO is needed before production. Hence 1 and 3 only.
76.tq: Two-stage consent from the SPCB: CTE before setting up, CTO before production.

76.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Category)
 a. Red
 b. Orange
 c. Green
 d. White

List-II (CPCB score)
 i. 21–40
 ii. 20 or less
 iii. 60 and above
 iv. 41–59

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
76.x: Red corresponds to 60 and above, Orange to 41–59, Green to 21–40 and White to 20 or less.
76.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes with mismatched ranges.

76.s: Which category is associated with cement and petrochemical industries under the CPCB colour classification?
76.x: Cement and petrochemical industries are examples of highly polluting industries in the Red category.
76.tq: Connect representative industries with the highest pollution category.

76.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the White category?
o: CPCB score of 41–59; moderately polluting, with no regulatory oversight
CPCB score of 20 or less; practically non-polluting, with no consent or environmental clearance needed
CPCB score of 21–40; highly polluting, with mandatory annual consent
CPCB score of 60 or above; low polluting, with automatic clearance
76.x: The White category covers industries with a CPCB score of 20 or less and is described as practically non-polluting, requiring no consent or environmental clearance.
76.tq: Check both the numerical range and the regulatory consequence.

76.s: A new category introduced for essential environmental services, such as Compressed Biogas, is:
76.x: The Blue category was introduced for essential environmental services, with Compressed Biogas cited as an example.
76.tq: Recall the newly added category by linking it to its representative activity.

76.s: The colour categorisation of industries by the CPCB is primarily based on the pollution potential arising from:
o: Energy consumption, exports and tax contribution
Land area, workforce and annual turnover
Water availability, raw material cost and product demand
Emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated
76.x: The basis of the colour categories is the pollution potential represented by emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated.
76.tq: Identify the exact regulatory basis instead of choosing general industrial characteristics.

76.s: Under the consent reform introduced in January 2026, which of the following is correct?
o: A single application covers Air and Water consents as well as waste authorisations, and CTO remains valid until cancelled.
A single application is available only for mining projects.
Only waste authorisations are covered and CTO is abolished.
Separate applications remain compulsory and CTO expires annually.
76.x: The January 2026 reform provides for a single application for Air and Water consents plus waste authorisations, while consent to operate remains valid until cancelled.
76.tq: Apply the reform to a compliance scenario by identifying both its procedural and validity changes.

76.s: Which of the following best describes the statutory role of the AP Pollution Control Board?
o: It implements the Water, Air and Environment Protection Acts and specified waste-management rules in Andhra Pradesh.
It administers only the Wildlife Protection Act in Andhra Pradesh.
It functions exclusively as an appellate judicial tribunal for environmental disputes.
It regulates only municipal drinking-water supply and not industrial pollution.
76.x: The APPCB implements the Water Act, Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act, along with rules relating to hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste.
76.tq: Select the comprehensive but precise description and reject the exclusive-function distractors.

76.s: Which of the following is an additional regulatory activity of the AP Pollution Control Board mentioned in relation to industrial pollution control?
o: Approving Union Budgets for pollution control
76.x: The APPCB issues siting guidelines for industries and also prepares SOPs for marine outfall monitoring and hazardous waste.
76.tq: Identify a practical regulatory function rather than an unrelated governmental power.

76.s: Under the computerised inspection-allocation system used for ease of doing business, which industries are inspected more frequently?
o: All industries at exactly the same frequency
76.x: The system allocates inspections based on risk, with high-risk industries inspected more often.
76.tq: Apply the risk-based inspection principle to the practical scenario.

76.s: The power of Pollution Control Boards to levy environmental compensation under Section 31A of the Air Act and Section 33A of the Water Act was upheld subject to which limitation?
o: It may be exercised without any connection to actual or imminent harm.
It may be exercised only against government-owned industries.
It may be exercised only when environmental harm is clear or imminent.
It may be exercised only after a criminal conviction.
76.x: The power to levy compensation has been upheld, but its exercise must be connected with clear or imminent environmental harm.
76.tq: Apply the legal power to a fact pattern while checking the limiting condition.

76.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vanashakti v. Union of India case:
1. The Supreme Court held that administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006.
2. The ruling on retrospective environmental clearance was prospective.
3. Ex post facto environmental clearance may be granted in every case merely on payment of a penalty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: The Court held that administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006, and its ruling was prospective. Ex post facto clearance is not available in every case merely on payment of a penalty; Article 142 may apply only in fit cases.
76.tq: Find the false absolute statement using the phrase “every case”.

76.s: The Supreme Court in M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India recognised environmental protection as inherently included in:
76.x: The Court held that environmental protection is inherently included within Corporate Social Responsibility.
76.tq: Associate the case with the precise legal principle rather than a neighbouring constitutional concept.

76.s: The NGT suo motu notice concerning sewage in drinking water was issued to which group of States?
o: Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
76.x: The National Green Tribunal issued the suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh regarding sewage entering drinking water.
76.tq: Recall the exact geographical group attached to the reported action.

76.s:
Consider the following statements comparing the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981:
1. The Water Act aims to maintain and restore the wholesomeness of water.
2. The Water Act has 8 chapters and 64 sections, while the Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections.
3. The power to declare pollution control areas is a special feature of the Water Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Water Act aims to maintain and restore wholesomeness of water. Statement 2 is correct: Water Act 8 chapters/64 sections; Air Act 7 chapters/54 sections. Statement 3 is wrong: declaring air pollution control areas is the Air Act's special power; the Water Act's is standards for effluent discharge. Hence 1 and 2 only; 1 only leaves out a true statement.
76.tq: Control areas = Air Act; effluent standards = Water Act.

76.s: The Central Pollution Control Board is best described as:
o: A constitutional body created under the Environment Protection Act
A judicial body constituted under Article 21
A statutory body under the Water Act, also functioning under the Air Act, 1981
A temporary body established under the EIA Notification, 2006
76.x: The CPCB was established in 1974 as a statutory body under the Water Act and also operates under the Air Act, 1981. It sets standards and monitors air and water.
76.tq: Identify the correct parent statute and distinguish a statutory body from constitutional and temporary bodies.

76.s: Which legislation added air-pollution-related functions to the CPCB?
76.x: The Air Act, 1981 added air pollution functions to the CPCB, which had originally been constituted under the Water Act.
76.tq: Distinguish the parent legislation from the later legislation that expanded the Board’s functions.

76.s: Which combination correctly identifies the FIRST and the LATEST laws in India’s pollution-control legislative sequence mentioned below?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 and Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
76.x: The Water Act of 1974 is regarded as India’s first pollution-control law, while the National Green Tribunal Act of 2010 is the latest in the stated legislative chain.
76.tq: Use the first-and-last method to identify the chronological extremes.

76.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in which year?
76.x: The APPCB was set up in 1976 under the Water Act.
76.tq: Discriminate between closely related years associated with environmental institutions and laws.

76.s: Which one of the following preceded the Air Act in the stated institutional sequence of environmental regulation in India?
76.x: The Central Pollution Control Board was established in 1974, before the enactment of the Air Act. The APPCB was established later, in 1976.
76.tq: Identify the institution that came earlier by separating the central and State-level pollution-control bodies.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of EIA in India:
1. The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
2. Before the 1994 notification, environmental clearance was only an administrative decision.
3. The EIA Notification, 2006 replaced the 1994 notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The 1994 notification was issued on 27 January under the EPA, clearance had earlier been only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.
77.tq: Arrange the legal transition in sequence and verify both the date and the status of clearance before 1994.

77.s: The global origin of Environmental Impact Assessment is associated with the National Environmental Policy Act of the:
77.x: The global origin of EIA is associated with the United States National Environmental Policy Act, enacted in 1969.
77.tq: Pair the legislation, country and year precisely.

77.s: In India, the Planning Commission asked the Department of Science and Technology to examine river-valley projects during:
77.x: India's EIA process began in 1976-77 when the Planning Commission asked DST to examine river-valley projects.
77.tq: Distinguish the institutional beginning from the later first-use date.

77.s: The first use of EIA in India is dated in some accounts to 1978 for:
77.x: The first use of EIA in India is dated to 1978 in connection with river-valley projects.
77.tq: Associate the earliest year with the first project sector.

77.s: After river-valley projects, EIA scrutiny in India extended to large public-sector projects requiring clearance from the:
77.x: Large public-sector projects requiring Public Investment Board clearance became another early area of EIA application.
77.tq: Identify the institutional trigger associated with the early expansion of EIA.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Tool)
a. Environmental Impact Assessment
b. Life-Cycle Assessment
c. Cumulative Impact Assessment
d. Environmental audit

List-II (Scope)
i. Compliance check of an operating unit after the fact
ii. A product or process across its whole life cycle
iii. A project evaluated before it starts
iv. Combined effect of several projects in one area or basin

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
77.x: EIA concerns a project before it starts; LCA covers a product or process through its life cycle; cumulative impact assessment examines combined effects; and an environmental audit checks an operating unit after the fact.
77.tq: Start from the sure EIA pair and complete the one-to-one matching without repeating a scope.

77.s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
77.x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.
77.tq: Identify the level of decision-making before choosing between project and strategic assessment.

77.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes EIA from LCA?
o: EIA evaluates a product from raw material to disposal, whereas LCA evaluates only a project before construction.
EIA evaluates a project before it starts, whereas LCA evaluates a product or process across its entire life cycle.
EIA is concerned with policies and programmes, whereas LCA is concerned only with public hearings.
Both EIA and LCA are compliance checks conducted only after operations begin.
77.x: EIA focuses on the impacts of a specific project before it starts. LCA considers the impacts of a product or process across its whole life cycle, from raw materials through disposal.
77.tq: Separate the object and time frame of assessment rather than treating the tools as interchangeable.

77.s: The proposal for sector-wide EIAs is intended primarily to strengthen which approach?
77.x: Sector-wide EIAs are intended to incorporate strategic and cumulative perspectives, allowing impacts across a sector or region to be assessed rather than examining projects in isolation.
77.tq: Infer the broader assessment level from the phrase sector-wide.

77.s: Cleaner production is best described as a strategy that:
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
77.x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.
77.tq: Distinguish prevention at source from treatment after pollution is generated.

77.s: Which organisation’s mandate includes encouraging cleaner production technologies?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
77.x: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board’s mandate includes encouraging cleaner production technologies.
77.tq: Match the institutional mandate with the correct environmental body.

77.s: Green chemistry primarily involves designing products and processes that:
o: Reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances
Increase the use of hazardous substances for higher efficiency
Transfer all pollution from production to disposal
Avoid consideration of raw materials and solvents
77.x: Green chemistry seeks to design products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances. It addresses environmental impacts at the design stage rather than merely treating pollution later.
77.tq: Choose the preventive design objective instead of an end-of-pipe measure.

77.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Renewable feedstocks are associated with green chemistry.
2. Designing products for degradation is an example of a green chemistry principle.
3. Cleaner production relies exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
4. Both cleaner production and green chemistry seek to reduce impacts at the design stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because cleaner production is preventive and seeks process or input changes at the source rather than relying exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
77.tq: Reject the extreme word exclusively and combine the related design-stage principles.

77.s: The 12 principles of green chemistry were formulated by:
77.x: The 12 principles of green chemistry (prevent waste, atom economy, safer solvents, renewable feedstocks, design for degradation) were set out by Anastas and Warner in 1998. The Brundtland Commission (1987) defined sustainable development; Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring (1962); the Club of Rome issued Limits to Growth (1972).
77.tq: Green chemistry = 12 principles, Anastas and Warner, 1998.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the early stages of EIA:
1. Screening decides whether a project needs EIA and which category it falls in.
2. Scoping identifies the key issues and sets the Terms of Reference.
3. Scoping is the stage at which an expert committee evaluates the final EIA report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statement 1 is correct: screening decides need for EIA and category. Statement 2 is correct: scoping fixes key issues and Terms of Reference. Statement 3 is wrong: evaluation of the EIA report by the expert committee is appraisal, not scoping. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
77.tq: Screening = whether/which category; Scoping = ToR; Appraisal = expert committee.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the EIA process:
1. Baseline data represents a survey of the existing environment.
2. Impact prediction includes comparison of alternatives.
3. The Environmental Management Plan forms part of the mitigation planning process.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Baseline environmental conditions are surveyed, alternatives are compared during impact prediction, and mitigation planning includes an Environmental Management Plan.
77.tq: Combine three linked components of the impact-assessment stage.

77.s: Public consultation in the EIA process consists of:
o: A public hearing and written responses
Only written objections submitted to the Ministry
77.x: Public consultation includes both a public hearing and the consideration of written responses.
77.tq: Test the exact components of a formal procedure.

77.s:
Match the stage of EIA with what happens at it:
List-I (Stage)
a. Appraisal
b. Decision
c. Monitoring
List-II (What happens)
i. Environmental clearance granted with conditions or rejected
ii. Expert committee evaluates the EIA report
iii. Implementation of the Environmental Management Plan is checked
Select the correct answer:
77.x: Appraisal is evaluation of the EIA report by the expert committee (a-ii); Decision is EC granted with conditions or rejected (b-i); Monitoring checks EMP implementation (c-iii). Option B swaps appraisal and decision; C and D wrongly link the EMP to appraisal or decision.
77.tq: Appraisal = committee reads report; Decision = grant/reject; Monitoring = EMP.

77.s:
Arrange the following stages of EIA in the correct chronological order:
A. Appraisal
B. Screening
C. Decision
D. Scoping
77.x: The sequence is Screening, Scoping, Appraisal and Decision; public consultation occurs before appraisal.
77.tq: Use the first and last stages, then place the intervening steps.

77.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 introduced which major change in the basis for appraisal?
o: A shift from investment size to impact potential
A shift from public consultation to administrative approval only
A shift from project categories to product certification
A shift from impact potential to investment size
77.x: The 2006 notification shifted the test from investment size to impact potential and made clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
77.tq: Focus on the reversed comparison between the old and new bases of appraisal.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Category)
a. Category A
b. Category B
c. Category A clearance
 d. Category B clearance

List-II (Authority)
i. State Environment Impact Assessment Authority
 ii. State Expert Appraisal Committee
 iii. Expert Appraisal Committee at the Centre
 iv. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
77.x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC. Category B projects are appraised by the State EAC and cleared by SEIAA.
77.tq: Separate the appraisal authority from the clearance authority before matching the categories.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the EIA Notification, 1994:
1. Schedule I projects needed clearance from the Ministry of Environment and Forests.
2. Industrial projects above Rs 500 million were covered.
3. Two-stage (site and final) clearance applied to all mining projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per the 1994 notification. Statement 3 is wrong: two-stage site and final clearance applied to pithead thermal and valley projects, not to all mining projects. So options with 3 are wrong and 2 only leaves out a correct statement.
77.tq: 1994: Schedule I to MoEF, Rs 500 million, two-stage only for pithead thermal and valley projects.

77.s: The requirement of mandatory public hearing under the 1994 EIA framework was added through the:
77.x: Mandatory public hearing was added by the 1997 amendment to the 1994 framework.
77.tq: Separate the original notification from a later amendment.

77.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 was notified on:
77.x: The EIA Notification, 2006 was notified on 14 September 2006 and replaced the 1994 notification.
77.tq: Use the date-year pairing to reject close distractors.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, environmental clearance is compulsory for how many project categories?
77.x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
77.tq: Direct quantitative recall with nearby numerical distractors.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the EIA Notification, 2006:
1. It provides safeguards relating to air, water and land.
2. It includes safeguards for biodiversity and wildlife habitat.
3. It replaced the EIA Notification, 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The 2006 notification addresses air, water, land, biodiversity and wildlife habitat, and replaced the 1994 notification.
77.tq: Check whether all elements of a regulatory framework belong together.

77.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Categories B1 and B2 under the EIA Notification, 2006?
o: B1 projects are cleared by EAC, whereas B2 projects are cleared by MoEFCC.
B1 projects do not require EIA, whereas B2 projects require full EIA.
B1 projects require EIA, whereas B2 projects do not require EIA.
Both B1 and B2 projects always require full EIA by MoEFCC.
77.x: Category B1 projects require an EIA, while Category B2 projects do not; both are associated with state-level appraisal and clearance arrangements.
77.tq: Discriminate between the closely named B1 and B2 categories.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT a correct feature of Category A projects under the 2006 EIA framework?
o: They are appraised by the EAC.
They undergo screening before full EIA is considered.
77.x: Category A projects do not undergo screening; they always require full EIA, are appraised by EAC and cleared by MoEFCC.
77.tq: Find the single reversed feature in a category description.

77.s: Public consultation for scheduled projects under the EIA framework is described as:
o: Optional for all Category A projects
A process conducted only after environmental clearance
A single-stage consultation conducted only through written submissions
77.x: Public consultation is a mandatory two-fold process involving public hearing and written responses for scheduled projects.
77.tq: Recall the procedural structure rather than one component alone.

77.s: Who presides over the public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board?
77.x: The State Pollution Control Board conducts the hearing, while the District Collector presides over it.
77.tq: Use the authority-role distinction to avoid swapping institutions.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, the public-hearing notice must be given at least how many days in advance, and the hearing must be completed within what period?
77.x: The notice period is at least 30 days, and the hearing is to be completed within 45 days.
77.tq: Pair two procedural time limits without reversing their order.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about exemption from public hearing in the EIA process:
1. Defence, national-security and strategic projects are exempt, as their details are kept confidential.
2. B2 projects and units inside notified industrial estates are exempt.
3. Whether a project is 'strategic' is decided by the State Pollution Control Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct exemptions. Statement 3 is wrong: 'strategic' is determined by the Central Government, which is criticised as arbitrary; the SPCB only conducts the hearing. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
77.tq: Exempt: defence/strategic, B2, industrial estates; 'strategic' is the Centre's call.

77.s: Under the July 2026 amendment, if a State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to decide a proposal within 120 days, the proposal may escalate to:
o: The new Standing Committee on Environmental Impact Assessment on PARIVESH
77.x: The July 2026 amendment provides for escalation after 120 days to the new SCEIA through PARIVESH.
77.tq: Link the time limit with the newly designated authority.

77.s: Which of the following was a provision of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework?
o: The Centre may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays.
Scientists alone must replace all administrative members.
All Category B projects must automatically be transferred to the central EAC.
State committees may retain proposals indefinitely without escalation.
77.x: The amendment permits the Centre to remove members of EAC, SEAC or SEIAA mid-term for persistent delays. It also introduced an escalation mechanism rather than automatic transfer of all Category B projects to the central EAC.
77.tq: Identify the precise institutional power among reversed alternatives.

77.s: The principal criticism of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework is that it may:
o: Replace scientists with bureaucrats and prioritise speed over science
Give excessive control to local communities over scientific appraisal
Make every project subject to a full EIA
77.x: The amendment has been criticised on the ground that bureaucratic control may replace scientific expertise and that speed may be prioritised over scientific appraisal.
77.tq: Identify the stated criticism rather than the procedural detail.

77.s: PARIVESH is best described as:
o: A single-window portal for online environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances
A programme for preparing baseline biodiversity data
A committee for appraisal of Category A projects
77.x: PARIVESH is an online single-window platform for environment, forest, wildlife and Coastal Regulation Zone clearances.
77.tq: Distinguish a digital clearance platform from statutory bodies.

77.s: PARIVESH was launched in:
77.x: The PARIVESH portal was launched in 2018.
77.tq: Recall the launch year against years of major EIA notifications.

77.s: What is the correct expansion of the acronym PARIVESH?
o: Public Assessment and Regulation of Industrial Ventures for Ecological Safety Hub
Provisional Assessment and Review Interface for Vigilance in Environmental Statutory Hearings
Participatory Authority for Regional Impact Verification and Environmental Safety Headquarters
Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub
77.x: PARIVESH expands to Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub.
77.tq: Test the exact official expansion rather than a look-alike phrase.

77.s: PARIVESH 3.0 is associated with the use of:
o: Artificial intelligence in the clearance portal
Satellite launch technology for biodiversity mapping
77.x: PARIVESH 3.0 uses artificial intelligence as part of the upgraded single-window clearance system.
77.tq: Match the technology with the correct environmental-governance platform.

77.s: Which of the following correctly represents the backup arrangement referred to for environmental appraisal bodies in 2026?
o: NGT for SEIAA and NEAA for SEAC
SCEIA for SEIAA and SAEIA for SEAC
EAC for SEIAA and CPCB for SEAC
SAEIA for SEIAA and SCEIA for SEAC
77.x: The stated backup bodies are SAEIA in place of SEIAA and SCEIA in place of SEAC.
77.tq: Discriminate between the similar abbreviations by matching each backup body to its parent body.

77.s: Under the stated revised arrangements, the tenure of SEIAA, EAC and SEAC members is:
o: Four years, with a maximum of two terms and an age limit of 70
Five years, with unlimited terms and no age limit
Three years, with one renewal and a maximum age of 65
77.x: The tenure was raised to four years, with a maximum of two terms and an age limit of 70 years for members of SEIAA, EAC and SEAC.
77.tq: Combine tenure, term limit and age limit to avoid selecting a partly correct option.

77.s: The Draft EIA Notification, 2020 proposed which of the following?
o: Post-facto clearance through appraisal, penalties, compensation and remediation plans
A complete ban on environmental clearance after project commencement
Clearance based only on investment size
Abolition of public consultation for all projects
77.x: The draft proposed post-facto environmental clearance through appraisal, penalties, compensation and remediation plans. It was not finalised.
77.tq: Recognise the controversial proposal associated with the draft notification.

77.s:
Consider the following provisions associated with the Draft EIA Notification, 2020:
1. The public-hearing notice period was proposed to be reduced from 30 days to 20 days.
2. More projects were proposed to be moved to Category B2 or exempted.
3. Compliance reports were proposed to be submitted yearly instead of half-yearly.
4. Violations could be reported by any member of the public without restriction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The draft proposed a 20-day notice period, more B2 or exempt projects and yearly compliance reports. It restricted reporting of violations to the violator or government, so statement 4 is false.
77.tq: Locate the false statement by testing the reporting restriction.

77.s: Which statement regarding the Draft EIA Notification, 2020 is correct?
o: It was not finalised and was criticised for provisions including post-facto clearance.
It proposed longer public consultation periods than the 2006 notification.
It was finally enacted without modification.
It abolished penalties and remediation plans for violations.
77.x: The 2020 draft was not finalised and was contested, particularly for proposing post-facto clearance and shorter consultation periods.
77.tq: Reject absolute claims about a draft becoming final law.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about Supreme Court cases on environmental clearance:
1. Common Cause v. Union of India (2017) concerned mining in Odisha without or beyond environmental clearance and directed compensation equal to 100% of the value of illegally extracted minerals.
2. Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India (2024) examined the 2020 exemption from environmental clearance for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects.
3. In Noble M. Paikada, the Supreme Court upheld the blanket exemption as valid.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statement 1 is correct: Common Cause (2017) dealt with Odisha mining without or beyond EC and ordered compensation of 100% of the value of illegally extracted minerals. Statement 2 is correct: Noble M. Paikada (2024) examined the 2020 exemption from EC for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects. Statement 3 is wrong: the Court held the blanket exemption arbitrary, not valid. Hence 1 and 2 only.
77.tq: Common Cause = Odisha mining, 100% value; Paikada = ordinary earth exemption, held arbitrary.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Alembic Pharmaceuticals v. Rohit Prajapati:
1. It was decided in 2020.
2. The Supreme Court held that ex post facto environmental clearance was contrary to the EIA regime.
3. The 2002 Ministry of Environment and Forests circular permitting such clearance was quashed.
4. The Court necessarily directed closure of every project concerned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because compensation was imposed instead of ordering closure in every case.
77.tq: Find the wrong consequence in an otherwise case-specific statement set.

77.s: In its May 2025 ruling in Vanashakti v. Union of India, the Supreme Court described retrospective environmental clearances as:
o: a gross illegality and an anathema to environmental law
a mandatory feature of the EIA Notification, 2006
77.x: The May 2025 Vanashakti ruling characterised retrospective environmental clearances as a gross illegality and an anathema to environmental law.
77.tq: Recall the exact judicial characterisation used in a landmark ruling.

77.s:
With reference to the Vanashakti litigation, consider the following statements:
1. The May 2025 ruling struck down the 2017 Notification and the 2021 Office Memorandum.
2. In November 2025, the ruling was recalled by a 2:1 majority.
3. The recall relied, among other decisions, on D. Swamy (2021) and Pahwa Plastics (2022).
4. Approximately ₹20,000 crore worth of projects was reported to be at stake.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All four statements are correct. The May 2025 ruling struck down the specified instruments, was recalled in November 2025 by a 2:1 majority, relied on the cited earlier cases, and affected projects valued at approximately ₹20,000 crore.
77.tq: Track multiple stages of a case without confusing the original ruling with its recall.

77.s: The final Vanashakti verdict dated 29 July 2026 was delivered by a Bench led by:
77.x: The final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026 was delivered by a Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.
77.tq: Use the date-and-presiding-authority pair to separate successive rulings.

77.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026?
o: It retrospectively validated all clearances obtained under the 2021 Office Memorandum.
It prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, while earlier clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived.
It made the 2017 Notification available to all fresh violators seeking regularisation.
It permanently prohibited the Centre from issuing any time-limited notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
77.x: The final verdict prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, but earlier environmental clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived. It did not open those instruments to fresh violators or permanently bar time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
77.tq: Distinguish prospective effect, retrospective validation and future eligibility.

77.s: In the context of environmental clearance, which of the following is the correct general rule?
o: Prior clearance is required only for products assessed through LCA.
Environmental clearance is needed only after an environmental audit identifies non-compliance.
Prior environmental clearance is mandatory under the EIA framework, while post-facto approval is only a narrow exception.
Post-facto approval is the normal rule and prior clearance is optional.
77.x: The general rule under the EIA framework is that prior environmental clearance is mandatory. Post-facto approval, where recognised at all, is treated only as a narrow exception.
77.tq: Distinguish the governing rule from exceptional regularisation mechanisms.

77.s: According to the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026, any ex post facto environmental clearance must satisfy the test of:
o: Article 252 read with the Water Act, 1974
Article 323B read with the NGT Act, 2010
77.x: The Court held that ex post facto EC must meet Articles 14 and 21 (a proportionality test), while the Supreme Court keeps its power under Article 142. Articles 48A and 51A(g) are a Directive Principle and a Fundamental Duty, not the test laid down. Article 252 is the Water Act's basis; Article 323B concerns tribunals generally.
77.tq: Vanashakti 2026: Arts 14 + 21 test; Art 142 reserved for the SC.

77.s: The time limit prescribed in the August 2023 direction for the Border Roads Organisation to plant the trees was:
77.x: The NGT directed the plantation of the trees within one month.
77.tq: Separate the quantity of the direction from its compliance period.

77.s: In 2022, the National Green Tribunal imposed fines on states in connection with waste mismanagement. Which pair was specifically associated with such fines?
77.x: Maharashtra and West Bengal were cited as examples of states fined by the NGT for waste mismanagement in 2022.
77.tq: Match the environmental violation with the correctly associated states.

77.s: Which of the following correctly describes the NGT action concerning the LG Polymers incident at Visakhapatnam?
o: It transferred the matter to the National Environment Appellate Authority without any financial direction.
It took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
It ordered a permanent ban on all chemical industries in Andhra Pradesh.
It directed the Border Roads Organisation to undertake plantation in Uttarakhand.
77.x: Following the Visakhapatnam styrene leak in May 2020, the NGT took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
77.tq: Match the authority’s action to the correct incident instead of confusing separate NGT orders.

77.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Great Nicobar project—High-Powered Committee on NGT directions
Sewage in drinking water—suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Styrene leak—Maharashtra and West Bengal waste-management fines
77.x: The styrene leak concerned LG Polymers at Visakhapatnam and led to an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore. Maharashtra and West Bengal were associated with fines for waste mismanagement.
77.tq: Find the swapped incident-and-state pairing.

77.s: The High-Powered Committee relating to the Great Nicobar project was set up pursuant to directions of the:
77.x: A High-Powered Committee was set up on the directions of the National Green Tribunal in relation to the Great Nicobar project.
77.tq: Use the ‘who directed the committee’ approach to distinguish environmental institutions.

77.s: The inter-state dispute concerning the Polavaram project primarily relates to submergence in:
77.x: The Polavaram inter-state dispute concerns submergence in neighbouring Odisha and Chhattisgarh and was raised before the Supreme Court.
77.tq: Identify the neighbouring states directly affected by the project’s submergence issue.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding criticisms of the Environmental Impact Assessment process:
1. EIA reports are often prepared by consultants paid by the project proponents.
2. There is no central baseline data bank for EIA purposes.
3. Emergency plans associated with projects may be weak.
4. Certain projects or situations may be exempted from public hearings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All four statements describe identified criticisms of the EIA process: proponent-paid consultants, absence of a central baseline data bank, weak emergency plans and exemptions from hearings.
77.tq: Test the complete set of criticisms by checking each statement independently.

77.s: Which one of the following has been suggested as a measure to address the criticism that EIA consultants may lack independence?
o: Transfer of EIA preparation entirely to project proponents
Permitting post-facto clearances as a routine measure
Creation of an independent EIA authority
77.x: An independent EIA authority has been suggested to improve the credibility and independence of environmental assessments.
77.tq: Match the identified institutional defect with the appropriate reform.

77.s:
With reference to environmental clearance issues in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Telangana approached the Supreme Court seeking a review of the EIA for the Indira Sagar Polavaram project.
2. The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board conducted a public hearing concerning a water aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage.
3. The Human Rights Forum described the draft EIA for the water aerodrome as error-ridden.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: All three statements are correct. Telangana sought Supreme Court review of the Polavaram EIA, while the APPCB hearing on the Prakasam Barrage water aerodrome drew criticism from the Human Rights Forum for an error-ridden draft EIA.
77.tq: Link the institution, project and criticism without confusing the two Andhra Pradesh examples.

77.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to EIA in chronological order:
A. Enactment of NEPA in the United States
B. First use of EIA in India
C. First formal EIA notification in India
D. EIA amendment creating SCEIA and prescribing a 120-day timeline
77.x: The sequence is NEPA in 1969, first use of EIA in India in 1978, the first formal notification in 1994, and the later amendment creating SCEIA with a 120-day timeline.
77.tq: Anchor the sequence using the earliest and latest dates first.

77.s: Post-facto environmental clearances have been criticised because they may become:
o: a substitute for baseline data collection before a project begins
the first stage of appraisal for river-valley projects
the design of the clearance system when violations are detected only after construction
a compulsory form of public hearing conducted before every project
77.x: The criticism is that post-facto clearances can become “the design” when state appraisal bodies identify violations only after construction has already occurred.
77.tq: Apply the criticism to the sequence of violation detection and construction.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: River-valley projects — first sector appraised in India
LG Polymers gas leak — Visakhapatnam, 2020 — National Green Tribunal
Great Nicobar EIA — absence of any baseline data collection
NEPA — first EIA law — United States, 1969
77.x: The Great Nicobar EIA was criticised for thin baseline data, not for the complete absence of baseline data collection. The other pairs are correctly matched.
77.tq: Find the overstatement by distinguishing thin or inadequate data from total absence of data.

78.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Ministry of Environment and Forests formed
B. Department of Environment created
C. Ministry renamed MoEFCC
D. Air-pollution functions added to CPCB by the Air Act
Select the correct sequence.
78.x: The correct sequence is Department of Environment in 1980, Air Act in 1981, Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985, and MoEFCC renaming in 2014.
78.tq: Place the dated institutional milestones from earliest to latest.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change:
1. It receives 0.07% of the Union Budget according to the stated current information.
2. It is the nodal agency for India’s NR7 biodiversity report.
3. It runs Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct according to the stated current information: the allocation is 0.07%, MoEFCC is nodal for India’s NR7 biodiversity report, and it runs Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan.
78.tq: Combine current institutional facts while checking each statement independently.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Pollution Control Board:
1. It was constituted in 1974 under the Water Act as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.
2. It was renamed CPCB by a 1988 amendment.
3. Its air-pollution functions were added by the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
4. It is a statutory body under MoEFCC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: air functions were added by the Air Act, 1981; EPA 1986 only widened its scope. So options including 3, and 1 and 2 only (missing 4), are wrong.
78.tq: CPCB: Water Act 1974 -> Air Act 1981 adds air -> renamed 1988 -> EPA 1986 widens scope.

78.s: The Chairman of the Central Pollution Control Board is:
o: The Secretary-General of the National Green Tribunal
A full-time chairman nominated by the Central Government
The Chairperson of the National Biodiversity Authority
A part-time member elected by the State Boards
78.x: The CPCB has a full-time Chairman nominated by the Central Government.
78.tq: Identify the appointing authority and full-time status precisely.

78.s: Which body is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework?
78.x: The CPCB is the body responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.
78.tq: Assign the enforcement function to the regulatory rather than adjudicatory body.

78.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to CPCB monitoring:
1. NAMP — National Air Monitoring Programme
2. RTWQMS — Real-time water-quality monitoring on the Ganga and Yamuna
3. PRANA — Daily National AQI bulletins
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
78.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong: PRANA is the portal tracking NCAP; daily bulletins come from the National AQI launched in 2015. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
78.tq: NAMP = air, RTWQMS = Ganga/Yamuna water, PRANA = NCAP tracker.

78.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated coordinating or supporting function of the CPCB?
o: Adjudicating appeals against orders of the Supreme Court
78.x: The CPCB coordinates SPCBs, provides technical help, supports research and training, and performs monitoring and regulatory functions. It does not adjudicate appeals against Supreme Court orders.
78.tq: Reject the judicial power wrongly attributed to a regulatory board.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about consents and powers of State Pollution Control Boards:
1. Consent to Establish is needed before setting up the unit.
2. Consent to Operate is needed before the unit is set up, while Consent to Establish is needed before discharge.
3. SPCBs can levy compensation under Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act where harm is clear or imminent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it reverses the two; Consent to Operate is needed before production or discharge. Statement 3 is correct: compensation can be levied under S.33A Water / S.31A Air where harm is clear or imminent. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 2 are wrong.
78.tq: Establish = before building; Operate = before production/discharge.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board:
1. It enforces the Water Act, Air Act and Environment Protection Act.
2. It enforces rules relating to hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste.
3. It issues siting guidelines and develops SOPs for marine outfalls and hazardous waste.
4. It promotes cleaner production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All four statements describe stated APPCB responsibilities, including enforcement, waste-management rules, siting guidance, SOPs and cleaner production.
78.tq: Test the full range of State Board responsibilities rather than only its core Acts.

78.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in 1976 under the authority of the:
o: Government of India under the Air Act, 1981
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
National Green Tribunal under the Water Act, 1974
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974
78.x: The APPCB was established in 1976 by the Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974.
78.tq: Combine the correct State authority, year and parent legislation.

78.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was distinctive because it provided for:
o: Strict liability for accidents involving hazardous substances
Establishment of the Central Pollution Control Board
78.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of accidents involving hazardous substances.
78.tq: Associate the predecessor law with its distinctive liability principle.

78.s: The National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 primarily provided for hearing appeals against:
78.x: The National Environment Appellate Authority heard appeals against environmental clearances.
78.tq: Distinguish the appellate authority’s subject matter from the NGT’s wider jurisdiction.

78.s: Which statement correctly describes the fate of the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995?
o: It was brought into force and remains the principal environmental tribunal law.
It was converted into the National Biodiversity Authority Act.
It was replaced by the Water Act, 1974 without repeal.
It was never brought into force and was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.
78.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was never brought into force and was repealed by the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
78.tq: Use the fate-of-legislation trap: enacted does not necessarily mean brought into force.

78.s: Which of the following statements about the NEAA is correct?
o: It was replaced by the NGT and its Act was repealed in 2010.
It was never concerned with environmental clearances.
It was converted into the CPCB in 1988.
78.x: The National Environment Appellate Authority was replaced by the NGT, and the National Environment Appellate Authority Act was repealed in 2010.
78.tq: Track institutional succession and the repeal year.

78.s: The NGT combines which two roles associated earlier with separate environmental institutions?
o: Original jurisdiction over environmental disputes and the appellate role of the NEAA
78.x: The NGT combines original jurisdiction over environmental disputes with the appellate role earlier performed by the NEAA.
78.tq: Link the predecessor authority’s appellate role with the NGT’s original jurisdiction.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status and powers of the National Green Tribunal?
o: It is a statutory body with powers similar to those of a civil court.
It is a constitutional body with powers exclusively of an administrative authority.
It is an executive body exercising only advisory jurisdiction.
It is a constitutional body established under Article 323B without civil-court powers.
78.x: The NGT is a statutory, not constitutional, body and possesses civil-court powers in matters within its jurisdiction.
78.tq: Discriminate between constitutional, statutory and executive bodies before considering their powers.

78.s: The establishment of the National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to which Fundamental Right?
o: Right to constitutional remedies under Article 32
78.x: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which is treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.
78.tq: Match the environmental entitlement with the relevant Fundamental Right.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Type of Bench)
 a. Principal Bench
 b. Zonal Bench
 c. Circuit Bench

List-II (Place)
 i. Jodhpur
 ii. New Delhi
 iii. Pune
 iv. Shillong
78.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi; Pune is a zonal bench location; and Jodhpur and Shillong are circuit bench locations.
78.tq: Start with the sure Principal Bench pair and then distinguish zonal from circuit locations.

78.s: Which one of the following is NOT a location of a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
78.x: Pune, Bhopal and Chennai are zonal bench locations. Shillong is a circuit bench location.
78.tq: Find the bench-type mismatch rather than merely identifying a place associated with the NGT.

78.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the Supreme Court within:
78.x: An appeal against an NGT order may be filed before the Supreme Court within 90 days.
78.tq: Use the exact statutory time limit and compare the middle numerical options carefully.

78.s:
With reference to the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. Its Chairperson is a retired judge of the Supreme Court.
2. It is bound by all the procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure.
3. It follows the principles of natural justice.
4. It is required to decide cases within six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, though it follows natural justice.
78.tq: Split the options by checking the procedural exception concerning the CPC.

78.s:
With reference to the composition of the National Green Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. It has a Chairperson who is a retired Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. It includes Judicial Members and Expert Members.
3. There are 10 to 20 Judicial Members and 10 to 20 Expert Members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: The NGT consists of a Chairperson who is a retired Supreme Court judge, along with Judicial and Expert Members, with 10 to 20 members in each category.
78.tq: Verify the composition by separating the chairperson, member categories and numerical range.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010.
2. The Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010.
3. The Tribunal started functioning in July 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act was passed on 2 June 2010. Statement 2 is correct: the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 (asked in APPSC 2018). Statement 3 is wrong: it started functioning in July 2011. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
78.tq: Act 2 June 2010 -> set up 18 Oct 2010 -> working July 2011.

78.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated purpose of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Relief and compensation for environmental damage
Conservation of forests and natural resources
Conducting elections to local bodies in environmentally sensitive areas
78.x: The NGT deals with environmental protection, conservation of forests and natural resources, enforcement of environmental legal rights, and relief and compensation for damage. Conducting local-body elections is not its function.
78.tq: Find the option outside the tribunal’s stated environmental jurisdiction.

78.s: According to the stated current information, the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal is:
78.x: Justice Prakash Shrivastava is identified as the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal as of 8 September 2026.
78.tq: Use the current office-holder without confusing the office with a former Supreme Court office-holder.

78.s:
Which of the following Acts is outside the scope of the National Green Tribunal as specified in its jurisdictional list?
1. Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
2. Forest Rights Act
3. Biological Diversity Act, 2002
4. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
78.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest Rights Act are outside the stated scope. The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 are covered Acts.
78.tq: Use exclusion testing to distinguish covered Acts from Acts outside the specified scope.

78.s:
Consider the following Acts:
1. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
2. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
3. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
4. Forest Rights Act, 2006
Which of the above are included among the Acts under which the NGT hears cases?
78.x: The Water Act, Forest (Conservation) Act and Environment (Protection) Act are included. The Forest Rights Act, 2006 is outside the NGT’s Schedule I list.
78.tq: Separate the included environmental statutes from the specifically excluded Forest Rights Act.

78.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Green Tribunal from the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: The NGT sets emission standards, whereas the CPCB awards compensation.
The CPCB hears appeals against NGT orders in environmental disputes.
The NGT adjudicates disputes and awards compensation, whereas the CPCB regulates, sets standards and monitors pollution.
Both bodies perform exactly the same adjudicatory and regulatory functions.
78.x: The NGT is an adjudicatory body that decides environmental disputes and awards compensation. The CPCB is a regulatory body that sets standards, monitors pollution and advises the Centre.
78.tq: Separate adjudication from regulation by asking who performs the job.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Biodiversity Authority:
1. It was established in 2003 under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
2. It is headquartered at Bengaluru.
3. The Biological Diversity Rules were issued in 2024, after the Act was amended in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NBA is headquartered at Chennai. Statement 3 is correct: the Act was amended in 2023 and BD Rules came in 2024. So options with 2 are wrong and 3 only leaves out statement 1.
78.tq: NBA: 2003, Chennai, Act 2002 amended 2023, Rules 2024.

78.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-tier institutional structure under biodiversity governance?
o: SBBs at the national level, NBA at the State level and BMCs at the district level
NBA at the national level, SBBs at the State level and BMCs at the local level
NBA at the local level, BMCs at the State level and SBBs at the national level
BMCs at the national level, SBBs at the local level and NBA at the State level
78.x: The three tiers are the National Biodiversity Authority at the national level, State Biodiversity Boards at the State level and Biodiversity Management Committees at the local level.
78.tq: Arrange the bodies by jurisdiction from national to local.

78.s: With reference to biopiracy, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Foreigners may access Indian bio-resources without approval if no patent is sought.
Foreigners require approval of the NBA to access bio-resources or traditional knowledge, and NBA approval precedes intellectual property rights on them.
Only local bodies can grant approval for foreign access to traditional knowledge.
NBA approval is required only after intellectual property rights have been granted.
78.x: Foreigners require NBA approval to access bio-resources or associated traditional knowledge, and such approval precedes the grant of intellectual property rights. Access and benefit-sharing with local communities is also an important safeguard.
78.tq: Apply the approval-sequence rule and reject options that reverse the order or shift authority.

78.s: Which of the following is NOT an initiative associated with the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board?
o: Implementation of the Namami Gange programme throughout Andhra Pradesh
Biodiversity parks on the flood plains of five polluted rivers
City Biodiversity Index in Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Kadapa and Tirupati
78.x: The City Biodiversity Index, biodiversity parks on the flood plains of five polluted rivers and the Gloriosa superba cultivation pilot are APSBB initiatives. Namami Gange is implemented by the NMCG.
78.tq: Find the option belonging to another environmental body rather than the APSBB.

78.s: Which one of the following bodies replaced the Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority (EPCA) in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas?
78.x: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), established under the CAQM Act, 2021, replaced EPCA in the NCR and adjoining areas.
78.tq: Use the replacement relationship and distinguish air-quality authority from water and biodiversity bodies.

78.s: The National Mission for Clean Ganga is the successor set-up to which body?
78.x: NMCG is the successor set-up to the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA), which was established in 2009 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
78.tq: Use the predecessor–successor relationship and distinguish river-basin institutions from pollution authorities.

78.s: The National River Conservation Plan covers pollution abatement in:
o: 16 rivers in 38 districts of the National Capital Region
38 rivers in 16 States outside the Ganga basin
16 rivers in 38 States outside the Ganga basin
38 rivers in all States within the Ganga basin
78.x: The National River Conservation Plan covers pollution abatement in 38 rivers in 16 States outside the Ganga basin.
78.tq: Keep the two figures attached to the correct units—rivers and States—and note the basin exclusion.

78.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: CGWA — Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act
78.x: NBA is associated with biodiversity governance, not the National Clean Air Programme. CAQM, CGWA and NMCG are correctly matched with their respective legal basis or programme.
78.tq: Find the body–function mismatch by separating biodiversity, air-quality, groundwater and river missions.

78.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Wildlife Institute of India — Dehradun
2. Botanical Survey of India — Kolkata
3. Forest Survey of India — Lucknow
4. G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment — Kosi-Katarmal, Almora
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
78.x: The Wildlife Institute of India is at Dehradun, the Botanical Survey of India is at Kolkata and GBPNIHE is at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora. The Forest Survey of India is also at Dehradun, not Lucknow.
78.tq: Find the wrong location by comparing institutes that are commonly associated with Dehradun and Kolkata.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institute)
a. Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History
b. Indian Institute of Toxicology Research
c. Central Marine Living Resources and Ecology

d. Zoological Survey of India

List-II (Location)
i. Kochi
ii. Coimbatore
iii. Lucknow
iv. Kolkata

Choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
78.x: SACON is located at Coimbatore, IITR at Lucknow, CMLRE at Kochi and ZSI at Kolkata.
78.tq: Start from the sure institute–location pair and verify the remaining pairs by elimination.

78.s: The Central Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE) is associated with which of the following?
o: A Himalayan environment institute at Almora
A toxicology research institute at Lucknow
A national deep-sea fauna repository named “Bhavasagara” at Kochi
A bird research centre at Coimbatore
78.x: CMLRE is associated with the “Bhavasagara” national deep-sea fauna repository at Kochi.
78.tq: Link the specialised function and distinctive name with the correct institute and location.

78.s: The Environmental Information System (ENVIS), now known as EIACP, is best described as:
o: A network of environmental-information centres of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
A statutory tribunal for environmental disputes
A pollution-abatement programme for rivers outside the Ganga basin
A biodiversity approval mechanism for foreign companies
78.x: ENVIS is the MoEFCC’s network of environmental-information centres and is now known as EIACP.
78.tq: Identify the institutional network by matching its function with the responsible ministry.

78.s: The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) is located at:
78.x: NEERI is at Nagpur. Lucknow hosts IITR (toxicology); Dehradun hosts WII and FSI; Coimbatore hosts SACON.
78.tq: NEERI-Nagpur, IITR-Lucknow, SACON-Coimbatore, WII/FSI-Dehradun.

78.s: The National Green Tribunal directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under which programme?
78.x: The NGT directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).
78.tq: Distinguish the air-quality programme from river-conservation and biodiversity programmes.

78.s: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 provide for financing of:
78.x: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 provide for financing CPCB and State Pollution Control Boards.
78.tq: Identify the recipient institutions rather than the ministry or tribunal associated with environmental governance.

78.s: In the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026, Guntur was ranked second in which category?
o: Metropolitan cities with more than one million population
78.x: Guntur stood second in the towns category of Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026, which covered 130 cities.
78.tq: Link the rank with the correct category and retain the survey’s city coverage as a numerical clue.

78.s: Which of the following best describes the criticism concerning the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
o: It has no statutory or administrative role in environmental information systems.
It is criticised only for transferring all functions to State governments.
It is criticised as overfunded and excessively centralised in implementation.
It is criticised as underfunded and siloed.
78.x: A stated criticism is that MoEFCC is underfunded and operates in silos.
78.tq: Select the precise criticism and avoid reversing the paired descriptors.

78.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the oldest national pollution body and the institution that replaced the NEAA?
o: NGT, established in 1974; CPCB, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1981; CAQM, established in 2010
CGWA, established in 1974; NMCG, established in 2010
CPCB, established in 1974; NGT, established in 2010
78.x: CPCB, established in 1974, is the oldest national pollution body. The NGT, established in 2010, replaced the National Environment Appellate Authority (NEAA).
78.tq: Pair the correct institution with its year and distinguish the pollution regulator from the appellate tribunal.

79.s: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at
79.x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar in Iran.
79.tq: Identify the treaty by its adoption place and year.

79.s: The Secretariat of the Ramsar Convention is located at
79.x: The Ramsar Convention Secretariat is located at Gland, Switzerland.
79.tq: Distinguish the treaty Secretariat’s location from other environment bodies’ headquarters.

79.s: Which of the following was among the first Indian sites designated under the Ramsar Convention?
79.x: Chilika Lake, along with Keoladeo National Park, was among the first Indian Ramsar sites, designated on 1 October 1981.
79.tq: Use first-in-sequence recall for national treaty-site facts.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Ramsar Convention?
o: Udaipur and Indore — India's first accredited Wetland Cities
Chilika and Kolleru — Wetland Cities accredited in 2025
Keoladeo and Loktak — first accredited Wetland Cities
Gland and Ramsar — Indian Wetland Cities
79.x: Udaipur and Indore became India's first accredited Wetland Cities in January 2025.
79.tq: Match the designation with the correct sites rather than the better-known Ramsar locations.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent Ramsar-related developments in India:
1. India's resolution on sustainable lifestyles for wise use of wetlands was adopted at Ramsar COP-15.
2. The resolution was adopted on 30 July 2025.
3. The Amrit Dharohar strategy was launched in June 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All three statements are correct: the resolution was adopted at COP-15 on 30 July 2025, and the Amrit Dharohar strategy dates to June 2023.
79.tq: Use a three-statement chronology-and-event combination.

79.s: Which of the following Indian wetlands are currently on the Montreux Record of the Ramsar Convention?
o: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
Keoladeo National Park and Wular Lake
79.x: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites under threat; India's sites on it are Keoladeo NP and Loktak Lake. Chilika was on it but was removed after restoration, so options with Chilika are wrong; Kolleru and Wular are not on the Record.
79.tq: Montreux = threatened list: Keoladeo + Loktak; Chilika removed.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and the Ramsar Convention:
1. India has been a Party to the Convention since 1982.
2. India has 101 Ramsar sites, the most in Asia.
3. The obligation of 'wise use' applies only to wetlands designated as Ramsar sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India joined in 1982 and now has 101 sites, the most in Asia. Statement 3 is wrong: the wise-use pillar covers all wetlands, not only designated sites. So the options containing 3 are wrong.
79.tq: Three pillars: designate sites, wise use of ALL wetlands, international cooperation.

79.s: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, 1972, was held at:
79.x: The UN Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm, Sweden, from 5 to 16 June 1972.
79.tq: Use the official conference name to distinguish Stockholm 1972 from UNCED 1992.

79.s:
Which of the following were outcomes of the Stockholm Conference, 1972?
1. Stockholm Declaration containing 26 principles
2. An Action Plan
3. Establishment of UNEP
4. Recognition of 5 June as World Environment Day
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
79.x: The Stockholm Conference produced the 26-principle Stockholm Declaration and an Action Plan, led to the establishment of UNEP and resulted in 5 June being observed as World Environment Day.
79.tq: Group the declaration, institutional outcome, action plan and commemorative date as conference results.

79.s: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme, established in 1972, is located at:
79.x: UNEP was established in 1972 and its headquarters is in Nairobi, Kenya.
79.tq: Distinguish UNEP’s headquarters from the venue of the Stockholm Conference and the CBD Secretariat.

79.s: In the context of the Stockholm Conference, the significance attributed to Indira Gandhi was that she was:
o: The author of the Rio Declaration
The chairperson of the CBD COP-1
The only visiting head of government to attend the Conference
79.x: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was described as the only visiting head of government who attended the Stockholm Conference.
79.tq: Use the unique-status phrase to distinguish the participant from later environmental office-holders.

79.s: The decisions of the Stockholm Conference in India were implemented through the:
79.x: The Stockholm decisions were implemented in India through the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
79.tq: Match the international conference outcome with the specific Indian legal instrument.

79.s: Which one of the following comparisons between the Stockholm Conference and the Rio Earth Summit is correct?
o: Stockholm established the CBD, whereas Rio established the UNEP in 1972.
Stockholm 1972 concerned the human environment, whereas Rio 1992 concerned environment and development.
Stockholm 1992 concerned biodiversity, whereas Rio 1972 concerned human rights.
Both were held in Rio de Janeiro and produced the same declaration.
79.x: The 1972 Stockholm Conference was the UN Conference on the Human Environment, while the 1992 Rio Summit was UNCED, focused on environment and development.
79.tq: Compare the official names and years before comparing their institutional outcomes.

79.s: Which one of the following was a significant institutional outcome of the 1972 Stockholm Conference?
o: Creation of the Sustainable Development Goals
Adoption of the Johannesburg Plan of Implementation
79.x: The Stockholm Conference led to the establishment of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
79.tq: Identify the outcome associated with the correct summit rather than a later conference.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding CITES:
