2. Section 11 also covers animals causing danger to crops.
3. Permits under Section 12 can be given for education and research but not for translocation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Section 11 covers danger to human life or crops. Statement 3 is wrong: Section 12 permits cover education, research and scientific management, including translocation. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: Sec 9 bans hunting; Sec 11 = danger to life or crops; Sec 12 = education, research, translocation.

90.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, enacted by Parliament in 1972, is structured into
90.x: The WPA 1972 has 66 sections arranged in 7 chapters. 51/6, 26/5 and 86/9 are made-up structures; the WPA's six original schedules were cut to four in 2022, which is a different count.
90.tq: WPA 1972 = 66 sections, 7 chapters.

90.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act?
o: Conservation Reserve — government-owned buffer or corridor
Community Reserve — exclusively Central Government land
Conservation Reserve — private land managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee
Community Reserve — statutory body for tiger conservation
90.x: Conservation Reserves are government-owned buffers or corridors. Community Reserves concern private or community land and are managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee.
90.tq: Separate the ownership basis of Conservation Reserves from that of Community Reserves.

90.s: The 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the
90.x: The 2002 amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the National Board for Wildlife.
90.tq: Track the institutional replacement rather than confusing it with bodies created in 2006.

90.s: The 2022 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act is associated with
o: introduction of the Tiger Conservation Plan requirement under Section 38V(3)
replacement of the Indian Board for Wildlife by the National Board for Wildlife
creation of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
rationalisation of schedules and addition of invasive alien species
90.x: The 2022 amendment rationalised the schedules and added invasive alien species. The other options relate to the 2002 or 2006 amendments.
90.tq: Use the amendment timeline to separate later schedule changes from earlier institutional reforms.

90.s: Section 38V(3), inserted in the Wildlife (Protection) Act by the 2006 amendment, requires
o: a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve
a Community Reserve Management Committee for every community reserve
the Centre to regulate invasive alien species
a Chief Wildlife Warden in every State
90.x: Sec. 38V(3) (2006 amendment) mandates a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve. CRMCs came with the 2002 amendment's community reserves; regulation of invasive alien species and the Chief Wildlife Warden in every State are 2022-amendment changes.
90.tq: 2006 amendment = tiger provisions (NTCA, Sec. 38V Tiger Conservation Plan).

90.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force in:
90.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force in April 2023.
90.tq: Separate the year in the title from the year of commencement.

90.s: Which international convention’s provisions were specifically brought into the Wildlife (Protection) Act through the 2022 amendment?
90.x: The 2022 amendment incorporated CITES-related provisions, including provisions concerning management and scientific authorities.
90.tq: Distinguish the wildlife-trade convention from other environmental treaties.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding changes made by the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022:
1. The Centre was empowered to regulate invasive alien species.
2. State Governments may declare conservation reserves.
3. Every State is required to have a Chief Wildlife Warden.
4. Captive animals may be voluntarily surrendered without compensation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: All four statements describe changes associated with the 2022 amendment. Examples of invasive alien species include African catfish and Lantana camara.
90.tq: Test the complete amendment package rather than a single isolated change.

90.s: Which of the following is an example of an invasive alien species specifically associated with the 2022 wildlife amendment provisions?
90.x: African catfish is an example of an invasive alien species referred to in connection with the amendment. Lantana camara is another example.
90.tq: Separate an invasive alien species from native wildlife species.

90.s: The general penalty for violations under the amended wildlife law was raised to a fine of up to:
90.x: The general maximum fine was raised from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh. The specially protected animal category has a separate minimum fine provision.
90.tq: Compare the revised penalty with the earlier amount.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the schedules before and after the 2022 amendment to the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The number of schedules was increased from four to six.
The separate vermin schedule was retained as Schedule IV.
Protected plants were shifted from Schedule VI to Schedule I without any new schedule structure.
The number of schedules was reduced from six to four.
90.x: The 2022 amendment reduced the schedules from six to four and deleted the separate vermin schedule.
90.tq: Compare the old and new frameworks by focusing first on the numerical change.

90.s: Which of the following species-category pairs is correctly matched under the post-2022 schedule framework?
o: Indian flying fox — Schedule IV as a CITES specimen
Dugong — Schedule II with lesser protection
Blackbuck — Schedule III as a protected plant
90.x: The Indian flying fox was formerly listed as vermin in Schedule V but is placed in Schedule II after the 2022 framework. Blackbuck and dugong are included in Schedule I.
90.tq: Track the change in status of a familiar species instead of applying the old vermin classification.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Schedule IV of the Wild Life (Protection) Act after the 2022 amendment:
1. It contains specimens listed in the CITES Appendices.
2. It is the schedule for protected plants.
3. It is the schedule for invasive alien species.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
90.x: Schedule IV contains CITES-listed specimens. Protected plants are in Schedule III, while invasive alien species are regulated through a separate power of the Centre.
90.tq: Reject options that swap neighbouring schedule subjects and statutory powers.

90.s: After deletion of the separate vermin schedule, which authority may declare a wild animal not included in Schedule I as vermin?
o: The National Board for Wildlife through a judicial order
The local authority without any restriction on area or period
The Central Government by notification under Section 62
The State Legislature by amendment of Schedule I
90.x: Under Section 62, the Central Government may declare a wild animal not in Schedule I as vermin for a specified area and period by notification.
90.tq: Ask who would perform the statutory power and check its area-and-period limits.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of inclusion of an animal in Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The species may be hunted freely without restriction during the notified period.
Hunting and trade are generally prohibited except in special cases allowed by the Act.
The species receives the highest statutory protection.
90.x: Schedule I species receive the highest protection; hunting and trade are prohibited except in special cases permitted by the Act. Free hunting is not allowed.
90.tq: Find the option that reverses the legal effect of the highest-protection category.

90.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
1. Mugger crocodile — Schedule I
2. Rock eagle-owl — Schedule I
3. Common crow — Schedule I
4. Blackbuck — Schedule I
90.x: The mugger crocodile, rock eagle-owl and blackbuck are in Schedule I. The common crow was included in the former vermin Schedule V, not Schedule I.
90.tq: Separate high-protection species from a former vermin species.

90.s: A specified plant included in the protected-plant schedule cannot ordinarily be
o: cultivated in every circumstance without regulatory permission
observed or photographed in its natural habitat
picked, uprooted or traded without permission
90.x: A specified plant cannot be picked, uprooted or traded without permission. The law regulates these activities rather than prohibiting observation or scientific description.
90.tq: Apply the statutory restriction to the conduct described in the scenario.

90.s: Under the Forest Conservation Amendment Act, 2023, central approval is not required for certain strategic projects located within what distance of an international border?
90.x: The amendment provides an exemption from central approval for strategic projects within 100 km of international borders, among other specified exemptions.
90.tq: Use the distance figure as the decisive numerical clue.

90.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the exemptions associated with the Forest Conservation Amendment Act, 2023?
o: Strategic projects within 100 km of international borders
Mandatory Gram Sabha consent for every new exemption
90.x: The amendment is criticised because it is silent on the Forest Rights Act and does not mandate Gram Sabha consent for the new exemptions. Strategic projects, eco-tourism and zoos are among the mentioned exemptions.
90.tq: Find the option that reverses the criticism about the absence of Gram Sabha consent.

90.s: The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022, became the subject of a dispute between which two bodies regarding the consent clause?
90.x: The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022, which dropped the consent clause, led to a dispute between the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
90.tq: Match the issue with the two authorities directly associated with it.

90.s:
Under the original Section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, prior approval of the Central Government was required for which of the following?
1. De-reservation of a forest
2. Use of forest land for a non-forest purpose
3. Clearing of trees on forest land
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: The original Section 2 required prior Central approval for de-reservation, non-forest use of forest land and clearing of trees.
90.tq: Treat each listed trigger for Central approval as a separate statutory condition.

90.s:
After the 2023 amendment, which categories of land are covered by the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980?
1. Land notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927 or another law
2. Land recorded as forest in government records on or after 25 October 1980
3. Every private agricultural field having one or more trees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: The amended Act covers land notified as forest under the IFA or another law and land recorded as forest in government records on or after 25 October 1980. It does not cover every private agricultural field with trees.
90.tq: Test the statutory definition by separating included categories from an overbroad claim.

90.s: Which land is excluded from the coverage of the amended forest-conservation law?
o: Forest land proposed for a non-forest purpose after the amendment
Land converted to non-forest use before 12 December 1996
Land recorded as forest in government records after 25 October 1980
Land notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927
90.x: Land converted to non-forest use before 12 December 1996 is excluded from the amended law's coverage.
90.tq: Look for the date-based exception to the general coverage rule.

90.s:
With reference to compensatory afforestation under the forest-conservation framework, consider the following statements:
1. It requires non-forest land of equal area where such land is available.
2. If equal non-forest land is unavailable, twice the area of degraded forest land is used.
3. Net Present Value is paid in addition to compensatory afforestation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: All three statements are correct. Equal-area non-forest land is preferred; otherwise twice the degraded forest area is used, along with payment of NPV.
90.tq: Check whether the alternatives are cumulative rather than mutually exclusive.

90.s: Under the Van (S.E.S.) Amendment Rules, 2025, which activities on leased forest land are treated as forestry activities?
o: Only tourism infrastructure and road widening
90.x: The 2025 rules treat assisted natural regeneration and plantation on leased forest land as forestry activities. Compensatory afforestation and NPV do not apply to these activities.
90.tq: Identify the exact paired activities and avoid substituting unrelated land uses.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: All biodiversity offences were made criminal offences with imprisonment only
Benefit-sharing was abolished for all users
Offences were decriminalised and civil penalties were introduced
Foreign entities were exempted from NBA approval
90.x: The amendment decriminalised offences and introduced civil penalties. It did not abolish benefit-sharing or exempt foreign entities from prior NBA approval.
90.tq: Identify the precise legal-consequence change and reject extreme alternatives.

90.s:
Which of the following categories was exempted from benefit-sharing requirements under the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
1. Registered AYUSH practitioners
2. Cultivated medicinal plants certified by Biodiversity Management Committees
3. All foreign-incorporated entities
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Registered AYUSH practitioners and BMC-certified cultivated medicinal plants received exemptions relating to benefit-sharing. Foreign-incorporated entities still require prior NBA approval.
90.tq: Reject the overbroad exemption extended to foreign entities.

90.s: Under the amended biodiversity framework, the ordinary time limit for NBA approval was reduced from 180 days to:
90.x: The ordinary NBA approval period was reduced from 180 days to 90 days. Applications relating to intellectual property rights continue to have a 180-day period.
90.tq: Distinguish the general time limit from the IPR exception.

90.s: Which category continues to require prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority under the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
90.x: Foreign nationals and foreign-incorporated entities continue to require prior NBA approval. The amendment did not remove this requirement.
90.tq: Use the foreign-entity approval rule as a legal-eligibility discriminator.

90.s: Under the Access and Benefit Sharing Regulations, April 2025, the share allocated to identifiable source institutions is:
90.x: The April 2025 ABS Regulations provide 25–40 percent for identifiable source institutions and 60–75 percent for local communities through SBBs or UTBCs.
90.tq: Compare the two percentage bands and assign each to the correct beneficiary.

90.s: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau was constituted in 2007 under the administrative control of
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
90.x: The Bureau was constituted in 2007 under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
90.tq: Apply the 'who established or administers the body?' method.

90.s: Which of the following correctly lists the five regional offices of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau?
o: Delhi, Jaipur, Hyderabad, Guwahati and Kochi
Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai and Jabalpur
New Delhi, Bhopal, Bengaluru, Patna and Srinagar
Kolkata, Lucknow, Pune, Ranchi and Visakhapatnam
90.x: The five regional offices are at Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai and Jabalpur.
90.tq: Check the complete membership of the fixed regional-office list.

90.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Operation)
A. Save Kurma
B. Softgold
C. Clean Art
D. Thunderbird

List-II (Focus)
1. Turtles
2. Shahtoosh
3. Mongoose-hair brushes
4. INTERPOL-led operation

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: Save Kurma concerns turtles, Softgold concerns shahtoosh, Clean Art targets mongoose-hair brushes, and Thunderbird is INTERPOL-led.
90.tq: Start from the sure operation–subject pair and eliminate codes.

90.s: The WCCB operation known as 'Birbil' is associated with illegal activities involving
90.x: Operation Birbil deals with wildlife crime involving wild cats and birds.
90.tq: Discriminate between similarly named wildlife-crime operations by their target species.

90.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. The Standing Committee of the NBWL is chaired by the Union Environment Minister and clears projects in or near protected areas and tiger corridors.
3. The National Tiger Conservation Authority is chaired by the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: the PM chairs the NBWL. Statement 2 is correct: the Environment Minister chairs its Standing Committee, which clears projects in or near PAs and tiger corridors. Statement 3 is wrong: the NTCA is also chaired by the Environment Minister, not the PM. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: Only the full NBWL has the PM as chair.

90.s: The State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the:
90.x: The State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Chief Minister of the concerned State.
90.tq: Match the state-level body with the state political executive.

90.s:
Arrange the following authorities according to the years associated with their establishment or constitution, from earliest to latest:
A. Animal Welfare Board
B. National Biodiversity Authority
C. National Tiger Conservation Authority
D. Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
90.x: The relevant years are Animal Welfare Board—1962, National Biodiversity Authority—2003, National Tiger Conservation Authority—2006, and Wildlife Crime Control Bureau—2007.
90.tq: Fix the earliest 1962 body first, then arrange the three later bodies by year.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB):
1. It is headquartered in New Delhi.
2. It was made a statutory body through the 2006 amendment of the Wildlife (Protection) Act on the recommendation of the Tiger Task Force.
3. It was created under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and is headquartered in Chennai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: WCCB HQ is New Delhi (APPSC 2022). Statement 2 is correct: it became statutory via the 2006 WPA amendment on the Tiger Task Force's recommendation. Statement 3 is wrong: the BD Act 2002 body headquartered in Chennai is the National Biodiversity Authority, not the WCCB. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: WCCB = New Delhi; NBA = Chennai.

90.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is best described as an umbrella law dealing with
o: only the diversion of forest land
access and benefit sharing from biological resources
only the declaration of tiger reserves
90.x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law for environmental protection and pollution control.
90.tq: Distinguish the umbrella environmental law from sector-specific statutes.

90.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 — Regulation of diversion of forest land
2. Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 — Parent Act of the Animal Welfare Board of India
3. Biological Diversity Act, 2002 — Access and benefit sharing
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
90.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The Forest (Conservation) Act checks deforestation and regulates diversion, the PCA Act led to the AWBI, and the Biological Diversity Act implements access and benefit sharing.
90.tq: Verify each Act against its distinctive subject before using the combination code.

90.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the National Green Tribunal's jurisdiction as described in the legal framework?
o: It hears cases under the Forest Rights Act but not under the Forest (Conservation) Act.
It has jurisdiction only over the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.
It hears cases under the Wildlife (Protection) Act but not under the Environment (Protection) Act.
It hears cases under seven laws, including the Forest (Conservation) Act, Environment (Protection) Act and Biological Diversity Act.
90.x: The NGT hears cases under seven specified laws, including the FCA 1980, EPA 1986 and BD Act 2002. The framework states that it cannot hear cases under the WPA 1972 or FRA 2006.
90.tq: Use the inclusion and exclusion of statutes to separate NGT jurisdiction from ordinary wildlife law.

90.s: Which one of the following is NOT the name of an Act in the environmental legal framework described here?
90.x: There is no Act called the Nature (Protection) Act, 2000. The other three are recognised environmental statutes.
90.tq: Spot the look-alike title rather than accepting a familiar-sounding statute.

90.s: Which one of the following Acts was enacted to protect wild animals, birds and plants and to manage their habitats?
o: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
90.x: The WPA 1972 protects wild animals, birds and plants and manages their habitats (APPSC 2025 key). The EPA 1986 is an umbrella law for environmental protection and pollution control; the FCA 1980 checks deforestation and regulates diversion of forest land; the PCA Act 1960 prevents cruelty to animals and is the parent Act of the AWBI.
90.tq: Wild animals, birds AND plants = WPA 1972, not EPA or FCA.

90.s: India’s protected areas covered 1,75,169.42 square kilometres in the 2026 figures. This was stated to be equivalent to approximately:
90.x: The protected areas covered 1,75,169.42 square kilometres, corresponding to 5.32% of India’s land area.
90.tq: Link the absolute area figure with its reported percentage instead of treating them as separate facts.

90.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The full National Board for Wildlife met in 2025 after a gap of 13 years.
2. A PIL concerning the clearance of diversion proposals was reported in the Delhi High Court.
3. The Standing Committee of the Board cleared over 97% of diversion proposals between 2014 and 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: All three statements correctly describe the reported current issue: the Delhi High Court PIL, the clearance rate of over 97%, and the 2025 full-Board meeting after a 13-year gap.
90.tq: Check whether the time period, forum and institutional event all fit the same current-affairs issue.

90.s: Why would a Maharashtra Bill amending Section 12 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 require the assent of the President of India?
o: Because relocation of leopards is exclusively a constitutional power of the President
Because the Bill concerns only private forests
Because it seeks to amend a central law
Because every wildlife sanctuary is administered by the President
90.x: The Bill requires Presidential assent because it amends a central law, the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The other statements assign incorrect constitutional or administrative reasons.
90.tq: Ask who has authority when a State Bill affects a central law.

90.s: The 2026 Maharashtra amendment proposal relating to leopards sought to permit relocation and also proposed moving the leopard from:
90.x: The proposal sought to enable relocation of leopards under Section 12 and move them from Schedule I to Schedule II. Environmentalists described the proposed down-listing as regressive.
90.tq: Watch the direction of the schedule change; the trap reverses the two schedules.

90.s: Which of the following best describes a criticism of the 2023 amendment relating to forest protection?
o: It abolished the Forest Rights Act and transferred all forests to local bodies.
It prohibited any diversion of forest land for non-forestry purposes.
It brought all deemed forests under the Act without exception.
It removed deemed forests from the Act’s scope and was criticised as diluting Godavarman protections and conflicting with the Forest Rights Act.
90.x: The criticism is that the 2023 amendment takes deemed forests out of the Act’s scope, potentially diluting the Godavarman protection and clashing with the Forest Rights Act.
90.tq: Select the option that captures both the legal change and the associated criticism.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported rescue of a Schedule-I bird in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A rock eagle-owl was rescued near Dharmavaram and released in Nelakota Reserve Forest.
A leopard was rescued near Kurnool and released in the Tungabhadra sanctuary.
A rock eagle-owl was rescued near Maharashtra and released in the Delhi Ridge.
A crocodile was rescued near Dharmavaram and released in Nelakota Reserve Forest.
90.x: A Schedule-I rock eagle-owl was rescued near Dharmavaram and released in Nelakota Reserve Forest. The other options substitute the species, location or release site.
90.tq: Use the species-place-release-site chain to eliminate swapped details.

91.s: The Miyawaki method is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Dense, multi-layered mini-forests of native species in urban areas
Conversion of agricultural land into pasture
Seed storage in inaccessible forest areas
91.x: The Miyawaki method creates dense, multi-layered mini-forests using native species, particularly in urban areas.
91.tq: Identify the defining application of the method rather than its associated criticism.

91.s: The term ‘social forestry’ was used by the National Commission on Agriculture in which year?
91.x: The National Commission on Agriculture used the term ‘social forestry’ in 1976.
91.tq: Distinguish the closely placed institutional and programme years.

91.s:
Consider the following statements regarding social forestry:
1. Farm forestry is one of its components.
2. Community forestry is one of its components.
3. Extension forestry includes roadside, canal and rail strips.
4. Agroforestry is excluded from social forestry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: Farm forestry, community forestry, extension forestry and agroforestry are components of social forestry. Statement 4 is false because agroforestry is included.
91.tq: Find the excluded component and use the detailed definition of extension forestry.

91.s: A major criticism of the implementation of social forestry is that it drifted towards:
o: Mixed native forests under community control
91.x: Social forestry has been criticised for drifting into commercial monocultures. The suggested corrective approach is the use of mixed native species.
91.tq: Test the criticism and its precise policy concern rather than the proposed remedy.

91.s: Seed balls, consisting of seeds packed in clay, compost and soil, are particularly used for:
o: Creating commercial monocultures in urban areas
91.x: Seed balls are used to facilitate regeneration on degraded or inaccessible land. They contain seeds packed in clay, compost and soil.
91.tq: Match the technique with its specific field application.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about Joint Forest Management (JFM):
1. JFM traces its origin to the Arabari experiment in West Bengal (1971-72).
2. The National Forest Policy, 1988 called for people's participation in forest management.
3. The MoEF issued the JFM guidelines on 1 June 1988.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: JFM began with the Arabari experiment in West Bengal in 1971-72. Statement 2 is correct: NFP 1988 called for people's participation. Statement 3 is wrong: the JFM guidelines were issued on 1 June 1990, two years after the policy. Hence 1 and 2 only.
91.tq: Arabari 1971-72, then NFP 1988, then JFM guidelines 1 June 1990.

91.s: The National Afforestation Programme is implemented through which village-level institutions?
91.x: The National Afforestation Programme runs through village-level Joint Forest Management Committees.
91.tq: Identify the implementing institution at the correct administrative level.

91.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the State Forest Development Agency in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It federates 22 Forest Development Agencies and runs NAP, GIM and NMPB schemes.
It issues Forest Rights Act titles in all ITDA areas.
It federates 22 Joint Forest Management Committees and runs only the Miyawaki programme.
It administers only compensatory afforestation under the Green Credit Programme.
91.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the State Forest Development Agency federates 22 Forest Development Agencies and runs the NAP, GIM and NMPB schemes.
91.tq: Test the federation count together with the agency’s programme responsibilities.

91.s: In Andhra Pradesh, capacity-building camps associated with forest programmes are held through:
91.x: The State Forest Development Agency conducts capacity-building camps through Vana Samrakshana Samithis.
91.tq: Match the capacity-building activity with the correct local institution.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016:
1. It set up both National and State Compensatory Afforestation Funds.
2. These funds are non-lapsable public accounts.
3. These funds do not earn interest.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Act created National and State funds as non-lapsable public accounts. Statement 3 is wrong: the funds are interest-bearing. Hence 1 and 2 only.
91.tq: CAF funds: national + state, non-lapsable, interest-bearing.

91.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the two-tier CAMPA arrangement?
o: National CAMPA carries out field work while State CAMPAs frame national policy.
State CAMPAs set national policy and National CAMPA implements village-level works.
National CAMPA is headed by the Union Environment Minister and sets policy, while State CAMPAs carry out the work.
Both National and State CAMPAs are headed by the State Forest Minister and perform identical functions.
91.x: National CAMPA is headed by the Union Environment Minister and sets policy; State CAMPAs undertake implementation.
91.tq: Compare the policy-setting and implementation roles rather than the names alone.

91.s: The prescribed distribution of CAMPA funds between State funds and the National fund is:
91.x: Ninety per cent is allocated to State funds and ten per cent to the National fund.
91.tq: Keep the direction of the split clear: the larger share goes to the States.

91.s: Before a project involving diversion of forest land starts, the agency diverting the land is required to pay:
o: Compensatory afforestation cost and the Net Present Value of the lost forest ecosystem
A wildlife management fee without compensatory afforestation cost
Only the cost of planting new trees
Only the Net Present Value of the lost ecosystem
91.x: The agency must pay for compensatory afforestation as well as the NPV of the lost forest ecosystem before the project begins.
91.tq: Apply the rule to the project-start condition and include both required components.

91.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated use of CAMPA funds?
o: Financing unrestricted private urban housing projects
91.x: CAMPA funds may support regeneration, wildlife management, catchment treatment, relocation from protected areas, human-wildlife conflict management and forest-fire prevention. Unrestricted private urban housing is not a stated use.
91.tq: Identify the option outside the listed public forestry and wildlife purposes.

91.s: Progress in the utilisation and implementation of CAMPA funds is tracked through the:
91.x: The e-Green Watch portal is used to track CAMPA progress.
91.tq: Distinguish the monitoring portal from similarly named forestry programmes.

91.s: With reference to compensatory afforestation, which of the following correctly describes the ‘land by land’ and ‘trees by trees’ principle?
o: It requires only degraded forest land and no non-forest land
It replaces land and trees on non-forest land for compensatory afforestation
It permits only exotic plantations on grasslands
It applies exclusively to urban mini-forests
91.x: Compensatory afforestation replaces ‘land by land’ and ‘trees by trees’ on non-forest land.
91.tq: Break the phrase into its two parallel obligations and identify the correct land category.

91.s: Under the compensatory afforestation rules, Central Public Sector Undertakings or projects for which no non-forest land is available may use:
o: The same area of non-forest land
Only urban land under the Miyawaki method
Twice the area of degraded forest land
Half the area of degraded forest land
91.x: Central PSUs, and projects where no non-forest land is available, may use twice the area of degraded forest land for compensatory afforestation.
91.tq: Focus on the quantitative exception to the normal land requirement.

91.s:
With reference to the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authorities (CAMPA) exist at both the national and state levels.
2. People's participation in compensatory afforestation programmes is mandatory under the Act.
3. By 2024 the fund held over Rs 66,000 crore, but only about 30-35% had been used.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: CAMPA works at both national and state levels. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2016 Act does not make people's participation mandatory (UPSC 2019 trap). Statement 3 is correct: the fund held over Rs 66,000 crore by 2024 with only 30-35% utilised. Hence 1 and 3 only.
91.tq: CAMPA at both levels = correct; 'people's participation mandatory' = wrong (UPSC 2019).

91.s:
Consider the following statements about compensatory afforestation (CA):
1. The Forest (Conservation) Rules, 2022 introduced Accredited Compensatory Afforestation.
2. Under Accredited Compensatory Afforestation, developers may only use plantations raised after the forest land is diverted.
3. Afforestation raised under the Green Credit Programme can be exchanged for CA, as allowed under the Van (S.E.S.) Rules, 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: the FC Rules 2022 introduced Accredited CA. Statement 2 is wrong: it lets developers use plantations raised in advance, which work as land banks. Statement 3 is correct: Green Credit afforestation can be exchanged for CA under the Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023. Hence 1 and 3 only.
91.tq: Accredited CA = plantations raised in advance (land banks).

91.s: Which change in the Forest (Conservation) Rules, 2022 was disputed by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes in its interaction with the MoEFCC?
o: Dropping the clause requiring forest-dwellers’ consent before diversion
91.x: The 2022 Rules dropped the clause requiring the consent of forest-dwellers before diversion, and the NCST disputed this with the MoEFCC.
91.tq: Identify the precise legal change rather than the surrounding forest programmes.

91.s: Accredited Compensatory Afforestation enables developers to meet their obligations by using:
o: Community titles issued under the Forest Rights Act
Plantations raised in advance, functioning effectively as land banks
Only plantations raised after diversion of forest land
Funds allocated exclusively to VSS camps
91.x: Accredited Compensatory Afforestation permits developers to use plantations raised in advance, effectively creating land banks for meeting obligations.
91.tq: Test the operational meaning of a legal term through a developer scenario.

91.s: The guidelines for linking afforestation under the Green Credit Programme with compensatory afforestation were issued on:
91.x: The relevant guidelines were issued on 16 September 2025.
91.tq: Use the exact date to separate the guideline from earlier JFM and later rule references.

91.s: The Nagar Van Yojana is run by the:
91.x: The National Afforestation and Eco-development Board (NAEB) runs the Nagar Van Yojana.
91.tq: Identify the correct implementing body rather than the research institution.

91.s: The Nagar Van Yojana targets, between 2020–21 and 2026–27:
91.x: The scheme targets 600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas during 2020–21 to 2026–27.
91.tq: Split the paired targets carefully; the figures are deliberately reversible.

91.s: The ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign commenced on:
91.x: The ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign began on 5 June 2024.
91.tq: Recall the exact launch date of the named campaign.

91.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Pradesh — Telangana Ku Haritha Haram
Telangana — Great Green Wall of AP
Andhra Pradesh — Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana
91.x: The Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana is associated with Chhattisgarh. Great Green Wall of AP, Namo Van-Nagar Van and School Nursery Scheme are listed for Andhra Pradesh, while Telangana has Telangana Ku Haritha Haram.
91.tq: Start from the sure State–scheme pair and eliminate swapped associations.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about Vanamahotsav:
1. It is observed in the first week of July.
2. It was started by K.M. Munshi in 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: Vanamahotsav is held in the first week of July. Statement 2 is wrong: K.M. Munshi started it in 1950, not 1960. Hence 1 only; '2 only' and 'both' include the wrong year, and 'neither' rejects the correct statement 1.
91.tq: Vanamahotsav: July, K.M. Munshi, 1950.

91.s:
The revised 2021–30 framework of the Green India Mission targets which of the following regions or ecosystems?
1. Aravallis
2. Western Ghats
3. Himalayas
4. Mangroves
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
91.x: The revised framework targets the Aravallis, Western Ghats, Himalayas and mangroves.
91.tq: Check whether the list is complete before selecting the coded option.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the Green India Mission:
1. It is one of the missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
2. It is implemented through Joint Forest Management Committees.
3. It is funded partly from National CAMPA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: The Green India Mission is one of the NAPCC missions, is implemented through JFMCs and receives partial funding from National CAMPA.
91.tq: Combine institutional status, implementation mechanism and funding source.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the institutional implementation of the Green India Mission:
1. It works through JFMCs.
2. It works through VFCs and SHGs.
3. It functions under Gram Sabha oversight.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: The Green India Mission works through JFMCs, VFCs and SHGs under the oversight of the Gram Sabha.
91.tq: Use the inclusive option when all three institutional relationships are correctly stated.

91.s: Agroforestry is best described as:
o: Growing trees together with crops and livestock on the same land
Growing crops only beneath naturally occurring forest canopies
Replacing agricultural land entirely with forest species
Growing only commercial tree plantations on degraded land
91.x: Agroforestry integrates trees, crops and livestock on the same land.
91.tq: Use the precise definition rather than a broad description of forestry.

91.s: India became the first country to adopt a National Agroforestry Policy in:
91.x: India adopted the National Agroforestry Policy in February 2014 and was the first country to do so.
91.tq: Distinguish the exact month and year from nearby policy dates.

91.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the GROW report:
1. GROW stands for Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry.
2. It was associated with NITI Aayog.
3. It estimated that about 8.65% of India’s geographical area is under agroforestry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: All three statements are correct. The GROW report by NITI Aayog uses the expansion ‘Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry’ and places the agroforestry area at about 8.65% of India’s geographical area.
91.tq: Check the expansion, institution and numerical estimate separately.

91.s: The Central Agroforestry Research Institute (ICAR-CAFRI) is located at:
91.x: ICAR-CAFRI is located at Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh.
91.tq: Use the institution-location association.

91.s: The Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF) is implemented under:
91.x: Agroforestry receives support through the Sub-Mission on Agroforestry under PM-RKVY.
91.tq: Separate the funding programme from related forestry schemes.

91.s:
With reference to Trees Outside Forests in India (TOFI), consider the following statements:
1. It is a programme of MoEFCC and USAID.
2. It was launched in 2023.
3. It was launched in seven States, including Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: TOFI is an MoEFCC-USAID programme launched in 2023 in seven States, one of which is Andhra Pradesh.
91.tq: Verify the partners, launch year and geographical coverage together.

91.s: The Koya and Kondh communities have opposed the Polavaram project primarily over:
o: The location of the Arabari experiment
91.x: The Koya and Kondh communities oppose the Polavaram project over land rights and rehabilitation concerns.
91.tq: Connect the affected communities with the specific tribal-conflict issue.

91.s: A CAG audit of the Green India Mission found that forest quality improved on only 0.11 million hectares against a target of:
91.x: The audit found improvement on only 0.11 million hectares against the target of 1.4 million hectares.
91.tq: Compare the achieved area with the target rather than selecting the repeated figure.

91.s: Which of the following convergence arrangements was reported as not having materialised in the implementation of the Green India Mission?
o: Convergence with JFMCs and VFCs under Gram Sabha oversight
Convergence between NAP and GIM from 2021–22
Convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS, now VB-G RAM G
Convergence between social forestry and agroforestry
91.x: The audit-related assessment stated that convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS, now VB-G RAM G, never happened.
91.tq: Identify the missing convergence arrangement by distinguishing it from institutional linkages that do exist.

91.s: Which of the following has been criticised in relation to the use of CAMPA funds?
o: Funding exotic plantations on native grasslands
Funding mixed native species in all historical forest zones
91.x: CAMPA money has been criticised for funding exotic plantations on native grasslands.
91.tq: Find the practice that represents the criticism, not the proposed corrective measures.

91.s: Which document is prepared every year by the Andhra Pradesh CAMPA?
91.x: The Andhra Pradesh CAMPA prepares an Annual Plan of Operations every year.
91.tq: Identify the recurring administrative document associated with the agency.

92.s: The atmosphere’s selective behaviour towards radiation is best described as follows:
o: It absorbs all incoming short-wave solar radiation and transmits all outgoing long-wave radiation
It is opaque to both incoming solar radiation and outgoing terrestrial radiation
It permits much of the incoming short-wave solar radiation but is relatively opaque to outgoing terrestrial long-wave infrared radiation
It reflects all solar radiation and absorbs only ultraviolet radiation
92.x: The atmosphere allows much incoming short-wave solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface but absorbs outgoing long-wave terrestrial infrared radiation through greenhouse gases.
92.tq: Apply the short-wave incoming and long-wave outgoing distinction to the atmospheric mechanism.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the role of carbon dioxide and water vapour in the greenhouse effect?
o: They absorb incoming visible light and convert it directly into ultraviolet radiation
They absorb only radio waves and transfer the energy exclusively to the upper atmosphere
They prevent all solar radiation from entering the atmosphere by reflecting it into space
They absorb outgoing infrared radiation mainly in the 14,000–25,000 nm range and re-radiate part of it back towards the surface
92.x: CO2 and water vapour strongly absorb infrared radiation in the 14,000–25,000 nm range and re-radiate energy in all directions, including back towards the surface.
92.tq: Link the wavelength range with the direction of re-radiation to identify the mechanism.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the natural and enhanced greenhouse effects:
1. The natural greenhouse effect occurs without human intervention and helps keep Earth habitable.
2. The enhanced greenhouse effect results when human activities raise atmospheric greenhouse-gas concentrations.
3. Greenhouse-gas levels in the natural greenhouse effect have remained stable for thousands of years, whereas fossil fuels, deforestation, industry, agriculture and waste contribute to the enhanced effect.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements correctly distinguish the natural greenhouse effect from its anthropogenically enhanced form.
92.tq: Compare the two columns by checking human role, stability of gas levels and consequences.

92.s: If the natural greenhouse effect did not exist, the approximate mean temperature of Earth’s surface would be:
92.x: The natural greenhouse effect raises Earth’s average surface temperature from approximately −18°C to about +15°C, making the planet habitable.
92.tq: Remember the paired comparison rather than either temperature in isolation.

92.s: Which one of the following is the primary cause of the present global warming?
o: Increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere
Depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer
Increase in the amount of incoming solar radiation
Rise in the proportion of nitrogen and oxygen in the air
92.x: The primary cause of global warming is the increase in greenhouse gases (APPSC 2025 key): heat from sunlight re-radiated by the Earth is absorbed by CO2 and other gases. Ozone depletion is a separate problem; the warming is not explained by more incoming sunlight; and nitrogen and oxygen are not greenhouse gases.
92.tq: Global warming = more GHGs trapping re-radiated infrared.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Global Warming Potential (GWP):
1. Carbon dioxide has a 100-year GWP of 1 and is the reference gas for GWP calculations.
2. Among carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and sulphur hexafluoride, nitrous oxide has the highest 100-year GWP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: CO2 is assigned a GWP of 1 and serves as the reference. Statement 2 is wrong: sulphur hexafluoride (about 23,900) has the highest GWP of these; nitrous oxide is about 265-298 and methane 28-36. Hence '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are ruled out.
92.tq: CO2 = 1 (reference); SF6 ~23,900 tops the list.

92.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the approximate atmospheric lifetime given for it?
92.x: Water vapour has an approximate atmospheric lifetime of nine days. Methane lasts about 12 years, nitrous oxide about 114 years, and carbon dioxide has a much wider lifetime range of about 100–1,000 years.
92.tq: Use the lifetime column to catch swapped values between similar greenhouse gases.

92.s: Perfluoromethane is associated principally with which industrial activity?
92.x: Perfluoromethane is released in association with aluminium production.
92.tq: Test the pollutant-industry association directly.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Water vapour is the most important greenhouse gas.
2. Human beings increase atmospheric water vapour mainly indirectly by warming the air.
3. Water vapour is primarily a synthetic greenhouse gas released by refrigeration equipment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Water vapour is the most important greenhouse gas, and human influence on it is mainly indirect through warming. It is natural, not primarily synthetic or refrigeration-derived.
92.tq: Use the natural-versus-synthetic distinction to reject the false statement.

92.s: Among the following, which is the correct order of the major natural contributors to the greenhouse effect, from highest to lowest contribution?
o: Water vapour > Methane > Carbon dioxide > Ozone > CFCs
Carbon dioxide > Water vapour > Methane > CFCs > Ozone
Carbon dioxide > Methane > Water vapour > Ozone > CFCs
Water vapour > Carbon dioxide > Methane > Ozone > CFCs
92.x: Water vapour is the largest natural contributor, followed by carbon dioxide, methane, ozone and CFCs.
92.tq: Use the complete contribution order rather than identifying only the largest gas.

92.s:
Consider the following gases in relation to the enhanced greenhouse effect:
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Methane
3. CFCs
4. Nitrous oxide
Which of the following represents their approximate shares in descending order?
92.x: The textbook distribution given is approximately CO2 60%, methane 20%, CFCs 15% and nitrous oxide 5%.
92.tq: Compare the numerical shares and check both the order and the percentages.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Global Warming Potential (GWP)?
o: The amount of solar radiation reflected by a gas in comparison with water vapour
The atmospheric concentration of a gas compared with that of oxygen over one year
The heat absorbed by a gas over a specified period, usually 100 years, relative to the same mass of carbon dioxide
The time required by a gas to disappear completely from the atmosphere
92.x: GWP compares the heat absorbed over a specified period, generally 100 years, by a given mass of a greenhouse gas with that absorbed by the same mass of CO2.
92.tq: Discriminate between GWP, atmospheric lifetime and concentration.

92.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists.

List-I (Gas)
a. Carbon dioxide
b. Methane
c. Nitrous oxide
d. Sulphur hexafluoride

List-II (Principal anthropogenic source)
i. Fertilisers and biomass burning
 ii. Fossil fuels, deforestation and cement production
 iii. Rice paddies, livestock and landfills
 iv. Dielectric fluid

Codes:
92.x: CO2 is associated with fossil fuels, deforestation and cement production; methane with rice paddies, livestock and landfills; N2O with fertilisers and biomass or coal burning; and SF6 with dielectric fluid.
92.tq: Start from the sure source pair and eliminate codes containing swapped sources.

92.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to 100-year GWP and atmospheric lifetime?
92.x: Methane has a 100-year GWP of about 28–36 and an atmospheric lifetime of approximately 12 years. Nitrous oxide, CO2 and water vapour have different values.
92.tq: Separate the GWP range from the atmospheric-lifetime figure before selecting the pair.

92.s: Which one of the following statements about the classification of atmospheric gases is correct?
o: Carbon monoxide is the largest natural contributor to the greenhouse effect
Nitrogen and oxygen are indirect greenhouse gases, while argon is the principal greenhouse gas
Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are major greenhouse gases, whereas carbon monoxide is a primary greenhouse gas
Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are not greenhouse gases, while carbon monoxide acts only as an indirect greenhouse gas
92.x: N2, O2 and Ar are not greenhouse gases. Carbon monoxide is considered only an indirect greenhouse gas rather than a primary one.
92.tq: Distinguish primary greenhouse gases from gases that influence warming indirectly.

92.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the relationship between deforestation and carbon dioxide?
o: Deforestation is an anthropogenic activity associated with enhanced greenhouse effect
Deforestation generally raises the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
Deforestation can reduce the capacity of vegetation to absorb carbon dioxide
Deforestation decreases atmospheric carbon dioxide by removing carbon-storing trees
92.x: Deforestation does not decrease atmospheric CO2; it reduces carbon uptake and may release stored carbon, thereby raising atmospheric CO2.
92.tq: Find the reversed cause-and-effect statement in the environmental process.

92.s: Which one of the following gases is a non-greenhouse gas that forms the largest proportion of the atmosphere?
92.x: Nitrogen is a non-greenhouse gas and constitutes about 78.08 percent of the atmosphere. It does not absorb terrestrial infrared radiation in the manner of greenhouse gases.
92.tq: Separate atmospheric abundance from greenhouse contribution.

92.s: The atmospheric concentration of CO2 in 2024, expressed as a percentage of air, was approximately:
92.x: A concentration of 423.9 ppm is approximately 0.04 percent of the atmosphere.
92.tq: Convert ppm to percentage and avoid shifting the decimal place.

92.s: Radiative forcing refers to which one of the following?
o: The change in Earth’s energy balance caused by a climatic driver, expressed in watts per square metre
The quantity of heat stored only in the oceans during El Niño events
The amount of rainfall received by a region due to increased evaporation
The rate at which greenhouse gases are removed from the atmosphere
92.x: Radiative forcing is the change in Earth’s energy balance produced by a driver and is expressed in W/m².
92.tq: Match the specialised term with its precise definition and unit.

92.s:
Consider the following statements based on the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin (October 2025):
1. Methane supplies about 16% of the radiative forcing from long-lived greenhouse gases.
2. Carbon dioxide accounted for about 81% of the 54% rise in the warming effect of long-lived greenhouse gases during 1990-2024.
3. Methane accounted for most of the rise in the warming effect of long-lived greenhouse gases during 1990-2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: CH4 gives about 16% of long-lived GHG forcing. Statement 2 is correct: CO2 accounted for about 81% of the 54% rise. Statement 3 is wrong: it was CO2, not methane, that drove most of the rise. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong.
92.tq: CH4 = 16% of forcing; CO2 = 81% of the rise.

92.s: Climate sensitivity refers to the warming that follows which of the following changes?
o: A doubling of the annual rainfall over oceans
A doubling of atmospheric oxygen over its present level
A doubling of atmospheric CO2 over its pre-industrial level
A 50% reduction in global methane emissions
92.x: Climate sensitivity is the warming response to a doubling of carbon dioxide relative to its pre-industrial concentration.
92.tq: Distinguish the formal definition from general descriptions of climate change.

92.s: The pre-industrial concentration of atmospheric carbon dioxide was approximately:
92.x: The pre-industrial CO2 concentration is generally taken as approximately 278–280 ppm.
92.tq: Use the central numerical range and reject nearby shifted values.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about climate feedbacks:
1. Melting ice lowers albedo and causes more heat to be absorbed.
2. A warmer atmosphere can hold more water vapour.
3. Increased water vapour can trap additional heat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements describe positive climate feedbacks: reduced ice albedo increases absorption, while additional atmospheric water vapour enhances heat trapping.
92.tq: Follow the linked cause-and-effect chain in a feedback loop.

92.s: Tipping points in the climate system are best understood as:
o: Thresholds beyond which small changes may trigger self-perpetuating shifts that cannot be reversed on human timescales
Fixed temperature values that apply equally to every ecosystem
Linear changes that can always be reversed immediately
Short-term daily variations in weather with no long-term effects
92.x: Tipping points are thresholds at which small changes can initiate self-perpetuating, non-linear shifts that are not reversible on human timescales.
92.tq: Distinguish threshold-driven non-linear change from ordinary gradual variation.

92.s: Why can warming of methane-hydrate deposits intensify climate change?
o: It converts methane into oxygen and increases atmospheric cooling.
It permanently removes methane from the atmosphere through carbonation.
It reduces the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
It can release methane, creating a positive feedback that causes further warming.
92.x: Warming can destabilise methane hydrates and release methane, a potent greenhouse gas, thereby producing a positive feedback.
92.tq: Apply the definition of positive feedback to a natural methane reservoir.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the short-lived climate pollutants listed?
92.x: The listed short-lived climate pollutants are black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone. Water vapour is not included in that list.
92.tq: Find the odd item outside the specified pollutant group.

92.s: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition is associated with action against:
92.x: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition works to address short-lived climate pollutants such as black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone.
92.tq: Match the coalition with the precise environmental problem it addresses.

92.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the source and lifetime of black carbon?
o: Incomplete combustion of diesel, biomass and coal — days to weeks
Rice paddies and livestock — about 12 years
NOx and VOCs in sunlight — weeks to months
92.x: Black carbon is produced by incomplete combustion of diesel, biomass and coal and remains in the atmosphere for days to weeks.
92.tq: Separate the source-lifetime pair of black carbon from those of methane, ozone and synthetic gases.

92.s: Tropospheric ozone is formed mainly from which combination in sunlight?
o: Nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds
92.x: Tropospheric ozone is formed through reactions involving nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in sunlight.
92.tq: Test the precursor-pollutant relationship rather than the lifetime of the pollutant.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Black carbon can darken snow and ice surfaces.
2. Darkening of snow and ice by black carbon can accelerate glacier melt.
3. Black carbon is produced exclusively by fossil-fuel combustion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Black carbon darkens snow and ice and accelerates melting. It is produced by incomplete combustion of both biomass and diesel, so statement 3 is false.
92.tq: Find the false statement containing the extreme word ‘exclusively’.

92.s:
With reference to tropospheric ozone, consider the following statements:
1. It is a short-lived greenhouse gas.
2. It can reduce crop yields.
3. Its effects are generally worst during summer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Tropospheric ozone is a short-lived greenhouse gas, harms vegetation and cuts crop yields; its pollution is generally most severe in summer.
92.tq: When all three statements describe linked effects of one pollutant, test the complete combination.

92.s: The United Nations Secretary-General’s Call to Action on Methane was launched during which event and covered which sectors?
o: Montreal Protocol Conference; refrigeration, aerosols and solvents
London Climate Action Week; waste, agriculture and fossil fuels
World Water Week; irrigation, fisheries and tourism
92.x: The Call to Action on Methane was launched at London Climate Action Week on 24 June 2026 and addresses waste, agriculture and fossil-fuel operations.
92.tq: Match the initiative with its event date and sectoral scope.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the Global Methane Pledge:
1. It aims to cut global methane emissions by 30% from 2020 levels by 2030.
2. It was launched at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
3. India is a signatory to the Pledge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Pledge targets a 30% cut in methane from 2020 levels by 2030 and was launched at COP26 (Glasgow, 2021). Statement 3 is wrong: India has not signed it (Global Methane Status Report 2025 by UNEP and CCAC). Hence 1 and 2 only.
92.tq: Methane Pledge = 30% by 2030 from 2020, COP26; India has NOT signed.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deforestation and land-use change can remove carbon sinks.
2. Agricultural fertilisers contribute to nitrous oxide emissions.
3. Livestock contribute to methane emissions.
4. Deforestation increases carbon sinks in all circumstances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Deforestation and land-use change generally remove or reduce carbon sinks rather than increase them in all circumstances.
92.tq: Find the absolute and reversed statement before selecting the coded option.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the contrasting climate effects of the aerosol types listed below?
o: All aerosols invariably cool the air
Black and brown carbon cool the air, while sulphate droplets warm it
All aerosols invariably warm the air
Black and brown carbon warm the air, while sulphate droplets cool it
92.x: Black and brown carbon have a warming effect on the air, whereas sulphate droplets exert a cooling effect.
92.tq: Test the reversed comparison between warming and cooling aerosol types.

92.s: Which one of the following is the largest contributor to greenhouse-gas emissions among the sources listed below?
o: Fossil-fuel combustion for energy, transport and industry
92.x: Fossil-fuel combustion involving coal, oil and gas for energy, transport and industry is the largest contributor. Other important sources include deforestation, industrial processes, agriculture and waste.
92.tq: Identify the dominant sector and distinguish it from other recognised sources.

92.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the agricultural source-gas pairs?
o: Synthetic fertilisers—N2O; enteric fermentation—CH4; rice paddies—CH4
Synthetic fertilisers—CH4; enteric fermentation—N2O; rice paddies—CO2
Synthetic fertilisers—CO2; enteric fermentation—N2O; rice paddies—SO2
Synthetic fertilisers—SO2; enteric fermentation—CO2; rice paddies—N2O
92.x: Synthetic fertilisers release nitrous oxide, while livestock digestion through enteric fermentation and rice paddies are important methane sources.
92.tq: Match each agricultural activity with its characteristic greenhouse gas.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to global carbon dioxide emissions in 2024:
1. China — 12 billion tonnes a year
2. United States of America — 4.9 billion tonnes a year
3. India — 3.2 billion tonnes a year
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: The reported 2024 figures are China 12 billion tonnes, the United States 4.9 billion tonnes and India 3.2 billion tonnes. India ranked third among these top emitters.
92.tq: Check both the ranking and the associated numerical values.

92.s: Under the GHG Emission Intensity Target (Amendment) Rules, 2025, which of the following groups represents sectors newly added under the Environmental Protection Act, 1986?
o: Petroleum refinery, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium
Coal mining, railways, shipping and aviation
Aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper
Fertiliser, sugar, leather and automobile manufacturing
92.x: The 2025 amendment added petroleum refinery, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium. The earlier sectors included aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper.
92.tq: Distinguish newly added sectors from the earlier covered sectors.

92.s: The Draft GHG Emissions Intensity Target Rules, 2025, focus on greenhouse gas emissions:
o: Only per person in rural households
Per unit of output, such as per tonne of cement
Only as total national emissions without reference to output
Per square kilometre of forest alone
92.x: The draft rules frame emissions intensity as greenhouse gas emissions per unit of output, for example per tonne of cement.
92.tq: Apply the denominator in an emissions-intensity measure rather than confusing it with total emissions.

92.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 2024 atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration is correct?
o: It was about 423.9 ppm, the highest level in approximately two million years.
It was close to the pre-industrial level and represented a two-century low.
It was below 280 ppm because of increased ocean absorption.
It was about 1,000 ppm, the highest level since the formation of Earth.
92.x: CO₂ reached about 423.9 ppm in 2024, described as the highest concentration in approximately two million years; the pre-industrial level was around 280 ppm.
92.tq: Combine a precise numerical value with its historical comparison.

92.s: The Keeling curve refers to the continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide measured at:
o: Mauna Loa, Hawaii, maintained since 1958 by Charles David Keeling
Barrow, Alaska, maintained by the IPCC
Vostok, Antarctica, maintained since 1979 by the WMO
92.x: The Keeling curve is the continuous atmospheric CO2 record from Mauna Loa, Hawaii, begun in 1958 by Charles David Keeling.
92.tq: Combine the place, starting year and scientist to avoid location and agency swaps.

92.s: Which source is particularly useful for reconstructing past atmospheric carbon dioxide and temperature from trapped air bubbles?
92.x: Ice cores preserve trapped air bubbles that provide evidence of past atmospheric CO2 concentrations and temperatures.
92.tq: Apply the indicator to the historical reconstruction it naturally provides.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin 2025 (data for 2024):
1. Atmospheric CO2 rose by 3.5 ppm in 2024, the largest annual rise since 1957.
2. Methane stood at about 266% of its pre-industrial level.
3. Nitrous oxide stood at about 152% of its pre-industrial level.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: CO2 rose 3.5 ppm to 423.9 ppm, the biggest rise since 1957. Statement 2 is correct: CH4 is at 266% of pre-industrial. Statement 3 is wrong: 152% is the figure for CO2; N2O is at 125%. So '1 and 2 only'.
92.tq: CO2 152%, CH4 266%, N2O 125% - don't swap them.

92.s: During 1971–2010, the oceans absorbed approximately what proportion of the extra energy associated with warming?
92.x: The oceans took up more than 90% of the extra energy during 1971–2010.
92.tq: Identify the approximate range rather than choosing an absolute claim.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about observed cryospheric changes:
1. Both the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets are losing mass.
2. Arctic sea ice shrank by approximately 3.5–4.1% per decade during 1979–2012.
3. Antarctic sea ice has shown uninterrupted expansion since 2015.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Both major ice sheets are losing mass, and Arctic sea ice declined by about 3.5–4.1% per decade during 1979–2012. The statement about uninterrupted Antarctic expansion is incorrect.
92.tq: Find the false trend statement among otherwise precise cryosphere observations.

92.s: The Antarctic sea-ice collapse since 2015 has been associated with which of the following processes?
o: Weakening of westerlies and permanent cooling of Circumpolar Deep Water
Complete cessation of greenhouse-gas emissions over Antarctica
Strengthening of westerlies, upward movement of warm Circumpolar Deep Water and a feedback loop inhibiting new ice formation
Increased formation of cold deep water that freezes the surrounding ocean
92.x: Greenhouse gases and the ozone hole strengthened the westerlies, which lifted warm Circumpolar Deep Water and initiated a feedback loop that prevents new ice formation.
92.tq: Trace the causal chain instead of selecting a single isolated factor.

92.s: Ocean acidification is primarily caused by which of the following processes?
o: Evaporation of seawater and formation of sulphuric acid
Absorption of atmospheric CO2 by oceans and formation of carbonic acid
Freezing of seawater and release of hydrochloric acid
Absorption of atmospheric oxygen and formation of nitric acid
92.x: When oceans absorb carbon dioxide, carbonic acid forms, lowering ocean pH and causing acidification.
92.tq: Link the environmental effect with the specific chemical process responsible.

92.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding coral bleaching and recovery?
o: Acidification permanently eliminates all coral species within one year.
Coral bleaching is caused only by sulphate aerosols and recovery is immediate.
Warming prevents bleaching by increasing coral growth.
Warming can drive coral bleaching, and recovery may take more than 15 years.
92.x: Warming contributes to coral bleaching, and recovery can take 15 years or more.
92.tq: Choose the precise effect-and-recovery statement rather than an absolute ecological claim.

92.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Issue — Principal effect
o: Habitat loss — Oxygen depletion caused by oil spillage
92.x: Global warming is associated with rising sea levels. Air pollution is associated with respiratory illness, whereas patches of cooling are linked with sub-regional temperature variation.
92.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate reversed cause-effect relationships.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Glacier melt and ocean acidification are observed or projected effects associated with global warming.
2. Extreme weather events and coral bleaching are environmental effects associated with climate change.
3. Species loss and health risks are among the wider consequences of climate change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements are correct. Climate change is associated with glacier melt, ocean acidification, extreme weather, coral bleaching, species loss and health risks.
92.tq: When all statements describe related effects without an exaggerated restriction, test the comprehensive option carefully.

92.s: With reference to environmental effects, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Burning plastic has no effect on plant growth.
Oil spillage can cause oxygen depletion in water bodies.
Oil spillage commonly increases dissolved oxygen in affected water bodies.
Burning plastic enhances seed germination by releasing nutrients.
92.x: Oil spillage can cause oxygen depletion in water bodies. Burning plastic can reduce seed germination, not enhance it.
92.tq: Identify the direct ecological consequence rather than choosing an absolute or reversed effect.

92.s: Which year marked the first occasion on which the global mean temperature exceeded 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level?
92.x: The year 2024 was reported as the first year in which the global mean temperature exceeded 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level.
92.tq: Distinguish the specific record year from nearby climate-policy years.

92.s: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 assessed that updated nationally determined contributions would lead approximately to warming of:
92.x: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 projected approximately 2.3–2.5°C of warming even with updated NDCs.
92.tq: Test the projected range and distinguish it from the Paris temperature goals.

92.s: According to the UNEP Limiting Overshoot assessment, which pair correctly represents the projected warming outcomes?
o: 2.6°C if every pledge is delivered; 1.8°C under current policies
1.5°C if every pledge is delivered; 2.0°C under current policies
1.8°C under current policies; 1.5°C if every pledge is delivered
1.8°C if every pledge is delivered; 2.6°C under current policies
92.x: The assessment indicates 1.8°C if every pledge is delivered and 2.6°C under current policies. It outlines an overshoot, peak and decline pathway back below 1.5°C by 2100.
92.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by matching each outcome to the policy condition.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding carbon bombs:
1. A carbon bomb is a fossil-fuel project capable of emitting over 1 gigatonne of CO2.
2. LINGO has identified 425 such carbon bombs.
3. The identified projects would use the 1.5°C carbon budget twice over.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Each carbon bomb can emit over 1 Gt CO2; LINGO identified 425, and their combined emissions would consume the 1.5°C carbon budget twice over.
92.tq: Combine the definition, count and consequence without confusing gigatonne with megatonne.

92.s: Which of the following pairs of Indian coal mines is included among the carbon-bomb projects identified by LINGO?
o: Gevra in Chhattisgarh and Rajmahal in Jharkhand
Jharia in Bihar and Neyveli in Tamil Nadu
Singrauli in Uttar Pradesh and Talcher in Odisha
Korba in Madhya Pradesh and Raniganj in West Bengal
92.x: The listed examples include the Gevra coal mine in Chhattisgarh and the Rajmahal coal mine in Jharkhand.
92.tq: Start from the sure mine-location pair and reject geographically swapped alternatives.

92.s: In the terminology used in climate-policy discussions, the sequence ‘overshoot, peak and decline’ refers to:
o: The successive stages of a tropical cyclone
The stages of change in greenhouse-gas emissions or warming before a subsequent reduction
The three phases of carbon capture equipment
The three layers of the atmospheric ozone column
92.x: ‘Overshoot, peak and decline’ describes the trajectory in which warming or emissions exceed a level, reach a maximum, and then decrease.
92.tq: Choose the option that preserves the stated sequence and its climate-policy context.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gases emitted by the activities of a person, organisation or product, expressed in tonnes of CO2 per year.
2. Carbon sequestration means storing carbon in sinks such as soil carbon, biochar, agroforestry and forests.
3. CCUS refers to machines that pull CO2 straight from ambient air.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: this is the definition of carbon footprint. Statement 2 is correct: sequestration stores carbon in sinks like soil, biochar, agroforestry and forests. Statement 3 is wrong: pulling CO2 from ambient air is direct air capture; CCUS captures CO2 from factory flue gases (point sources). So '1 and 2 only'.
92.tq: CCUS = point source (flue gas); DAC = ambient air.

92.s: India’s CCUS road map, as described in the context of sectoral application, covers primarily:
o: Industry, while agricultural removal is associated with soil carbon, biochar and agroforestry
Only household cooking, while agriculture and industry are excluded
Only direct air capture facilities in urban areas
92.x: India’s CCUS road map covers industry. Agricultural carbon removal is associated with measures such as soil carbon management, biochar and agroforestry.
92.tq: Identify the correct sectoral allocation and reject the reversed scope.

92.s: Why does India's CCUS road map leave out agriculture?
o: Agriculture is legally prohibited from participating in carbon-removal programmes.
Farm emissions are diffuse and therefore are not treated as a concentrated CCUS source.
Agricultural emissions consist exclusively of ozone-depleting substances.
Agriculture does not produce any greenhouse-gas emissions.
92.x: Agriculture is left out because farm emissions are diffuse, making them unsuitable for treatment as a concentrated source in the CCUS road map.
92.tq: Link the policy omission to the stated practical characteristic of the sector.

92.s:
Which of the following combinations is correct regarding the present climate situation and the expected near-term event?

1. The world is described as being in a 1.5°C world.
2. A strong El Niño is expected in 2027.
3. The first calendar year above 1.5°C was 2024.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All three statements are correct: the current climate is described as a 1.5°C world, a strong El Niño is expected in 2027, and 2024 was the first calendar year above 1.5°C.
92.tq: Separate present-status, forecast and first-occurrence facts before selecting the coded combination.

92.s: India sought clarity at the Bonn talks on the use of which concept for climate policy?
92.x: India sought clarity at the Bonn talks on how tipping points could be used for policy-making.
92.tq: Use the distinctive policy term associated with the reported diplomatic discussion.

92.s: India's country-level social cost of carbon is reported to be:
92.x: India's country-level social cost of carbon is reported as $86 per tonne of CO2, the highest globally.
92.tq: For numerical options, distinguish the exact reported figure from nearby values.

92.s: The 2009 United States endangerment finding was legally connected with which case?
92.x: The 2009 US 'endangerment finding' on six greenhouse gases, which let the EPA regulate vehicle GHG emissions, flowed from the Supreme Court's ruling in Massachusetts v. EPA (2007). The US has since repealed that finding.
92.tq: Use the exact authority and case-name pairing rather than a thematically similar title.

92.s: Which one of the following statements about the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is correct?
o: It was fully enforced from 1 January 2025.
It was fully enforced from 1 January 2024.
It is scheduled to be fully enforced from 1 January 2027.
It was fully enforced from 1 January 2026.
92.x: The European Union's CBAM was fully enforced from 1 January 2026.
92.tq: Distinguish the implementation year from nearby transition or proposed dates.

93.s: Which statement best explains why ocean acidification is sometimes called the ‘evil twin of global warming’?
o: It refers to the cooling of the deep ocean during global warming.
Ocean acidification causes only atmospheric warming and not marine effects.
Ocean acidification is another major consequence of anthropogenic carbon dioxide affecting the oceans.
Both phenomena are caused exclusively by methane emissions.
93.x: Ocean acidification is called the ‘evil twin of global warming’ or ‘the other CO2 problem’ because anthropogenic carbon dioxide produces a distinct chemical threat to marine systems.
93.tq: Translate the descriptive epithet into its underlying environmental relationship.

93.s: Approximately what fraction of anthropogenic carbon dioxide is absorbed by the oceans?
93.x: The oceans absorb about one-third of anthropogenic carbon dioxide; the estimate is also expressed as roughly 30–40%.
93.tq: Distinguish the approximate fraction from nearby percentage ranges.

93.s:
Consider the following sequence in ocean carbonate chemistry:
1. Carbonic acid releases hydrogen ions and bicarbonate.
2. Atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater.
3. Extra hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions.
4. Less carbonate remains available for shell formation.
Which is the correct sequence?
93.x: Dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid, which releases hydrogen ions and bicarbonate. The hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions, reducing carbonate availability for shells.
