The agency districts carry most of the State’s malaria and scrub typhus burden.
Agency districts have no significant vector-borne disease burden.
The burden is concentrated exclusively in the major coastal cities.
114.x: The agency or tribal districts carry most of Andhra Pradesh’s malaria and scrub typhus burden, making them a priority for surveillance and control.
114.tq: Use the AP-specific geographical trend and reject absolute location claims.

114.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh in 2025, which of the following is correct?
o: Malaria: 5,268 cases and no deaths; dengue: 6,453 cases and 2 deaths
Malaria: 7,119 cases and 8 deaths; dengue: 2,686 cases and 5 deaths
Malaria: 7,895 cases and 8 deaths; dengue: 1,475 cases and 5 deaths
Malaria: 7,871 cases and no deaths; dengue: 5,555 cases and 5 deaths
114.x: In 2025, Andhra Pradesh recorded 7,119 malaria cases with 8 deaths and 2,686 dengue cases with 5 deaths in the cited data.
114.tq: Read the paired case-and-death figures together rather than matching cases alone.

114.s: Which statement correctly describes the 2025 Andhra Pradesh figures for AES/JE and chikungunya?
o: AES/JE: 2 cases and 146 deaths; chikungunya: 52 deaths
AES/JE: 146 cases and 8 deaths; chikungunya: 941 cases
AES/JE: 52 cases and 2 deaths; chikungunya: 146 cases
AES/JE: 146 cases and 2 deaths; chikungunya: 52 cases
114.x: The reported 2025 figures were 146 AES/JE cases with 2 deaths and 52 chikungunya cases.
114.tq: Keep case and death figures separate while matching the two diseases.

114.s: Which of the following correctly represents Andhra Pradesh’s 2024 malaria and dengue figures?
114.x: The 2024 figures were 7,871 malaria cases and 5,555 dengue cases, with zero malaria deaths reported in the cited APSES data.
114.tq: Use the year-number association and reject figures belonging to adjacent years.

114.s: Free long-lasting insecticidal nets were reported to cover approximately how many people in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam, at a cost of Rs 19.25 crore?
114.x: Free LLINs were reported for approximately 7.80 lakh people in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam, involving an expenditure of Rs 19.25 crore.
114.tq: Separate the beneficiary count from the expenditure figure.

115.s: The term 'triple burden' in public health refers to the simultaneous presence of:
o: Maternal diseases, childhood diseases and old-age diseases
Communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and injuries
115.x: The triple burden combines communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and injuries such as road accidents and trauma.
115.tq: Use the defining components of the term rather than confusing it with the dual burden.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Non-communicable diseases account for 57% of all deaths in India.
2. Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in India.
3. The share of non-communicable diseases in deaths has declined from 61.8% in 2016 to 37.9% in 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the trend: the recorded share was 37.9% in 1990 and 61.8% in 2016 in the cited study.
115.tq: Check the direction of the numerical trend before selecting the coded combination.

115.s: Dual burden of malnutrition means the coexistence of:
o: Undernutrition with adult overweight and obesity
115.x: The dual burden of malnutrition refers to undernutrition existing alongside adult overweight and obesity.
115.tq: Distinguish the nutritional dual burden from the public-health dual burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases.

115.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the leading causes of death in India and in the world?
o: Tuberculosis leads in India, while dengue is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cardiovascular diseases lead in India, while ischaemic heart disease is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cancer leads in India, while cardiovascular disease is absent from the global ranking.
Injuries lead in India, while chronic respiratory disease is the single biggest global killer.
115.x: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death in India, while WHO estimates identify ischaemic heart disease as the world's single biggest killer.
115.tq: Keep the country-level and global-level comparisons separate before matching the two answers.

115.s: The India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative is associated with which combination of institutions and study?
o: ICMR, PHFI and IHME; Global Burden of Disease study
WHO, UNICEF and FAO; World Health Survey
NCDC, FSSAI and NITI Aayog; National Family Health Survey
ICMR, ISRO and DRDO; Census of India
115.x: The estimates are produced through the ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative, which forms part of the Global Burden of Disease study.
115.tq: Match the institutional group with the named study rather than with a nearby health survey.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding non-communicable disease mortality in India:
1. The probability of dying from an NCD rose in India between 2001 and 2019.
2. The rise was especially noted among women over 40 and men over 55.
3. Most countries reduced NCD deaths during the same period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct: most countries reduced NCD deaths, whereas India's probability of dying from an NCD rose, particularly in the specified age-sex groups.
115.tq: Compare the general international trend with India's contrasting trend and retain all supported statements.

115.s: The 'dual burden of disease' in India refers to:
o: Rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases
Coexistence of undernutrition and obesity in the same household
High maternal mortality alongside high infant mortality
Simultaneous rise of injuries and mental illness
115.x: Dual burden (PYQ answer) means persistent communicable diseases such as TB, malaria and dengue coexisting with rising NCDs. Undernutrition with obesity is the dual burden of malnutrition; adding injuries gives the triple burden; the other option is not the term.
115.tq: Dual = CDs + NCDs; triple adds injuries.

115.s:
Arrange the following stages of epidemiological transition in the correct chronological order:
A. Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases
B. Age of Pestilence and Famine
C. Age of Receding Pandemics
115.x: Omran's sequence proceeds from the Age of Pestilence and Famine to the Age of Receding Pandemics and then to the Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases.
115.tq: Identify the initial high-infection stage and the final NCD-dominant stage, then place the intermediate stage.

115.s: Which stage of epidemiological transition is characterised by declining infectious deaths due to improvements in sanitation and vaccination?
o: Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases
115.x: In the Age of Receding Pandemics, infectious deaths decline as sanitation and vaccination improve.
115.tq: Associate the stage with its defining health pattern rather than its name alone.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is undergoing a linear shift from infectious diseases to non-communicable diseases.
2. Life expectancy in India rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023.
3. Maternal mortality ratio has fallen by 86% since 1990.
4. Under-five mortality rate has fallen by 78% since 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All four statements correctly describe the epidemiological and mortality transition reported for India.
115.tq: Check each numerical and trend statement independently before selecting the complete combination.

115.s: Which one of the following is NOT a communicable disease?
115.x: Hypertension is a non-communicable lifestyle-related disease. Chikungunya, typhoid and Nipah are communicable diseases.
115.tq: Classify each option by whether it is caused by a transmissible pathogen.

115.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of the four major non-communicable disease groups?
o: Cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes
115.x: The four major NCD groups are cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes.
115.tq: Look for a set in which every item belongs to the same classification, not merely one or two items.

115.s: Meningococcal meningitis is primarily transmitted through:
o: Respiratory droplets from person to person
115.x: Meningococcal meningitis spreads from person to person through respiratory droplets. Vomiting and neck stiffness are among its symptoms.
115.tq: Separate a respiratory-droplet infection from mosquito-borne diseases by identifying the mode of transmission.

115.s: Which one of the following is NOT a lifestyle disease?
115.x: Malaria is a communicable disease caused by Plasmodium and spread by mosquitoes, so it is not a lifestyle disease (PYQ). Diabetes, hypertension and obesity are lifestyle-related NCDs.
115.tq: Odd one out: malaria (pathogen-caused).

115.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the ICMR initiatives associated with tuberculosis and malaria respectively?
o: India TB Research Consortium and MERA
MERA and India TB Research Consortium
NCDC and India TB Research Consortium
115.x: The India TB Research Consortium is associated with tuberculosis, while MERA is the ICMR initiative associated with malaria.
115.tq: Use the disease-specific association and beware of reversing the two initiatives.

115.s: A national tuberculosis prevalence survey in India is notable because it covers:
o: All States but not Union Territories
115.x: The national TB prevalence survey covers all States and Union Territories.
115.tq: Watch for restrictive words such as 'only' and distinguish complete national coverage from partial coverage.

115.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Dengue — Aedes mosquito
2. Chikungunya — Aedes mosquito
3. Zika — Aedes mosquito
4. Japanese encephalitis — Culex mosquito
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
115.x: Dengue, chikungunya and Zika are carried by Aedes mosquitoes, whereas Japanese encephalitis is carried by Culex mosquitoes.
115.tq: Start with the repeated Aedes association and verify the contrasting Culex pair.

115.s: Which one of the following statements regarding infectious disease surveillance in India is correct?
o: NCDC wastewater surveillance covers 10 cities and excludes antimicrobial resistance.
ICMR wastewater surveillance declined from 50 to 5 cities and tracks only one virus.
ICMR wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities and tracks 10 viruses, along with antimicrobial resistance.
The programme tracks only dengue and chikungunya and does not include avian influenza.
115.x: ICMR's wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities, tracks 10 viruses including avian influenza, and also monitors antimicrobial resistance.
115.tq: Check the direction of expansion, the number of cities and the scope of surveillance together.

115.s: Which agency's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre was activated following the two Nipah cases reported in January 2026?
115.x: The NCDC's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre, or PHEOC, was activated in response to the reported Nipah cases.
115.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to distinguish the public-health response authority.

115.s: According to NFHS-5 data for 2019–21, which of the following statements is correct regarding overweight or obesity?
o: 24% of women and 23% of men were overweight or obese.
34% of women and 33% of men were overweight or obese.
23% of women and 24% of men were overweight or obese.
14% of women and 13% of men were overweight or obese.
115.x: NFHS-5 reported overweight or obesity among 24% of women and 23% of men for 2019–21.
115.tq: Read the sex-wise figures carefully; the close reversal is the intended trap.

115.s: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has capped trans fat in fats and oils at:
115.x: FSSAI has capped trans fat in fats and oils at 2%.
115.tq: Use the precise regulatory limit rather than the broader dietary-risk information.

115.s:
The United Nations General Assembly declaration on non-communicable diseases and mental health includes which of the following newer areas or determinants?
1. Oral health and lung health
2. Childhood cancer
3. Air pollution and lead
4. Digital harms such as screen time
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: The declaration covers oral and lung health, childhood cancer, air pollution, lead and digital harms such as screen time. It also calls for stronger regulation of tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes.
115.tq: When all listed items belong to the stated expansion of scope, select the complete combination.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bakery products are often rich in hydrogenated fats containing trans fats.
2. Excess intake of trans fats raises the risk of non-communicable diseases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Both statements are correct (PYQ): bakery products use hydrogenated fats containing trans fats, and excess trans fats raise NCD risk, which is why FSSAI caps trans fat at 2% in fats and oils. '1 only' and '2 only' each reject a true statement; 'Neither' rejects both.
115.tq: Trans fats: bakery + NCD risk, both true.

115.s:
Which of the following are main risk factors for lifestyle (non-communicable) diseases?
1. Unhealthy diet
2. Physical inactivity
3. Tobacco use
4. Alcohol use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: All four are main NCD risk factors (UPSC), along with urbanisation and ageing. Every other option leaves out at least one listed risk factor.
115.tq: NCD risks: diet, inactivity, tobacco, alcohol.

115.s: According to the Global Cancer Observatory projection, the number of cancer cases in India is expected to increase from approximately 1.41 million in 2022 to what number by 2045?
115.x: The projected number of cancer cases is expected to rise from 1.41 million in 2022 to 2.46 million in 2045.
115.tq: Use the precise projected figure rather than estimating from the percentage increase.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cancer notification in India:
1. Cancer is not nationally notifiable in India.
2. Seventeen States have made cancer a notifiable disease.
3. Telangana was the most recent State to make cancer notifiable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct: cancer is not nationally notifiable, 17 States have notified it, and Telangana was the most recent State to do so.
115.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the distinction between national and State-level notification.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD):
1. It was formerly known as NPCDCS.
2. It runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and Community Health Centres.
3. It screens everyone above 40 years of age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: NP-NCD was formerly NPCDCS (2010). Statement 2 is correct: NCD clinics are run at district hospitals and CHCs. Statement 3 is wrong: screening covers everyone over 30, not 40. So '1 and 2 only'; '2 only' omits a true statement, and the options with 3 include the wrong age.
115.tq: NP-NCD: ex-NPCDCS, clinics at DH/CHC, screening 30+.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the funding pattern of NP-NCD:
1. The usual Centre-State funding ratio is 60:40.
2. The funding ratio for North-Eastern and hilly States is 90:10.
3. The 90:10 ratio applies uniformly to all States and Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: The usual funding ratio is 60:40, while North-Eastern and hilly States receive funding in the ratio of 90:10. The latter ratio does not apply uniformly to all States and Union Territories.
115.tq: Reject the overgeneralised statement by separating the normal ratio from the special-category ratio.

115.s:
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs screen beneficiaries for which of the following conditions?
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes
3. Oral cancer
4. Breast and cervical cancers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs screen for hypertension, diabetes, and oral, breast and cervical cancers.
115.tq: Use the inclusive option when all listed screening services belong to the same programme.

115.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the relevant SDG 3 health target?
o: Premature NCD deaths — reduce by one-half
Premature NCD deaths — reduce by one-third
115.x: SDG 3 includes the target of reducing premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by one-third. It also promotes mental health and seeks to halve road-traffic deaths.
115.tq: Discriminate between the different numerical targets under the same goal.

115.s: Tele-MANAS, available in all 36 States and Union Territories, provides:
o: Online registration of every UIP vaccination
115.x: Tele-MANAS gives round-the-clock tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and UTs. Vaccination registration is U-WIN; cancer screening and trauma surgery are not its role.
115.tq: Tele-MANAS = 24x7 mental-health helpline.

115.s: Which initiative provides 24×7 tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and Union Territories?
115.x: Tele-MANAS provides round-the-clock tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and Union Territories.
115.tq: Link the service function—tele-mental health—with the correct national initiative.

115.s: Which one of the following public-health measures was undertaken in Andhra Pradesh in relation to scrub typhus?
o: A ban on all poultry products was imposed.
A national TB prevalence survey was discontinued.
A Culex eradication mission was launched.
115.x: Andhra Pradesh set up task forces for scrub typhus under the cited state health measures.
115.tq: Identify the exact administrative response and reject measures not stated for the disease.

115.s: Uddanam, located in which district of Andhra Pradesh, is associated with chronic kidney disease of unknown cause (CKDu)?
115.x: Uddanam is in Srikakulam district and is associated with CKDu. Palasa is the location of the kidney centre, while Mangalagiri is the location of AIIMS.
115.tq: Separate the geographical region from the nearby institutions associated with it.

115.s:
With reference to the investigation into chronic kidney disease of unknown cause (CKDu) in Uddanam, consider the following statements:
1. Soil, water, blood and urine samples are being tested for viruses and protozoa.
2. The testing is being done with CSIR-IICT, Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the samples are tested for pesticides and heavy metals, not viruses and protozoa. Statement 2 is correct: testing is with CSIR-IICT Hyderabad. So '2 only'; '1 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong statement, and 'Neither' rejects the true one.
115.tq: Uddanam CKDu: pesticides/heavy metals, CSIR-IICT Hyderabad.

115.s: Which institution conducts CKDu screening camps in the Uddanam region?
115.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri conducts screening camps for chronic kidney disease of unknown cause in the Uddanam region.
115.tq: Distinguish the institution conducting field screening from the laboratory involved in testing.

115.s: Which one of the following places is associated with Andhra Pradesh's first Diabetic Foot and Ulcer Clinic?
115.x: Andhra Pradesh's first Diabetic Foot and Ulcer Clinic was opened at Vizianagaram.
115.tq: Identify the location of the specialised clinic, not the locations of the kidney-related facilities.

115.s: The increasing importance of non-communicable diseases requires the health system to shift primarily from:
o: Hospital care to environmental sampling only
Curative care to screening and prevention
Prevention and screening to curative care
115.x: The growing NCD burden requires a shift from a predominantly curative approach towards screening and prevention.
115.tq: Apply the policy implication of changing disease patterns to the health-system approach.

115.s: The interim report on Uddanam CKDu found a high incidence of kidney disease particularly in:
115.x: The interim report found a high level of kidney disease in Kaviti mandal of the Uddanam region.
115.tq: Identify the specific mandal rather than selecting the broader district or a related town.

115.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26 reference, the share of non-communicable diseases in the disease burden is approximately:
115.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 says NCDs cause about 57% of all deaths in India. 37.9% was the NCD share in 1990 (Lancet study), and the other figures are not NCD shares.
115.tq: Distinguish the NCD share from the separate outbreak and mortality-reduction percentages.

115.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital associated with the Uddanam kidney disease issue is located at:
115.x: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam district.
115.tq: Use the place-specific association instead of confusing the hospital with the screening institution.

116.s: A disease remains constantly present at a baseline level in a particular area. This condition is termed:
116.x: A disease constantly present at a baseline level in an area is described as endemic.
116.tq: Apply the definition to a short public-health situation rather than memorising the term in isolation.

116.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

Term — Meaning
o: Pandemic — Spread across countries and continents
Endemic — Sudden severe outbreak in a region
Epizootic — Constant human disease at baseline level
116.x: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across countries and continents. Epizootic refers to an epidemic among animals, while endemic refers to constant baseline presence.
116.tq: Distinguish the four near-sounding terms by their geographical or host scope.

116.s: An epidemic occurring among animals is called:
116.x: An epidemic among animals is termed an epizootic.
116.tq: Break the terminology into its host-specific meaning and reject human-population terms.

116.s: A sudden outbreak of a disease in a severe form in a particular region at a particular time is termed:
116.x: An epidemic is a sudden, severe outbreak in a region at a particular time. Endemic means constantly present at a baseline level; a pandemic is an epidemic spread across countries and continents; an epizootic is an epidemic among animals.
116.tq: Epidemic = sudden + regional; pandemic = cross-continent.

116.s: Ebola virus was first found in 1976 near which river and in which country?
o: Ebola River, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Congo River, Republic of the Congo
116.x: Ebola virus was first found in 1976 near the Ebola River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
116.tq: Combine the year, geographical feature and country rather than relying on the river name alone.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about Ebola:
1. Its genus is Orthoebolavirus.
2. It belongs to the family Filoviridae.
3. The Zaire species is regarded as the deadliest.
4. Fruit bats are identified as its reservoir.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: All four statements are correct. Ebola is associated with the genus Orthoebolavirus, family Filoviridae, fruit-bat reservoirs and the particularly deadly Zaire species.
116.tq: Test the complete classification-reservoir cluster through an all-inclusive option.

116.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Outbreak — Intermediate host
116.x: Civet cats were identified as the intermediate host associated with SARS. Dromedary camels are associated with MERS, while pangolins were suspected intermediate hosts for SARS-CoV-2.
116.tq: Discriminate between closely related outbreak-host associations.

116.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

1. H1N1 — Influenza A subtype
2. H5N1 — Avian influenza A
3. MERS — 2012 outbreak
4. SARS — 2002–03 outbreak
116.x: All four associations are correct. H1N1 is an Influenza A subtype, H5N1 is avian influenza A, MERS is associated with 2012 and SARS with 2002–03.
116.tq: Check each outbreak against its virus type or period before selecting the complete combination.

116.s: Which of the following statements regarding the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak is NOT correct?
o: The fourth India-Africa Forum Summit was postponed.
It involved the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
It was officially declared a pandemic emergency.
It was declared a PHEIC in May 2026.
116.x: The outbreak was declared a PHEIC but not a pandemic emergency. It involved the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, and the fourth India-Africa Forum Summit was postponed.
116.tq: Find the single reversed or overstated institutional description.

116.s: The 2014–16 West African Ebola outbreak mainly affected which countries?
116.x: The 2014–16 West African Ebola outbreak mainly affected Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.
116.tq: Identify the three-country cluster rather than selecting neighbouring regional states.

116.s: Which one of the following combinations contains only diseases or outbreaks that were declared PHEICs before or during the COVID-19 period listed?
116.x: The listed earlier PHEICs included H1N1 in 2009, polio in 2014 and Zika in 2016. The listed PHEIC chronology also included Ebola in 2014 and 2019 and COVID-19 on 30 January 2020.
116.tq: Use chronology and exact PHEIC status to eliminate plausible but unsupported outbreaks.

116.s: The H1N1 'swine flu', an Influenza A subtype first found in North America, was declared a pandemic by WHO in:
116.x: WHO declared H1N1 a pandemic in June 2009. March 2020 (11 March) is the COVID-19 pandemic declaration; 2006 is the first Indian avian influenza outbreak (Navapur); 2014 is the year of the polio PHEIC and the West African Ebola outbreak.
116.tq: Swine flu pandemic = June 2009; COVID pandemic = 11 March 2020.

116.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched with a major outbreak in India?

1. Nipah — Kerala from 2018 onwards
2. Zika — Kerala, 2021
3. Chandipura — Gujarat, 2024
4. Plague — Surat, Gujarat, 1994
116.x: All four pairs are correct: Nipah has struck Kerala from 2018 onwards, Zika appeared in Kerala in 2021, Chandipura (sandfly-borne) broke out in Gujarat in 2024, and plague (Yersinia pestis) hit Surat, Gujarat, in 1994. Hence '1, 2, 3 and 4'.
116.tq: Check each disease-location-year association before accepting the complete combination.

116.s: Chandipura outbreak in 2024 was reported in which State and was spread by which vector?
116.x: The Chandipura outbreak occurred in Gujarat in 2024 and was spread by sandflies.
116.tq: Combine place, year and vector to avoid partial-match distractors.

116.s: The causative organism of the plague outbreak reported in Surat in 1994 was:
116.x: The plague outbreak in Surat, Gujarat, in 1994 was associated with Yersinia pestis and transmission through rat fleas.
116.tq: Distinguish a bacterial causative organism from viral outbreak agents.

116.s: The first Indian outbreak of avian influenza was reported at Navapur in:
116.x: The first Indian outbreak of avian influenza was reported at Navapur in Maharashtra in 2006.
116.tq: Combine the first-outbreak location with the year and State.

116.s: In January 2026, two Nipah cases were reported in:
116.x: Two Nipah cases were reported in West Bengal in January 2026.
116.tq: Link the disease, number of cases, place and month instead of relying only on the disease's usual geographic association.

116.s: SARS-CoV-2 causes which disease, and what does its name signify?
o: MERS, meaning Middle East Respiratory Syndrome
SARS, meaning Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome
116.x: SARS-CoV-2 causes COVID-19, which stands for Coronavirus Disease 2019.
116.tq: Separate the virus name from the disease name and its formal expansion.

116.s: SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in which place and month-year?
116.x: SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in Wuhan in Hubei province of China in December 2019.
116.tq: Combine location and time rather than selecting the correct place with a wrong date.

116.s: Which receptor enables SARS-CoV-2 to enter human cells?
116.x: SARS-CoV-2 enters cells through the ACE2 receptor.
116.tq: Identify the precise receptor instead of confusing it with a viral protein or immune-cell marker.

116.s: WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on:
116.x: WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March 2020. The date 30 January 2020 refers to the declaration of COVID-19 as a PHEIC.
116.tq: Discriminate between the PHEIC date and the later pandemic declaration date.

116.s: Which COVID-19 variant was first found in India?
116.x: The Delta variant was first found in India. Alpha was associated with the United Kingdom, Beta with South Africa and Omicron with southern Africa.
116.tq: Test one distinctive variant-location association directly.

116.s:
Arrange the following COVID-19 events in chronological order:
A. Omicron third wave in India
B. First COVID-19 case in Kerala
C. Delta second wave
D. Peak of the first wave
116.x: The first case in Kerala occurred on 30 January 2020, the first wave peaked in September 2020, the Delta second wave occurred in April–May 2021 and the Omicron third wave came in January 2022.
116.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two intervening waves by date.

116.s: The first COVID-19 case in India was reported in which State and on what date?
116.x: The first COVID-19 case in India was reported in Kerala on 30 January 2020.
116.tq: Pair the correct State with the exact date and reject date-state swaps.

116.s:
Which of the following formed part of India's COVID-19 strategy?

1. Test-track-treat-vaccinate
2. COVID-appropriate behaviour
3. A three-tier facility arrangement
4. MHA Empowered Groups
116.x: All four were components of India's COVID-19 response strategy: test-track-treat-vaccinate, COVID-appropriate behaviour, MHA Empowered Groups and a three-tier facility arrangement.
116.tq: Recognise the complete policy cluster and avoid excluding the administrative component.

116.s: The Lancet report released on 24 February 2022 estimated that approximately how many children in India lost a parent or caregiver?
116.x: The Lancet report of 24 February 2022 estimated that about 19 lakh children in India lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19. The figure covers loss of a parent or caregiver, not only children who lost both parents.
116.tq: Use the approximate figure and distinguish it from other child-impact estimates.

116.s: Which statement regarding PM CARES for Children is correct?
o: It covers children who lost both parents, the surviving parent or a guardian, with support at 23 years.
It covers only children who lost one parent and provides no education support.
It provides only health insurance to COVID-19 patients of all ages.
It is an international vaccine-access mechanism.
116.x: PM CARES for Children covers children who lost both parents, the surviving parent or a guardian. It provides health insurance and education support, with financial support at 23 years.
116.tq: Test the scheme's beneficiary categories and benefit structure together.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about the PMGKP insurance scheme for health workers:
1. It provided an insurance cover of Rs 50 lakh.
2. It was implemented by the National Health Authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct: PMGKP gave health workers Rs 50 lakh cover. Statement 2 is wrong: it was implemented by New India Assurance. So '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong implementer, and 'Neither' rejects the true cover amount.
116.tq: PMGKP: Rs 50 lakh, New India Assurance.

116.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Vaccine — Platform or route
116.x: Covaxin is based on an inactivated whole-virus platform and is administered by injection. Covishield is a viral-vector vaccine, Corbevax is a protein-subunit vaccine and Sputnik V is a viral-vector vaccine.
116.tq: Start from the sure vaccine-platform pair and eliminate swapped platforms.

116.s:
Consider the following pairs (COVID-19 vaccine - developer):
1. Covaxin - Bharat Biotech with ICMR-NIV
2. Corbevax - Biological E, Hyderabad
3. ZyCoV-D - Serum Institute of India
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
116.x: Pair 1 is correct: Covaxin is from Bharat Biotech with ICMR-NIV. Pair 2 is correct: Corbevax is from Biological E, Hyderabad. Pair 3 is wrong: ZyCoV-D is from Zydus; the Serum Institute made Covishield. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses Corbevax and the options with pair 3 are wrong.
116.tq: Serum Institute = Covishield; Zydus = ZyCoV-D (DNA).

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Covishield:
1. It was based on the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine.
2. It was manufactured in India by the Serum Institute of India.
3. It used an adenovirus viral-vector platform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: All three statements are correct. Covishield was the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine made in India by the Serum Institute and used an adenovirus viral vector.
116.tq: Check whether all statements describe the same vaccine before selecting the combined option.

116.s: Which of the following vaccines was described as the world's first intranasal COVID-19 vaccine approved for the primary two-dose schedule and the heterologous booster?
116.x: iNCOVACC, developed by Bharat Biotech, was described as the world's first intranasal COVID-19 vaccine approved for the primary two-dose schedule and the heterologous booster.
116.tq: Use the distinctive route and approval description to identify the vaccine.

116.s: Which vaccine was described as the world's first DNA vaccine approved for use in humans and was administered through a needle-free injector?
116.x: ZyCoV-D, developed by Zydus, was described as the world's first DNA vaccine approved for humans and used a needle-free injector.
116.tq: Match the unusual delivery route and platform with the correct vaccine.

116.s:
Which of the following vaccines used an mRNA platform?

1. Moderna
2. Pfizer-BioNTech
3. Gemcovac-OM
116.x: Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech and Gemcovac-OM are all identified with the mRNA platform.
116.tq: Group all items sharing the same platform and reject the vector and protein-subunit alternatives.

116.s: Vaccine Maitri primarily supplied COVID-19 vaccines to which group of countries?
116.x: Vaccine Maitri supplied vaccines to low- and middle-income countries. It was an international vaccine-support initiative of India.
116.tq: Watch for the scope trap created by restrictive words such as only.

116.s: COVAX was the global equitable-access pillar co-led by which combination?
116.x: COVAX was co-led by the World Health Organization, Gavi and the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations.
116.tq: Identify the exact institutional trio instead of substituting other international bodies.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about India's COVID-19 vaccination drive:
1. It began on 16 January 2021.
2. It was guided by NEGVAC.
3. It crossed 200 crore doses by 17 July 2021.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct: vaccination began on 16 January 2021. Statement 2 is correct: it was guided by NEGVAC. Statement 3 is wrong: 200 crore doses were crossed by 17 July 2022, not 2021. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses NEGVAC, and the options with 3 have the wrong year.
116.tq: Start 16 Jan 2021 (NEGVAC); 200 crore by 17 Jul 2022.

116.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I: Digital vaccination function
(a) Booking
(b) Tracking
(c) Digital certification

List-II: Platform
(i) CoWIN
(ii) PM CARES for Children
(iii) PMGKP

Choose the correct answer:
116.x: CoWIN handled booking, tracking and digital certificates. Therefore all three functions are matched with CoWIN.
116.tq: Identify the single platform responsible for all three digital vaccination functions.

116.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly represents the COVID-19 vaccination milestones in India?
o: 200 crore doses by 21 December 2023; 220.67 crore by 17 July 2022
200 crore doses by 24 February 2022; 220.67 crore by 11 March 2020
200 crore doses by 17 July 2022; 220.67 crore by 21 December 2023
200 crore doses by 16 January 2021; 220.67 crore by 30 January 2020
116.x: India crossed 200 crore doses by 17 July 2022 and 220.67 crore doses by 21 December 2023.
116.tq: Match each cumulative figure with its later date and reject reversed milestones.

116.s: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed which of the following combinations of challenges in India?
o: Health infrastructure and oxygen supply gaps, migrant crisis, and dependence on imported supplies
Only vaccine hesitancy, urban congestion, and shortage of agricultural labour
Defence production gaps, decline in exports, and shortage of school textbooks
Decline in forest cover, coastal erosion, and shortage of irrigation water
116.x: The pandemic exposed gaps in health infrastructure and oxygen supply, created a migrant crisis, and revealed dependence on external supply chains.
116.tq: Use the combination approach to identify the option containing all the linked pandemic lessons.

116.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the digital tools that emerged in response to lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic with their stated area of relevance?
o: CoWIN, U-WIN, ABDM and eSanjeevani — digital health and vaccination-related platforms
CoWIN, Aarogyasri, Covid Pharma and U-WIN — forest and wildlife monitoring platforms
ABDM, YSR Aarogyasri, eSanjeevani and Mo Jeeban — agricultural marketing platforms
U-WIN, Covid Pharma, CoWIN and ward secretariats — disaster-warning platforms
116.x: CoWIN, U-WIN, ABDM and eSanjeevani are the digital tools identified as emerging from the pandemic experience. The other options mix them with unrelated or state-specific response measures.
116.tq: Start from the sure group of four digital health tools and reject options that insert unrelated programmes.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the lessons emerging from the COVID-19 pandemic:
1. One Health is associated with a Quadripartite approach.
2. Equitable access to vaccines is identified as an important lesson.
3. Pandemic preparedness can be separated entirely from animal and environmental health.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the One Health approach links human, animal and environmental health rather than separating them entirely.
116.tq: Find the statement with the extreme word 'entirely'; it reverses the integrated One Health approach.

116.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Initiative — State
o: Door-to-door fever surveys by village volunteers — Gujarat
116.x: Door-to-door fever surveys by village volunteers were an Andhra Pradesh initiative, not a Gujarat initiative. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
116.tq: Find the single wrong State association among familiar containment models.

116.s:
Consider the following pairs (COVID-19 containment initiative - State):
1. Mo Jeeban - Odisha
2. Dharavi model - Kerala
3. Door-to-door fever surveys by village volunteers - Andhra Pradesh
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
116.x: Pair 1 is correct: Mo Jeeban was Odisha's initiative. Pair 2 is wrong: the Dharavi model ('chasing the virus') was in Mumbai, Maharashtra; Kerala's was Break the Chain. Pair 3 is correct: AP ran door-to-door fever surveys through village volunteers. So '1 and 3 only'.
116.tq: Mo Jeeban-Odisha, Dharavi-Mumbai, Bhilwara-Rajasthan, Break the Chain-Kerala, volunteer surveys-AP.

116.s: During the COVID-19 response in Andhra Pradesh, COVID-19 treatment was added to:
116.x: COVID-19 treatment was added to the YSR Aarogyasri scheme in Andhra Pradesh.
116.tq: Discriminate between a state health-coverage scheme and national digital health platforms.

116.s: The Covid Pharma app in Andhra Pradesh was used to track:
o: the number of migrant workers returning to villages
over-the-counter sales of fever and cough medicines
116.x: The Covid Pharma app tracked over-the-counter sales of medicines used for fever and cough, helping monitor possible disease trends.
116.tq: Match the app with its concrete monitoring function rather than with broader pandemic-response activities.

116.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its stated recent relevance?
o: Ebola — PHEIC in May 2026; H1N1 — spike in August 2026; Nipah — West Bengal in January 2026
Ebola — spike in August 2026; H1N1 — PHEIC in May 2026; Nipah — Kerala in January 2026
Ebola — West Bengal in January 2026; H1N1 — PHEIC in May 2026; Nipah — spike in August 2026
Ebola — PHEIC in January 2026; H1N1 — West Bengal in May 2026; Nipah — spike in August 2026
116.x: The stated current-relevance associations are Ebola as a PHEIC in May 2026, an H1N1 spike in August 2026, and Nipah in West Bengal in January 2026.
116.tq: Use the sure event-month pair and then verify the disease-location association.

116.s: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda was declared a PHEIC in:
116.x: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri region and Uganda was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2026.
116.tq: Use the exact month-year combination to distinguish the declaration from earlier PHEICs.

116.s: Which vaccine was identified as the first DNA vaccine?
116.x: ZyCoV-D was identified as the first DNA vaccine in the stated COVID-19 vaccine distinctions.
116.tq: Use first/last terminology to distinguish the DNA-vaccine milestone from the intranasal-vaccine milestone.

116.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: CoWIN — digital tool associated with COVID-19 vaccination management
116.x: YSR Aarogyasri is a health-coverage scheme to which COVID-19 treatment was added in Andhra Pradesh; it is not a vaccine. ZyCoV-D and iNCOVACC are correctly matched with the stated vaccine distinctions.
116.tq: Find the option that swaps a health-coverage scheme with a vaccine classification.

116.s: Door-to-door fever surveys conducted by village volunteers were a COVID-19 containment initiative of:
116.x: Andhra Pradesh conducted door-to-door fever surveys through village volunteers as a containment initiative.
116.tq: Identify the State from the distinctive operational method rather than the model name.

117.s: The Bhore Committee was appointed primarily to:
o: Survey the state of public health
117.x: The Bhore Committee was appointed to survey the state of public health.
117.tq: Match a committee with its stated mandate, not merely its broad sector.

117.s: Which of the following recommendations is associated with the Bhore Committee?
o: Integrated preventive and curative care with a three-tier PHC-based system
Referral Services Complex through village health guides
Consolidation of existing PHCs before expansion only
117.x: The Bhore Committee recommended integrated preventive and curative care and a three-tier PHC-based system.
117.tq: Avoid swapping recommendations among committees with similar health-sector mandates.

117.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their reporting or recommendation period:
A. Shrivastava Committee
B. Bhore Committee
C. Kartar Singh Committee
D. Mudaliar Committee
117.x: The correct sequence is Bhore (1943–46), Mudaliar (1959–62), Kartar Singh (1973), and Shrivastava (1975).
117.tq: Fix the earliest and latest committees first, then arrange the middle two.

117.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Committee)
a. Mudaliar Committee
b. Kartar Singh Committee
c. Shrivastava Committee
List-II (Recommendation)
i. Multipurpose health workers; one PHC per 50,000 people
ii. Community health volunteers or village health guides; Referral Services Complex
iii. Consolidate existing PHCs before expanding; strengthen district hospitals
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: Mudaliar (1959-62) asked to consolidate PHCs and strengthen district hospitals (iii); Kartar Singh (1973) recommended multipurpose workers and one PHC per 50,000 (i); Shrivastava (1975) recommended village health guides and a Referral Services Complex (ii). Only 'a-iii, b-i, c-ii' fits; the other codes swap at least two of these.
117.tq: Mudaliar = consolidate; Kartar Singh = multipurpose workers; Shrivastava = village health guides.

117.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the first contact point in the primary healthcare tier?
117.x: The Sub Health Centre is the first contact point in the primary healthcare tier.
117.tq: Directly identify the facility associated with the stated function.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about population norms for health facilities:
1. A Sub Health Centre covers 5,000 people in plain areas and 3,000 in hilly-tribal areas.
2. A Community Health Centre covers 1,20,000 people in plain areas and 80,000 in hilly-tribal areas.
3. An Urban PHC covers 25,000-30,000 people within a 10 km radius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct (SHC 5,000/3,000). Statement 2 is correct (CHC 1,20,000/80,000). Statement 3 is wrong: an Urban PHC covers 25,000-30,000 people within a 2-3 km radius, not 10 km. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the CHC norm and the others include statement 3.
117.tq: SHC 5k/3k, PHC 30k/20k, CHC 1.2 lakh/80k; UPHC 25-30k within 2-3 km.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the primary healthcare tier:
1. The PHC functions as a referral centre for Sub Health Centres.
2. The population norm for a PHC is 30,000 in plain areas and 20,000 in hilly-tribal areas.
3. The PHC belongs to the secondary healthcare tier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the PHC belongs to the primary tier.
117.tq: Find the statement that reverses the classification of a facility.

117.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
117.x: A PHC is a primary-level referral centre for Sub Health Centres, not a tertiary referral hospital.
117.tq: Find the facility placed in the wrong healthcare tier.

117.s: Community Health Centres are distinguished in the healthcare structure by the provision of:
117.x: CHCs function as referrals for PHCs and are equipped with operation theatres and beds.
117.tq: Use the distinctive infrastructure feature to identify the correct facility.

117.s: According to the stated figures, the number of PHCs as of December 2021 was:
117.x: The stated December 2021 figure is 23,391 PHCs.
117.tq: Distinguish the dated count from the historical and alternative counts.

117.s: The latest revision of the Indian Public Health Standards is:
117.x: IPHS 2022 is the latest revision stated for Indian Public Health Standards.
117.tq: Recall the latest revision year and avoid substituting a policy year.

117.s: IPHS 2022 sets norms for which of the following groups of facilities?
o: Only district hospitals and medical colleges
SHC and HWC, PHC, CHC, sub-district hospitals and district hospitals
Only private hospitals and nursing homes
117.x: IPHS 2022 covers SHC and HWC, PHC, CHC, sub-district hospitals and district hospitals.
117.tq: Select the complete scope instead of an artificially restricted list.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs):
1. They were launched in 2018.
2. 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centres were set up by December 2022 by upgrading SHCs and PHCs.
3. Fewer than 1 lakh AAMs are functioning in 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: launched in 2018. Statement 2 is correct: 1,50,000 HWCs by December 2022, later renamed AAMs. Statement 3 is wrong: more than 1.79 lakh AAMs are functioning in 2026. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options either omit a true statement or include statement 3.
117.tq: AAM: 2018 launch; 1.5 lakh by Dec 2022; 1.79 lakh+ now.

117.s:
Consider the following services:
1. Mental health
2. ENT and eye care
3. Geriatric and palliative care
4. Yoga and wellness
Which of the services given above form part of the CPHC package at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs?
117.x: Mental health, ENT, eye care, geriatric and palliative care, and Yoga and wellness are all included in the stated CPHC package.
117.tq: Check each service against the complete package before choosing the all-inclusive option.

117.s: Which pair correctly states the medicines and diagnostics available at AAM-PHCs?
117.x: AAM-PHCs provide 172 drugs and 63 diagnostics.
117.tq: Keep the drug count and diagnostic count paired with the correct facility level.

117.s: Under the Comprehensive Primary Health Care package at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, NCD screening covers hypertension, diabetes and which cancers?
117.x: The CPHC package screens for hypertension, diabetes and the three common cancers: oral, breast and cervical. Lung, liver, stomach, blood, bone, skin, prostate, colon and pancreatic cancers are not part of the stated population-based screening.
117.tq: AAM cancer screening = oral, breast, cervical (the 'common three').

117.s:
Consider the following statements about India's doctor-population ratio:
1. The ratio for NMC-registered allopathic doctors is about 1:834.
2. The WHO norm it is compared with is 1:1000.
3. Real availability of doctors is higher than this ratio suggests because doctors are spread evenly across rural areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: about 1:834 against the WHO norm of 1:1000. Statement 3 is wrong: real availability is lower, because doctors cluster in cities. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' omits the WHO norm and the options with 3 are wrong.
117.tq: 1:834 looks better than 1:1000, but urban clustering lowers real access.

117.s: Which of the following correctly describes human-resource challenges in rural healthcare?
o: The nurse ratio exceeds global norms and rural CHCs have no vacancies.
The nurse ratio is below global norms and specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
Only urban CHCs face specialist vacancies.
Rural CHCs have surplus specialists and no nursing shortage.
117.x: The nurse ratio is below global norms, while specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
117.tq: Identify the option that preserves both linked shortages.

117.s: Which category of health personnel is stated to carry the heaviest workload?
117.x: Community workers are stated to carry the heaviest workload.
117.tq: Identify the workload-related observation without confusing it with staffing numbers.

117.s: The Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), intended to establish AIIMS-like institutions and upgrade government medical colleges, was launched in which year?
117.x: PMSSY was launched in 2003. Its two major objectives are the establishment of AIIMS-like institutions and the upgradation of government medical colleges.
117.tq: Use the year-based numerical distinction among closely spaced options.

117.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the AIIMS serving Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the AIIMS institution associated with Andhra Pradesh.
117.tq: Discriminate among nearby place-based institutional names.

117.s: Under PM-JAY, the annual health cover provided per family is:
117.x: PM-JAY provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year.
117.tq: Recall the scheme amount by separating it from other plausible insurance figures.

117.s: eSanjeevani was developed by which organisation?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi
117.x: eSanjeevani was built by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Mohali.
117.tq: Identify the correct technology agency rather than the health-sector organisation.

117.s: Which of the following correctly describes eSanjeevani AAM?
o: Teleconsultation exclusively for armed forces personnel
Patient-to-provider consultation from the patient's home
Mental-health counselling through a national helpline
Provider-to-provider consultation through a hub-and-spoke model
117.x: eSanjeevani AAM provides provider-to-provider teleconsultation through a hub-and-spoke model.
117.tq: Separate the two eSanjeevani variants by user relationship and service setting.

117.s: A patient seeks medical advice from home through a digital platform. Which eSanjeevani variant is intended for this patient-to-provider interaction?
117.x: eSanjeevani OPD provides patient-to-provider consultation from home. eSanjeevani AAM is the provider-to-provider hub-and-spoke variant.
117.tq: Apply the patient-to-provider versus provider-to-provider distinction.

117.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Platform)
A. Tele-MANAS
B. ONCONET
C. SeHAT

List-II (Primary focus)
1. Armed forces healthcare
2. Mental health
3. Cancer-centre connectivity

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: Tele-MANAS concerns mental health, ONCONET links cancer centres, and SeHAT serves the armed forces.
117.tq: Start with the sure platform-purpose pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.

117.s: According to NFHS-3, the private sector was the main source of care for what proportion of urban households?
117.x: NFHS-3 reported that the private sector was the main source of care for 70% of urban households.
117.tq: Recall the survey-linked percentage without confusing it with other health-sector shares.

117.s: Which one of the following correctly states the current private-sector care shares given for India?
o: 43.4% of inpatient care and 1.43% of outpatient care
Over 60% of inpatient care and about 70% of outpatient care
30% of inpatient care and 70% of outpatient care
About 70% of inpatient care and over 60% of outpatient care
117.x: The private sector handles over 60% of inpatient care and about 70% of outpatient care.
117.tq: Keep inpatient and outpatient percentages in their correct order.

117.s: Which of the following was included among the recommendations of the committee concerning hospitalisation costs?
o: Uniform tariffs based only on rural PHC costs
Standard package rates and tariffs capped near nearby three-star hotel rates
A ban on private inpatient care
117.x: The committee made 368 recommendations, including standard package rates and tariffs capped near nearby three-star hotel rates.
117.tq: Identify the specific regulatory recommendation among plausible policy alternatives.

117.s: Approximately what proportion of health infrastructure is located in urban areas, which contain what proportion of the population?
117.x: About 70% of health infrastructure is in urban areas, which contain only 30% of the population.
117.tq: Identify the reversed infrastructure-population distribution trap.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about healthcare delivery in India:
1. The public health system is largely curative, with limited preventive and promotive care.
2. In cities, the private sector dominates secondary, tertiary and quaternary care.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: the public system is largely curative with limited preventive and promotive care (UPSC 2023 statement). Statement 2 is correct: the private sector dominates secondary, tertiary and quaternary care in cities. So 'Both'; '1 only' and '2 only' each reject a true statement, and 'Neither' rejects both.
117.tq: Public = curative-heavy; private = dominant in urban higher-tier care.

117.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the stated number of Village Health Clinics in Andhra Pradesh?
117.x: The stated number of Village Health Clinics is 10,032.
117.tq: Separate the Village Health Clinic count from the Sub Centre and CHC counts.

117.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh's emergency and mobile health services, which statement is correct?
o: 104 is the emergency ambulance service and 108 is the advisory service.
104 is a specialty hospital network and 108 is a telemedicine platform.
108 is the emergency ambulance service, while 104 is the mobile medical unit and health advisory service.
Both 104 and 108 are emergency ambulance services.
117.x: The 108 service provides emergency ambulances, whereas 104 provides mobile medical units and health advisory services.
117.tq: Discriminate between two easily reversed service numbers.

117.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh is located at:
117.x: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam.
117.tq: Use the location-specific hospital association.

117.s: Which institution functions as the telemedicine anchor in Andhra Pradesh and has over 2,500 out-patients a day?
117.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the telemedicine anchor and has over 2,500 OPD patients a day.
117.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive service role and patient figure.

117.s: Greyfield super-specialty blocks were being completed at which set of places?
117.x: The Greyfield super-specialty blocks were being finished at Anantapur, Nellore and Eluru.
117.tq: Identify the complete location set rather than a partially correct pair.

117.s: Which statement regarding Andhra Pradesh's Urban Primary Health Centres is correct?
o: They have not been brought under IPHS norms.
They have been upgraded to IPHS norms; 92 are NQAS-certified and 267 scored above 70% for Kayakalp.
117.x: AP's UPHCs have been upgraded to IPHS norms; 92 are NQAS-certified and 267 scored above 70% for Kayakalp.
117.tq: Combine the norm, certification and performance figures without dropping one part.

117.s: Which of the following is a feature of Andhra Pradesh's Sanjeevani digital health programme, rolled out from August 2026?
o: It provides only cancer treatment through ONCONET.
It replaces all village health clinics with AIIMS institutions.
It is restricted to armed forces personnel through SeHAT.
It issues ABHA IDs and integrates 104, 108, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine.
117.x: The programme issues ABHA IDs and integrates the 104 and 108 services, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine. The other options wrongly assign functions of separate platforms or make unsupported claims.
117.tq: Identify the option that combines the programme's stated functions without importing another platform's role.

117.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of healthcare initiatives or institutions specifically associated with the Andhra Pradesh angle?
o: Village health clinics, 104 and 108 services, Palasa, AIIMS Mangalagiri, CCBs and IPHLs
Tele-MANAS, ONCONET, SeHAT, AIIMS Delhi, PM-JAY and PMSSY
eSanjeevani OPD, MDS colleges, regional cancer centres, SeHAT and Tele-MANAS
AIIMS-like institutions, 17,893 hubs, 319 BDS colleges, ONCONET and PM-JAY
117.x: The Andhra Pradesh-specific references include village health clinics, the 104 and 108 services, Palasa, AIIMS Mangalagiri, and the new CCBs and IPHLs.
117.tq: Choose the option in which every item belongs to the same regional set.

117.s: Which of the following is identified as a major criticism or concern in India's healthcare system?
o: Excessive coverage of the missing middle and equal distribution of doctors
Low out-of-pocket expenditure and rural concentration of doctors
Absence of any public healthcare infrastructure and universal insurance coverage
High out-of-pocket expenditure, a missing middle of over 40 crore people without cover, and urban concentration of doctors
117.x: The stated concerns are high out-of-pocket expenditure, more than 40 crore people forming a 'missing middle' without cover, and the urban concentration of doctors.
117.tq: Reject options that reverse the direction of the stated healthcare problems.

118.s: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is defined as the number of deaths of infants below one year of age per how many live births in a year?
118.x: IMR denotes deaths of infants under one year per 1,000 live births in a year.
118.tq: Distinguish the population base used for IMR from that used for MMR.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding mortality indicators:
1. Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR) counts deaths in the first 28 days of life per 1,000 live births.
2. Under-Five Mortality Rate (U5MR) is expressed per 1,00,000 live births.
3. Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is expressed per 1,00,000 live births.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: NMR covers the first 28 days, per 1,000 live births. Statement 2 is wrong: U5MR, like IMR, uses a base of 1,000 live births. Statement 3 is correct: MMR alone uses 1,00,000 live births. Hence '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 are wrong and '1 only' misses 3.
118.tq: Only MMR uses the 1,00,000 base; IMR, NMR and U5MR all use 1,000.

118.s: According to the SRS 2023 figure cited for the latest estimates, India’s IMR was
118.x: The IMR was 25 according to SRS 2023, as cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26. The figures 28 and 35.2 refer to older or different sources.
118.tq: Match the latest year with the correct numerical value rather than using a stale estimate.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s IMR trend:
1. IMR was 40 in 2013.
2. IMR was 39 in 2014.
3. IMR was 37 in 2015.
4. IMR was 34 in 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: The reported IMR values were 40, 39, 37 and 34 for 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016 respectively.
118.tq: Check each year-value pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

118.s: The IMR declined from 40 in 2013 to 25 in 2023. This represents a decline of
118.x: The decline was 15 points from a base of 40, which is 37.5%; hence it was more than 37%.
118.tq: Calculate the percentage change from the original base, not from the final value.

118.s: Which State is credited with having the lowest IMR owing to adequate basic health and education facilities?
118.x: Kerala has the lowest IMR, attributed to adequate basic health and education facilities.
118.tq: Use the state-specific association rather than confusing it with AP or Telangana figures.

118.s: During 1990–2023, the NMR and U5MR declined by approximately
118.x: The NMR fell by 70%, while the U5MR fell by 78% during 1990–2023.
118.tq: Match each indicator with its distinct trend percentage.

118.s: As per SRS 2018-20, India's Maternal Mortality Ratio (maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births) was:
118.x: India's MMR was 97 per 1,00,000 live births in SRS 2018-20. 25 is India's IMR (SRS 2023), which is per 1,000 live births; 45 is Andhra Pradesh's MMR; 130 is not the SRS 2018-20 figure.
118.tq: MMR 97 per lakh; IMR 25 per thousand: watch the base.

118.s: At the time of Independence, life expectancy in India was approximately
118.x: Life expectancy at Independence was approximately 32 years.
118.tq: Identify the historical baseline rather than a later SRS life-table value.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SRS abridged life tables for 2016–20:
1. India’s male life expectancy was 68.6 years.
2. India’s female life expectancy was 71.4 years.
3. Andhra Pradesh’s male life expectancy was 69.1 years.
4. Andhra Pradesh’s female life expectancy was 72.2 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements correctly state the SRS abridged life-table values for India and Andhra Pradesh during 2016–20.
118.tq: Verify each sex-state-value combination before selecting the complete code.

118.s: Which of the following correctly describes the gender gap in life expectancy in the cited SRS 2016–20 figures?
o: Men live about three years longer than women in both India and AP.
There is no gender difference in either India or AP.
Women live exactly one year longer than men in both India and AP.
Women live about three years longer than men in both India and AP.
118.x: Women’s life expectancy exceeded men’s by about 2.8 years in India and 3.1 years in Andhra Pradesh, or approximately three years in both.
118.tq: Compare the paired male and female values before interpreting the direction of the gap.

118.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's life expectancy rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to how many years in 2023?
118.x: Life expectancy rose from 49.7 years (1973) to 70.3 years (2023). 68.3 years is the older SRS 2011-15 figure; 72.2 years is AP's female life expectancy in SRS 2016-20; 32 years was the level at Independence.
118.tq: 32 at Independence, 49.7 in 1973, 70.3 in 2023.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (NFHS Round)
a. NFHS-1
b. NFHS-2
c. NFHS-3
d. NFHS-4

List-II (Year)
i. 2005-06
ii. 1992-93
iii. 2015-16
iv. 1998-99
118.x: NFHS-1 was conducted in 1992-93, NFHS-2 in 1998-99, NFHS-3 in 2005-06 and NFHS-4 in 2015-16.
118.tq: Start with the sure earliest and latest pairs, then complete the middle matches.

118.s: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with which institution serving as the nodal agency?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, Hyderabad
International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
118.x: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, is the nodal agency.
118.tq: Apply the institutional-authority trap by distinguishing the conducting ministry from the nodal agency.

118.s: Which of the following is NOT ordinarily covered as an indicator in the National Family Health Survey?
o: India’s annual gross domestic product growth rate
118.x: NFHS covers health, mortality, nutrition, immunisation, fertility, family planning and related social indicators. It does not report India’s annual GDP growth rate as a survey indicator.
118.tq: Find the unrelated macroeconomic indicator among the health and demographic indicators.

118.s:
Which of the following was an addition in NFHS-5?
1. Death registration
2. Menstrual hygiene
3. Alcohol and tobacco use
4. NCD screening for all persons aged 15 years and above
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: NFHS-5 added death registration, pre-school education, menstrual hygiene, alcohol and tobacco use, and NCD screening for all aged 15 years and above. Thus all four listed additions are correct.
118.tq: Treat the additions as a cumulative list and check each item before choosing the complete combination.

118.s: Which statement best describes the reporting of malnutrition in the National Family Health Survey?
o: NFHS reports one single overall malnutrition percentage for the country.
NFHS reports only wasting and excludes stunting and underweight.
NFHS reports malnutrition only for urban children.
NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight separately rather than providing one single overall malnutrition percentage.
118.x: NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight as separate indicators; it does not provide one single overall ‘malnutrition percentage’.
118.tq: Distinguish separate indicators from an aggregated figure that the survey does not provide.

118.s: According to NFHS-5, which statement regarding sex ratio is correct?
o: The overall sex ratio was 1020; the rural ratio was 1,037 and the urban ratio was 985.
The overall sex ratio was 920, with the rural ratio lower than the urban ratio.
The overall sex ratio was 985; the rural ratio was 1,020 and the urban ratio was 1,037.
The overall sex ratio was 1,037, while both rural and urban ratios were below 1,000.
118.x: NFHS-5 reported an overall sex ratio of 1020, with 1,037 in rural areas and 985 in urban areas. The figure 920 refers to the child sex ratio mentioned separately.
118.tq: Avoid the confusable-pair trap between overall sex ratio and child sex ratio, and compare rural with urban values correctly.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about State-level nutrition findings in NFHS-6:
1. Madhya Pradesh recorded high child wasting and underweight.
2. Meghalaya recorded a rise in stunting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: Madhya Pradesh showed high child wasting and underweight. Statement 2 is wrong: Meghalaya showed a decline, not a rise, in stunting. Hence '1 only'.
118.tq: MP = the bad extreme; Meghalaya = the stunting success story.

118.s:
According to the WHO classification, malnutrition in all its forms includes:
1. Undernutrition, including wasting, stunting and underweight.
2. Inadequate vitamins and minerals.
3. Overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: WHO’s broad definition includes undernutrition, micronutrient inadequacy, and overnutrition with diet-related non-communicable diseases.
118.tq: Recognise the comprehensive definition instead of treating malnutrition as undernutrition alone.

118.s: The term ‘double burden of malnutrition’ refers to the coexistence of
o: Micronutrient deficiency and sanitation deficiency only
118.x: The double burden refers to the simultaneous presence of undernutrition and overnutrition.
118.tq: Distinguish the two-burden concept from the broader triple-burden description.

118.s: SOFI 2025 described India’s malnutrition situation as a triple burden comprising
o: Undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency or anaemia, and overweight
Food insecurity, poverty and poor sanitation
118.x: The triple burden consists of undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency or anaemia, and overweight.
118.tq: Separate the named forms of malnutrition from their social and health drivers.

118.s: Which indicator is defined as low height-for-age, more than two standard deviations below the WHO median?
118.x: Stunting is low height-for-age, defined here as more than two standard deviations below the WHO median.
118.tq: Distinguish anthropometric indicators by the body measurement they use.

118.s: Low weight-for-height is the characteristic measure of
118.x: Wasting is measured by low weight-for-height. Underweight uses weight-for-age, while stunting uses height-for-age.
118.tq: Swap-test the height, weight and age components carefully.

118.s: Which of the following correctly presents the NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 figures for underweight children?
118.x: Underweight declined from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6. The 35.8% figure belongs to NFHS-4.
118.tq: Track both survey round and indicator before choosing the pair.

118.s: The decline between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 was approximately what percentage for stunting and severe wasting respectively?
118.x: Stunting fell by approximately 17%, while severe wasting fell by approximately 32%. Underweight showed little change.
118.tq: Match each percentage decline to the correct nutrition indicator.

118.s: According to NFHS-5, anaemia affected approximately what proportions of children aged 6–59 months and women aged 15–49 years respectively?
118.x: NFHS-5 reported anaemia among 67.1% of children aged 6–59 months and 57.0% of women aged 15–49 years.
118.tq: Keep the age group and percentage in the same order as asked.

118.s: Underweight prevalence was highest among which of the following social groups according to NFHS-5?
o: Other Backward Classes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Scheduled Tribes, followed by Scheduled Castes
Scheduled Castes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Urban households, followed by rural households
118.x: Underweight was highest among Scheduled Tribes at 44.1%, followed by Scheduled Castes at 39.1%. It was also higher in rural areas.
118.tq: Rank the groups using the reported percentages rather than merely identifying both groups.

118.s: SOFI 2025 reported India’s wasting rate among children as approximately
118.x: SOFI 2025 reported India’s wasting rate as 18.7%, involving approximately 21 million children.
118.tq: Match the global report with its specific indicator and percentage.

118.s: Which of the following NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 pairs relating to children under five is correctly matched?
118.x: Severe wasting declined from 7.7% in NFHS-5 to 5.2% in NFHS-6. The other options interchange the values of stunting, underweight and severe wasting or use an unsupported anaemia comparison.
118.tq: Use paired numerical values to detect indicator swapping.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 findings for children under five years?
118.x: Stunting fell from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6. Options A and D reverse the order of the underweight (32.1% → 31.8%) and severe-wasting (7.7% → 5.2%) figures, and the breastfeeding figures in C are not among the stated NFHS findings.
118.tq: Check the direction of change and reject reversed pairs.

118.s: Food insecurity and poverty may contribute to both undernutrition and overnutrition because they can lead to consumption of
o: Only locally produced fruits and vegetables
118.x: Food insecurity and poverty can produce undernutrition while also encouraging consumption of inexpensive energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods that contribute to overnutrition.
118.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship to a realistic dietary situation.

118.s:
Which of the following were identified as linked to child nutrition through NFHS tracking?
1. Sanitation and drinking water
2. Women’s schooling
3. Child marriage
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: NFHS tracks sanitation, drinking water, women’s schooling and child marriage, all of which are linked to child nutrition.
118.tq: Treat the listed social determinants as a combined set rather than isolating dietary factors.

118.s:
Consider the following NFHS-5 figures linked to child nutrition:
1. About 41% of women had 10 or more years of schooling.
2. About 41% of women were married before the age of 18.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: 41% of women had 10+ years of schooling (NFHS-5). Statement 2 is wrong: the share married before 18 was 23.3%, not 41%. Hence '1 only'.
118.tq: 41% = schooling 10+ years; 23.3% = child marriage.

118.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the main driver of malnutrition in India?
o: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
118.x: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity are the main driver of malnutrition (APPSC 2025 key). Fortified rice is a remedy, not a cause; women's schooling improves child nutrition; overuse of supplements is not cited as a driver.
118.tq: Malnutrition driver = poor diet + food insecurity.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about POSHAN Abhiyaan:
1. It was launched in 2018 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
2. It aims to reduce stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight.
3. It works through convergence of ICDS, the National Health Mission and Swachh Bharat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is wrong: POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018) is under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, not Health. Statement 2 is correct: it targets stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight. Statement 3 is correct: it rests on convergence of ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
118.tq: POSHAN Abhiyaan = National Nutrition Mission = WCD ministry, not MoHFW.

118.s: Which of the following correctly describes the beneficiaries of Anganwadi Services under ICDS?
o: Only children below six months of age
Only elderly persons and persons with disabilities
Children aged six months to six years, and pregnant and lactating women
Only school-going children aged six to fourteen years
118.x: Anganwadi Services cover children from six months to six years and pregnant and lactating women.
118.tq: Distinguish the programme’s target groups from beneficiaries of school or social-security schemes.

118.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six services provided through Anganwadi Services?
118.x: The six services include supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up and referral services. Old-age pension distribution is not one of them.
118.tq: Locate the option that does not belong to the programme’s fixed list of six services.

118.s: The school meal programme formerly known as the Mid-Day Meal Scheme was renamed as PM POSHAN in:
118.x: The Mid-Day Meal programme was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021.
118.tq: Separate the launch year of one nutrition programme from the renaming year of another.

118.s: The 6x6x6 strategy is associated with which programme?
o: Rice fortification under the Public Distribution System
118.x: Anemia Mukt Bharat uses a 6x6x6 strategy consisting of six interventions, six target groups and six institutional mechanisms.
118.tq: Discriminate between similarly themed nutrition programmes by their signature strategy.

118.s: Fortified rice supplied through the Public Distribution System, ICDS and PM POSHAN is fortified with:
o: Calcium, vitamin C and vitamin D
Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12
Iodine, zinc and vitamin A only
118.x: The specified fortified rice contains iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 and is supplied through the PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN.
118.tq: Match the intervention with its exact micronutrient combination and delivery channels.

118.s: Which Andhra Pradesh scheme provides a nutritious meal along with iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis?
118.x: Anna Amrutha Hastam provides a nutritious meal and iron-folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis.
118.tq: Match the scheme name with its specific beneficiary and service.

118.s: The primary intended outcomes of Anna Amrutha Hastam include reduction of
o: Crude birth rate and crude death rate
118.x: The scheme aims to reduce infant and maternal mortality through nutrition support and iron-folic acid supplementation.
118.tq: Link the intervention to its stated health outcomes rather than to unrelated demographic indicators.

118.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the other maternal services in Andhra Pradesh?
118.x: JSY, PMSMA and LaQshya are listed among the maternal services in Andhra Pradesh. SOFI is an international food-security report, not an AP maternal service.
118.tq: Find the item belonging to a different category or institution.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Andhra Pradesh health indicators is correctly matched?
118.x: Andhra Pradesh has an MMR of 45 and an IMR of 24, both better than the corresponding national averages.
118.tq: Keep the two similarly abbreviated mortality indicators in their correct order.

119.s: According to the National Health Accounts data, Government Health Expenditure as a percentage of GDP increased from 2013–14 to 2022–23 by approximately:
119.x: Government Health Expenditure increased from 1.15% of GDP in 2013–14 to 1.43% in 2022–23, a rise of 0.28 percentage points.
119.tq: Subtract the two percentage values instead of confusing percentage points with percentage growth.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about India's National Health Accounts (NHA):
1. They are prepared by the National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat (NHATS) under NHSRC.
2. They use the System of Health Accounts (SHA) 2008 framework.
3. They were first published for the year 2013-14.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: NHATS under NHSRC (MoHFW) prepares the NHA. Statement 2 is wrong: the framework is SHA 2011 (with NHA Guidelines 2016), not SHA 2008. Statement 3 is correct: the first NHA was for 2013-14. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
119.tq: NHA: NHATS-NHSRC, SHA 2011, first year 2013-14.
